##### Grammar

- पीतये — पा पाने धातुः । स्थागा पापचोभावे (पा. सू. ३-३-९५) इति क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । घुमास्थागा— (पा. सू. ६-४-६६) इति धातोः ईत्वं । व्यत्ययेन आद्युदात्तं भवति । चतुर्थी एकवचनांतरूपं ।
- विदुः — विद ज्ञाने धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचने विदो लटो ना (पा. सू. ३-४-८३) इति जुसादेशः । शपः लुक् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तं भवति ।
- वीरस्य — अज गतिक्षेपणयोः धातुः । स्थायितंचि-- (उ. सू. २-१७०) इति रक् प्रत्ययः । अजेर्व्यघ-- (पा. सू. २-४-५६) इति धातोः वी भावः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तं भवति ।
- पौंस्या — पुंसः इमानि पौंस्यानि । ष्यञ् प्रत्ययः । ञित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (पा. सू. ६-१-७०) इति शेः लोपः । **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तभु॑जिभि॒स्तम॒भिह्रु॑तेर॒घात्पू॒र्भी र॑क्षता मरुतो॒ यमाव॑त ।  
> जनं॒ यमु॑ग्रास्तवसो विरप्यनः पा॒थना॒ शंसा॒त्तन॑यस्य  ॒॑
> पुष्टिषु ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतभुजिभिः । तं । अभिह्रुतेः । अघात् । पूभिः । रक्षत । मरुतः । यं । आवत ।  
> जनं । यं । उग्राः । तवसः । विरप्सिनः । पाथन । शंसात् । तनयस्य । पुष्टिषु ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः यूयं शतभुजिभिः । शतमित्यपरिमितनाम । असंख्यातभोगवद्भिः
> पूर्भिः पालनैर्जेतव्यैः शत्रूणां नगरैर्वा तं रक्षथ । पालयत । तमित्युक्तं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, you protect him with the शतभुजिभिः (*śatabhujibhiḥ*) पूर्भिः (*pūrbhiḥ*)." "Hundred" (शतं (*śataṃ*)) here is a name for the unlimited: the forts are those with countless enjoyments; पूर्भिः (*pūrbhiḥ*) means "with protections" or "with enemy cities that are to be conquered". तं रक्षथ (*taṃ rakṣatha*): "you protect him", that is, "him of whom it is said".

### Printed p. 38

> कमित्याह । यं जनमभिह्रुतेरभिभवकारणात्कुटिलस्वभावादघात्पापादवत अरक्षत ।
> किंच हे उग्रा उद्धूर्णतेजसो हे तवसो बलवंतो वेगवंतो ना हे विरप्पिनः ।
> महन्नामैतत् । महांतः । रपणीयाः शब्दा रपाः । ते येषां ते रप्पिनः ।
> विविधा रप्पिनः स्तोतारो येषां ते तथोक्ता हे तादृशाः यूयं यं च
> जनं पाथन पाथ रक्षथ । कस्मान्निमित्तादिति उच्यते । तनयस्य । उपलक्षणमेतत् ।
> पुत्रादीनां पुष्टिसु निमित्तभूतेषु शंसादभिशंसनात् । यमेवं कुरुथ तं रक्षतेति
> शेषः । पापक्षयाद्यनिष्पपरिहारेण पुत्रादिपोषरूपेष्टप्राप्ता च रक्षतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues: whom? The man whom you protect from अभिह्रुतेः (*abhihruteḥ*), a cause of overpowering, from crooked-natured sin (अघात् (*aghāt*)). Further, O fierce ones (उग्रा (*ugrā*), of surging splendour), तवसः (*tavasaḥ*), mighty and swift; विरप्पिनः (*virappinaḥ*): this (रप्पिनः (*rappinaḥ*)) is a name for "great", the great ones. Words worth uttering are रपाः (*rapāḥ*); those who have them are रप्पिनः (*rappinaḥ*); those who have various रप्पिनः (*rappinaḥ*), that is, praisers, are so called. Such as you, whomever you protect (पाथन (*pāthana*) = पाथ रक्षथ (*pātha rakṣatha*)). On what ground is it said? तनयस्य (*tanayasya*) is only illustrative: because of calumny (शंसात् (*śaṃsāt*)) in the matters that cause the nourishment of sons and the rest. "Him who does so, protect" is the remainder. The meaning: protect him by averting what is undesired, such as the destruction through sin, and in the attainment of the desired, in the form of nourishment of sons and others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom (which man)
- अभिह्रुतेः (*abhihruteḥ*)—from what causes overpowering (of crooked nature)
- अघात् (*aghāt*)—from sin
- आवत (*āvata*)—you protect
- उग्राः (*ugrāḥ*)—fierce ones
- तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)—mighty ones
- विरप्पिनः (*virappinaḥ*)—endowed with greatness (having various praisers)
- यं जनं (*yaṃ janaṃ*)—whichever man
- तनयस्य (*tanayasya*)—of a son (of sons and the rest)
- पुष्टिषु (*puṣṭiṣu*)—in the matter of nourishments
- शंसात् (*śaṃsāt*)—from calumny
- पाथन (*pāthana*)—you protect
- तं (*taṃ*)—that man
- शतभुजिभिः (*śatabhujibhiḥ*)—endowed with countless enjoyments
- पूर्भिः (*pūrbhiḥ*)—with protective acts, or with enemy cities to be conquered
- रक्षत (*rakṣata*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, fierce, exceedingly mighty, and praised by various praisers: some you protect from sin that brings about overpowering; others you protect by the nourishment of sons and the rest; for all of them, having conquered the enemy cities that give unlimited enjoyment, be their protectors.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Maruts, gratify, with infinite and complete enjoyments, him, whom you protect from degrading sin: that man whom, fierce and mighty, and glorified (as you are), you defend from calumny, by (providing for) the nourishment of his descendants.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अभिह्रुतेः (*abhihruteḥ*)—अभिभवकारणात्कुटिलस्वभावात् (*abhibhavakāraṇātkuṭilasvabhāvāt*): from an evil nature that brings about harm. This word is formed from the root ह्रु (*hru*). The root ह्रु (*hru*) is not stated in the Dhātupāṭha. When explaining the word ह्रुणाति (*hruṇāti*), formed from this root, in the 12th Ṛk of this same sūkta, the commentator explained its meaning through another root with the same meaning, ह्वरति (*hvarati*).

### Printed p. 39

In the Ṛk

स नस्त्रासते दुरितादभिह्रुतः शंसादघावभिह्रुतः (*sa nastrāsate duritādabhihrutaḥ śaṃsādaghāvabhihrutaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-128-5)

for the word अभिह्रुतः (*abhihrutaḥ*) the commentator explained: आभिमुख्येन पापैः ह्रियमाणान् नोऽस्मान् दुरितात्पापात्रासते त्रायते (*ābhimukhyena pāpaiḥ hriyamāṇān no 'smān duritātpāpātrāsate trāyate*). That is: he protects us from sin, from assault, from evil speech and from violence. (He protects us from evil, from assault, from evil-speaking, from assault).

In the Ṛk

विश्वाद्रिरिक्षोरुत ना निनित्सोरभिह्रुतामसि हि देव विष्पट् (*viśvādririkṣoruta nā ninitsorabhihrutāmasi hi deva viṣpaṭ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-189-6)

for the word अभिह्रुतां (*abhihrutāṃ*) Sāyaṇa explained: अभिह्रुतामाभिमुख्येन कुटिलं कुर्वतां द्विषां (*abhihrutāmābhimukhyena kuṭilaṃ kurvatāṃ dviṣāṃ*)—"of the enemies who especially cause us trouble". Besides, the word विह्रुत (*vihruta*), formed with the prefix वि (*vi*) added to this root, occurs only in the two Ṛks

संधाता संधिं मघवा पुरूवसुरिष्कर्ता विह्रुतं पुनः (*saṃdhātā saṃdhiṃ maghavā purūvasuriṣkartā vihrutaṃ punaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-12)

क्षमा रपो मरुत आतुरस्य न इष्कर्ता विह्रुतं पुनः (*kṣamā rapo maruta āturasya na iṣkartā vihrutaṃ punaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-20-26)

The word suggests the meaning "(already) injured". Further, in

ता हि क्षत्रमविह्रुतं सम्यगसुर्य १ माशाते (*tā hi kṣatramavihrutaṃ samyagasurya 1 māśāte*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-66-2)

विभ्राड् बृहत्पिबतु सोम्यं मध्वायुर्दधद्यज्ञ पतावविह्रुतं (*vibhrāḍ bṛhatpibatu somyaṃ madhvāyurdadhadyajña patāvavihrutaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-170-1)

the word अविह्रुतं (*avihrutaṃ*) indicates negation; that is, it says that निह्रुत (*nihruta*) has the sense of obstruction. The meaning: free of any kind of trouble or injury.

पूर्भिः (*pūrbhiḥ*)—पालनैर्जेतवैः शत्रुणां नगरैर्वा (*pālanairjetavaiḥ śatruṇāṃ nagarairvā*): with protections, or with the enemy cities (that you conquer and give).

तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)—बलवंतो वेगवंतो वा (*balavaṃto vegavaṃto vā*): possessing strength, or swift of motion. The word तवसः (*tavasaḥ*) is read among the twenty-five names of strength beginning with महत् ब्रह्मः (*mahat brahmaḥ*) (Ni. 3-13).

विरप्यनः (*virapyanaḥ*)—महन्नामैतत् । महांतः । रपणीयाः शब्दा रपाः । ते येषां ते रप्यनः । विविधा रप्यनः स्तोतारो येषां ते (*mahannāmaitat | mahāṃtaḥ | rapaṇīyāḥ śabdā rapāḥ | te yeṣāṃ te rapyanaḥ | vividhā rapyanaḥ stotāro yeṣāṃ te*). The word विरप्य (*virapya*) is read among the twenty-five names of "great" beginning with महत् ब्रथ्नः (*mahat brathnaḥ*)

### Printed p. 40

(Ni. 3-13); so विरप्सिनः (*virapsinaḥ*) means the great, the excellent. Moreover, explaining the parts of the word, the commentator says: distinctly uttered words are called रपाः (*rapāḥ*); hymns that contain those words, or the praisers, are called रप्सिनः (*rapsinaḥ*); those (the Maruts) who are praised by such manifold hymns (or by praisers) are called विरप्सिनः (*virapsinaḥ*).

##### Grammar

- शतभुजिभिः — शतं भुजयः येषां ते, तैः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ।
- अभिह्रुतेः — तादौ च निति (पा. सू. ६-२-५०) इति गतेः (अभि) प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति । पंचमी एकवचनांतरूपं ।
- पूर्भिः — स्य पालनपूरणयोः धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । उदोष्य पूर्वस्य (पा. सू. ७-१-१०२) इति उत् । रपरत्वं भवति । भिस् परे हलि च इति उपधादीर्घः । **NOTE**
- रक्षत — रक्ष पालने धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरं भवति ।
- आवत — अव रक्षणे धातुः । लज् मध्यमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपं । यद्वृत्तान्वितं (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधो भवति । तास्यनुदात्तेत्—सूत्रेण लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वात् आद्युदात्तं भवति ।
- तवसः — छांदसत्वेन मतुपः लोपो भवति । आमंत्रितस्य च—(पा. सू. ८-१-१९) इति निघातस्वरं भवति ।
- विरिष्यिनः — रस व्यक्तायां वाचि धातुः । उणादिषु बहुलवचनसामर्थ्यात् विपूर्वस्य अस्य शक् प्रत्ययः । विविधं शब्दं रसंति इति विरप्याः—स्तोतारः ते येषां संति इति विरप्पिनः । मत्त्वर्थे इनि प्रत्ययः । आमंत्रितनिघातस्वरं भवति ।
- पाथन — पा रक्षणे धातुः । अदादौ लोट् प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचनस्य तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च (पा. सू. ७-१-४५) इति थनादेशः । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरेण मध्योदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- शंसात् — शंसु स्तुतौ धातुः । भावार्थे घञ् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, in your cars" (वो रथेषु (*vo ratheṣu*)), in the cars that belong to you, the instruments of swift going, "all good things" (विश्वानि भद्रा (*viśvāni bhadrā*)): all auspicious things, substances fit for enjoyment, or fruits to be given to us, "have been placed" (आहिता (*āhitā*)). Likewise अंसेषु (*aṃseṣu*), on your shoulders, that is, on the arms indicated by them; the particle आ (*ā*) has the sense of "also". "As if vying with one another" (मिथस्पृध्येव (*mithaspṛdhyeva*)): from excess of strength, the तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*), the strengths, which are matters of mutual rivalry, namely the weapons of the kind stated, are placed on the shoulders. Further, वः प्रपथेषु (*vaḥ prapatheṣu*): प्रपथानि (*prapathāni*) are resting places on which the paths go forward; in them खादयः (*khādayaḥ*), edibles and foods, have been placed. Or else: प्रपथेषु (*prapatheṣu*) means "at the tips of the feet", where the paths go forward, and खादयः (*khādayaḥ*) are firm special ornaments, placed there. Further, अक्षः (*akṣaḥ*), your chariot's axle, and the wheels fixed on it (चक्रा (*cakrā*)): समया (*samayā*), near them, in their vicinity, वि ववृते (*vi vavṛte*), it turns specially; the meaning is that it never becomes stuck to the wheels. His purport: since such means for going to the place of divine sacrifice are ready, therefore come quickly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- रथेषु (*ratheṣu*)—in the cars
- विश्वानि भद्रा (*viśvāni bhadrā*)—all things that serve enjoyment, or things to be given to us
- आ हिता (*ā hitā*)—have been placed
- अंसेषु आ (*aṃseṣu ā*)—on your shoulders too
- मिथस्पृध्या इव (*mithaspṛdhyā iva*)—as if from mutual rivalry
- तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*)—strengths (weapons that display strength)
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- प्रपथेषु (*prapatheṣu*)—in the resting places on the road
- खादयः (*khādayaḥ*)—edible things (have been placed)

### Printed p. 42

(Continuing the list:) [or प्रपथेषु (*prapatheṣu*)—at the tips of the feet; खादयः (*khādayaḥ*)—firm special ornaments (have been worn)]

- किंच (*kiṃca*)—and further
- वः अक्षः (*vaḥ akṣaḥ*)—your (chariot's) axle
- चक्रा (*cakrā*)—of the wheels (fixed to it)
- समया (*samayā*)—near
- वि ववृते (*vi vavṛte*)—are specially present

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, in your cars all things that serve enjoyment, or things to be given to us, are made ready; the weapons that are the means of our protection are carried on your shoulders; in the resting houses on your road, edibles are made ready (the special ornaments that should be on the tips of your feet are also worn); the wheels of your car are fitted correctly to the axle of the car. (Thus, when everything is ready for your journey, set out quickly for our sacrificial hall.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Maruts, all good things are in your cars : on your shoulders abides emulous strength: at your resting-places on the road refreshments (are ready): the axle of your (chariot) wheels holds them firmly together.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विश्वानि भद्रा महतो रथेषु वः (*viśvāni bhadrā mahato ratheṣu vaḥ*)—In this Ṛk the seer, desiring the coming of the Maruts, describes everything as ready for their coming. O Maruts, in your car all excellent or choice things have been made ready. These things are fit for enjoyment; the main purport of this sentence is that these substances have been prepared and placed in your car in order to be given to us, who praise.

रथेषु (*ratheṣu*)—Yāska in his Nirukta says of the word रथ (*ratha*): रथो रंहतेर्गतिकर्मणः । स्थिरतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य । रममाणोऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति वा रपतेर्वा रसतेर्वा (*ratho raṃhatergatikarmaṇaḥ | sthiratervā syādviparītasya | ramamāṇo 'smiṃstiṣṭhatīti vā rapatervā rasatervā*) (Ni. 9-11). That is, it may be formed from the root रंह् (*raṃh*) denoting the action of going, or from the root स्थिरति (*sthirati*) meaning "be firm". Because this car is always going (moving about), it is called रथ (*ratha*). Or else, the warrior who sits in it remains steady: whereas the body shakes when one sits on horses and the like, one can sit steadily without shaking in a car, so it is called रथ (*ratha*). Or else, because one sits in this car and moves about happily, it is called रथ (*ratha*); thus he has explained the parts of the word. **NOTE**

मिथस्पृधैव (*mithaspṛdhaiva*)—बलाधिक्यात्परस्परस्पर्धाविषयाणि (*balādhikyātparasparaspardhāviṣayāṇi*): from excess of strength, touching one another (striking against) and rubbing, clashing against each other, metal and the like **NOTE**

### Printed p. 43
…made of metals, various weapons are gathered together and placed in one spot in the chariot; as the chariot moves, those weapons strike against one another and make a noise. This is the intention.

तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*)—The word तविष (*taviṣa*) is read among the names of strength (Ni. 3-13). But since the word is used here in the neuter plural, it is not proper to explain तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*) in the first Ṛk of this sūkta as "capacities, prowess, daring deeds". For capacities and daring deeds are not things that are placed in chariots; they are only names of actions. Or, even if तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*) is taken to mean armies, it is impossible to place armies in a chariot, however large it may be. Therefore the meaning "strong weapons" alone is proper for the word तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*). Hence the sentence मिथस्पृधैव तविषाण्याहिता (*mithaspṛdhaiva taviṣāṇyāhitā*) means: many excellent weapons, which clash against one another with the motion of the chariot, are placed in your chariot.

अंसेष्वा वः (*aṃseṣvā vaḥ*)—Besides the weapons in the chariot mentioned above, you bear some other weapons on your arms.

प्रपथेषु खादयः (*prapatheṣu khādayaḥ*)—वः प्रपथेषु । प्रगताः पंथानो येषु विश्रामस्थानेषु तानि । प्रपथानि । तेषु खादयः खाद्यानि भक्ष्याण्याहितानि । यद्वा प्रगतः पंथा मैस्तेषु पादाग्रेषु खादयः स्थिरा आभरणविशेषा अहिताः ॥ (*vaḥ prapatheṣu | pragatāḥ paṃthāno yeṣu viśrāmasthāneṣu tāni | prapathāni | teṣu khādayaḥ khādyāni bhakṣyāṇyāhitāni | yadvā pragataḥ paṃthā maisteṣu pādāgreṣu khādayaḥ sthirā ābharaṇaviśeṣā ahitāḥ ‖*) The commentator has given two kinds of meaning for this sentence. A प्रपथ (*prapatha*) is a place where, on a journey, one sits to rest when tired from walking for some time. It is natural to sit in such a place and eat the foods one has brought along; this matter is what is indicated here. Or else प्रपथ (*prapatha*) means the feet used for walking, and the anklets worn on them are called खादयः (*khādayaḥ*); this is the other meaning he has given.

The German scholar Max Müller treats the two sentences अंसेष्वा वः प्रपथेषु खादयः (*aṃseṣvā vaḥ prapatheṣu khādayaḥ*) as one sentence and explains it thus: "When you are on your journeys, you carry rings on your shoulders." (You wear ornaments (weapons?) on your shoulders when you travel.) To support this, while explaining the word वृषखादयः (*vṛṣakhādayaḥ*) in Ṛk 1-64-10 of the Ṛ. Saṃ., he discusses the word खादि (*khādi*) thus:

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
In वृषखादयः (*vṛṣakhādayaḥ*) the meaning of खादि (*khādi*) is by no means clear. Sayana evidently guesses and proposes two meanings-weapon or food. In several

### Printed p. 44
passages where खादि (*khādi*) occurs, it seems to be an ornament rather than
a weapon, yet if derived from khad to bite, it may originally have signified
some kind of weapon. Roth tranlates it by ring, and it is certain that
these khadis were to be seen not only on the arms and shoulders, but
likewise on the feet of the Maruts. There is a famous weapon in India,
the चक्र (*cakra*) or quoit, a ring with sharp edges (चक्रायुध (*cakrāyudha*)) which is thrown from
a great distance with fatal effect. Bollensen (Orient and Occident Vol. II.
p. 46) suggests for वृषन् (*vṛṣan*) the meanig of hole in the ear, and then translates
the compound as having earrings in the hole of the ear. But वृषन् (*vṛṣan*) does not
mean the hole in the lap of the ear, nor has वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*) that meaning either in
the Veda or elsewhere. Wilson gives for वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*), not for वृषन् (*vṛṣan*), the meaning
of orifice of the ear, but this is very different from the hole in the lap of
the ear. Benfey suggests that the khadis were made of the teeth of wild
animals and hence their name of biters. वृषन् (*vṛṣan*) conveys the meanig of
strong, though possibly with the implied idea of rain-producing, fertlising.
In वृषन् (*vṛṣan*) we have one of those words which it is almost impossible to
translate accurately. It occurs over and over again in the Vedic Hymns, and
if we once know the various ideas which it either expreesss or implies, we
have little difficulty in understanding its import in a vague and genaral
way, though we look in vain for corresponding terms in any modern
language. In the Veda, and in ancient languages generally, one and the
same word is frequently made to do service for many. Words retain their
general meaning, though at the same time they are evidently used with
a definite purpose. This is not only a peculiar phase of language, but
a peculiar phase of thought, and as to us this phase hase become strange and
unreal, it is very difficult to transport ourselves back into it, still more to
translate the pregnant terms of the Vedic poets into the definite languages
which we have to use.

There is another mantra that says that the Marut deities wear the ornaments or special weapons called खादि (*khādi*) on their shoulders:

### Printed p. 45
अंसेष्वा मरुतः खादयो वो वक्षःसु रुक्मा उपशिश्रियाणाः । वि विद्युतो न वृष्टिभी रुचाना अनु स्वधामायुधैर्यच्छमानाः ॥ (*aṃseṣvā marutaḥ khādayo vo vakṣaḥsu rukmā upaśiśriyāṇāḥ | vi vidyuto na vṛṣṭibhī rucānā anu svadhāmāyudhairyacchamānāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-13)
In this Ṛk the description is: O Maruts, on your shoulders are the special weapons called खादि (*khādi*); on your chests golden chains are fastened.

In the Ṛks
ऐषामंसेषु रंभिणीव रारभे हस्तेषु खादिश्च कृतिश्च सं दधे । (*aiṣāmaṃseṣu raṃbhiṇīva rārabhe hasteṣu khādiśca kṛtiśca saṃ dadhe |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-3)
त्वेषं गणं तवसं खादिहस्तं धुनिव्रतं मायिनं दातिवारं । (*tveṣaṃ gaṇaṃ tavasaṃ khādihastaṃ dhunivrataṃ māyinaṃ dātivāraṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-28-2)
the weapon called खादि (*khādi*) is described as held in the hand.

Where the special weapons of the Marut deities and the places where they are worn are described, in the Ṛk
अंसेषु वः ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षस्सु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः । (*aṃseṣu vaḥ ṛṣṭayaḥ patsu khādayo vakṣassu rukmā maruto rathe śubhaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-11)
the खादि (*khādi*) weapons (or ornaments) are described as worn on the feet. (The khadis are on your forefeet.) But since it is not possible to wear weapons on the feet, the word खादि (*khādi*) here must mean a kind of ornament. Although we do not now know the shape and nature of the खादि (*khādi*), it is beyond dispute that it is a special weapon shaped like a wheel. Since it is round, like a bangle, it may be conjectured that the anklets worn on the feet for decoration (wheel-like) are what is described in many places under the name खादि (*khādi*). Whether it was worn on the foot, the shoulder or the hands at other times, in fighting it had to be worn in the hands alone. So the seers have described this matter in different ways. The special weapon called the wheel (चक्र (*cakra*)) in the hand of Viṣṇu may also have come into use on the basis of the weapon called खादि (*khādi*).

Many Western scholars do not accept as proper the meaning "edibles fit for eating" which the commentator gives for the word खादि (*khādi*) (खाद्यानि भक्ष्याणि (*khādyāni bhakṣyāṇi*)). Max Müller on this matter:

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
What however is quite certain is this, that खादि (*khādi*) in the Veda never
means food, as Sayana optionally interprets it. This interpretation is
accepted by Wilson, who translates-at your resting places on the road

### Printed p. 46
refreshments (are ready). Nay, he goes on in a note to use this passage as
a proof of the advanced civilisation of India at the time of the Vedic
Rishis. " The expression " he says " is worthy of note as indicating the
existence of accomodations for the use of travellers: the प्रपथ (*prapatha*) is the choltri
(छत्र (*chatra*)) of the south of India, the Sarai of Mohammadans, a place by the
roadside whare the travellers may find shelter and provisions."

As for the meaning of the word प्रपथ (*prapatha*), although in this Ṛk the commentator explains प्रपथेषु (*prapatheṣu*) as पंथानो विश्रामस्थानेषु (*paṃthāno viśrāmasthāneṣu*), resting places met with on the road, yet in Ṛks such as
आयुर्विश्वायुः परि पासति त्वा पूषा त्वा पातु प्रपथे पुरस्तात् । (*āyurviśvāyuḥ pari pāsati tvā pūṣā tvā pātu prapathe purastāt |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-4)
प्रपथे पथामजनिष्ट पूपा प्रपथे दिवः प्रपथे पृथिव्याः । (*prapathe pathāmajaniṣṭa pūpā prapathe divaḥ prapathe pṛthivyāḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-6)
स्वस्तिरिद्दि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्ण स्वत्यभि या वाममेति । (*svastiriddi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇa svatyabhi yā vāmameti |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-63-16)
he gives for the word प्रपथे (*prapathe*) the meaning प्रकृष्टे मार्गे (*prakṛṣṭe mārge*), "on an excellent road". Therefore, for the words प्रपथेषु पादयः (*prapatheṣu pādayaḥ*) in this Ṛk, the proper meaning is that the Marut deities wear the special weapons called खादि (*khādi*) while travelling on excellent roads.

अक्षो वश्चक्रा समया वि वावृते (*akṣo vaścakrā samayā vi vāvṛte*)—अक्षो वो युष्मत्संबंधी रथ्योऽक्षश्चक्रा तत्रोपनिबद्धानि चक्राणि समया समीपे तेषां परिसरे वि ववृते विशेषेण वर्तते न कदाचिदपि चक्रेषु संलग्नो भवतीत्यर्थः । (*akṣo vo yuṣmatsaṃbaṃdhī rathyo 'kṣaścakrā tatropanibaddhāni cakrāṇi samayā samīpe teṣāṃ parisare vi vavṛte viśeṣeṇa vartate na kadācidapi cakreṣu saṃlagno bhavatītyarthaḥ |*) O Maruts, the axle of your chariot makes the wheels on its sides turn round at one and the same time. They are firmly joined; they do not come off the axle. The same meaning is stated in the Ṛk
सत्रा ते अनु कृष्टयो विश्वा चक्रेन वावृतुः । (*satrā te anu kṛṣṭayo viśvā cakrena vāvṛtuḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-2)
The main intention is that your chariot travels happily without any obstruction. To say here that the axle makes the wheel turn is not correct. The wheels turn because the horses pull the chariot. Still, since the wheels are near the axle and connected with it, the seer may have described it so.

### Printed p. 47
In the Veda the word समया (*samayā*) means "together" or "at one time".

##### Grammar

- भद्रा — भदि कल्याणे सुखे च धातुः । अस्मात् औणादिकः रक् प्रत्ययः । नपुंसकबहुवचने शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (पा. सू. ६-१-७०) इति शेः लोपः ।
- आहिता — आज् उपसर्गः । डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । कर्मणि निष्ठा इति क्तप्रत्ययः । दधातेर्हिः (पा. सू. ७-४-४२) इति धातोः हि आदेशः । गतिरनंतरः (पा. सू. ६-२-४९) इति गतेः (आ) उदात्तस्वरः भवति । पूर्ववत् नपुंसकबहुवचने शेः लोपः ।
- मिथस्पृध्या — स्पर्ध संघर्षे धातुः । अस्मात् क्विप् आगते बहुलं छंदसि इति धातुरेफस्य संप्रसारणं । अकारलोपः । स्पर्धंते इति स्पृधः । अस्मात् भावार्थे यत् प्रत्ययः । यतो नावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । पूर्ववत् शेः लोपः ।
- प्रपथेषु — प्रगताः पंथानो येसु तासि प्रपथासि, तेषु । ऋक् पूरब् धूःपथामानक्षे (पा. सू. ५-४-७४) इति अकारप्रत्ययः समासांतः भवति । टिलोपः । बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । **NOTE**
- चक्रा — चक्राणि इति रूपे जाते शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (पा. सू. ६-१-७०) इति शेः लोपः । अग्रे समया इति योगः अस्ति इति कारणात् अभितः परितः समया इति वचनेन षष्ठ्याः अपवादतया द्वितीया भवति ।
- ववृते — वृतु वर्तने धातुः । छांदसतया लिट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति । ॥ ९ ॥

> वि धिरे । विविधं धारयंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वयो न पक्षान् पक्षिणः पक्षानिव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Maruts, in their arms that are beneficial to men, bear abundant auspicious (भद्रा (*bhadrā*)) riches to give to the praisers; धिरे (*dhire*) is a form of धारयंति (*dhārayaṃti*), "they hold". So too on their chests they wear ornaments (रुक्माः (*rukmāḥ*)) made of gold, jewels and the like. Of what kind? रभसासः (*rabhasāsaḥ*) means full of impetuosity or radiant, and अंजयः (*aṃjayaḥ*) means manifest. On the shoulder-roots are these white garlands. On their vajra-like weapons are razor-edges (क्षुराः (*kṣurāḥ*)). अधि (*adhi*) only restates the sense of the locative. Thus the Maruts variously bear splendour (श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)) on all their limbs in due order. The illustration: वयो न पक्षान् (*vayo na pakṣān*)—as birds bear wings. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते मरुतः (*te marutaḥ*)—those Maruts
- नर्येषु (*naryeṣu*)—beneficial to men
- बाहुषु (*bāhuṣu*)—in the arms
- भूरीणि (*bhūrīṇi*)—abundant
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—auspicious (riches to be given to the praisers)
- धिरे (*dhire*)—they bear
- वक्षस्सु (*vakṣassu*)—on the chests
- रभसासः (*rabhasāsaḥ*)—radiant, and
- अंजयः (*aṃjayaḥ*)—manifest
- रुक्माः (*rukmāḥ*)—ornaments made of gold and the like (they bear)
- अंगेषु (*aṃgeṣu*)—on the shoulder-roots
- एताः (*etāḥ*)—white garlands also
- पविषु (*paviṣu*)—on the vajra-like weapons
- क्षुराः (*kṣurāḥ*)—sharp edges also
- अधि (धिरे) (*adhi (dhire)*)—they have (thus the Maruts)
- श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)—(various) ornaments
- अनु (*anu*)—in the (stated) order
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—birds
- पक्षान् न (*pakṣān na*)—as (they bear) wings (of various colours)
- वि (धिरे) (*vi (dhire)*)—variously (they bear)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

On the arms of the Maruts, who bring benefit to men, are many auspicious things dear to men; on their chests are gleaming, clearly visible golden ornaments; on their shoulders are clean garlands, and (in their hands) sharp, vajra-like weapons. Just as birds have wings of many colours, the Maruts too are variously adorned. (Or, they spread their radiance all around.)

### Printed p. 49

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Maruts, in your arms, propitious to man, are many good things: on your breasts are golden (ornaments), brilliant and conspicuous : white garlands (hang) on your shoulders : sharp are (the edges of) your weapons : the Maruts have various decorations, as birds have (many coloured) wings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the ornaments and weapons that the Maruts wear on their various limbs for decoration are described.

भूरीणि भद्रा नर्येषु बाहुषु (*bhūrīṇi bhadrā naryeṣu bāhuṣu*)—The Maruts carry excellent things in their strong arms (hands) in order to give them (to the sacrificer). That is, they hold in their hands many auspicious, excellent things, to be given to the sacrificers who praise them. Here the commentator explains the word नर्येषु (*naryeṣu*) as नरेभ्यो हितेषु (*narebhyo hiteṣu*), "beneficial to men", that is, "desired by men". Max Müller renders it "manly", that is, (arms) strong as men ought to have.

वक्षस्सु रुक्मा (*vakṣassu rukmā*)—उरःस्थलेषु रुक्माः सुवर्णरत्नादिनिर्मितान्याभरणानि धार यंति । (*uraḥsthaleṣu rukmāḥ suvarṇaratnādinirmitānyābharaṇāni dhāra yaṃti |*) On the chest, that is, on the breast, they wear necklaces and other ornaments made of gold, jewels and the like. This matter is also described in the Ṛk वक्षःसु रुक्मा (*vakṣaḥsu rukmā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-4). The word रुक्मा (*rukmā*), in the nominative plural, is used to indicate the golden necklaces and other ornaments the Maruts wear on their breasts. For this very reason, in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-2; 5-55-1; 5-57-5 the Maruts are called रुक्मवक्षसः (*rukmavakṣasaḥ*) (wearers of gold ornaments on the breast—gold-breasted). In the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. Śrau. Sū. 9-4)**NOTE** and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-18-1), रुक्मं होत्रॆ (*rukmaṃ hotrè*) designates the golden ornament given in the sacrifice, as the priest's fee, to the priest called the Hotṛ. This ornament is said to be circular in shape; perhaps it was like the ornament called a necklace.

रभसासः (*rabhasāsaḥ*)—राभस्ययुक्तानि कांतिमंति वा । (*rābhasyayuktāni kāṃtimaṃti vā |*) Shining brilliantly. This word is derived from the root रभ् (*rabh*), "to rush upon, to fall upon". The word always expresses strength accompanied by speed. The word रभस (*rabhasa*) is found used not only of the Maruts but also of Agni and Indra.

### Printed p. 50
पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः स्वय्या मत्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः । (*pṛśneḥ putrā upamāso rabhiṣṭhāḥ svayyā matyā marutaḥ saṃ mimikṣuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-58-5)
In this Ṛk the word रभिष्ठाः (*rabhiṣṭhāḥ*) (most powerful) is used as an epithet of the Maruts.

पृथुं तिरश्चा वयसा बृहंतं व्यचिष्ठमन्नॆ रभसं दृशानं । (*pṛthuṃ tiraścā vayasā bṛhaṃtaṃ vyaciṣṭhamannè rabhasaṃ dṛśānaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-10-4)
Here the word रभसं (*rabhasaṃ*) is used as an epithet of Agni.

विष्कभ्यंतः स्कंभनेना जनित्री आसीना ऊर्ध्वं रभसं वि मिन्वन् । (*viṣkabhyaṃtaḥ skaṃbhanenā janitrī āsīnā ūrdhvaṃ rabhasaṃ vi minvan |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-12)
In this Ṛk the word रभसं (*rabhasaṃ*) is used as an epithet of Indra; and in some places this word is found used in the senses of cruel, terrible, rushing swiftly and falling upon.

अधा शयीत निर्ऋतेरुपस्थेऽधैनं वृका रभसासो अद्युः । (*adhā śayīta nirṛterupasthe 'dhainaṃ vṛkā rabhasāso adyuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-14)
In this Ṛk the word रभसासः (*rabhasāsaḥ*) is an epithet of वृकाः (*vṛkāḥ*) (wolves), in the sense of "rushing swiftly, terrible". In the present Ṛk the word रभस (*rabhasa*) is used in the sense of "glittering, brilliant".

भद्रान्‌कृण्वन्निंद्रहवान्त्सखिभ्य आ सोमो वस्त्रा रभसानि दत्ते । (*bhadrānkṛṇvanniṃdrahavāntsakhibhya ā somo vastrā rabhasāni datte |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-96-1)
In this Ṛk too it is used in this same sense, as an epithet of the word वस्त्रा (*vastrā*).

The ornaments and weapons of the Maruts are described in detail in the Ṛks:

चित्रैरंजिभिर्वपुषे व्यंजते वक्षःसु रुक्मा अधि येतिरे शुभे । अंसेष्वेषां नि मिमृक्षुर्ऋष्ययः साकं जज्जिरे स्वधया दिवो नरः ॥ (*citrairaṃjibhirvapuṣe vyaṃjate vakṣaḥsu rukmā adhi yetire śubhe | aṃseṣveṣāṃ ni mimṛkṣurṛṣyayaḥ sākaṃ jajjire svadhayā divo naraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-4)
अंसेषु व ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षःसु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः । अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः ॥ (*aṃseṣu va ṛṣṭayaḥ patsu khādayo vakṣaḥsu rukmā maruto rathe śubhaḥ | agnibhrājaso vidyuto gabhastyoḥ śiprāḥ śīrṣasu vitatā hiraṇyayīḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-11)

एताः (*etāḥ*)—शुक्लवर्णा मालाः । (*śuklavarṇā mālāḥ |*) White garlands or necklaces: this is the commentator's explanation. The word एताः (*etāḥ*) would indicate a spotted deer. For this reason

### Printed p. 51
Western scholars hold that the sense suggested here is that the Maruts wear (wrap round) on their shoulders the skin of a spotted deer. For in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra and in other Gṛhya Sūtras there is a rule that a Brahmin should wear a deer-skin like a garment (or in place of one). A student who studies the Veda after the initiation (upanayana) is to wear, if a Brahmin, the skin of the ऐणेय (*aiṇeya*) (deer); if a Kṣatriya, the skin of the रौरव (*raurava*) (the deer called ruru); if a Vaiśya, the skin of the अज (*aja*) (goat). And when wearing garments, the Brahmin is to wear a काषाय (*kāṣāya*) garment (dark red), the Kṣatriya a garment of मांजिष्ठ (*māṃjiṣṭha*) colour (bright red), the Vaiśya a garment of हारिद्र (*hāridra*) colour (yellow). It can therefore be said that it was the custom to use deer-skin instead of a garment. For this very reason the seer in the present Ṛk may have described the Maruts as wearing deer-skin on their shoulders. Dressed deer-skin used as a garment is called अजिन (*ajina*). It is also called कृष्णाजिन (*kṛṣṇājina*) (red deer-skin). Though the word अजिन (*ajina*) is not used in the Ṛgveda, it is especially frequent in the Yajurveda and the other Vedas.

क्षुराः (*kṣurāḥ*)—Weapons with sharp edges. क्षुराः (*kṣurāḥ*) is also the name of the shaving knife (razor), because a razor has to be very sharp. In speaking of a sharp weapon it is the custom to cite the example of the razor, क्षुराः (*kṣurāḥ*). It appears that in the Ṛgveda period, and even before it, shaving with a knife was customary. On this point:

यदा ते वातो अनुवाति शोचिर्वप्तेव स्मश्रु वपसि प्र भूम । (*yadā te vāto anuvāti śocirvapteva smaśru vapasi pra bhūma |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-142-4)
केशश्मश्रु वपते नखानि निकृंतते मृता वा एषा त्वगमेध्या यत्केशश्मश्रु मृतामेव त्वचममेध्यामपहत्य यज्ञियो भूत्वा मेधमुपैति । (*keśaśmaśru vapate nakhāni nikṛṃtate mṛtā vā eṣā tvagamedhyā yatkeśaśmaśru mṛtāmeva tvacamamedhyāmapahatya yajñiyo bhūtvā medhamupaiti |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-1-2)
These and similar mantras support the fact that shaving with a knife was customary.

वयो न पक्षान् वि अनु श्रियो धिरे (*vayo na pakṣān vi anu śriyo dhire*)—Here श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*) means splendour, beauty. The meaning is that, as birds spread their wings open when they fly, so when the Maruts travel their splendour spreads all around, in every direction.

##### Grammar

- नर्येषु—नराय हिताः नर्याः । यत् प्रत्ययः । यस्येति च इत्यनेन अकारलोपः । यतोनावः इत्यनेन आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- रुक्माः—रुच दीप्तौ धातुः । युजि रुजितिजांकुश्च (उ. सू. १-१४३) इत्यनेन मक् प्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेन धातोरंत्यस्य कुत्वं । कित्त्वात् लघूपधगुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- रभसासः—रभ राभस्ये धातुः । अत्यःविचमित—(उ. सू. ३-३९७) इत्यनेन असच् प्रत्ययः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इत्यनेन अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । जस् परे आज्जसेरसुक् इत्यनेन आसुक् आगमः ।
- अंजयः—अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणगतिषु । खनिकप्यंजि—(उ. सू. ४-५७९) इत्यनेन इ प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपं ।
- एताः—इण् गतौ धातुः । हसि मृग्रिह्वा—(उ. सू. ३-३६६) इत्यनेन तन् प्रत्ययः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोरिको गुणः । इत्यादिर्नित्यं इत्यनेन आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- पविषु—पूञ् पवने धातुः । अच इः (उ. सू. ४-५७८) इत्यनेन इ प्रत्ययः । तन्निमित्तं धातोरिको गुणोऽवादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- क्षुराः—क्षुर विलेखने धातुः । यजेंद्राग्र—(उ. सू. २-१८६) इत्यनेन रन्नंतत्वेन निपातितः । व्यत्ययेन अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- धिरे—धृञ् धारणे धातुः । छांदसे लिटि परे व्यत्ययेन वर्णलोपः । छंदसि द्वित्वविकल्पत्वात् न भवति । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।

> म॒हांतो॑ म॒ह्ना वि॒भ्वो॒३॒॑३विभू॑तयो दूरे॒दृशो॒ ये दि॒व्या ॒॑ ॑

> परिष्टुभः ॥ ११ ॥
