##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एते मरुतः स्वयुक्ताः स्वैर्युक्ताः परस्परं संयुक्ताः स्वेन धनेन वा
> युक्ताः संतो दिवो म्यलोकाद्वथानायासेना वा ययुः । अवाङ्मुखमागच्छंति । हे अमर्त्या मरुतः यूयं त्मनात्मना स्वयमेव कशया । वाज्ञामैतत् । वाचा स्तुतिरूपया चोदत । प्रेरयत । स्तोतुमिति शेषः । ते च मरुतोS
> रेणवोऽपापास्तुविजाता बहुयज्ञेषु प्रादुर्भूता भ्राजदृष्टयो दीप्ता एवंभूताः संतो दृळ्हानि चिद्बृढान्यपि पर्वतान्यचुच्यवुः । च्यावयंति । चालयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These Maruts, स्वयुक्ताः (*svayuktāḥ*), joined with one another or provided with their own wealth, come down effortlessly (वृथा (*vṛthā*)) from the heavenly world, facing downwards. O immortal Maruts, you yourselves (त्मना (*tmanā*) = आत्मना (*ātmanā*)) urge us with the कशा (*kaśā*), which is speech (कशा (*kaśā*) is a name of speech), in the form of praise, to praise you; "to praise" is the word to be supplied. And those Maruts, free of stain (अरेणवः (*areṇavaḥ*): sinless), born in many sacrifices (तुविजाताः (*tuvijātāḥ*)), brilliant-spearing (भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*): shining), being such, shake and set in motion even the firmest mountains.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (एते (*ete*)—these Marut deities)
- स्वयुक्ताः (*svayuktāḥ*)—mutually joined (endowed with their own wealth)
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the world of the gods
- वृथा (*vṛthā*)—effortlessly
- अव (*ava*)—facing downwards
- आ ययुः (*ā yayuḥ*)—come
- (हे (*he*)) अमर्त्याः (*amartyāḥ*)—O immortal Maruts (you)
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—yourselves
- कशया (*kaśayā*)—with speech (in the form of praise)
- चोदत (*codata*)—urge (us to praise)
- (ते (*te*)) मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—those Marut deities
### Printed p. 125
- अरेणवः (*areṇavaḥ*)—sinless
- तुविजाताः (*tuvijātāḥ*)—appearing (at many sacrifices)
- भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*)—shining (being)
- दृळ्हानि चित् (*dṛḷhāni cit*)—even the very firm mountains and the like
- अचुच्युवुः (*acucyuvuḥ*)—shake

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, joined with one another, come effortlessly from the world of the gods to this world. O immortal Maruts, urge us with your own speech (to praise you). Those Maruts, sinless, appearing at many sacrifices, shining, make even the very firm mountains and the like move.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Mutually supported, they descend readily form the sky: immortal Maruts, animate us by your own words (to praise you): exempt from toil, present at many (sacrifices) brilliant-eyed, the Maruts have shaken the firmest mountains.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स्वयुक्ताः (*svayuktāḥ*)—The Maruts are forty-nine in number (49 persons). It is described in two ways: that they live among themselves in mutual affection, or that, the word स्व (*sva*) being explained as wealth, they are endowed with wealth.
वृथा अव आययुः (*vṛthā ava āyayuḥ*)—The manner of the Maruts' coming is described: they descend from heaven to the sacrificial hall effortlessly, head downwards.
त्मना कशया चोदत (*tmanā kaśayā codata*)—आत्मना स्तुतिरूपया वाचा स्तोतुं प्रेरयत। (*ātmanā stutirūpayā vācā stotuṃ prerayata|*) The word त्मना (*tmanā*) is quoted by Yāska as used in the sense of आत्मना (*ātmanā*).
तन्नस्तुरीपमद्भुतं पुरु वारं पुरु शृना । कृष्णा पोषाय वि पृथु राये नाभा नो अस्मयुः ॥ (*tannasturīpamadbhutaṃ puru vāraṃ puru śṛnā | kṛṣṇā poṣāya vi pṛthu rāye nābhā no asmayuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142-10)
Here the meaning आत्मना (*ātmanā*) for त्मना (*tmanā*) is made clear. The word कशा (*kaśā*) is stated among the names of speech (Ni. 2-13). The wish is expressed that the Maruts may bestow words in the form of praise, in order to impel those who praise them to the manner of praising.

### Printed p. 126
The words अरेणवः (*areṇavaḥ*), तुविजाताः (*tuvijātāḥ*), भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*) are epithets of the word मरुतः (*marutaḥ*): the greatness of the Maruts is described as being sinless, born (manifested) in many sacrifices, and of abundant lustre. And their power is explained: that they shake even firm mountains.

##### Grammar

- स्वयुक्ताः — युजिर् योगे इति धातुः । कर्मणि क्तप्रत्ययः । स्वैः युक्ताः स्वयुक्ताः । तृतीया कर्मणि (पा. सू. ६-२-४८) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- ययुः — या प्रापणे इति धातुः । छांदसत्वेन वर्तमानार्थे लिटः प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- चोदत — चुद प्रेरणे इति धातुः । चुरादिः । लोटो मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचने लङ्वद्भावात् तादेशः । व्यत्ययेन शप् विकरणः । पुगंतलघूपधस्य च इति लघूपधस्य गुणः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति । **NOTE**
- त्मना — मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरात्मनः (पा. सू. ६-४-१४१) इति तृतीयायां परत आत्मन्शब्दस्याकारस्य लोपः ।
- अरेणवः — न विद्यते रेणुः येषां ते अरेणवः । नञ्सुभ्यां (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) इत्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- अचुच्यवुः — चुज् गतौ इति धातुः । प्रयोजकव्यापारदर्शनादंतर्भावितण्यर्थो भवति । छांदसत्वेन लज् व्यत्ययो बहुलं इति परस्मैपदी भवति । झौ परे बहुलं छंदसि इति शसि श्ल्वादेशः । धातोर्द्वित्वे सिजभ्यस्तवितिभ्यश्च (पा. सू. ३-४-१०९) इति झेर्जुसादेशः । जुसि च (पा. सू. ७-३-८३) इत्युकारस्य गुणः । अवादेशः । अंगस्याडागमः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- दृढानि — दृह वृद्धौ इति धातुः । क्तप्रत्ययः । होढः इति सूत्रेण हकारस्य ढत्वे रुषस्तथोः इति तकारस्य धत्वम् । ष्टुत्वेन तस्य ढत्वे ढोढे लोपः इति पूर्वढकारस्य लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तो भवति ।

##### Grammar

- भ्राजदृष्टयः — भ्राज्य दीप्तौ धातुः । व्यत्ययेन लटः शत्रादेशः । तास्यनुदात्तेत् इति सूत्रेण लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । ऋषी गतौ धातुः । क्तिच्क्तौचसंज्ञायां (पा. सू. ३-३-१७४) इति क्तिच्प्रत्यये सति ऋष्टि इति रूपं भवति । बहुव्रीहिसमासे पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

> अहन्योऽहि भव एतशो नाश्व इव । स यथा शिक्षकेण नानाप्रकारं प्राप्यते तद्वत् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, O ऋष्टिविद्युतः (*ṛṣṭividyutaḥ*), shining with the special cloud-splitting weapon: who, standing among you, sets you in motion (रेजति (*rejati*): moves, impels)?" The answer is त्मना (*tmanā*), by yourselves alone. An illustration of the moving is given: जिह्वया हन्वेव (*jihvayā hanveva*), like the two jaws (the dual ending is replaced by ā), which are moved by the tongue. Even so, in the arrival (यामनि (*yāmani*)) of foods (इषां (*iṣāṃ*)), that is, of the plants that are their means, for abundance, you are desired like धन्वच्युतः (*dhanvacyutaḥ*) clouds that shed water. धन्व (*dhanva*) is a word for the atmosphere, and by it the water standing there is meant. In the same way the sacrificer, wishing for many kinds of fruit (पुरुप्रैषाः (*purupraiṣāḥ*)), calls you in many ways with hymns to obtain food and the like. The illustration: अहन्यः (*ahanyaḥ*), "born of the day", is एतशः (*etaśaḥ*), a horse; as it is made to go in various ways by its trainer, so are you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋष्टिविद्युतः (*ṛṣṭividyutaḥ*)—shining with the cloud-splitting weapon
- (हे) मरुतः (*(he) marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the midst (standing)
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who

- हन्वा (*hanvā*)—the two jaws
- जिह्वया इव (*jihvayā iva*)—as (moved) by the tongue
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—by yourselves
- रेजति (*rejati*)—makes you move?
- *(tathāpi)*—even so
- इषां (*iṣāṃ*)—of foods (of the plants that are the means of food)
- यामनि (*yāmani*)—in the matter of obtaining (for abundance)
- धन्वच्युतः न (*dhanvacyutaḥ na*)—like clouds that shed the water of the sky
- *(vaḥ)*—you
- अहन्यः (*ahanyaḥ*)—on every day
- एतशः न (*etaśaḥ na*)—like a horse trained in many ways by the trainer
- पुरुप्रैषाः (*purupraiṣāḥ*)—(the sacrificer desiring many fruits) impels you in many ways by hymns

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, armed with the cloud-splitting weapon! Who indeed could make you move, while remaining in your very midst, as the tongue moves the two jaws? Yet, as at exercise-time a trainer turns a horse about in many ways, and as clouds are necessary for plants, so the sacrificer, for whom you are necessary for the many kinds of fruit of the sacrifice, makes you favourable to himself with his hymns.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Maruts, lightning-armed, who, (standing) amongst you, sets you of yourselves in motion, as the jaws are (set in moticn) by the tongue : as falling rains (are essential) for the obtaining of food, so (those, desirous of sustenance), excite you in various ways, like a horse in (his) daily (training).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋष्टि विद्युतः (*ṛṣṭi vidyutaḥ*): the meaning is explained thus: the word ṛṣṭi denotes a special weapon. Who is it that impels the Maruts, shining with this weapon, in the act of splitting the cloud? This question is asked by the sentence को रेजति (*ko rejati*), and in reply, to remove the impossibility of the act of moving, the solution त्मना (*tmanā*) is given. Rain does not come merely because the Maruts shine bearing the weapon, with the splitting of the cloud following. Since there is no one else to impel the Maruts to be ready for action, so that the act of splitting the cloud takes place, the meaning described is that they themselves split the cloud with their weapon.
जिह्वया हन्वेव (*jihvayā hanveva*): the comparison is: as the tongue impels the jaws. When the Maruts, self-impelled, split the cloud, the impelling arises in the Maruts themselves; as an illustration it is said that from the moving of the tongue the moving of the jaw arises by itself.

### Printed p. 129

इषां यामनि धन्वच्युतो न (*iṣāṃ yāmani dhanvacyuto na*): अन्नानां तत्साधनानां सस्यानां प्राप्तौ समृद्ध्यर्थं उदकस्राविणो मेघा इव (*annānāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ sasyānāṃ prāptau samṛddhyarthaṃ udakasrāviṇo meghā iva*). The word धन्वन् (*dhanvan*) is listed among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). And Yāska, quoting the Ṛk यः परस्याः परावशस्तिरो धन्वाति रोचते । स नः पर्षदति द्विषः । (*yaḥ parasyāḥ parāvaśastiro dhanvāti rocate | sa naḥ parṣadati dviṣaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-187-2), has explained the word धन्वन् (*dhanvan*) as धन्वांतरिक्षं धन्वंतस्यादापः (*dhanvāṃtarikṣaṃ dhanvaṃtasyādāpaḥ*). Sāyaṇa explains: the word धन्वन् (*dhanvan*) denotes the atmosphere, but here by the word the water that is in the atmosphere is meant. As people wish for clouds that pour water for the production of food and so on, or of the plants that are the cause of food, so the sacrificer, with abundant hymns, wishes for the coming of the Maruts.
By the sentence अहन्यः एतशो न (*ahanyaḥ etaśo na*) the comparison is made: as a horse every day, subject to the trainer's command, learns many kinds of gaits, so the coming of the Maruts is of many kinds.
The word एतशः (*etaśaḥ*) is read among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27).
पुरुप्रैषाः (*purupraiṣāḥ*): for this word the meaning given is बहुविधं फलमिच्छन् (*bahuvidhaṃ phalamicchan*), the sacrificer who desires many kinds of benefits. The analysis of the compound is stated as पुरुप्रैषः स्तोत्रं यस्य (*purupraiṣaḥ stotraṃ yasya*). The sacrificer praises with many kinds of hymns and wishes to obtain food and the like through the many kinds of comings of the Maruts.

##### Grammar

- ऋष्टिविद्युतः — ऋष्ट्या विद्योतंते इति ऋष्टिविद्युतः । संबोधनाबहुवचनांतरूपम् । आमंत्रितस्य च इति निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- रेजति — रेज्य कंपने धातुः । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- हन्वा — हनुशब्दः । तस्मात् द्विवचने (औ) परे सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति तस्य आकारादेशः । यणादेशः ।
- धन्वच्युतः — च्युतिर् क्षरणे धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । धन्वानं ज्योतयंति इति धन्वच्युतः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

### Printed p. 130

- इषां — षष्ठीबहुवचनांतरूपम् । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१८) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- अहन्यः — अह्नि भवः अहन्यः । भवे छंदसि (पा. सू. ४-४-११०) इति यत्प्रत्ययः । तित्स्वरितं (पा. सू. ६-१-१८५) इति स्वरितस्वरो भवति ।
- एतशः — इण् गतौ धातुः । इणस्तशन् तशुनसौ (उ. सू. ४-४२९) इति तशन्प्रत्ययः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोर्गुणः । इत्यादिर्नित्यं (पा. सू. ६-१-१६९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क्व॑ स्विद॒स्य रज॑सो म॒हस्परं॒ क्वाव॑रं मरुतो॒ यस्मि॑नाय॒य ।  
> यच्चा॒वय॑थ विधु॒रेव॒ संहि॑तं॒ व्यद्रि॑णा पतथ त्वे॒षम॑र्ण॒वं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> क्व । स्वित् । अस्य । रजसः । महः । परं । क्व । अवरं । मरुतः । यस्मिन् । आयय ।  
> यत् । च्यवयथ । विधुराइव । संहितं । वि । अद्रिणा । पतथ । त्वेषं । अर्णवं ॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः यूयं यस्मिन्नुदकनिमित्तभूते सत्यायय आगच्छत अस्य
> रजसो वृष्टु्यदकस्य लोकस्य वा महो महतः परं पारमंतं क्व स्वित् । कुत्रास्तीति । नास्तीत्यर्थः । तथावरमवाज्ञाग आदिश्च क्व स्वित् । कुत्रास्ति । आद्यंतं न कोऽपि
> जानातीत्यर्थः । यद्यदा यूयं विधुरेव विधुराणि शिथिलानि तृणानीव संहितमेकभूतमुदकं च्यावयथ स्वस्थानाच्चालयथ तदाद्रिणा वज्रेण त्वेषं दीप्तमर्णवमुदकवंतं मेघं वि पतथ । विशीर्णं पातयथ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, on account of which water you come (आयय (*āyaya*)), where is the far end (परं (*paraṃ*)) of this great रजसः (*rajasaḥ*), that is, of the rain-water or of the world?" The meaning is that there is none. Likewise, where is its अवरं (*avaraṃ*), the lower part or the beginning? No one knows its beginning or end. When you shake loose from its place the massed water, like loose, slack blades of grass (विधुरेव (*vidhureva*)), then with the अद्रिणा (*adriṇā*), the thunderbolt, you make the brilliant (त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)) cloud full of water (अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*)) fall scattered (वि पतथ (*vi patatha*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) मरुतः (*(he) marutaḥ*)—O Maruts (you)
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—on account of which water
- आयय (*āyaya*)—you come
- अस्य (*asya*)—of that
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—immense
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—water (world)
- परं (*paraṃ*)—the end
- क्व स्वित् (*kva svit*)—where is it?
- (तथा (*(tathā*)—likewise
- अवरं (*avaraṃ*)—its beginning part
- क्व (*kva*)—where is it?
- यत् (*yat*)—when (you)
- संहितं (*saṃhitaṃ*)—the water gathered together
- विधुरा इव (*vidhurā iva*)—(as one scatters) slack (light) grass
- च्यावयथ (*cyāvayatha*)—scatter
- *(tat)*—then
- अद्रिणा (*adriṇā*)—with the thunderbolt weapon
- त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—brilliant

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, for the sake of which water do you come: what are its beginning and end? And you split with the thunderbolt the water that has gathered in one place, and the water-bearing clouds, and make them fall down.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Where, Maruts, is the limit of the vast region (whenee you eome) : where is the beginning of that to which you proceed : when you scatter the dense vapour like light grass, and hurl down the brilliant rain-cloud by the thunderbolt.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अस्य रजसः महः परं क्व स्वित् (*asya rajasaḥ mahaḥ paraṃ kva svit*): *vṛṣṭuyadakasya lokasya vā mahataḥ pāraṃ aṃtaṃ kutrāsti*. The word रजः (*rajaḥ*) is stated among the names of night (Ni. 2-18). Yāska explains the derivation: the word रजः (*rajaḥ*), denoting colouring, is formed from the root रज (*raja*). He says रजो रजतेर्जोती रज उच्यते (*rajo rajaterjotī raja ucyate*): light is called रजः (*rajaḥ*) because it pervades all things with its radiance; and उदकं रज उच्यते लोका रजांस्युच्यंते (*udakaṃ raja ucyate lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte*): waters and worlds are denoted by the word रजः (*rajaḥ*) (Ni. 4-19). He cites usages (examples) for each meaning.
अज्जामुक्थैरहिं गृणीषे बुद्धे नदीनां रजस्सु सीदन् (*ajjāmukthairahiṃ gṛṇīṣe buddhe nadīnāṃ rajassu sīdan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-16). Here the word रजस्सु (*rajassu*) is explained as उदकेषु (*udakeṣu*).

### Printed p. 132

एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमंजते (*etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumaṃjate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1). Here the meaning given is रजसः अंतरिक्षलोकस्य (*rajasaḥ aṃtarikṣalokasya*). Sāyaṇa explains that, addressing the Maruts, they come in order to bestow waters on the world. Asking where the end that completes the greatness of the waters and the worlds is, he describes that, because it is visible, it is boundless. Likewise, asking by way of a question अवरं अवाज् भागः आदिश्च क्व स्वित् (*avaraṃ avāj bhāgaḥ ādiśca kva svit*), where is the beginning of the waters, he explains न कोपि जानाति (*na kopi jānāti*): no one knows even the beginning and end of the waters.
विधुरेव संहितं च्यावयथ (*vidhureva saṃhitaṃ cyāvayatha*): शिथिलानि तृणानीव एकभूतं उदकं स्वस्थानात् चालयथ (*śithilāni tṛṇānīva ekabhūtaṃ udakaṃ svasthānāt cālayatha*). When the Maruts move the condensed waters from their places as one moves loose blades of grass, अर्णवं वि पतथ (*arṇavaṃ vi patatha*), उदकवंतं मेघं विशीर्णं पातॆयथ (*udakavaṃtaṃ meghaṃ viśīrṇaṃ pātèyatha*): you strike and split with the thunderbolt the cloud full of water and make the rain-water pour down. Thus the extraordinary power of the Maruts is described here.
अद्रिणा (*adriṇā*): the word अद्रि (*adri*) is read among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 3-11). The meaning given is the thunderbolt weapon.
श्वेषं (*śveṣaṃ*)—दीप्तं (*dīptaṃ*): this word is explained as used by Yāska in the sense of "having radiance"
तैषमित्था समरणं शिमीवतोरिंद्राविष्णू सुशपा वामुरुष्यति (*taiṣamitthā samaraṇaṃ śimīvatoriṃdrāviṣṇū suśapā vāmuruṣyati*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-155-2). Here the word श्वेषं (*śveṣaṃ*) is explained as "having radiance".

##### Grammar

- आयय — या प्रापणे धातुः । छांदसत्वेन लिट् । मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचने अ आदेशः । द्वित्वम् । असंयोगाल्लिट् कित् इति प्रत्ययस्य कित्त्वात् आतो लोप इटि च (पा. सू. ६-४-६४) इति धातोराकारस्य लोपः । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति । शिजिचोदात्तवति (पा. सू. ८-१-७१) इति आजेर्निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- च्यावयथ — च्युज् गतौ धातुः । हेतुमति च (पा. सू. ३-१-२६) इति णिच् । अचोञ्णिति इति वृद्धिः । आवादेशः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । णिच्स्वरः शिष्यते ।

### Printed p. 133
Vidhurā iva—the root व्यथ भयसंचलनयोः (*vyatha bhayasaṃcalanayoḥ*). By व्यथेः संप्रसारणं किच्च (*vyatheḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ kicca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-39) the affix urac. The root takes saṃprasāraṇa. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the final-acute accent comes. In the neuter, by शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70) the śi takes luk.
Patatha—the root पत्ल्य गत्. (*patlya gat.*) Because the action of an instigator is shown, it has the causative sense contained within. It is the form in the laṭ, madhyama-puruṣa, plural. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.
Tveṣaṃ—the root त्विष दीप्तौ (*tviṣa dīptau*). By नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यः (*naṃdigrahapacādibhyaḥ*) the affix ac. Guṇa of the short penultimate. Since the affix has c as its marker, the final-acute accent comes.
Arṇavaṃ—arṇavaḥ is "that which has arṇa". By अर्णसो लोपश्च (*arṇaso lopaśca*) (Kā. 5-2-109-2) the affix va in the sense of possession, and loss of s; by the affix-accent it becomes final-acute. ॥ 6 ॥

> यथा राजेवामवान् । ऋ. ४-४-१ । इत्यत्रामशब्दोऽमात्यवचनः तद्वत् । यद्वा।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, your sāti is like a sāti, a sharing or association: as the company of you is of excellent quality, so your gift, the gift of rain, is अमवती (*amavatī*), accompanied by Indra and others as helpers. As in यथा राजेवामवान् (*yathā rājevāmavān*) (Ṛ. 4-4-1) the word अम (*ama*) means a minister, so here likewise. Or else:

### Printed p. 134
your sāti, your allotment, is not अमवती (*amavatī*), not diseased, but स्वर्वती (*svarvatī*), full of happiness; त्वेषा (*tveṣā*), brilliant; विपाका (*vipākā*), with fully ripened fruit; पिपिष्वती (*pipiṣvatī*), possessing driving or ploughing by husbandmen (it is well known that they plough when rain has fallen), or crushing its own enemies. भद्रा (*bhadrā*): to be desired, praiseworthy. Further, it is like the dakṣiṇā of a wealthy man who fills (the priest), making prosperous; पृथुजयी (*pṛthujayī*): of wide speed, swift-going; and like the power of an Asura belonging to him, overcoming all. As that power can take from others and give to another, so this gift too can take the water that stands in the cloud and give it to the world. Such a gift be ours: this is the idea."

> वः सातिः संविभक्तिर्नामवती । रोगवती न भवति । किंतु स्वर्वती सुखवती त्वेषा
> दीप्ता विपाका परिपक्वफला पिपिष्टती प्रेषणवती कृषीवलैः कर्षणवती । वृष्टौ
> सत्यां कर्षंतीति प्रसिद्धं । स्वविरोधिपेषणवती वा । भद्रा छंदनीया स्तुत्या । किंचॆ
> पृणतो धातुर्धनिकस्य दक्षिणा न दक्षिणेव तद्वत्समृद्धकरी पृथुजयी पृथुजवा
> शीघ्रगामिनी किंचासुर्यॆवासुरस्य स्वभूता जंजती सर्वानभिभवंती शक्तिरिव । सा
> यथान्येभ्योऽपहृत्यान्यस्मै दातुं समर्था तद्वदियमपि मेघस्थमुदकमपहृत्य
> जगतो दातुं शक्तेत्यर्थः । ईदृशी रातिरस्यभ्यमस्त्विति भावः ॥

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, the rain that you pour with Indra's help is, like your coming, a means of heavenly happiness, brilliant, bearing ripe fruit, favourable to husbandmen, auspicious, prosperous like a wealthy man's dakṣiṇā, bringing fruit in very short time, and like the Asura power that overcomes everything (by which one can seize from one and give to another). May such a gift of yours be ours.

eral (of Indra's bounty), heaven-bestowing, brilliant, fruitful, favorable to
the husbandman. propitions: : it is like the donation of a wealthy (donor),
prompt (of distribution), and like the all-subduing force of the Asuras.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वः सातिर्न वः रातिः अमवती (*vaḥ sātirna vaḥ rātiḥ amavatī*)—युष्माकं संबंधिनी सातिर्न संभक्तिरिव युष्मत्संभजनं यथा प्रशस्तगुणं तद्वद्वो रात्रिर्वृष्ट्वा दिविषयामवत्यमात्यवशींद्रातिसहायवती । (*yuṣmākaṃ saṃbaṃdhinī sātirna saṃbhaktiriva yuṣmatsaṃbhajanaṃ yathā praśastaguṇaṃ tadvadvo rātrirvṛṣṭvā diviṣayāmavatyamātyavaśīṃdrātisahāyavatī |*) यद्वा वः सातिः संविभक्तिः न अमवती रोगवती न भवति । (*yadvā vaḥ sātiḥ saṃvibhaktiḥ na amavatī rogavatī na bhavati |*) The word sāti has been explained as service. The word rāti is said to mean gift. The author of the Nirukta has explained the word अमवती (*amavatī*) as meaning minister.
कृणुष्वपाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीं याहि राजेवामवा इभेन । तृष्टिमनु प्रसितिं द्रोणानोऽस्तासि विध्य रक्षसस्तपिष्ठैः ॥ (*kṛṇuṣvapājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīṃ yāhi rājevāmavā ibhena | tṛṣṭimanu prasitiṃ droṇāno 'stāsi vidhya rakṣasastapiṣṭhaiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-1)
In this Ṛk, for the word अमवान् (*amavān*) (राजेव (*rājeva*)) the meaning अमात्यवान् अभ्यमनर्वा (*amātyavān abhyamanarvā*) is given. Durgācārya has explained it in two ways: that the king, knowing policy, sets out to win victory with a minister who knows policy; or अभ्यमनवान्-रोगभूतः परेभ्यो भयदाता (*abhyamanavān-rogabhūtaḥ parebhyo bhayadātā*), one who causes fear to enemies as a disease causes fear to others. Here Sāyaṇa has supported both meanings.
The comparison is made thus: as the Maruts' coming has abundant and excellent qualities, the gift of rain-water that the Maruts make has Indra's help. As a king, endowed with policy, joined by a minister who knows policy, and rich in helpers, sets out to conquer his enemies, so the Maruts, when giving rain, keep Indra himself as minister (helper). This is one meaning.
In the second meaning, the Maruts' gift of rain-water is described as: the king is frightening to enemies like a disease, not to others. Of the two meanings of अमवती (*amavatī*), one agrees with the comparison to the king, the other does not.
Sāyaṇa also gives a further meaning, in which a contrast with the king is suggested: the king's coming is attended by fear, but in the Maruts' coming there is never occasion for fear of disease. Though the contrast is suggested, the other epithets also state superiority over the king's coming.

### Printed p. 136
The Maruts' coming is described as स्वर्वती (*svarvatī*)—always producing happiness; त्वेषा (*tveṣā*)—bright; विपाका (*vipākā*)—producing excellent fruit; पिपिष्टती (*pipiṣṭatī*)—the earth being split by farmers for the growth of crops, and enemies being destroyed; भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—worthy of praise.
पृणतः दक्षिणा न (*pṛṇataḥ dakṣiṇā na*)—दातुर्धनिकस्य दक्षिणेव समृद्धिकरी । (*dāturdhanikasya dakṣiṇeva samṛddhikarī |*) The word पृणतः (*pṛṇataḥ*) has been explained by the Nirukta-author in तमूर्दरं न पृणता यवेन (*tamūrdaraṃ na pṛṇatā yavena*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-11) as used in the sense of filling: यवेन पूरयति (*yavena pūrayati*). Here it is taken to mean a wealthy man filled with wealth. As the wealth a rich man gives as dakṣiṇā brings prosperity, so the Maruts' coming brings prosperity; the comparison is shown.
असुर्येव जंजती (*asuryeva jaṃjatī*)—असुरस्य स्वभूता सर्वानभिभवंती शक्तिरिव । (*asurasya svabhūtā sarvānabhibhavaṃtī śaktiriva |*) The word असुर्या (*asuryā*) is explained as "belonging to the Asura". The word असुर (*asura*) is stated among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-22). And it is explained: असोरसुरानसृजत तदसुराणामसुरत्वमिति विज्ञायते (*asorasurānasṛjata tadasurāṇāmasuratvamiti vijñāyate*) (Ni. 3-8). Durgācārya has explained: असुराः असुरताः स्थानेषु (*asurāḥ asuratāḥ sthāneṣu*)—those not steady in their own places are Asuras; or अस्ताः स्थानेभ्यः (*astāḥ sthānebhyaḥ*)—those driven by the gods from their places.
The power of these Asuras overcomes all. And Sāyaṇa describes the nature of the Asura power: अन्येभ्यो अपहृत्य अन्यस्मै दातुं समर्था (*anyebhyo apahṛtya anyasmai dātuṃ samarthā*)—able to seize one person's goods or property and give it to another. Likewise the Maruts' power is described: मेघस्थमुदकं अपहृत्य जगतः दातुं समर्था (*meghasthamudakaṃ apahṛtya jagataḥ dātuṃ samarthā*)—ready to give the waters in the clouds to the world as rain.
Here, addressing the Maruts with युष्माकं संबंधिनी सातिः यथा प्रशस्तगुणं तद्वत् वः रातिः (*yuṣmākaṃ saṃbaṃdhinī sātiḥ yathā praśastaguṇaṃ tadvat vaḥ rātiḥ*): as your coming has excellent qualities, so also the gift of rain-water that you bestow. Since the comparison is stated in this way, it is indicated that all the other epithets of sāti relate also to rāti. And ईदृशी रातिः अस्मभ्यं अस्तु इति (*īdṛśī rātiḥ asmabhyaṃ astu iti*): such a gift of yours be for us, the sacrificers.

- सातिः—ऊतियूतिजूति-(पा. सू. ३-३-९७) इति क्विन् उदात्तः निपातितः ।

- अमवती—अमः अस्याः अस्ति । मतुप् प्रत्ययः । माडुपधायाश्च इति वत्वम् । उगित्त्वात् स्त्रीत्वे जेप् ।
- स्वर्वती—पूर्ववत् मतुप्, वत्त्वम् । जीप् । प्रत्ययः पित्त्वात् अनुदात्तः भवति । न्यज्‌स्वरौ स्वरिशौ (फि. सू. ७५) इति स्वर् इति स्वरितः भवति ।
- राशिः—रा आदाने । धातुः । क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । मंत्रेवृषेषपच—(पा सू. ३-३-९६) इति प्रत्ययः उदात्तः भवति ।
- पृणतः—पृण प्रीणने । धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । नुम्रहितस्य शतृः परस्मिन् षष्ठीविभक्तेः आगतत्वात् कतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३) इति तस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- असुर्या—असुरस्य इयम् । संबंधार्थे यत् प्रत्ययः । यस्येति च इति अकारलोपः । तित्स्वरितं (पा. सू. ६-१-१८५) इति स्वरितस्वरः भवति । स्त्रीत्वे टाप् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"From the pavis, the thunderbolts belonging to the Maruts, the sindhus, the flowing waters, प्रति ष्टोभंति (*prati ṣṭobhaṃti*), move forth. When? When the thunderbolts utter the अभ्रियां वाचं (*abhriyāṃ vācaṃ*), the sound born of cloud, characterised as thunder. Further, the विद्युतः (*vidyutaḥ*), the shining lightnings, in पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*), the atmosphere,

### Printed p. 138
(पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) is a name of the atmosphere, since the hymn of its names reads *pṛthivī bhūḥ*), there अव स्वयंत (*ava svayaṃta*), shine with faces turned downward. Or *pṛthivyām* may be construed with what follows: यदि (*yadi*), when on the earth the Maruts पुष्णुवंति (*puṣṇuvaṃti*), sprinkle, pour, the ghee-like water that flows. (The root पुष (*puṣa*) of the kryādi class takes श्नुः (*śnuḥ*) by vyatyaya.) When this is so, then: this is the meaning."

> पृथिवीत्यंतरिक्षनाम । पृथिवी भूरिति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् । तत्राव स्वयंत । स्वयंते ।
> अपाज्मुखं प्रकाशंते । पृथिव्यामित्येतदुत्तरत्र वा योज्यं । यदि यदा पृथिव्यां
> भूम्यां धृतं क्षरदुदकं मरुतः पुष्णुवंति पुष्णंति सिंचंति ॥ पुषेः क्रैयादिकस्य
> व्यत्ययेन श्नुः ॥ यदैवं तदेत्यर्थः ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- (वज्राणि (*vajrāṇi*)—the thunderbolts)
- अभ्रियां (*abhriyāṃ*)—in the clouds
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—the sound (in the form of thunder)
- उत् ईरयंति (*ut īrayaṃti*)—send forth
- (तत् (*tat*)—then)
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—the waters of flowing nature
- पविभ्यः (*pavibhyaḥ*)—from the thunderbolts (belonging to the Maruts)
- प्रति स्तोभंति (*prati stobhaṃti*)—move forth
- (किंच (*kiṃca*)—further)
- यदि (*yadi*)—when
- पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—on the earth
- धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*)—the water
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- पुष्णुवंति (*puṣṇuvaṃti*)—sprinkle
- (तदा (*tadā*)—then)
- विद्युतः (*vidyutaḥ*)—the shining lightnings
- (पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—in the atmosphere)
- अव स्वयंत (*ava svayaṃta*)—laugh (shine) with faces turned downward

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the cloud thunders, the waters are sent forth by the thunderbolts (of the Maruts); thus, while the Maruts sprinkle water on the earth, lightning shines in the sky.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The rivers are arrested by the thunderbolts when they utter the voice of the clouds; but the lightnings smile in the firmament when the Maruts sprinkle water on the earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अभ्रियां वाचं उदीरयंति (*abhriyāṃ vācaṃ udīrayaṃti*)—अभ्रभवां स्तनितलक्षणां वाचं शब्दं उच्चारयंति (*abhrabhavāṃ stanitalakṣaṇāṃ vācaṃ śabdaṃ uccārayaṃti*): when through the thunderbolt the sound of thunder arises in the clouds and the lightnings shine downward-faced in the atmosphere, the Maruts squeeze out the waters so that they flow on the earth. Then सिंधवः प्रति ष्टोभंति स्यंदनशीलाः आपः प्रतिचलंति (*siṃdhavaḥ prati ṣṭobhaṃti syaṃdanaśīlāḥ āpaḥ praticalaṃti*): the waters, flowing by nature, move on the earth and in the atmosphere; this is the meaning explained. That is, the rain-water that has fallen as rain falls on the earth and flows.

### Printed p. 139
पविभ्यः (*pavibhyaḥ*)—belonging to the Maruts, "to the thunderbolts" (मरुत्संबंधि वज्रेभ्यः (*marutsaṃbaṃdhi vajrebhyaḥ*)). The word पवि (*pavi*) is stated both among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23) and among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 3-11). Yāska explains पविः रथनेमिर्भवति यद्विपुनाति भूमिं (*paviḥ rathanemirbhavati yadvipunāti bhūmiṃ*): the mark made by the edge of the chariot wheel that cuts the earth is well known as पवि (*pavi*). He then cites the Ṛk उत स्म ते परुष्ण्यामूर्णा वसत शुंध्यवः । उत पव्या रथानामद्रिं भिंदंत्योजसा ॥ (*uta sma te paruṣṇyāmūrṇā vasata śuṃdhyavaḥ | uta pavyā rathānāmadriṃ bhiṃdaṃtyojasā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-9) and gives the meaning of पविः रथनेमिर्भवति (*paviḥ rathanemirbhavati*) as the rim of the chariot wheel.
Durgācārya describes the meaning thus: देवा वै वृत्रस्य मर्म नाविदन् तं मरुतः क्षुरपविना व्ययुः (*devā vai vṛtrasya marma nāvidan taṃ marutaḥ kṣurapavinā vyayuḥ*)—when the gods did not know the vital spot of the demon Vṛtra, the Maruts split it with the wheel-rims, which are like thunderbolts with sharp razor-like edges; that is, the Maruts split the cloud with the keen edges (पवि (*pavi*)) of their chariots. Sāyaṇa accepts this meaning in his commentary, and in the sentence पविभ्यः सिंधवः प्रति ष्टोभंति (*pavibhyaḥ siṃdhavaḥ prati ṣṭobhaṃti*) explains मरुत्संबंधि वज्रेभ्यः (*marutsaṃbaṃdhi vajrebhyaḥ*) as the wheel-rims belonging to the Maruts (that is, the streams of rain).
सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—"those whose nature is to flow": waters. अपः सिंधवः (*apaḥ siṃdhavaḥ*) is stated among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24). And in the Ṛk सुदेवो असि वरुण यस्य ते सप्त सिंधवः । अनुक्षरंति काकुदं सूम्यं सुषिरामिव ॥ (*sudevo asi varuṇa yasya te sapta siṃdhavaḥ | anukṣaraṃti kākudaṃ sūmyaṃ suṣirāmiva ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-69-12) the meaning is explained: सिंधुः स्रवणात् (*siṃdhuḥ sravaṇāt*)—water is well known by the name सिंधु (*siṃdhu*) because it flows.
पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—"in the intermediate space, on the earth". The word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) is stated both among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5) and among the names of the intermediate space (Ni. 2-10). Here two meanings (intermediate space, earth) are explained.
धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*)—"flowing water". The word धृत (*dhṛta*) is read among the names of water (Ni. 224)**NOTE**. And in the Ṛk कृष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत्पतंति । त आववृत्रन्तदनादृतस्यादिद्घृतेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते । (*kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divamutpataṃti | ta āvavṛtrantadanādṛtasyādidghṛtena pṛthivī vyudyate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-47)

### Printed p. 140
the word घृतेन (*ghṛtena*) is interpreted as उदकेन (*udakena*). Yāska explains the word घृत (*ghṛta*), derived from the root फ्रा (*phrā*)**NOTE** meaning "to sprinkle", as "water": घृतमित्युदकनाम जिघर्तेः सिंचतिकर्मणः (*ghṛtamityudakanāma jigharteḥ siṃcatikarmaṇaḥ*).

##### Grammar

- स्तोभंति — ष्टुभु स्तंभे इति धातुः । व्यत्ययेन परस्त्रैपदी भवति । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपं । प्रति इत्युपसर्गस्य पूर्वस्थितत्वात् उपसर्गात् सुनोति— (पा. सू. ८-३-६५) इत्यनेन धातुसकारस्य षत्वं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- पविभ्यः — पूञ् पवने इति धातुः । अच इः (उ. सू. ५७८) इत्यनेन इ प्रत्ययः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोरिको गुणः अवादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरो भवति ।
- अभ्रियां — अभ्रे भवा अभ्रिया । समुद्राभ्राद्भः (पा. सू. ४-४-११८) इत्यनेन घ प्रत्ययः । आयनेयिा- (पा. सू. ७-१-२) इत्यनेन तस्य इयादेशः । यस्यॆति च इत्यनेन अकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्याद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । स्त्रीत्वे अदंतत्वात् टाप् ।
- उदीरयंति — ईर गतौ प्रेरणे च इति धातुः । हेतुमति च इत्यनेन णिच् । णिजंतात् लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपं । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । णिच्स्वरो अवशिष्यते । तिजिचोदात्तवति (पा. सू. ८-१-७१) इत्यनेन गतेः (उत्) निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- स्वयंत — स्मिञ् ईषद्धसने इति धातुः । छांदसत्वेन वर्तमानार्थे लज् । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपं । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्‌योगेऽपि इत्यनेन अडागमो न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- यदि — निपातस्य च (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६) इत्यनेन संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
- पुष्णुवंति — पुष स्नेहनसेवनपूरणेषु इति धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झेरंतादेशः । व्यत्ययो बहुलं इत्यनेन श्नु विकरणं भवति । प्रत्ययानां जित्वादेशत्वात् गुणो न भवति । अचिश्नुधातु— इत्यनेन उवजादेशः । निपातैर्यद्यदि— (पा. सू. ८-१-३०) इत्यनेन यदिसंबंधत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्याद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> असू॑त॒ पृश्नि॑र्मह॒ते रणा॑य त्वे॒षम॒यासां॑ म॒रुता॒मनी॑कं ।  
> ते स॑प्स॒रासो॑ऽजनयं॒ताभ्व॒मादित्स्व॒धामि॑षि॒रां पर्य॑पश्यन् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असूत । पृश्निः । महते । रणाय । त्वेषं । आयासां । मरुतां । अनेकं ।  
> ते । सप्सरासः । अजनयंत । अभ्वं । अत् । इत् । स्वधां । इषिरां । परि । अपश्यन् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पृश्निर्मरुन्माता नानावर्णा । पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः । तै. सं.
> २-२-११-४ । पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासः । ऋ. ५-५८-५ । इत्यादिश्रुतेः । तामेवांतरिक्षदेवतां केचिदाहुः । सा देवी त्वेषं दीप्तमयासां गंत्यणां मरुतामनीकं
> समूहमेकोनपंचाशत्सख्याकमसूत । उत्पादितवती । किमर्थं । महते रणाय
> संग्रामाय । मेघजयायेत्यर्थः । ते च मरुतः सप्सरासः समानरूपा हिंसका
> वा मेघानामभ्वं मेघं जनयंति । उत्पादितवंतः । आदिदनंतरमेवेषिरां
> सर्वैरेष्टव्यां स्वधामन्नं सस्यादिसमृद्धिलक्षणं पर्यपश्यन् । परिपश्यंति सर्वे
> जनाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Pṛśni is the mother of the Maruts, of many colours. Sāyaṇa supports this with the Śruti texts पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः (*pṛśniyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-4) and पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासः (*pṛśneḥ putrā upamāsaḥ*) (Ṛ. 5-58-5), and adds that some say she is that very deity of the intermediate space. That goddess bore the bright (त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*) = *dīptaṃ*) troop (अनीकं (*anīkaṃ*) = *samūhaṃ*) of the moving (आयासां (*āyāsāṃ*) = गंत्यणां (*gaṃtyaṇāṃ*)**NOTE** ) Maruts, forty-nine in number. For what purpose? For the great battle (महते रणाय (*mahate raṇāya*) = संग्रामाय (*saṃgrāmāya*)), that is, for the conquest of the cloud. And those Maruts, सप्सरासः (*sapsarāsaḥ*)—of the same form, or destroyers of the clouds—bring forth (जनयंति (*janayaṃti*), "have produced") the cloud (अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*) = मेघं (*meghaṃ*)). Immediately after that, all people behold (पर्यपश्यन् (*paryapaśyan*) = परिपश्यंति (*paripaśyaṃti*)) the इषिरां (*iṣirāṃ*)—that which all desire—स्वधां (*svadhāṃ*), food, marked by the prosperity of crops and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*)—the many-coloured sky (the deity named Pṛśni)
- त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—brilliant
- आयासां (*āyāsāṃ*)—of the moving
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of the Marut deities
- अनीकं (*anīkaṃ*)—the host
- महते रणाय (*mahate raṇāya*)—for the great battle (in the form of conquering the cloud)
- असूत (*asūta*)—produced
- सप्सरासः (*sapsarāsaḥ*)—of the same form, or destroyers of the clouds
- ते (*te*)—those Marut deities
- अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*)—the cloud
- अजनयंत (*ajanayaṃta*)—created
- अत् इत् (*at it*)—immediately after
- इषिरां (*iṣirāṃ*)—desirable to all
- स्वधां (*svadhāṃ*)—food (in the form of crops and the like)
- परि अपश्यन् (*pari apaśyan*)—(the people) saw

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

After the many-coloured sky (or the deity named Pṛśni) had created the brilliant troop of Maruts for the great battle in the form of the conquest of the cloud, the cloud was created by those Marut deities. Immediately afterwards (the people) saw the prosperity of crops and the like.

### Printed p. 142

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Prishni bore the brilliant troop of the quick-moving Maruts for the great combat (with the clouds), whereupon (mankind) immediately beheld the desiderated food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पृश्नि (*pṛśni*)—मरुन्माता नानावर्णा । तामेवांतरिक्षदेवतां केचिदाहुः । (*marunmātā nānāvarṇā | tāmevāṃtarikṣadevatāṃ kecidāhuḥ |*) The word पृश्नि (*pṛśni*) is stated among the common names of the intermediate space and the Ādityas, स्वः नाकः (*svaḥ nākaḥ*) (Ni. 2-13), and also पृश्निरादित्यो भवति प्राश्नुत एनं वर्ण इति नैरुक्ताः (*pṛśnirādityo bhavati prāśnuta enaṃ varṇa iti nairuktāḥ*) (Ni. 2-14). Yāska explains that the Āditya is called Pṛśni because abundant colour pervades him in a surpassing manner. Sāyaṇa gives one explanation—the goddess Pṛśni is the mother of the Maruts and has many colours—and then states the view of some who say that she herself is the deity presiding over the intermediate space. And on the point that Pṛśni is the mother of the Maruts he cites the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence “पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः (*pṛśniyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ*)” (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-4) and the Ṛk Saṃhitā sentence पृश्ने पुत्राः उपमासः (*pṛśne putrāḥ upamāsaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-58-5).
सा देवी तेषं अयासां मरुतामनीकं असूत (*sā devī teṣaṃ ayāsāṃ marutāmanīkaṃ asūta*)—the goddess Pṛśni has produced the troop of the Maruts, bright and ever moving, forty-nine (49 persons) in number. Having explained the meaning thus, he describes महते रणाय संग्रामाय मेघ जयाय (*mahate raṇāya saṃgrāmāya megha jayāya*) as: so that these Maruts may fight with the clouds and be victorious.
सप्सरासः अभ्वं (*sapsarāsaḥ abhvaṃ*)—समानरूपा हिंसका ना मेघानां । मेघं जनयंति उत्पादितवंतः । (*samānarūpā hiṃsakā nā meghānāṃ | meghaṃ janayaṃti utpāditavaṃtaḥ |*) The word सप्सरासः (*sapsarāsaḥ*) is explained as: the Marut deities are all of one and the same form, and they torment the clouds. The word अभ्व (*abhva*) is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24) and is also stated among the names of the great (Ni. 3-13). Here the word is explained as "cloud", and it is said that the Maruts produce the cloud.
आदित् इषिरां स्वधां पर्यपश्यन् (*ādit iṣirāṃ svadhāṃ paryapaśyan*)—अनंतरमेव सर्वैरेष्टव्यां अन्नं सस्यादि समृद्धि लक्षणं परिपश्यंति सर्वे जनाः । (*anaṃtarameva sarvaireṣṭavyāṃ annaṃ sasyādi samṛddhi lakṣaṇaṃ paripaśyaṃti sarve janāḥ |*) It is explained that only after the Marut deities have produced the cloud do all the people of the world understand that the food they desire arises from the prosperity of crops and the like.

### Printed p. 143
The word स्वधा (*svadhā*) is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24) and among the names of food (Ni. 2-9). As *svadhe* it is stated among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22 **NOTE**)**NOTE**. Here it is used in the sense of food arising from crops and the like.

##### Grammar

- असूत — षूज् प्राणिगर्भविमोचने इति धातुः । लज् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपं । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । अडागमस्योदात्तत्वात् आद्युदात्तं भवति ।
- अयासां — अय गत् इति धातुः । अयंते इति अयाः तेषां अयासां । सचादौ समाविष्टत्वात् नंदिग्रह पचा— (पा. सू. ३-१-१३४) इत्यनेन अच् प्रत्ययः । षष्ठीबहुवचने परे व्यत्ययेन तस्य सुटागमः ।
- अनीकं — अन प्राणने इति धातुः । अनिहृषिभ्यां किच्च (उ. सू. ४५७) इत्यनेन ईकन् प्रत्ययः । इत्यादिर्नित्यं इत्यनेन आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- सप्सरासः — प्सा भक्षणे । प्साति भक्षयति इति प्सरः रूपं । औणादिको डर प्रत्ययः । डित्वसामर्थ्यात् धातोः टेः (आकारस्य) लोपः । समानः प्सरः येषां ते सप्सरासः । समानस्य छंदसि— (पा. सू. ६-३-८४) इत्यनेन समानस्य सभावः । समानस्य (पा. सू. ६-१-२२३) इत्यनेन अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । अस्मात् जस् परे अज्जसेरसुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-६०) इत्यनेन तस्य असुकागमः ।
- अजनयंत — जनी प्रादुर्भावे इति धातुः । छंदसि लुज्— (पा. सू. ३-४--६) इत्यनेन वर्तमानार्थे लज् । हेतुमति च इत्यनेन णिच् । उपधावृद्धौ प्राप्तायां मित्संज्ञत्वात् मितां ह्रस्वः इत्यनेन ह्रस्वो भवति । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- इषिरां — इषु इच्छायां इति धातुः । इषिमदिमुदि (उ. सू. ५१) इत्यनेन किरच् प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् लघूपधगुणो न भवति । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इत्यनेन अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । स्त्रीत्वे अदंतत्वात् टाप् ।
- अपश्यन् — दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे इति धातुः । छांदसत्वेन वर्तमाने लज् । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपं । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ पंचदश्यां सूक्तोपक्रममारभ्य कृतां स्तुतिं मरुद्घो निवेद्याभिमतमाशास्ते ॥
> हे मरुतः एष स्तोम इदानीं क्रियमाणप्रकारं स्तोत्रं वो युष्मदर्थं ।
> युष्मश्रीणनाय भवत्वित्यर्थः । तथेयं गीः स्तुतिरूपा वागपि वो युष्मदर्थाय ।
> यस्मादेवं तस्मान्मांदार्यस्य स्तुतिविशेषैर्मंदयितुः स्तुतिभिर्मदस्य प्रेरयितुर्वा मान्यस्य वरप्रदानादिना माननीयस्य कारोः स्तोतुरिषेच्छया यासीष्ट ।
> आगच्छत । किमर्थं । त्वने शरीराय । तत्पोषायेत्यर्थः । वयां वयमपीषमन्नं
> वृजनं बलं जीरदानुं जयशीलदानमेतत्सर्वं विद्याम । युष्मा स्वागतेषु यज्ञसंपूर्त्येष्ट्वादिद्वारा लभेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Having offered, in the fifteenth**NOTE** (verse), the praise begun at the opening of the sūkta to the Maruts, the poet now prays for what he desires. O Maruts, may this hymn (स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)), of the kind now being made, be for you—that is, for your gratification; likewise this गीः (*gīḥ*), speech in the form of praise, is for you. Since this is so, come at the desire for food (*iṣe*) of the praiser (कारोः (*kāroḥ*))—who is मांदार्यस्य (*māṃdāryasya*), one who gladdens by special praises, or one who impels delight by praises, and मान्यस्य (*mānyasya*), worthy of honour through the bestowing of boons and the like. For what purpose? For the body (तन्वे (*tanve*) = शरीराय (*śarīrāya*)), that is, for its nourishment. We also (वयां (*vayāṃ*) = *vayamapi*) would obtain all this: food (इषं (*iṣaṃ*)), strength (वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)), and a gift that brings victory (जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*) = *jayaśīladānaṃ*). The last sentence युष्मा स्वागतेषु यज्ञसंपूर्त्येष्ट्वादिद्वारा लभेमहि (*yuṣmā svāgateṣu yajñasaṃpūrtyeṣṭvādidvārā labhemahi*) says that we would obtain these through the completion of the sacrifice, offerings and the like.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) मरुतः (*(he) marutaḥ*)—O Marut deities
- मांदार्यस्य (*māṃdāryasya*)—of the one who gives delight by praises
- मान्यस्य (*mānyasya*)—and who is worthy of honour
- कारोः (*kāroḥ*)—of the praiser
- एषः स्तोमः (*eṣaḥ stomaḥ*)—this praise made up to now
- वः (*vaḥ*)—for you (let it be); likewise
- इयं गीः (*iyaṃ gīḥ*)—this speech (in the form of praise) also (for you). [मांदार्यस्य (*māṃdāryasya*)—of the one who satisfies you with praises; मान्यस्य (*mānyasya*)—therefore worthy of worship; कारोः (*kāroḥ*)—of this praiser]

### Printed p. 145

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इषा (*iṣā*)—with desire
- तन्ने (*tanne*)—for the growth of (your) body
- आ यासीष्ट (*ā yāsīṣṭa*)—may (the praise) go towards you
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—strength
- जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*)—long life
- विद्याम (*vidyāma*)—may we obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, may our praise, we who are praisers, who please you with laudations and are worthy of worship, be (a delight) to you. By our wish, may this praise bring about the growth of your bodies; and may food, strength and long life also be granted to us (by your favour).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This praise, Maruts, is for you : this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations): may the praise reach you for (the good of your) persons, so that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Māndārya and Mānya: when Sāyaṇa gives the component meanings of these words, he explains Māndārya as one who produces joy and Mānya as one who is worthy of reverence. Both are epithets of Agastya. Both are also used as proper names. In the Bṛhaddevatā, where the birth of Agastya is told:
मानेन संमितो यस्मात् तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते । यद्वा कुंभादृषिर्जातः कुंभेनापि हि मीयते ॥ (*mānena saṃmito yasmāt tasmānmānya ihocyate | yadvā kuṃbhādṛṣirjātaḥ kuṃbhenāpi hi mīyate ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 5-153)
It states that the name Mānya is well known for Agastya either because he is worthy of reverence, or because he was born in a kumbha, which indicates a kind of measure (māna); that is, because he was born of a measure in the form of a pot.
In the same sequence, the words मांदार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः (*māṃdāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ*) stand also in the last Ṛks of the 165th, 166th and 167th sūktas.
There are two words meaning praise, स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*) and गीः (*gīḥ*). They indicate different kinds of praise. The importance of the stoma has been explained in detail in Part 11 of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, pp. 50-52.

### Printed p. 146

##### Grammar

- इषा — इषा सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) इति तृतीयाविभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- यासीष्ट — या प्रापणे धातुः । व्यत्ययो बहुलं (पा. सू. ३-१-८५) इति आत्मनेपदी भवति । लिज् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने त प्रत्ययः । लिजः सीयुट् (पा. सू. ३-४-१०२) इति सीयुडागमः । सुट् तिथोः (पा. सू. ३-४-१०७) इति सुटागमः । यलोपः । व्यत्ययेनैव एकवचनं आगतं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- विद्याम — विद्‌ल्य लाभे धातुः । लिट् उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपं । पादादिस्थत्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । यासुट् उदात्तः इति आकारः उदात्तः भवति ।
- वृजनं — वृजी वर्जने धातुः । कृष्यव्यजि (उ सू २-३३९) इति क्यु प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् गुणः न भवति । युवोरनाकौ (पा सू. ६-१-१) इति अनादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- जीरदानुं — बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।

## Sūkta 169 (Maṇḍala 1)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the fifth sūkta of the twenty-third anuvāka, beginning महश्चित्त्वं (*mahaścittvaṃ*), of eight Ṛks. The seer is Agastya, the deity Indra, the metre Triṣṭubh. The second Ṛk is a चतुष्पदा विराट् (*catuṣpadā virāṭ*): four pādas of ten syllables are called Virāṭ, as stated by Piṅgalanāga in the Chandonukramaṇikā (Pi. 3-5), and the Anukramaṇikā says महोऽष्टौ द्वितीया विराट् (*maho 'ṣṭau dvitīyā virāṭ*). In the ten-day Samūḍha sacrifice, at the recitation of the second Chandoma, this sūkta is used for the Marutvatīya śastra mantras, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the section विश्वजितोऽग्निं नर (*viśvajito 'gniṃ nara*) by the sūtra द्वितीयस्य शंसा महां महश्चित्त्वमिंद्र (*dvitīyasya śaṃsā mahāṃ mahaścittvamiṃdra*) (Ā. 8-7).

### Printed p. 147
Sūkta 169. Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 23, Sūkta 169. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Vargas 8, 9. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Ṛṣi: Agastya. Devatā: Indra. Chandas: 1, 3-8 Triṣṭubh; 2 Catuṣpadā Virāṭ.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒हश्चि॒त्त्वमिं॑द्र य॒त ए॒तान्म॒हश्चि॑दसि॒ त्यज॑सो वरू॒ता ।  
> स नो॑ वेधो म॒रुतां॑चिक्ति॒त्वान्॒नुस्मा व॑नुष्व॒ तव॒ हिप्रेष्ठा॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महः । चित् । त्वं । इंद्र । यतः । एतान् । महः । चित् । आसि । त्यजसः । वरूता ।  
> सः । नः । वेधः । मरुतां । चिकित्वान् । सुम्मा । वनुष्व । तव । हि । प्रेष्ठा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं यतः कारणादेतान्मरुतो महश्चिन्महतोऽपि सामर्थ्यातिशयवत्वात्त्वं निरपेक्षेणापि स्नेहान्न त्यजसीति शेषः । अतः कारणान्महश्चिदसि । चिदिति
> पादपूरणः । महतोऽपि त्यजसस्त्यागात् । यद्वा । एतत्क्रोधनाम । क्रोधाद्वा ।
> वरूथा वरिता रक्षितासि । भवसि । यद्वा। मरुतोऽपि त्यागाद्वृष्ट्या दिविषयाद्वारयितासि । यस्मादेवं तस्मात् हे मरुतां वेधो विधातः स तादृशस्त्वं चिकित्वांश्चतनावानस्मदनुग्रहविषयज्ञानोपेतः सन्नोऽस्मभ्यं सुम्मा सुखानि मरुदायत्तानि
> वृष्ट्यादिरूपाणि वनुष्व । देहि । तानि सुम्मानि तव हि प्रेष्ठा । तव खलु प्रियतमानि ।
> हिशब्दः आयमिंद्रो मरुत्सखा ।ऋ. ८-७६-२ । इत्यादिश्रुतिषु प्रसिद्ध्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, because you do not abandon these Maruts, though they are great and exceedingly powerful, even when you are independent of them, out of affection — "do not abandon" is the supplied remainder — for that reason you are great. चित् (*cit*) fills out the pāda. Since you refrain from abandoning even the great, you are great. Alternatively, त्यजसः (*tyajasaḥ*) is a name for anger: you are the protector against (their) anger. Or again: you restrain the Maruts even from abandoning, that is, from the matter of rain and the like. Since this is so, O creator (vedhas) of the Maruts, being such and knowing (cikitvān), endowed with the knowledge that concerns favour to us, grant (vanuṣva) to us the comforts (सुम्मा (*summā*), pleasures) which depend on the Maruts and take the form of rain and so on. Those comforts are indeed most dear to you. The word हि (*hi*) is for the sake of what is well known in śruti texts such as आयमिंद्रो मरुत्सखा (*āyamiṃdro marutsakhā*) (Ṛ. 8-76-2).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) इंद्र (*(he) iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यतः (*yataḥ*)—for which reason
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- महः चित् (*mahaḥ cit*)—though exceedingly great
- एतान् (*etān*)—these Maruts
- त्यजसः (*tyajasaḥ*)—from anger

### Printed p. 148
- (continued) त्यजसः (*tyajasaḥ*)—from anger (from abandonment as regards rain and the like)
- वरूता (असि) (*varūtā (asi)*)—you are the protector
- *(ataḥ) mahaḥ cit asi*—(therefore) you are truly great
- *(he) marutāṃ vedhaḥ*—O Indra, creator of the Maruts
- सः (*saḥ*)—such as you are
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—having the knowledge of favour towards us
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सुम्ना (*sumnā*)—(obtainable through the Maruts) the pleasures in the form of rain and so on
- वनुष्व (*vanuṣva*)—become the giver
- तव (*tava*)—to you
- प्रेष्ठा हि (*preṣṭhā hi*)—they are well known as the dearest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, since you protect even the Maruts, who are exceedingly great, without abandoning them, you are truly a great soul. O Indra, creator of the Maruts, being favourably minded towards us, grant us the pleasures in the form of rain and the like, which are most dear to you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You, Indra, are mighty from the might of those of whom you are the protector against abandonment : therefore, creator of the Maruts, favourably-minded towards us, grant us those blessings which are most dear to you

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मरुतः महश्चित्; त्यजसः वरूता (*marutaḥ mahaścit; tyajasaḥ varūtā*); since you are exceedingly powerful, you do not abandon (them) out of affection even when independent. For that reason महश्चिदसि (*mahaścidasi*). Here Indra is addressed.
The origin of the Maruts is told in the Bṛhaddevatā and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The goddess Diti, wishing for a son who would subdue Indra, obtained the favour of the sage Kaśyapa and was keeping a vow. Indra entered the womb of the pregnant woman and with his thunderbolt split the embryo into seven parts. When the child wept, Indra said "मारुद (*māruda*)" (do not weep) (मारुद (*māruda*)), and so it came to be called Marut. Afterwards Diti awoke and said to Indra that these fragments of the embryo should live and be his helpers; Indra agreed and made the Maruts his friends. This is indicated here.
Indra and the Maruts are both of great power; both are independent in action and do not seek another's help. Even so, although Indra is greatly powerful by his own power, his friendliness towards these Maruts makes his abundant greatness manifest — this is one kind of meaning, stated by giving the word त्यजसः (*tyajasaḥ*) the sense त्यागात् (*tyāgāt*)

### Printed p. 149
(abandonment). Very heroic persons are accustomed to strengthen their friendship with the powerful out of some desire for advantage. Indra is not so: independent, he abandoned them (the Maruts) at the time of their birth, and yet afterwards he is friendly with them; this shows Indra's abundant greatness. Thus the meaning is described.
In the second meaning the word त्यजसः (*tyajasaḥ*) is given the sense of anger. The word त्यजस् (*tyajas*) is listed among the names of anger (Ni. 3-9). Knowing at the time of the Maruts' birth that they would regard him as an enemy and later subdue him, Indra was angry with them; yet afterwards he is their protector (वरूता (*varūtā*)); therefore Indra's greatness is praiseworthy. This is the meaning explained.
In the third meaning: मरुतोऽपि त्यागात् वृष्ट्यादि विषयात् वारयितासि (*maruto 'pi tyāgāt vṛṣṭyādi viṣayāt vārayitāsi*). Because Indra has set the Maruts to the work of producing rain, Indra is मरुतां वेधः विधातः (*marutāṃ vedhaḥ vidhātaḥ*), the creator with regard to the Maruts; thus Indra's greatness is described.
चिकित्वान् न सुम्मा वनुष्प (*cikitvān na summā vanuṣpa*): although चिकित्वा (*cikitvā*) generally means one who is conscious, knowing, here it is explained, as अस्मदनुग्रहविषयज्ञानोपेतः (*asmadanugrahaviṣayajñānopetaḥ*), as one who has the knowledge to favour and protect us sacrificers. Since the word सुम्मा (*summā*) is listed among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-13), the happiness granted to the sacrificers by Indra is explained as मरुदायत्तानि वृष्टिरूपाणि (*marudāyattāni vṛṣṭirūpāṇi*), that is, happiness in the form of rain, dependent on the work done by the Maruts; and the wish is that Indra grant us sacrificers all the happiness produced through it.
By the sentence तव हि प्रेष्ठा (*tava hi preṣṭhā*) it is described that happiness of this form is the object of Indra's love because it comes from the Maruts, his friends. And in the Ṛk अयमिंद्रो मरुत्सखा (*ayamiṃdro marutsakhā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-76-2) the fact that Indra is a friend of the Maruts is stated.

##### Grammar

- महः — महतः इत्यत्र छांदसत्वेन अतिलोपः ।
- असि — अस भुवि । लट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- त्यजसः — त्यज हानौ धातुः । सर्वधातुभ्य असुन् इति असुन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । पंचमी एकवचनांतरूपं ।

### Printed p. 150
- वरूताः — वृञ् वरणे धातुः । ग्रसितस्कभित (पा. सू. ७-२-३४) इति तृजंतत्वेन निपातितं । चित् प्रत्ययांतत्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति । प्रथमा एकवचनांतरूपं ।
- प्रेष्ठा — अतिशयेन प्रियतमानि । प्रियशब्दस्य अतिशयार्थे इष्ठन् प्रत्ययः । अतिशायनेतमबिष्ठनौ (पा.सू. ५-३-५५) इति सूत्रेण भवति । प्रियस्थिर (पा.सू. ६-४-१५६) इति प्रियशब्दस्य प्रादेशः । प्रकृत्यैकाच् इति प्रकृतिभावः । गुणः । प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- वेधः — डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । वि उपसर्गपूर्वे विधाञ्छो वेधच (उ. सू. ६६४) इति असुन् प्रत्ययः । उपसर्गविशिष्टस्य वेधादेशः । संबुद्धौ आमंत्रितस्य च (पा. सू. ८-१-१९) इति निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- चिकित्वान् — कित ज्ञाने धातुः । अस्मात् लिटि आगते क्वसुश्च (पा. सू. ३-२-१०७) इति क्वसुरादेशः । धातोः द्वित्वादि । वसोः स्वरः भवति । प्रथमा एकवचनांतरूपं ।
- सुम्ना — शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (पा सू. ६-१-७०) इति शेः लोपः ।
- वनुष्व — वनु दाने अनेकार्थको धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अयु॑ज्रंत इंद्र वि॒श्वकृ॑स्टीर्विदा॒नासो॑ नि॒ष्पिधो॑ मर्त्य॒त्रा ।  
> म॒रुतां॑ पृत्सु॒तिर्हास॑माना॒ स्व॑र्माळ्लस्य प्र॒धन॑स्य सा॒त् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयुज्रन् । ते । इंद्र । विश्वकृष्टीः । विदानासः । निःसिधः । मर्त्यत्रा ।  
> मरुतां । पृत्सुतिः । हासमाना । स्वमीळहस्य । प्रधनस्य । सातौ ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 151

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वमंत्रे मरुतामिंद्रसाहाय्यमुक्तं । अत्रेंद्रस्य मरुत्साहाय्यमुच्यते । हे इंद्र ते मरुतोऽयुजन् । युज्यंते । त्वया युक्ता भवंतीत्यर्थः ।
> कीदृशास्ते । विश्वकृष्णीर्विश्वकृष्टयो राज्यत्वेन सर्वजनवंतः । किंच मर्त्यत्रा
> मर्त्येषु मर्त्यार्थं निष्पिधो निःशेषेणोदकस्य सेत्यन्नेघान्विदानासो
> जानानाः । किंच येषां मरुतां पृत्सुतिः सेना स्वर्माळस्य प्रधनस्य सुखसेक्तुः
> प्रकृष्णधनवतो वृत्रादिसंग्रामस्य सातौ लाभे जये निमित्तभूते सति सेना हासमाना हासं कुर्वती हर्षयुक्ता भवति । यद्वा । सुखेन मिह्यते जलं यस्मिन्
> तादृशस्य प्रधानस्य प्रकृष्टोदकाख्यधनसाधनस्य संग्रामस्य सातौ । मेघभेदनायेति
> यावत् । येषामिवृशी सेनास्ति ते मरुतोऽयुजन्निति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the previous mantra the Maruts' help to Indra was stated; here Indra's help from the Maruts is stated. "O Indra, the Maruts are yoked (अयुज्रन् (*ayujran*)), that is, they become joined with you." What are they like? विश्वकृष्टीः (*viśvakṛṣṭīḥ*) is explained as विश्वकृस्टयः (*viśvakṛsṭayaḥ*): by way of sovereignty they have all people. Further, मर्त्यत्रा (*martyatrā*) means among mortals, for the sake of mortals; they are विदानासः (*vidānāsaḥ*), knowing the clouds that pour out water without remainder. Further, the Maruts' host (पृत्सुतिः (*pṛtsutiḥ*), the army) becomes joyful, laughing, when victory is to be won in the battle against Vṛtra and others, which is स्वर्माळस्य (*svarmāḷasya*), a giver of happiness, and प्रधनस्य (*pradhanasya*), one with excellent wealth. Alternatively: a battle in which water is sprinkled easily, a means of winning the excellent wealth called water; that is, for the splitting of the cloud. The connection is: those whose army is such, those Maruts are joined (with you).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of which Marut deities
- पृत्सुतिः (*pṛtsutiḥ*)—the army
- स्वर्मिळस्य (*svarmiḷasya*)—heaven-bestowing (happiness-bestowing)
- प्रधनस्य (*pradhanasya*)—of one with excellent wealth (in the battle with Vṛtra and others)
- सातौ (*sātau*)—in the matter of gain (victory) obtained by you
- [or स्वर्मिळस्य (*svarmiḷasya*)—having water easily obtained; प्रधनस्य (*pradhanasya*)—of the cloud possessing the excellent wealth in the form of water; सातौ (*sātau*)—in the matter of the victory you win]
- हासमाना (*hāsamānā*)—is laughing
- ते (*te*)—such
- विश्वकृष्टीः (*viśvakṛṣṭīḥ*)—possessing all people
- मर्त्यत्रा (*martyatrā*)—for men
- निष्विधः (*niṣvidhaḥ*)—the clouds that pour out much water
- विदानासः (*vidānāsaḥ*)—the Marut deities who know
- अयुज्रन् (*ayujran*)—join (with you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Marut deities, who are lords over all people (masters of all men) and who impel the rain-making clouds for the sake of men, remain with you alone; through the victory over Vṛtra and others that you accomplish, or through the splitting of the cloud, these Maruts become delighted.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Rulers over all men, and impelling towards man the water-shedding clouds, they are united, Indra, (with you) : the host of Maruts is delighted by (your) acquisition of heaven-bestowing wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Since the help Indra gave the Maruts was stated in the previous mantra, the help Indra receives from the Maruts is stated in this mantra.

विश्वकृष्टीः (*viśvakṛṣṭīḥ*)—Sāyaṇa changes this word into विश्वकृस्टयः (*viśvakṛsṭayaḥ*), a word ending in the nominative plural, and explains राज्यत्वेन सर्वजनवंतः (*rājyatvena sarvajanavaṃtaḥ*): the Marut deities regard everything as their kingdom, and with the thought that everything is the object of their protection, they stay with a uniform affection toward all creatures.

मर्त्यत्रा निष्पिधः विदानासः (*martyatrā niṣpidhaḥ vidānāsaḥ*)—he also describes the meaning as मर्त्यार्थं निश्येषेण उदकस्य सेक्त्र्यन् मेघान् विदानासः जानानाः (*martyārthaṃ niśyeṣeṇa udakasya sektryan meghān vidānāsaḥ jānānāḥ*): they remain knowing that the clouds pour down waters for the prosperity of men.

मरुतां पृत्सुतिः प्रधनस्य सात् हासमाना (*marutāṃ pṛtsutiḥ pradhanasya sāt hāsamānā*)—for the word पृत्सुति (*pṛtsuti*) the meaning "army" is given; the word प्रधन (*pradhana*) has been explained by the Nirukta-author:
न्यक्रंदयन्नु पयंत एनममेहयन्वृषभं मध्य आजेः । तेन सूभव० शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः प्रधने जगाय । (*nyakraṃdayannu payaṃta enamamehayanvṛṣabhaṃ madhya ājeḥ | tena sūbhava0 śatavatsahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pradhane jagāya |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-12-5)
Here "प्रधन (*pradhana*) is a name of battle; in it wealth is scattered about"; because wealth is spent here in great measure, battle is the meaning of the word प्रधन (*pradhana*). Following the meaning of the Nirukta-author, Sāyaṇa describes it as "battle", and takes it as productive of happiness: सुखसेकुः प्रकृष्टधनवतो वृत्रादिसंग्रामस्य लाभे जये निमित्तभूते सति सेना हर्षयुक्ता भवति (*sukhasekuḥ prakṛṣṭadhanavato vṛtrādisaṃgrāmasya lābhe jaye nimittabhūte sati senā harṣayuktā bhavati*). He explains the meaning thus: the army of the Marut deities is joyful because victory is to be gained in the battle to be fought with Vṛtra and other asuras, rich in abundant wealth, a producer of happiness.

In the second meaning, since the word स्वर्मिक्षस्य (*svarmikṣasya*) is an adjective of the word प्रधनस्य (*pradhanasya*), [Sāyaṇa says] सुखेन मिह्यते जलं यस्मिन् तादृशस्य प्रधनस्य प्रकृष्टोदकाख्यधनसाधनस्य संग्रामस्य सात् मेघभेदनाय (*sukhena mihyate jalaṃ yasmin tādṛśasya pradhanasya prakṛṣṭodakākhyadhanasādhanasya saṃgrāmasya sāt meghabhedanāya*). The meaning is laid out: the army of the Marut deities stands ready to help Indra for the battle in the form of the splitting of the cloud, which is the cause of obtaining the wealth called water, a setting in which water is obtained easily.

##### Grammar

- आयुज्रन्—युजिर् योगे धातुः । छांदसत्वाद् वर्तमानार्थे लज् । कर्मणि व्यत्ययेन विकरणस्य लुक् । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झेरंतादेशः । इकारलोपः । बहुलं छंदसि इति तस्य रुट् आगमः । अंगस्य अडागमः । पादादित्वान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । आद्युदात्तं भवति ।
- विश्वकृष्टीः—विश्वे सर्वे कृष्टयो जना यस्य सः । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदं इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । जसि परे सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घो भवति ।
- विदानासः—विद ज्ञाने धातुः । लटः शानचादेशः । विकरणस्य लुक् । प्रत्ययस्य जित्त्वातिदेशात् लघूपधगुणो न भवति । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इत्यंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । जसि परे आज्जसेरसुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-५०) इत्यसुक् आगमः ।
- निष्षिधः—षिध गत्यां धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । प्रादिसमासे कृन्मत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपं ।
- मर्त्यत्रा—देवमनुष्यपुरुषपुरुमर्त्येभ्यो द्वितीयासप्तम्योर्बहुलं त्रल् (पा. सू. ५-४-५६) इति सप्तम्यंतात् त्रा प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तं भवति । **NOTE**
- हासमाना—हसे हसने धातुः । लटः शानचादेशः । प्रत्ययादुपधावृद्धिः । लसार्वधातुकं तास्यनुदात्तेत् इति सूत्रेणानुदात्तत्वाद् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- स्वर्मिळस्य—मिह सेचने धातुः । निष्ठा इति क्तप्रत्ययः । होढः (पा. सू. ८-२-३१) इति हकारस्य ढत्वं । झुषस्तथोः इति तकारस्य धत्वं । तस्य ष्टुत्वे जाते ढोढे लोपः (पा. सू. ८-३-१३) इति पूर्वढकारस्य लोपः । ढ्रलोपे पूर्वस्य (पा. सू. ६-३-१११) इति पूर्वस्य दीर्घः । न्यङ्स्वरौ स्वरितौ इति स्वर् इति स्वरितो भवति । बहुव्रीहिसमासे पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । षष्ठ्येकवचनांतरूपं ।
- सातौ—षणु दाने । ऊतियूति (पा. सू. ३-३-९७) इति क्तिन् उदात्तो निपातितः । सप्तम्येकवचनांतरूपं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रते तव सा प्रसिद्धा ऋष्टिर्वज्राख्यायुधविशेषोऽस्मे अस्मद्वृष्ट्यर्थमम्यक् । प्राप्नोति मेघसमीपे । एवं च सति मरुतोऽपि सनेमि । आह्न्यायेति
> षट् पुराणनामानीत्युक्तत्वात्सनेमाति पुराणनाम । पुराणं चिरकालं संगृहीतमभ्वमुदकं जुनंति । क्षिपंति । वर्षंतीत्यर्थः । वृष्ट्या सस्यादिसमृद्धौ सत्यामग्निश्चिद्दि
> ष्म । हि स्मेति पूरणे । अग्निरप्यतसे संतते कर्मणि निमित्तभूते सति शुशुक्वान्दीप्यमानो वर्तते । पश्चा प्रयांसि चरुपुरोडाशादिहवींषि दधति । धारयंति ददति वा
> यजमानाः । किमिव आपो न द्वीपं । द्विपार्श्वस्थोदकवान्सर्वतादिर्द्वीपः । तं
> यथापो धारयंति तद्वत् । यद्वा। आयुधमेवोच्यते। वज्राख्यायुधविशेषोतसे
> काष्ठसमूहे शुशुक्वान्दीपयन्नग्निश्चित् । चिच्छब्द उपमार्थे वधि चिदित्युपमार्थे ।
> नि. १-४ । इति यास्केनोपमार्थस्योक्तत्वात् ॥ काष्ठे ज्वलन्नग्निरिव । तद्दद्दीप्तो
> वर्तते । एतदेव दीप्तत्वमपेक्ष्य सेत्युक्तं । एवं च सत्यापो द्वीपमिव वृष्टुदकानि प्रयांसि सस्याद्यन्नानि दधति । धारयंति । एतत्सर्वं महानुभावस्येंद्रस्यर्प्पेः
> सामर्थ्यमितींद्रस्य स्तुतिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, that well-known ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*) of yours, the special weapon called vajra, reaches (अम्यक् (*amyak*)) the neighbourhood of the cloud for the sake of our rain. This being so, the Maruts too cast down (जुनंति (*junaṃti*), that is, rain) the अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*), water, long since collected (सनेमि (*sanemi*))." He supports this by the statement that "सनेमि (*sanemi*) is a name for 'ancient'", since the six ancient names beginning with अह्नाय (*ahnāya*) are listed. When crops and the like flourish through the rain, even Agni (हि स्म (*hi sma*) being expletive) blazes (शुशुक्वान् (*śuśukvān*)) for the continuous rite (अतसे (*atase*)); afterwards the sacrificers hold or give the oblations (प्रयांसि (*prayāṃsi*)), such as cooked rice and cakes. Like what? आपो न द्वीपं (*āpo na dvīpaṃ*): द्वीप (*dvīpa*) is a mountain or the like with water on both sides; as waters hold it, so.

Alternatively, the weapon itself is meant: the special weapon called vajra, like fire blazing in a heap of wood (अतसे (*atase*)). The word चित् (*cit*) is used in the sense of comparison, since Yāska has said so: चिदित्युपमार्थे (*cidityupamārthe*) (Ni. 1-4). As fire burning in wood, so it is blazing. Having regard to this very brilliance, सा (*sā*) is said. This being so, the waters, like an island, bear the foods, the crops and so on, that is, the rain-waters hold them. All this is the power of the greatly glorious Indra's ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*); thus it is praise of Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- सा (*sā*)—that well-known
- ऋष्टिः (*ṛṣṭiḥ*)—vajra weapon
- अस्मे (*asme*)—for us (to produce rain)
- अम्यक् (*amyak*)—approaches (the clouds)
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Marut deities
- सनेमि (*sanemi*)—long since (collected)
- अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*)—water
- जुनंति (*junaṃti*)—cast down (pour down)
- अग्निः चित् हि स्म (*agniḥ cit hi sma*)—Agni also

- शुशुक्वान् (*śuśukvān*)—blazing (he is)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, your weapon called vajra approaches (the clouds) for us (in order to shed rain); Agni too is blazing for the sacrificial rite; (the sacrificers) stand round Agni with oblations of cooked rice, cakes and the like, as waters surround an island.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Your weapon, Indra, is at hand for our (good); the Maruts send down the long-accumulated rain; Agni is blazing for the ceremony; the oblations encompass him as the waters (surround) an island.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋष्टिः अस्मे अम्यक् (*ṛṣṭiḥ asme amyak*)—here Indra is addressed. For the word ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*) he gives the meaning वज्राख्यायुधविशेषः (*vajrākhyāyudhaviśeṣaḥ*), Indra's weapon famed under the name of the vajra weapon, and describes the meaning of अस्मद्वृष्ट्यर्थं मेघसमीपे प्राप्नोति (*asmadvṛṣṭyarthaṃ meghasamīpe prāpnoti*): that weapon is employed near the clouds, so that for us the sacrificers the waters of rain may be poured down. The Nirukta-author, explaining the word अम्यक् (*amyak*), quotes this very Ṛk अम्यक् सा त इंद्र ऋष्टिरस्मे सनेम्यभ्वं (*amyak sā ta iṃdra ṛṣṭirasme sanemyabhvaṃ*) and comments अमाक्तेशि वा अभ्युक्तेशि वा (*amākteśi vā abhyukteśi vā*). Durgācārya explains the sense: ऋष्टिरभिधेया मां एषा प्रत्यंचि तामामेषाप्रत्यंचितेति क्षिप्तेशि शत्रवः मन्यंते (*ṛṣṭirabhidheyā māṃ eṣā pratyaṃci tāmāmeṣāpratyaṃciteti kṣipteśi śatravaḥ manyaṃte*): enemies think that Indra's weapon called ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*) is directed against them; and नित्यकालं शत्रून् प्रति अभिगतैव-भवतीशि अम्यगित्युच्यते (*nityakālaṃ śatrūn prati abhigataiva-bhavatīśi amyagityucyate*): because it is always used against enemies it is known as अम्यक् (*amyak*).

मरुतः सनेमि अभ्वं जुनंति (*marutaḥ sanemi abhvaṃ junaṃti*)—चिरकालं संगृहीतं उदकं वर्षंति (*cirakālaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ udakaṃ varṣaṃti*). When Indra's weapon called ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*) is applied near the cloud, the waters the clouds have long collected are made to fall out and rain is produced. This is the meaning given.

### Printed p. 156
The word अभ्व (*abhva*) is read both among the names of water (Ni. 2-24) and among the names of "great" (Ni. 3-13); here the meaning "water" is given.

The word सनेमि (*sanemi*), though listed among the names for "ancient" (Ni. 3-20), is shown in the sense क्षिप्रं (*kṣipraṃ*) in the Ṛk
शं नो भवंतु वाजिनो हवेषु देवताता मितद्रवः स्वर्काः । जंभयंतोऽहिं वृकं रक्षांसि सनेम्यस्मद्युयुवन्न मीवाः ॥ (*śaṃ no bhavaṃtu vājino haveṣu devatātā mitadravaḥ svarkāḥ | jaṃbhayaṃto 'hiṃ vṛkaṃ rakṣāṃsi sanemyasmadyuyuvanna mīvāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-38-7)
Of the two meanings the Nirukta-author gives for सनेमि (*sanemi*), "ancient, of very early time" and क्षिप्र (*kṣipra*) (swift), Sāyaṇa accepts "ancient" alone. In his commentary he says सनेमि अह्नाय इति षट् पुराणनामानि इत्युक्तत्वात् सनेमि इति पुराणनाम पुराणं चिरकालं संगृहीतं (*sanemi ahnāya iti ṣaṭ purāṇanāmāni ityuktatvāt sanemi iti purāṇanāma purāṇaṃ cirakālaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ*): because it is read in the Nirukta among the six names for "ancient", he justifies the meaning "ancient (old)" for सनेमि (*sanemi*) and explains that the waters were accumulated for a very long time.

Two kinds of meaning are given for the second half of this Ṛk. Both arise from the expletive and comparative senses of the word चित् (*cit*) in अग्निश्चिद्भिष्ट (*agniścidbhiṣṭa*). **NOTE** In the first meaning the word Agni is the subject. *atase saṃtate karmaṇi nimittabhūte sati śuśukvān*: after the crops have arisen through rain and the like, Agni shines brilliantly on account of rites such as sacrifice; and to satisfy the Agni thus shining, प्रयांसि दधति चरुपुरोडाशादिहवींषि धारयंति ददति वा यजमानाः (*prayāṃsi dadhati carupuroḍāśādihavīṃṣi dhārayaṃti dadati vā yajamānāḥ*): the sacrificers hold the oblations, or offer them in the fire. The oblations held by the sacrificers are compared आपो न द्वीपं (*āpo na dvīpaṃ*), as waters hold an island. The meaning of the word द्वीप (*dvīpa*) is made plain as द्विपार्श्वस्थोदकवान् पर्वतादिः (*dvipārśvasthodakavān parvatādiḥ*), a tract of land surrounded by water on both sides; and the mode of comparison is described: तं यथा अपो धारयंति (*taṃ yathā apo dhārayaṃti*), as waters hold an island, so the oblation is held between Agni and the sacrificers.

The Nirukta-author, explaining the particle चित् (*cit*), says चिदित्येषो अनेककर्मा (*cidityeṣo anekakarmā*): the particle चित् (*cit*) is used in many senses; and then explains them

### Printed p. 157

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the particle चित् (*cit*) (cit), the Nirukta authors state with the sentence दधिचिदित्युपमार्थे (*dadhicidityupamārthe*) that the word is used in the sense of a comparison. Following this, Sāyaṇa cites it as चिच्छब्दः उपमार्थे दधिचिदित्युपमार्थे (नि. १-४) इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् (*cicchabdaḥ upamārthe dadhicidityupamārthe (ni. 1-4) iti yāskenoktatvāt*) (Ni. 1-4). He then gives an alternative: यद्वा आयुधमेवोच्यते । वज्राख्यायुधविशेषो अतसे काष्ठसमूहे शुतुक्वान् दीपयन्नग्निश्चित् (*yadvā āyudhamevocyate | vajrākhyāyudhaviśeṣo atase kāṣṭhasamūhe śutukvān dīpayannagniścit*). The weapon of Indra called the thunderbolt is what is meant here; it shines like a fire shining in a heap of wood. This meaning he explains with the commentary काष्ठे ज्वलन्नग्निरिव तद्वद्दीप्तो वर्तते (*kāṣṭhe jvalannagniriva tadvaddīpto vartate*). The abundant brilliance of Agni is expressed, he explains, by the word सा (*sā*). The comparison-sentence आपो न द्वीपं (*āpo na dvīpaṃ*) he explains and supports with अपः द्वीपमिव वृष्णुदकानि सस्याद्यन्नानि धारयंति (*apaḥ dvīpamiva vṛṣṇudakāni sasyādyannāni dhārayaṃti*): as waters enclose and hold an island, the rain-waters hold plants and the like, and food.

आतसे (*ātase*)—संतते कर्मणि (*saṃtate karmaṇi*): for the word अतस् (*atas*) the meaning given is "in an action carried on continuously". The Nirukta authors (quote the verse):
आपांतमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिश्यिविमावाञ्चरुमा यजीषी । सोमो विश्वान्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि देभुः ॥ (*āpāṃtamanyustṛpalaprabharmā dhuniśyivimāvāñcarumā yajīṣī | somo viśvānyatasā vanāni nārvāgiṃdraṃ pratimānāni debhuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-5)
Here, for the word अतसा (*atasā*), Durgācārya gives the meaning अनुपक्षीणानि (*anupakṣīṇāni*), "growing, increasing". Sāyaṇa states the same meaning with संतते (*saṃtate*).

##### Grammar

- अम्यक् — छांदसे वर्तमानार्थे लज् । पादादित्वान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । आद्युदात्तं भवति ।
- अस्मे — सुपां सुलक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३४) इति चतुर्थ्याः शे आदेशः ।
- जुनंति — जु इति गत्यर्थकः सौत्रो धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झि अंतादेशः । क्रादिभ्यः श्ना इति श्नाविकरणम् । श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (पा. सू. ६-४-११२) इति तदाकारस्य लोपः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- आतसे — आत सातत्यगमने धातुः । अत्यविचवितमि-(उ. सू. ३९७) इति असच् प्रत्ययः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । सप्तम्यंतरूपम् ।
- शशुक्वान् — शुच दीप्तौ धातुः । अस्मात् लिट् आगते क्वसुष्ट (पा. सू. ३-२-१०६)

- इति तस्य क्वसुरादेशः । प्रत्ययनिमित्ते द्वित्वादौ प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन कुत्वं भवति । वसोः स्वरो अवशिष्यते ।
- द्वीपं — द्विर्गता आपो यस्मिन् इति द्वीपं । द्व्यंतरुपसर्गेभ्योऽप ईत् (पा. सू. ६-३-४७) इति द्वि उपपदे अप इत्यस्याकारस्य ईत्वं भवति ।
- दधति — डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । हिचॆ (पा. सू. ८-१-३४) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधे प्राप्ते अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१८९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, you indeed (तु (*tu*) is for emphasis) give that wealth, cows and the like, that is fit to be given by you." Since you are the most generous even compared with others, give us very great wealth. We please you, the giver (रातिं (*rātiṃ*)), with a gift (दक्षिणया (*dakṣiṇayā*)) that is ओजिष्ठया (*ojiṣṭhayā*), the most forceful, fit to circulate, a means of prosperity and consisting of cows and the like, just as one pleases a priest. Alternatively: दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*) is a general word for a gift-substance, and the word राति (*rāti*) means a kinsman; as people win over a kinsman by giving substantial things such as gold, so we win you over. Further, of you, Vāyu, who throw down the washed (cleansed) youth and quickly grant boons, ते (*te*) stands in the genitive in the sense of the object: our praisers who have praised you, Vāyu, desire you; or the praises that desire you alone. The Sanskrit of
