##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(O Hotṛ,) praise that Indra who is of great prowess, a hero, rich in wealth, standing in his chariot, who fights facing his enemies, who wields the thunderbolt, and who destroys the cloud and the like, the darkness that covers everything.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Glorify that Indra who is mighty, who is a hero, possessing abundant wealth, standing in his car, a valiant combatant against adversaries, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the disperser of all-enveloping gloom.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तमुष्टुहि (*tamuṣṭuhi*)—By this sentence the command of the seer who saw the mantra is given here: addressing the priest called Hotṛ, "praise Indra."

यो ह सत्वा (*yo ha satvā*)—अतिप्रभूतबलः, यद्वा सावकः तत्राणां (*atiprabhūtabalaḥ, yadvā sāvakaḥ tatrāṇāṃ*): the meaning is explained as Indra being one of abundant strength, or one who destroys enemies. **NOTE**

मघवा (*maghavā*)—बलवानन्नर्वा वा (*balavānannarvā vā*). The authors of the Nirukta read the word मघ (*magha*) among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9) and explain: मघमिति धननामधेयं महतेर्दानकर्मणः (*maghamiti dhananāmadheyaṃ mahaterdānakarmaṇaḥ*), that is, the word मघ (*magha*), derived from the root मंह (*maṃha*) which conveys the sense of giving, denotes wealth. Sāyaṇa accepts the use of the word मघ (*magha*) in the senses of strength or food, and explains that Indra is possessed of strength or of food.

Indra is प्रतिचश्चित् योधीर्यान् (*praticaścit yodhīryān*), the best among the heroes who fight facing the enemy who is engaged in battle; and वृषण्वान् (*vṛṣaṇvān*), possessing weapons such as the thunderbolt that assist in pouring rain. For the word वृषण्वान् (*vṛṣaṇvān*) Sāyaṇa gives the meaning वर्षितारः (*varṣitāraḥ*), and explains the sense through the thunderbolt and the like as producers of rain; to convey this same meaning he quotes—

### Printed p. 269
वृषा ते वज्र उत ते वृषा रथो वृषणा हरी वृषभाण्यायुधा । वृष्णो मदस्य वृषभ त्वमीशिष इंद्र सोमस्य वृषभस्य तृप्नुहि ॥ (*vṛṣā te vajra uta te vṛṣā ratho vṛṣaṇā harī vṛṣabhāṇyāyudhā | vṛṣṇo madasya vṛṣabha tvamīśiṣa iṃdra somasya vṛṣabhasya tṛpnuhi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-16-6)

And he describes Indra's abundant greatness: वववुषश्चित्तमसः विहंता (*vavavuṣaścittamasaḥ vihaṃtā*), the destroyer of the darkness that covers.

##### Grammar

- स्तुहि — ष्टुञ् स्तुत् इति धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- सत्वा — षड्ल्‌ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु इति धातुः । प्रईर सद्योस्तुट् च (उ. सू. ४-५२६) इत्यनेन विधीयमानः क्वनि प्रत्ययो बहुलवचनात् केवलस्यास्य धातोरपि भवति । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वाद् धातुस्वरो अवतिष्ठते ।
- प्रतीचः — प्रति इति उपसर्गः । अंचु गतिपूजनयोः इति धातुः । ऋत्विक् दधृक्—(पा. सू. ३-२-५९) इति क्विन् प्रत्ययः । अनिदितांहलउप—(पा. सू. ६-४-२४) इत्युपधानकारलोपः । शस् परे भसंज्ञत्वादाचः (पा. सू. ६-४-१७८) इति धातोरकारस्य लोपः । लुप्तनकाराकारस्यांचुधातोः परत्वाच्चौ (पा. सू. ६-३-१३८) इति पूर्वस्य दीर्घः । अंचेश्चंदस्युपसंख्यानम् इति वचनाद् विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- योधीयान् — योधितृशब्दादतिशयार्थ ईयसुन् प्रत्ययः । तुरिष्टेमेयः सु (पा. सू. ६-४-१५४) इति तृचो लोपः । प्रकृत्यैकाच् इति सूत्रेण प्रकृतिभावात् टिलोपो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वाद् इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१६९) इत्याद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- ववप्रुषः — वृञ् आवरणे इति धातुः । चुरादिः । लिटः क्वसुरादेशः । प्रत्ययनिमित्तं द्वित्वादि । छांदसत्वेन वकारोऽधिको भवति । षष्ठ्यां वसोः संप्रसारणम् (पा. सू. ६-४-१३१) इति संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपम् । शासिवसिघसीनां च (पा. सू. ८-३-६) इति षत्वम् । क्वसुप्रत्ययस्वरो अवतिष्ठते । **NOTE**
- विहंता — हन हिंसागत्योः इति धातुः । कर्तरि तृच् प्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that when this Indra, by his greatness, by his own lordship, is able over the leaders, the sacrificers who carry out the rites, to bestow heaven and the like and to protect them, for this protecting Indra the two world-halves, heaven and earth, though treated as girths, are not sufficient for his movement. That is, since they are too small for the movement of Indra, the overlord of the world, heaven and earth do not suffice; the sense is that the creator's greatness exceeds even that of what is created. This Indra encompasses the earth or the beings, like a वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*), an enclosure; the word is a form of the root *vṛj* in the sense of cutting (**NOTE**). As that encloses, so he with his own brilliance encloses the three worlds. Moreover, this Indra, possessing स्वधा (*svadhā*), food, or water in the form of rain, bears the sky, the day, भर्ति (*bharti*), that is, बिभर्ति (*bibharti*). The example for bearing is ओपशमिव (*opaśamiva*): that which lies slightly upon something is ओपशं (*opaśaṃ*), a horn; as a bull bears it. Or else: the two worlds called earth and atmosphere, lying close to each other, are ओपशं (*opaśaṃ*); like that he bears the sky; the meaning is that he bears the three worlds.

- इत्या (*ityā*)—truly
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by his greatness (lordship)
- वृभ्यः (*vṛbhyaḥ*)—to the leaders (the sacrificers who carry out the rites)
- प्र आस्ति (*pra āsti*)—becomes able to bestow fruits such as heaven, or to protect

- कक्ष्ये (*kakṣye*)—those that are like girths
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—earth and atmosphere
- न अरं (*na araṃ*)—are not wide enough (for his movement)
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—this Indra
- भूम (*bhūma*)—the earth
- वृजनं न (*vṛjanaṃ na*)—as the sky encloses

- (किंच आयं (*kiṃca āyaṃ*)—moreover

- स्वधावान् (*svadhāvān*)—endowed with food (water in the form of rain)
- ओपशं इव (*opaśaṃ iva*)—as a bull bears a horn; or, as he also upholds the earth and the atmosphere, which lie close to each other

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the protector and the supremely glorious one of the sacrificers who carry out the rites, surpasses heaven and earth. As the sky encompasses the earth, so he too encompasses the three worlds with his splendour. Endowed with food (water in the form of rain), he is the support of the heavenly world, just as he is the support of earth and sky.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Heaven and earth are insufficient for the girth of that Indra, who, with his greatness, rules over the leaders (of sacrifice) : as the atmosphere encompasses the earth, so he encompasses (the three worlds), and, being the master of the rain, he upholds the sky as well as the firmament and the earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

महिना नृभ्यः प्र अस्ति—महत्वेन स्वैश्वर्येण नेतृभ्यः कर्मनिर्वाहकेभ्यः । यजमानेभ्यः प्रभवति । (*mahinā nṛbhyaḥ pra asti—mahatvena svaiśvaryeṇa netṛbhyaḥ karmanirvāhakebhyaḥ | yajamānebhyaḥ prabhavati |*). The meaning is explained thus: Indra is worshipful toward the sacrificers who perform the sacrificial rites, through his own majestic power (lordship) full of greatness. The word नरः (*naraḥ*) is stated among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27) and among the names of man (Ni. 3-7). Here it is used in the sense of the sacrificers who perform the rites.

The word इत्था (*itthā*) is read among the names meaning "true", श्रत् (*śrat*) and so on (Ni. 3-13). In showing the nirvacana of the word इत्था (*itthā*), Yāska says इत्था अमुथेत्येतेन व्याख्यातं (*itthā amuthetyetena vyākhyātaṃ*) (Ni. 5-5): it is to be understood like the nirvacana of the word अमुथा (*amuthā*). अमुथा यथासाविति व्याख्यातं (*amuthā yathāsāviti vyākhyātaṃ*) (3-16): अमुथा (*amuthā*) is used in the sense of truth and also in the sense of comparison, and the word इत्था (*itthā*) is likewise used. Having shown this, he cites the Ṛk
त्यं चिदित्था कत्पयं शयानमसूर्ये शमसि वावृधानं । (*tyaṃ ciditthā katpayaṃ śayānamasūrye śamasi vāvṛdhānaṃ |*)

### Printed p. 272

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-6)
and shows that the word इत्था (*itthā*) means "truly" (Ni. 6-3). Durgācārya explains it as अमुना प्रकारेण (*amunā prakāreṇa*), and Sāyaṇa as अमुष्मिन्नंतरिक्षलोके (*amuṣminnaṃtarikṣaloke*). In the present Ṛk it is used in the sense of truth.

कक्ष्ये (*kakṣye*): कक्ष्या रज्जुरश्वस्य-कक्षं सेवते; कक्षो गाहतेः क्स इति नामकरणः । ख्यातीर्वानर्थकोऽभ्यासः । किमस्मिन् ख्यानमिति । कषतेर्वा । तत्सामान्यान्मनुष्यकक्षो बाहुमूलसामान्यादश्वस्य । (*kakṣyā rajjuraśvasya-kakṣaṃ sevate; kakṣo gāhateḥ ksa iti nāmakaraṇaḥ | khyātīrvānarthako 'bhyāsaḥ | kimasmin khyānamiti | kaṣatervā | tatsāmānyānmanuṣyakakṣo bāhumūlasāmānyādaśvasya |*) (Ni. 2-2). Because it is tied around the neck of the horse, the strap around its neck is called kakṣā. The affix क्स (*ksa*) joined with the root गाह् (*gāh*), used in the sense of entering within, may give the formation कक्ष्या (*kakṣyā*). Or it may be formed by reduplication of the root ख्या (*khyā*). Or the root कषा (*kaṣā*), meaning "to rub", may be its origin. Hence this name is also well known for the armpit (kakṣa) of a man; that is, heaven and earth, which have an interval equal to this armpit, may be meant.

Moreover, the Nirukta author has read the word कक्ष्या (*kakṣyā*) among the names of the "fingers" (Ni. 3-8), and he cites the Ṛk in which the word is used,
दशावनिभ्यो दशकक्ष्मेभ्यो दशयोक्रेभ्यो दशयोजनेभ्यः । दशाभीशुभ्यो अर्चताजरेभ्यो दश धुरो दश युक्ता वहद्भ्यः ॥ (*daśāvanibhyo daśakakṣmebhyo daśayokrebhyo daśayojanebhyaḥ | daśābhīśubhyo arcatājarebhyo daśa dhuro daśa yuktā vahadbhyaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94),
and explains the word कक्ष्या (*kakṣyā*) there as fingers. In the present Ṛk it means the interval of heaven and earth.

अस्मै रोदसी कक्ष्ये नालं (*asmai rodasī kakṣye nālaṃ*): the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is stated among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22). Although heaven and earth move along their own paths, they are not sufficient for the movement of Indra, who protects the sacrificers performing the rites. The meaning is explained: जगतोऽधीशस्य इंद्रस्य संचाराय अल्पत्वात् द्यावापृथिव्यौ न पर्याप्ते । सृष्टादपि स्रष्टुर्महिम्मो अधिकत्वात् । (*jagato 'dhīśasya iṃdrasya saṃcārāya alpatvāt dyāvāpṛthivyau na paryāpte | sṛṣṭādapi sraṣṭurmahimmo adhikatvāt |*). Since the greatness of the creator exceeds the greatness of the thing created, the room that heaven and earth afford is not sufficient for the movement of Indra, the lord of the whole world. This implies that the greatness of heaven and earth is less than the greatness of Indra.

आरं—अलं । पराप्त इत्यर्थः (*āraṃ—alaṃ | parāpta ityarthaḥ*). The meaning here is "sufficient, so as to give satisfaction". Besides giving the sense "sufficient", this word is also used in the senses "make ready" and "serve".

### Printed p. 273

वायवा याहि दर्ततेमे सोमा आरंकृताः । (*vāyavā yāhi dartateme somā āraṃkṛtāḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-1)
अरं कृण्वंतु वेदिं समग्निमिंधतां पुरः (*araṃ kṛṇvaṃtu vediṃ samagnimiṃdhatāṃ puraḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-170-4)
In such Ṛks, आरंकृत (*āraṃkṛta*) and आरंकृण्वंतु (*āraṃkṛṇvaṃtu*) give the sense "make ready"; and in
त्वमग्ने प्रविणोदा आरंकृते त्वं देवः सविता रत्नधा असि । (*tvamagne praviṇodā āraṃkṛte tvaṃ devaḥ savitā ratnadhā asi |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1.7)
and similar Ṛks it gives the sense "worship, serve". In the present Ṛk, as in
सोमारुद्रा धारयेथामसुरं प्र वामिष्टयोऽरमश्नुवंतु । ( (*somārudrā dhārayethāmasuraṃ pra vāmiṣṭayo 'ramaśnuvaṃtu | (*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-74-1)
and similar Ṛks where it is used in the same way, it means "sufficient, so as to give satisfaction".

वृजनं न भूम संविव्ये-भूमिं भूतानि वा वृजनमिव । तदिव तव्यथा आवृणोति तथा आयमपि स्वतेजसा सम्यगावृणोति लोकत्रयं । (*vṛjanaṃ na bhūma saṃvivye-bhūmiṃ bhūtāni vā vṛjanamiva | tadiva tavyathā āvṛṇoti tathā āyamapi svatejasā samyagāvṛṇoti lokatrayaṃ |*). The word वृजन (*vṛjana*) is read among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). The comparison is: as strength covers the earth and living beings. Here the word भूम (*bhūma*) is given the sense "earth" or "living beings". The meaning is described thus: as that strength covers the earth and the beings, so Indra covers the three worlds with his splendour.

स्वधावान् अन्नवान् (*svadhāvān annavān*) … or वृष्टिलक्षणोदकवान् वा (*vṛṣṭilakṣaṇodakavān vā*). The word स्वधा (*svadhā*) is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24) and among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). The name is also used in yet other senses. Here the meaning is explained thus: Indra, possessing food and possessing waters in the form of rain, upholds the heavenly world.

Sāyaṇa has explained स्वधावान् (*svadhāvān*) as "possessing food, or possessing water in the form of rain". In some places Sāyaṇa himself explains the word स्वधया (*svadhayā*) in two ways: आत्मीयेन तेजसा; हनिर्लक्षणेन अन्नेन वा (*ātmīyena tejasā; hanirlakṣaṇena annena vā*). Since this is so, and since in the present Ṛk Indra's power is described as surpassing the greatness of heaven and earth, the meaning "possessing splendour" appears the more fitting here. The Nirukta authors have read this word together in the names of water (Ni. 2-23) and in the names of food (Ni. 3-9). In many contexts the word स्वधा (*svadhā*) is explained as one's own greatness, one's own splendour, or one's own support. For example—

### Printed p. 274

शश्वत्पुरोषा व्युवास देव्यथो अद्येदं व्यावो मघोनी । अथो व्युच्छादुत्तरा अनु द्यूनजरामृता चरति स्वधाभिः ॥ (*śaśvatpuroṣā vyuvāsa devyatho adyedaṃ vyāvo maghonī | atho vyucchāduttarā anu dyūnajarāmṛtā carati svadhābhiḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-13)
In this Ṛk the word, used with reference to Ushas, is explained as आत्मीयैस्तेजोभिः (*ātmīyaistejobhiḥ*), "with her own splendours". Likewise in
यदंतरिक्षे पतथः पुरुभुजा यद्वेमे रोदसी अनु । यद्वा स्वधाभिरधितिष्ठथो रथमत आ यातमश्विना ॥ (*yadaṃtarikṣe patathaḥ purubhujā yadveme rodasī anu | yadvā svadhābhiradhitiṣṭhatho rathamata ā yātamaśvinā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-10-6)
the explanation is आत्मीयैस्तेजोभिर्बलैर्वा सार्धं (*ātmīyaistejobhirbalairvā sārdhaṃ*): "together with your own splendours or with your own powers".

In the Ṛk
न मृत्युरासीदमृतं न तर्हि न रात्रा अह्न आसित्प्रकेतः । आनीदवातं स्वथया तवेकं तस्माद्धान्यन्न परः किं चनास ॥ (*na mṛtyurāsīdamṛtaṃ na tarhi na rātrā ahna āsitpraketaḥ | ānīdavātaṃ svathayā tavekaṃ tasmāddhānyanna paraḥ kiṃ canāsa ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-2)
Sāyaṇa has described स्वधा (*svadhā*), with the explanation स्वस्मिन् धीयते ध्रियते आश्रित्य वर्तते इति स्वधा (*svasmin dhīyate dhriyate āśritya vartate iti svadhā*)—"because it depends on itself for support"—as a qualifier of Māyā, the wondrous power of Īśvara (the Supreme Brahman). In the same way, in the present Ṛk too it may be explained that Indra has pervaded all the worlds with his unique, world-protecting splendour, greatness and power. Moreover, in
स्वधामनु श्रियं नशो महि श्लेषा अमवंतो वृषप्सवः । वहंते अह्रुतप्सवः । (*svadhāmanu śriyaṃ naśo mahi śleṣā amavaṃto vṛṣapsavaḥ | vahaṃte ahrutapsavaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-20-7)
वि विद्युतो न वृष्टिभी रुचाना अनु स्वधा मायुधैरच्छमानाः । (*vi vidyuto na vṛṣṭibhī rucānā anu svadhā māyudhairacchamānāḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-13)
and similar Ṛks, where the expressions स्वधां अनु (*svadhāṃ anu*) and अनु स्वधां (*anu svadhāṃ*) occur, the meanings are "naturally", "by nature", "according to custom".

In
अचक्रया यत्स्वधया सुपर्णो हव्यं भरन्मनवे देवजुष्टं । (*acakrayā yatsvadhayā suparṇo havyaṃ bharanmanave devajuṣṭaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-4)
it is explained as "by the chariot", and in
अपश्यं ग्रामं वहमानमारादचक्रया स्वधया वर्तमानं । (*apaśyaṃ grāmaṃ vahamānamārādacakrayā svadhayā vartamānaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-27-19)

### Printed p. 275

and similar places as "by the army". On the whole, it indicates the nature of the thing as "endowed with splendour". It may be said that in the present Ṛk the word स्वधावान् (*svadhāvān*) describes the power of the supremely glorious Indra.

ओपशमिव—ईषदुपशेते इत्योपतं शृंगं तद्वृषभ इव । (*opaśamiva—īṣadupaśete ityopataṃ śṛṃgaṃ tadvṛṣabha iva |*). Because it arises to a small extent, the horn is given as the meaning of the word ओपश (*opaśa*). In regard to Indra's upholding the three worlds, one kind of meaning is explained by comparing him to a bull (ox) that bears effortlessly a horn that has grown to a small extent. In the second meaning: पतस्पतं समीपे वर्तमानं क्षित्यंतरिक्षाख्यं लोकत्वयं तडिव ह्यां बिभर्ति । (*pataspataṃ samīpe vartamānaṃ kṣityaṃtarikṣākhyaṃ lokatvayaṃ taḍiva hyāṃ bibharti |*) **NOTE** लोकत्रयमपि बिभर्तित्यर्थः (*lokatrayamapi bibhartityarthaḥ*). The comparison is: as one upholds the two worlds, well known as earth and atmosphere, which lie close to each other, so Indra upholds the heavenly world. It is thereby made clear that Indra's abundant greatness, by which he effortlessly protects the three worlds, is described.

तोषसी (*toṣasī*)—**NOTE** the word means heaven and earth. As a proper name, the word also denotes in many contexts a person (a female attendant). Hence the word is used both in the singular and in the dual; its meaning is to be taken according to each context. The Nirukta author, citing the Ṛk
उताभये पुरुहूत श्रवोभिरेको दृळहमवदो वृत्रहा सन् । इमे चिदिंद्र रोदसी अपारे यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन् काशिरित्ते ॥ (*utābhaye puruhūta śravobhireko dṛḷahamavado vṛtrahā san | ime cidiṃdra rodasī apāre yatsaṃgṛbhṇā maghavan kāśiritte ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-5)
and stating the nirvacana of the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) there, says
रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य विरोधनात् (*rodasī dyāvāpṛthivya virodhanāt*)
(Ni. 6-1).
It is to be understood that heaven and earth are well known by the name रोदसी (*rodasī*) because they are bound and restrained by a limited boundary (sīmā). This is the nirvacana of the dual form रोदसी (*rodasī*). Again, giving the meaning of the singular form, he explains
कोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि (*kodasī rudrasya patni*)
(Ni. 11-49):
Rodasī is the wife of Rudra; and then cites
रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हुवामहे । आ यस्मिन्तस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥ (*rathaṃ nu mārutaṃ vayaṃ śravasyumā huvāmahe | ā yasmintasthau suraṇāni bibhratī sacā marutsu rodasī ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-56-8).

### Printed p. 276

Citing this Ṛk, he shows that here the proper name Rodasī, "wife of Rudra", is used. But another question arises here. Sāyaṇa has explained in two places in a way that leaves room for doubt: is "wife of Rudra" the wife of the deity Rudra, or does the word Rudra mean Marut, so that she is the wife of the Marut deities? Explaining the present Ṛk, he says
कोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि मरुतां माता । यद्वा रुद्रो वायुः । तत्पत्नी माध्यमिका देवी ॥ (*kodasī rudrasya patni marutāṃ mātā | yadvā rudro vāyuḥ | tatpatnī mādhyamikā devī ‖*)
(Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya).
One meaning may be that Rodasī is the wife of Rudra and the mother of the Maruts. Or, since the word Rudra has the meaning Vāyu, Rodasī is the Mādhyamikā Vāk, the wife of Vāyu: thus he has explained it in two ways. And in explaining the Ṛk
परा शुभ्रा अयासो यव्या साधारण्येव मरुतो मिमिक्षुः । न रोदसी अप नुदंत घोरा जुषंत वृधं सख्याय देवाः ॥ (*parā śubhrā ayāso yavyā sādhāraṇyeva maruto mimikṣuḥ | na rodasī apa nudaṃta ghorā juṣaṃta vṛdhaṃ sakhyāya devāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167-4)
he says, as stated earlier,
रोदसा शब्देन रोदनस्वभावो रुद्रः । तस्य स्त्री रोदसीति केचिदाहुः । आदरे तु मरुतां स्त्रीयो रोदसीति नामधेयमित्याहुः । अयमेव पक्षो युक्त उत्तरत्रैवं व्यवहारात् । (*rodasā śabdena rodanasvabhāvo rudraḥ | tasya strī rodasīti kecidāhuḥ | ādare tu marutāṃ strīyo rodasīti nāmadheyamityāhuḥ | ayameva pakṣo yukta uttaratraivaṃ vyavahārāt |*).
That Rodasī is the wife of Rudra is one view; that she is the wife of the Maruts is another. Of these, the second appears to be the correct one: thus he has stated his own opinion. Besides, in explaining the Ṛk
जोषद्यदीमसुर्य्या सचध्यै विषितस्तुका रोदसी नृमणाः ॥ (*joṣadyadīmasuryyā sacadhyai viṣitastukā rodasī nṛmaṇāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167-5)
he has stated रोदसी मरुत्पत्नी विद्युद्वा (*rodasī marutpatnī vidyudvā*): Rodasī is the wife of the Maruts, or lightning is known by this name; and he has cited the subject described there, that this Rodasī is in the following of the Maruts. And if we examine some further contexts in which the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is used,
त इदुग्राः तवसा धृष्णुषेणा उभे युजंत रोदसी सुमेके । अथ स्मैषु रोदसी स्वशोचिरामवत्सु तस्थौ न रोकः ॥ (*ta idugrāḥ tavasā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇā ubhe yujaṃta rodasī sumeke | atha smaiṣu rodasī svaśocirāmavatsu tasthau na rokaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-66-6)
in this one Ṛk the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is used in two senses. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the first occurrence as व्यावापृथिव्य (*vyāvāpṛthivya*) and the second as रुद्रस्य पत्नि माध्यमिकी वाक्य (*rudrasya patni mādhyamikī vākya*). And,

### Printed p. 277
and,

मिम्मक्ष येषु रोदसी नु देवी सिषक्ति पूषा अभ्यर्धयज्वा । श्रुत्वा हवं मरुतो यद्ध याथ भूमा रेजंते अध्वनि प्रविक्ते ॥ (*mimmakṣa yeṣu rodasī nu devī siṣakti pūṣā abhyardhayajvā | śrutvā havaṃ maruto yaddha yātha bhūmā rejaṃte adhvani pravikte ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-50-5).

Here too, देवी (*devī*) is explained as the shining speech of the middle region (the thunder). Giving the explanation of Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167-3, the scholar Max Muller describes the word रोदसी (*rodasī*), used in the senses of lightning, the speech of the middle region, and heaven-and-earth, as follows.

In our verse, we take वाक् (*vāk*) in the sense of thunder, but as a
feminine, of the lightning and thunder as the two companions of
the Maruts, represents the first, रोदसी (*rodasī*) or lightning, as the
recognised wife, hiding herself in the house, while the other, the
loud thunder, is represented as a more public companion of
the Maurts. This contrast, if it is really what the poet intended,
throws a curious light on the social character of the Vedic times,
as it presupposes two classes of wives, not necessarily simultanious,
however—, a house wife, who stays at home and is not much seen,
and a wife who appears in public and takes part in the society........
The loud voice of the thuuder as well as the usual hiding of the
lightning might well suggest this comparison.
[S. B. E. XXXII P. 276]

Pointing out in this way the difference between the singular and the dual use, the Bṛhaddevatā says:

रोदसी देवपत्नीनां अथर्वांगिरसे यथा । (*rodasī devapatnīnāṃ atharvāṃgirase yathā |*) (Bṛ. De. 2-143)

Here is an example of the singular use: according to the view of the Atharvāṅgirasa (Atharvaveda), Rodasī is one of the wives of the gods. And,

द्वे द्वे पदे संस्तुते रोदसी च देवाश्चार्थर्चेन विभक्तमन्यत् । (*dve dve pade saṃstute rodasī ca devāścārtharcena vibhaktamanyat |*) (Bṛ. De. 4-6)

In all such places where the dual is used, heaven and earth are meant.

##### Grammar

- महिना — मह पूजायां धातुः । इन् सर्वधातुभ्यः इति इन् प्रत्ययः । तृतीया एकवचनांतरूपं । व्यत्ययेन विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।

### Printed p. 278
- आस्ति — यद्योगात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । तिप् पित्त्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- अरम् — नालमूललघु-(पा. म. ८-२-१८) इति लकारस्य रेफादेशः ।
- विव्ये — वी गत्यादिषु धातुः । छंदसि लुज्लज्लिटः इति वर्तमानार्थे लिट् । प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- वृजनम् — वृजी वर्जने धातुः । अत्र कर्तर्यर्थे प्रयुक्तः । कृष्यवृजिमंदि—(उ. सू. २-२३९) इति क्यु प्रत्ययः । युवोरनाकौ (पा सू. ७-१-१) इति तस्य अनादेशः । कित्त्वात् लघूपधगुणः न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- भर्ति — भृञ् भरणे धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने तिप् । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपः लुक् । सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः इति इकः गुणः । र परत्वेन भवति । पादादौ इति निघातस्वरः न भवति । तिप् पित्त्वात् अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- स्वधावान् — माधुपधायाश्च—इति मतुपः मकारस्य वत्वं । दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा.सू. ८-३-९) इति नकारस्य रुत्वं । आतोटि नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-३-३) इति सूत्रेण नित्यं आकारस्य अनुनासिकत्वं भवति ।
- ओपशम् — शीञ् स्वप्ने धातुः । आज्, उप, द्वौ उपसर्गौ उपपदत्वे बहुलग्रहणात् अस्मात् ड प्रत्ययः । डित्त्वात् टिलोपः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ॥ ६ ॥

#### Ṛk 7

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing Indra as शूर (*śūra*), Sāyaṇa says: in battles (समत्सु (*samatsu*)) you cause very abundant strength and the like (उरूणि अतिप्रभूतानि बलादीनि (*urūṇi atiprabhūtāni balādīni*)) for the creatures who live relying on you; you are प्रपथिंतमं (*prapathiṃtamaṃ*), the best of paths for the virtuous, and Indra, the render of enemies. The Maruts, here called क्षोणीः (*kṣoṇīḥ*) (his retinue, the people) and सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*) (serving together, or of equal affection), strive to adorn you (परितंसयध्यै (*paritaṃsayadhyai*): to make you an ornament, or to decorate you) and for your exhilaration (मदे (*made*)). Who are they? Those who (ये (*ye*)) with their strengths (वाजैः (*vājaiḥ*)) gladden you favourably (अनुमदंति (*anumadaṃti*)): in battle the Maruts, making him alone their lord, delight him. Alternatively: the sacrificers who gladden you with oblations (वाजैः (*vājaiḥ*)), united in affection, being your human priests and sacrificers, your subjects, strive in the sacrifices (समत्सु (*samatsu*), places of joint rejoicing) to honour you, who have the stated qualities, and for your exhilaration.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे शूर (*he śūra*)—O heroic Indra
- ये (*ye*)—which Marut gods
- वाजैः (*vājaiḥ*)—with their own strength
- सूरिं चित् (*sūriṃ cit*)—you, the wise one
- अनु मदंति (*anu madaṃti*)—follow (so as to be favourable to you) and cause delight
- ते (*te*)—those
- क्षोणीः (*kṣoṇīḥ*)—the retinue (Maruts)
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—serving together
- समत्सु (*samatsu*)—in battles
- सतां (*satāṃ*)—for the creatures who rely on you
- उराणं (*urāṇaṃ*)—the giver of abundant strength
- प्रपथिंतमं (*prapathiṃtamaṃ*)—the best path (for the doers of good deeds)
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the destroyer of enemies
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- परितंसयध्यॆ (*paritaṃsayadhyè*)—to adorn (and)
- मदे (*made*)—for your delight (they strive)
- Or: हे शूर (*he śūra*)—O heroic Indra; ये (*ye*)—which sacrificers; वाजैः (*vājaiḥ*)—with oblations and the like; सूरिं, चित् (*sūriṃ, cit*)—you, the wise one; अनु मदंति (*anu madaṃti*)—gladden; ते (*te*)—those; क्षोणीः (*kṣoṇīḥ*)—the sacrificers, who are like the retinue; सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—of equal affection; सतां उराणं (*satāṃ urāṇaṃ*)—the strength-giver to those who rely on you; प्रपथिंतमं (*prapathiṃtamaṃ*)—the best path; इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the destroyer of enemies; त्वा (*tvā*)—you; परितंसयध्यॆ (*paritaṃsayadhyè*)—in order to worship; and मदे (*made*)—for your delight; समत्सु (*samatsu*)—in sacrifices, the places of delight (they strive).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O heroic Indra, you who give strength to those who rely on you, are the best path for the doers of good deeds, and destroy enemies: the Maruts (or the sacrificers) strive with their own strength to worship you and to delight you.

### Printed p. 280

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Those people, who, jointly worshipping Indra, diligently endeavour,
O hero, to propitiate you, the invigorator in combats, the guide in the
rightway : provide, for his gratification, with sacrificial viands.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the unique help of the Maruts, who always give and will give Indra help in times of battle, is described. In the same way it is also explained how the sacrificers who perform sacrifices strive to worship Indra in the sacrifices.

समत्सु सतां उराणं (*samatsu satāṃ urāṇaṃ*)—Here Indra is addressed by the word शूर (*śūra*), and the meaning is explained thus: in times of battle Indra graciously grants that even the creatures who rely on him obtain surpassing ability and the like (उरूणि अतिप्रभूतानि बलादीनि कुर्वाणं (*urūṇi atiprabhūtāni balādīni kurvāṇaṃ*)). The word समत्सु (*samatsu*) is listed among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). And the Nirukta author, giving the derivation of this word, states the alternatives:

समहः समदो वात्तॆः; संमदो वा मदतेः । (*samahaḥ samado vāttèḥ; saṃmado vā madateḥ |*) (Ni. 9-17)

That is, the prefix सम् (*sam*) joined with the root अद् (*ad*) may become समद् (*samad*); or the prefix सम् (*sam*) joined with the root मद् (*mad*), meaning to be excited, to be roused with ardour, may become समद् (*samad*). He cites the Ṛk in which the word समत्सु (*samatsu*) is used,

आ जंघंति सान्वेषां जघना उप जिघ्नते । अश्वाजनि प्रचेतसोऽश्वान्समत्तु चोदय ॥ (*ā jaṃghaṃti sānveṣāṃ jaghanā upa jighnate | aśvājani pracetaso 'śvānsamattu codaya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-13)

and explains there the special sense of this word.

प्रपंचितमं—सुकृतिनामुत्तममार्गभूतं (*prapaṃcitamaṃ—sukṛtināmuttamamārgabhūtaṃ*): since Indra shows the best path to the virtuous, he is stated, by the identification of cause and effect, to be the best path itself.

इंद्रं-शत्रुणां दारकं (*iṃdraṃ-śatruṇāṃ dārakaṃ*): the Nirukta authors derive the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) in many ways. Of these Sāyaṇa follows इंदर् शत्रुणां दारयिता (*iṃdar śatruṇāṃ dārayitā*) (Ni. 10-8), "Indra is the one who splits enemies", and so describes him here as the destroyer of enemies.

### Printed p. 281
सजोषसः क्षोणीः—सह सेवमानाः समानप्रीतयो ना क्षोण्यो विशः परिजनाः । (*sajoṣasaḥ kṣoṇīḥ—saha sevamānāḥ samānaprītayo nā kṣoṇyo viśaḥ parijanāḥ |*) These two words are derived and explained as epithets of the Maruts. Although the Maruts are many (एकोन पंचाशत्संख्याकाः (*ekona paṃcāśatsaṃkhyākāḥ*)—forty-nine persons), they are in affection through unity among themselves, or all of them serve Indra with one and the same affection; and though they are like Indra's friends, they are like subjects. This is the meaning explained.

ये वाजैः अनु मदंति (*ye vājaiḥ anu madaṃti*)—This sentence is explained in two ways, with regard to the Maruts and with regard to the sacrificers. First: मरुतस्तमेव स्वामिनं कृत्वा संग्रामे बलैः हर्षयंति । (*marutastameva svāminaṃ kṛtvā saṃgrāme balaiḥ harṣayaṃti |*) The Maruts, knowing Indra alone as lord, delight him in times of battle with their strength. In this sense the word वाज (*vāja*) is used in the meaning of strength. Yāska lists the word वाज (*vāja*) among the names of food (Ni. 3-9), among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9), and as the name of a person (Ni. 11-17), and on the Ṛk

सावका नः स्वरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः । (*sāvakā naḥ svarasvatī vājebhirvājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-10)

he explains the meaning as oblations or water (हविषोदकेन (*haviṣodakena*)).**NOTE**

Second: ये यजमानाः (*ye yajamānāḥ*), the sacrificers who perform sacrifices, वाजैः हविर्भिर्मादयंति ते समानप्रितियुक्ताः तव मनुष्यभूता ऋत्विजः यजमानभूताः प्रजाः समत्तु सहमादनस्थानेषु यागेषु उक्तलक्षणविशिष्टं त्वामेव पूजयितुं तव मादाय च प्रयतंते । (*vājaiḥ havirbhirmādayaṃti te samānapritiyuktāḥ tava manuṣyabhūtā ṛtvijaḥ yajamānabhūtāḥ prajāḥ samattu sahamādanasthāneṣu yāgeṣu uktalakṣaṇaviśiṣṭaṃ tvāmeva pūjayituṃ tava mādāya ca prayataṃte |*) United in a single affection towards Indra, they delight him with oblations. Being in human form both priests and sacrificers, Indra's subjects, in the sacrifices, which are occasions that cause delight to Indra and to themselves, they worship Indra, who is endowed with abundant greatness, and strive to cause him delight. This is the meaning explained.

The word समत्सु (*samatsu*) is listed among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Here Sāyaṇa takes the word in the sense of सहमादनस्थानेषु यागेषु (*sahamādanasthāneṣu yāgeṣu*), the sacrifice, an occasion which increases exhilaration in all at one time, and so explains the meaning.

Sāyaṇa has not explained the word सूरिंजित् (*sūriṃjit*) in this Ṛk.

सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—the Nirukta authors read this word among the 13 names of praisers, रेभः, जरिता, कारुः (*rebhaḥ, jaritā, kāruḥ*) and so on (Ni. 3-19). सूरि (*sūri*) may mean the devotee who praises, or it may mean wise, discerning, intelligent. When it is used as an epithet of the seers who have the supernatural power of vision, both of the eye and of the mind, which grasps the true natures of the gods and the secret principles of the universe,

### Printed p. 282
the word has a special sense.

तद्विष्टो ४ पॆरमं पवं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः । (*tadviṣṭo 4 pèramaṃ pavaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-20)

In such contexts it does not merely mean those who praise, but also indicates the seers' extraordinary power of vision. And it is used as an epithet not only of seers but also of the gods, Indra and others.

मंहिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै । (*maṃhiṣṭhamacchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ vāvṛdhadhyai |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-81-3)

In Ṛks such as this, with विपश्चितमिंद्रं (*vipaścitamiṃdraṃ*), it shows the wisdom of the gods, Indra and others. Besides, the word सूरि (*sūri*) is also used when the meaning lord, impeller, or leader on the good path is indicated. And as examples,

जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवानश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः । (*jano yaḥ pajrebhyo vājinīvānaśvāvato rathino mahyaṃ sūriḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-8)

असद्यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिंद्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता । (*asadyathā jaritra uta sūririṃdro rāyo viśvavārasya dātā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-23-10)

मुह्यंत्वन्ये अभितो जनास इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु । (*muhyaṃtvanye abhito janāsa ihāsmākaṃ maghavā sūrirastu |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-81-6)

In these and similar contexts this epithet is applied to gods who are lords and leaders on the good path, and describes their quality.

आदस्य ते कृष्णासो दक्षि सूरयः शूरस्येव श्वेषथादीषते वयः । (*ādasya te kṛṣṇāso dakṣi sūrayaḥ śūrasyeva śveṣathādīṣate vayaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-141-8)

In such contexts it also gives the meaning of path. In the present Ṛk it may be explained as wise or lord.

सजोषसः क्षोणीः (*sajoṣasaḥ kṣoṇīḥ*)—"those of equal affection" and "those who are like retinue" indicate the eternal and close relationship between Indra and the Maruts. This relationship was explained earlier in this same volume, in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-171-4. It is because of such companionship that, on all occasions when Indra accompanied by the Maruts is addressed, Indra is called मरुत्वान् (*marutvān*); so the Bṛhaddevatā explains this epithet that indicates the relationship of these deities.

मरुद्भिः सह यत्रेंद्रो मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् । (*marudbhiḥ saha yatreṃdro marutvāṃstatra so 'bhavat |*) (Bṛ. De. 4-56)

### Printed p. 283
By sentences of this kind the fellowship of the Maruts and Indra in joy is shown. The word क्षोणीः (*kṣoṇīḥ*) is explained as "people" (निशः (*niśaḥ*)). Passages of the Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas, which show the relation that Indra is the lord and the Maruts are the subjects, were also cited earlier in the Special Topics on Ṛk 1-171-4.

##### Grammar

- सताम्—षष्ठी बहुवचनांतरूपम् । शतुरनुमोनद्यजादी (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- प्रपथिन्तमम्—अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ इति तमप् प्रत्ययः । पित्त्वात् अनुदात्तः भवति ।
- परितंसयध्ये—परि उपसर्गः । तसि अलंकारे इति धातुः । चुरादिः । सत्यापपाश— (पा. सू. ३-१-२५) इति स्वार्थे णिच् । इदितो नुम् धातोः (पा. सू. ७-१-५८) इति नुमागमः । अस्मात् तुमनर्थे विवक्षिते तुमनर्थे सेसेनसे— (पा. सू. ३-४-९) इति अध्यै प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । एजंतकृदंतत्वात् अव्ययसंज्ञा भवति ।
- सजोषसः—समानं जोषः येषां ते सजोषसः । समानस्य छंदस्य— इति समानशब्दस्य स भावः ।
- अनुमदंति—मद तृप्तियोगे इति धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधः भवति । तिजिचोदात्तवति (पा. सू. ८-१-७१) इति गतेः (अनु) निघातस्वरः भवति । ॥ ७ ॥

> विश्वा॑ ते॒ अनु॒ जोष्या॑ भू॒द्गौः सू॒रींश्चि॒द्यदि॑ धि॒षा वेषि॒ जना॑न् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र एवा ह्येवं हि सति ते तव संबंधीनि सवनानि । सूयते
> सोमोऽत्रेति सवनानि सोमयागाः । ते शं सुखकरा भवंति । कथं सति । यद्यदि
> देवीर्देवो द्योतमाना आपः समुद्र उदकसमुद्रवणापादानभूतेऽंतरिक्ष
> आसु प्रजासु निमित्त भूतासु ते त्वां मदंति मादयंति ॥ अंतर्भावितण्यर्थोऽयं ॥
> यदा प्राण्युपकारार्थं वर्षणाय त्वां प्रेरयंति वृष्टुदकानि तदा खलु तव
> सोमयागा। सुखकरा भवंति यज्ञसाधनवृष्टिप्रदानेन यागान्निर्वर्तयेत्यर्थः ।
> किंच हे इंद्र विश्वा गौः सर्वापि स्तोत्रशस्त्ररूपा वाक्ते त्वामनुक्रमेण जोष्या
> जोषणार्हा प्रीणयित्रि भूत् । भवति । कदा । यदि सूरींत्चित् स्तोत्रादिप्रेरयित्थन् स्तोतृजनानपि धिषा धिषणया प्रज्ञया वृष्टिप्रदानरूपेण कर्मणा
> ना वेषि कामयसे तदा सर्वापि स्तुतिस्त्वदर्था भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, this being so, your Soma sacrifices (सवनानि (*savanāni*), so called because Soma is pressed in them) become pleasant to you. How? If the divine, shining waters in the ocean—that is, in the atmosphere, the place from which water is drawn like an ocean—gladden you for the sake of these creatures. The verb here has an inner causative sense. When the rain-waters urge you to rain for the benefit of living beings, then your Soma sacrifices become pleasant: the meaning is that, by giving rain, the means of sacrifice, you should bring the sacrifices to completion. Further, O Indra, all speech, in the form of stotra and śastra, becomes in due order fit to be loved by you and pleasing to you. When? When, by understanding (धिषा (*dhiṣā*)), that is by the act of giving rain, you favour even the sages who urge on the praises, the singers; then every praise comes to be for your sake.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*) (hey)—O Indra
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—shining (divine)
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters
- समुद्रे (*samudre*)—in the atmosphere
- आसु (*āsu*)—with regard to the creatures
- ते (*te*)—to you
- यत् मदंति (*yat madaṃti*)—if they give delight
- एवा हि (*evā hi*)—if so
- ते (*te*)—your
- सवना (*savanā*)—Soma sacrifices
- शं (*śaṃ*)—(to you) become pleasant (and)
- यदि (*yadi*)—when
- सूरीन् चित् (*sūrīn cit*)—those who urge on the praises and so on
- धिषा (*dhiṣā*)—with knowledge (by the act of giving rain)
- वेषि (*veṣi*)—you desire
- (तदा (*tadā*)—then)
- विश्वा गौः (*viśvā gauḥ*)—all speech in the form of stotra and śastra
- अनु (*anu*)—in due order
- ते (*te*)—to you
- जोष्या (*joṣyā*)—pleasing
- भूत् (*bhūt*)—becomes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when the rain-waters urge you to rain for the benefit of living beings, the Soma sacrifices become pleasant to you; and only after the hymns have received understanding from you do all the praises, in the form of stotra and śastra, reach you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The libations (offered) to you are, verily, the cause of happiness, since the divine waters (effused) in the firmament for the benefit of mankind

### Printed p. 285
afford you satisfaction. All praise, Indra, is acceptable to you, and you reward with understanding those who praise you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सवना (*savanā*)—सूयते सोमः अत्रेति सवनानि सोमयागाः । (*sūyate somaḥ atreti savanāni somayāgāḥ |*) The word सवन (*savana*) is listed among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19).

एता विश्वा सवना तूतुमाकृषे स्वयं सूनो सहसो यानि दधिषे । वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मंत्रो ब्रह्मोद्यतं वचः । (*etā viśvā savanā tūtumākṛṣe svayaṃ sūno sahaso yāni dadhiṣe | varāya te pātraṃ dharmaṇe tanā yajño maṃtro brahmodyataṃ vacaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-50-6).

In this Ṛk the word सवना (*savanā*) is explained as meaning स्थानानि (*sthānāni*). Here it is described that the word सवन (*savana*) means the Soma sacrifices, the occasions on which the Soma juice is pressed.

By the word सवन (*savana*) here are indicated the pre-eminence of the sacrifice, which establishes a mutual relation between earth and atmosphere, and the relation between the sacrifice and Indra, who is the lord of this sacrifice, is satisfied by it, and therefore bestows favour on the world. It is also indicated that the savana is the chief means of the well-being and peace of both earth and atmosphere.

The meaning of the word सवन (*savana*) is very deep; it reflects the principle of the universe. Just as the sacrifice has the division into the three savanas, so the Śruti passages describe that the affairs of the universe too have divisions following this one; that every individual life too has three stages corresponding to the three savanas; and that the creation of the Brāhmaṇa and the other castes also follows this division. Moreover, all the Śrutis explain that the deities Indra and the rest, who preside over the three savanas, themselves regulate the divisions of the universal principle and reflect them. Each savana too indicates its presiding deity, its metre and its act of creation. Only about the deity of the third savana is there disagreement in the Śruti itself.

About the greatness of the savana the Taittirīya Saṃhitā speaks thus:

प्रजापतिर्नाव ज्येष्ठस्स ह्येते नाग्रेयजत प्रजापतिरकामयत प्रजायेयेति स मुखतस्त्रिवृतं निरमिमीत तमग्निर्देवतान्नसृज्यत गायत्री छंदो रथंतरग्‌ंसाम ब्राह्मणो मनुष्याणामजः पशूनां तस्मात्ते मुख्या मुखतो ह्यसृज्यंतोरसो बाहुब्यां पंचदशं निरमिमीत तमिंद्रो देवतान्नसृज्यत त्रिष्टुप्‌ छंदो बृहत्साम राजन्यो मनुष्याणामविः पशूनां तस्मात्ते वीर्यावंतो वीर्याद्दस्यृज्यंत मध्यतस्स- (*prajāpatirnāva jyeṣṭhassa hyete nāgreyajata prajāpatirakāmayata prajāyeyeti sa mukhatastrivṛtaṃ niramimīta tamagnirdevatānnasṛjyata gāyatrī chaṃdo rathaṃtaragṃsāma brāhmaṇo manuṣyāṇāmajaḥ paśūnāṃ tasmātte mukhyā mukhato hyasṛjyaṃtoraso bāhubyāṃ paṃcadaśaṃ niramimīta tamiṃdro devatānnasṛjyata triṣṭup chaṃdo bṛhatsāma rājanyo manuṣyāṇāmaviḥ paśūnāṃ tasmātte vīryāvaṃto vīryāddasyṛjyaṃta madhyatassa-*)

### Printed p. 286
प्रदशं निरमिमित तं विश्वे देवा देवता अन्वसृज्यंत जगतीछंदो वैरूपग्ं साम वैश्यो मनुष्याणां गावः पशूनां तस्मात्त आद्या अन्नधानाद्य सृज्यंत तस्माद्भूयाग्ंसोन्येभ्यो भूयिष्ठा हि देवता अन्वसृज्यंत पत्त एकविगंशं निरमिमित ॥ (*pradaśaṃ niramimita taṃ viśve devā devatā anvasṛjyaṃta jagatīchaṃdo vairūpagṃ sāma vaiśyo manuṣyāṇāṃ gāvaḥ paśūnāṃ tasmātta ādyā annadhānādya sṛjyaṃta tasmādbhūyāgṃsonyebhyo bhūyiṣṭhā hi devatā anvasṛjyaṃta patta ekavigaṃśaṃ niramimita ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-14, 5).

Because he performed the sacrifice at the beginning, Prajāpati is the eldest. Desiring to create, he poured forth the trivṛt stoma from his mouth. From it arose, among deities, Agni; among metres, Gāyatrī; among sāmans, Rathantara; among men, the Brāhmaṇa; among animals, the goat. When he poured forth the pañcadaśa stoma from his arm, there arose among deities Indra; among metres Triṣṭup; among sāmans Bṛhat; among men the Rājanya; among animals the sheep. When he poured forth the saptadaśa stoma from the middle, there arose among deities the Viśvedevas; among metres Jagatī; among sāmans the cow.

Following this order, in the Soma sacrifice the offering of the morning savana is addressed to Agni, that of the midday savana to Indra, and that of the third savana to the Viśvedevas. As stated in the Atharvaveda, the morning savana is assigned to the Aśvins, the midday savana to Indra and Agni, and the third savana to the Ṛbhus (Atha. Ve. 9-1-2). As stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, the third savana belongs to the Ṛbhus; it is called Ārbhava Pavamāna. There is a legend about the Ṛbhus' qualification to receive the oblation in the sacrifice together with the gods. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa narrates it thus:

ऋभवो वै देवेषु तपसा सोमपीथमभ्यजयंस्तेभ्यः प्रातःसवने वाचि कल्पयिषंस्तानग्निर्वसुभिः प्रातस्सवनादनुदत । (*ṛbhavo vai deveṣu tapasā somapīthamabhyajayaṃstebhyaḥ prātaḥsavane vāci kalpayiṣaṃstānagnirvasubhiḥ prātassavanādanudata |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-6).

By their supernatural power of action the Ṛbhus attained the place of the gods. When the gods then prepared to take them along with themselves to the drinking of Soma, Agni, joining with the Vasus, drove them away.

तेभ्यो माध्यंदिने सवने वाचि कल्पयिसंस्तानिंद्रो रुद्रैर्माध्यंदिनात्सवनादनुडत । (*tebhyo mādhyaṃdine savane vāci kalpayisaṃstāniṃdro rudrairmādhyaṃdinātsavanādanuḍata |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-6).

Later, when the gods prepared to make room for them at the midday savana, Indra, joining with the Rudras, drove them away.

### Printed p. 287
तेभ्यस्तृतीयसवने वाचि कल्पयिषंस्तान्विश्वेदेवाः अनोनुद्यंत नेह पास्यंति नेहेति स प्रजापतिरब्रवीत्सवितारं तव वा इमेऽंतेवासास्त्वमेवैभिः संपिबस्वेति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्सविता तान्वै त्वमुभयतः परिपिबेति तान्प्रजापतिरुभयतः पर्यपिबत् ॥ (*tebhyastṛtīyasavane vāci kalpayiṣaṃstānviśvedevāḥ anonudyaṃta neha pāsyaṃti neheti sa prajāpatirabravītsavitāraṃ tava vā ime 'ṃtevāsāstvamevaibhiḥ saṃpibasveti sa tathetyabravītsavitā tānvai tvamubhayataḥ paripibeti tānprajāpatirubhayataḥ paryapibat ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 6-13).

At the time of the third savana, when the Viśvedevas did not admit them, Prajāpati said to Savitṛ, "These are your pupils; drink together with them"; and Savitṛ and Prajāpati drank along with the Ṛbhus. Thus the place of the Ṛbhus in the third savana is shown. As said in another place of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

प्रजापतिर्नै यज्ञं छंदांसि देवोभ्यो भागधेयानि व्यभजत्स गायत्रीमेवाग्नये वसुभ्यः प्रातःसवनेऽभजत्रिष्टुभमिंद्राय रुद्रॆभ्यो मध्यंदिने जगतीं विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्य आदित्येभ्यस्तृतीयसवने ॥ (*prajāpatirnai yajñaṃ chaṃdāṃsi devobhyo bhāgadheyāni vyabhajatsa gāyatrīmevāgnaye vasubhyaḥ prātaḥsavane 'bhajatriṣṭubhamiṃdrāya rudrèbhyo madhyaṃdine jagatīṃ viśvebhyo devebhya ādityebhyastṛtīyasavane ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 12-2).

Prajāpati divided the sacrificial shares and the metres among the gods. In the morning savana he gave Gāyatrī to Agni and the Vasus; in the midday savana Triṣṭup to Indra and the Rudras (the Maruts?); and in the third savana Jagatī to the Viśvedevas and the Ādityas.

Since Agni reflects Brahmanical radiance, Indra the Kṣatriya power, and the Viśvedevas the Vaiśya activity, it is understood from the passages of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā cited above that the distinctions of caste in creation also follow these divisions of the savana. The Chāndogya Upaniṣad, explaining the same division from the spiritual point of view, says:

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति यद्वसूनां प्रातःसवनं रुद्राणां माध्यंदिनं सवनमादित्यानां च विश्वेषां च देवानां तृतीयसवनं ॥ (*brahmavādino vadaṃti yadvasūnāṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ rudrāṇāṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanamādityānāṃ ca viśveṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ ‖*) (Bhā. U. 2-24-1).

It is told that the morning savana is allotted to the Vasus, the midday savana to the Rudras, and the third savana to the Ādityas and the Viśvedevas; and the special mantras to be recited at the times of these savanas are given. From these mantras it is understood that excellent places in earth, atmosphere and heaven are obtained by the offerings made in these savanas.

लोकद्वारमपावार्णा पश्येम त्वा वयं............अथ जुहोति नमोऽग्नये पृथिविक्षिते लोकक्षिते लोकं मे यजमानाय विंदैष वै यजमानस्य लोक एतास्मि ॥ (*lokadvāramapāvārṇā paśyema tvā vayaṃ............atha juhoti namo 'gnaye pṛthivikṣite lokakṣite lokaṃ me yajamānāya viṃdaiṣa vai yajamānasya loka etāsmi ‖*) (Chā. U. 2-24).

### Printed p. 288
Before the morning savana, addressing the Vasus, one prays: "Open the door to the entrance of your world; may we too obtain your sight"; and offering the oblation to Agni one becomes fit to obtain the excellent place in the world of earth. In the same way, praying to the Rudras and the Ādityas and offering oblations to them in the midday and third savanas, one becomes fit for the excellent place in the atmosphere and in heaven. Thus the greatness of the three savanas and the fruit of serving them are described. Moreover, the whole consciousness of man is described as a reflection of the Soma sacrifice, as stated below.

पुरुषो वाव यज्ञस्तस्य यानि चतुर्विंशतिवर्षाणि तत्प्रातःसवनं चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रं प्रातःसवनं तदस्य वसवोऽन्वायत्ताः प्राणा नाव वसव एते हीदं सर्वं वासयंति ॥ (*puruṣo vāva yajñastasya yāni caturviṃśativarṣāṇi tatprātaḥsavanaṃ caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ tadasya vasavo 'nvāyattāḥ prāṇā nāva vasava ete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vāsayaṃti ‖*) (Bhā. U. 3-16-1).

Man is the sacrifice. Since the Gāyatrī metre, of twenty-four syllables, is the metre of the morning savana, the first twenty-four years of man are the morning savana. The Vasus are the presiding deities of this offering; the vital breaths are the Vasus. Those breaths are the means of dwelling on earth.

तं चेदेतस्मिन्वयसि किंचिदुपतपेत्स ब्रूयात्माना वसव इदं मे प्रातःसवनं माध्यंदिनं सवनमनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानां वसूनां मध्यॆ यज्ञो विलोप्सियेत्युद्धैव तत एत्यगदो ह भवति ॥ (*taṃ cedetasminvayasi kiṃcidupatapetsa brūyātmānā vasava idaṃ me prātaḥsavanaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanamanusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ vasūnāṃ madhyè yajño vilopsiyetyuddhaiva tata etyagado ha bhavati ‖*) (Bhā. U. 3-16-2).

If in the course of these twenty-four years the body suffers any weakness, then, if one prays to the Vasus: "O breaths (Vasus), the means of dwelling, let this morning savana of mine not be cut off in the middle, but carry me on to the midday savana; let this sacrifice of my life not be broken off", the man is freed from the weakness.

अथ यानि चतुर्विंशद्वर्षाणि तन्नाध्यंदिनं सवनं चतुश्चत्वांशदक्षरा त्रिष्टुप् त्रैष्टुभं माध्यंदिनं सवनं तदस्य रुद्रा अन्वायत्ताः प्राणा नाव रुद्रा एते हीदं सर्वं रोदयंति । (*atha yāni caturviṃśadvarṣāṇi tannādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ catuścatvāṃśadakṣarā triṣṭup traiṣṭubhaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ tadasya rudrā anvāyattāḥ prāṇā nāva rudrā ete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ rodayaṃti |*) (Bhā. 3-16-3)

The Triṣṭup metre has forty-four syllables; Triṣṭup is the metre of the midday savana. Therefore the next forty-four years, the second stage of man, form the midday savana in the sacrifice of life. The Rudras preside over it. Since, when the breath departs, they make everyone weep, these breaths are the Rudras.
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 289
If anything afflicts him at this age, let him say: "O Prāṇas, O Rudras, may this my midday pressing carry me on to the third pressing; let me, the sacrifice, not be cut off in the midst of the Prāṇas, the Rudras." He then recovers from it and becomes free of illness. तं चेहेतस्मिन्वयसि किंचिदुपतपेत्स ब्रूयात् प्राणा रुद्रा इदं मे माध्यंदिनं सवनं तृतीयसवनमनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानां रुद्राणां मध्यॆ यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेत्युद्धैव तत एत्यगदो ह भवति । (*taṃ cehetasminvayasi kiṃcidupatapetsa brūyāt prāṇā rudrā idaṃ me mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ tṛtīyasavanamanusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ madhyè yajño vilopsīyetyuddhaiva tata etyagado ha bhavati |*) (Chā. U. 3-16-4)

If, during these forty-four years that make up the midday pressing, any bodily weariness comes upon a man, he should then address the Rudras: "O Rudras, who are of the nature of the vital breaths, may this my midday pressing carry me on until the third pressing. May my life-sacrifice not be broken off in the middle." If he prays thus, the man is freed from the weariness.

Then the forty-eight years are the third pressing. The jagatī has forty-eight syllables, and the third pressing belongs to the jagatī. The Ādityas depend upon it. The Prāṇas are the Ādityas, for they take up all this to themselves. अथ यान्यष्टाचत्वारिंशद्वर्षाणि तत्तृतीय सवनमष्टाचत्वारिंशदक्षरा जगती बागतं तृतीयसवनं तदस्यादित्या अन्वायत्ताः प्राणा नावादित्या एते हीदं सर्ववाददते । (*atha yānyaṣṭācatvāriṃśadvarṣāṇi tattṛtīya savanamaṣṭācatvāriṃśadakṣarā jagatī bāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ tadasyādityā anvāyattāḥ prāṇā nāvādityā ete hīdaṃ sarvavādadate |*) (Bhā. U. 3-16-5)**NOTE**

The jagatī of forty-eight syllables is the metre of the third pressing; therefore the last forty-eight years of a man's life are of the nature of the evening pressing. Since at the time of the release of the vital breaths they draw everything into themselves, the Prāṇas are of the form of the Ādityas. And the Prāṇas, of the nature of the Ādityas, are the presiding deities of this third pressing.

If at this age anything afflicts him, let him say: "O Prāṇas, O Ādityas, may this my third pressing extend my life; let me, the sacrifice, not be cut off in the midst of the Prāṇas, the Ādityas." He then recovers and becomes free of illness. तं चेदेतस्मिन्वयसि किंचिदुपतपेत्स ब्रूयात्पाणा आदित्या इदं मे तृतीयसवनमायुरनु संतनोतीति माहं प्राणानामादित्यानां मध्ये यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेत्युद्धैव तत एत्यगदो हैव भवति. (*taṃ cedetasminvayasi kiṃcidupatapetsa brūyātpāṇā ādityā idaṃ me tṛtīyasavanamāyuranu saṃtanotīti māhaṃ prāṇānāmādityānāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyetyuddhaiva tata etyagado haiva bhavati.*) (Bhā. U. 3-16-6)

If weariness arises at this time, he should address the Ādityas: "May my sacrifice not be broken off in the middle. May my life live out in full." If he prays thus, the life-sacrifice is not broken off but is completed in all its parts.

Mahidāsa Aitareya, knowing this, said: "Why do you afflict me with this, I who shall not die of it?" And he lived a hundred and sixteen years. He who knows thus lives a hundred and sixteen years. एतद्भस्म वै तद्विद्वानाह महिदास ऐतरेयः स किं म एतदुपतपसि योऽहमनेन न प्रेष्यामीति स ह षोडशं वर्षशतमजीवत्प्र ह षोडशं वर्षशतं जीवति य एवं वेद । (*etadbhasma vai tadvidvānāha mahidāsa aitareyaḥ sa kiṃ ma etadupatapasi yo 'hamanena na preṣyāmīti sa ha ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśatamajīvatpra ha ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśataṃ jīvati ya evaṃ veda |*) (Bhā. U. 3-16-7)

Because Mahidāsa Aitareya had this knowledge of the truth, he was not afraid of the bodily weariness and the like that did not befall him, and he lived a hundred and sixteen years so as to complete his life-sacrifice fully and in all its parts. Thus the greatness of the three pressings, which are of the nature of a man's life, is described. In the present Ṛk the relation between Indra, the presiding deity of all the means of sacrifice such as rain, and the pressing is described. And to Indra

### Printed p. 290
at the time when the Soma sacrifice that gives him satisfaction is performed, "all speech, both stotra and śastra, becomes pleasing to you". Since this is said, the stotras and śastras belonging to the Soma sacrifice are set out in order as follows.

For the Prāśaṃsavana:**NOTE**
Stotras: the बहिष्पवमान (*bahiṣpavamāna*) stotra; 4 आज्य स्तोत्रगळु (*ājya stotragaḷu*).
Śastras: the Hotṛ's आज्य शस्त्र (*ājya śastra*); the Hotṛ's प्रलुग शस्त्र (*praluga śastra*)**NOTE**; 3 आज्यशस्त्र (*ājyaśastra*)s of the hotrakas (Maitrāvaruṇa, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Acchāvāka).

For the midday pressing:
Stotras: the माध्यंदिनपवमानस्तोत्र (*mādhyaṃdinapavamānastotra*); 4 पृष्ठस्तोत्र (*pṛṣṭhastotra*)s.
Śastras: the Hotṛ's मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र (*marutvatīyaśastra*); the Hotṛ's निष्केवल्यशस्त्र (*niṣkevalyaśastra*); 3 निष्केवल्यशस्त्र (*niṣkevalyaśastra*)s of the hotrakas.

For the क्रियासवन (*kriyāsavana*):
Stotras: the आर्भवपवमानस्तोत्र (*ārbhavapavamānastotra*); the अग्निष्टोव-साम (*agniṣṭova-sāma*).
Śastras: the Hotṛ's वैश्वदेवशस्त्र (*vaiśvadevaśastra*); the Hotṛ's आग्निमारुतशस्त्र (*āgnimārutaśastra*).

Thus the explanation of गौः (*gauḥ*) as speech consisting of stotra and śastra also indicates the close relation between Indra, the sacrifice, and the speech connected with the sacrifice. This relation is explained in the Śatapatha as follows.

सोऽयं यज्ञो वाचमभिदध्यौ । मिथुनेनया स्यामिति ताग्ं संबभूव ॥ इंद्रो ह वा ईक्षां चक्रे । महद्वाइतोऽभ्वं जनिष्यते यज्ञस्य च मिथुनाद्वाचश्च यॆन्मा तन्नाभिभवेदिति स इंद्र एव गर्भो भूत्वैतन्निथुनं प्रविवेश । स ह संवत्सरे जायमान ईक्षांचक्रे । महावीरा वा इयं योनिर्या मामदीधरत यद्वै मैतो महदेवाभ्वं नानुप्रजायेत यन्ना तन्नाभिभवेदिति ।............इंद्रस्य योनिरसीतींद्रस्य हैषा योनिरतो वा हैनां प्रनितन्प्रविशत्यतो वा जायमानो जायते तस्मादाहेंद्रस्य योनिरसीति ॥ (*so 'yaṃ yajño vācamabhidadhyau | mithunenayā syāmiti tāgṃ saṃbabhūva ‖ iṃdro ha vā īkṣāṃ cakre | mahadvāito 'bhvaṃ janiṣyate yajñasya ca mithunādvācaśca yènmā tannābhibhavediti sa iṃdra eva garbho bhūtvaitannithunaṃ praviveśa | sa ha saṃvatsare jāyamāna īkṣāṃcakre | mahāvīrā vā iyaṃ yoniryā māmadīdharata yadvai maito mahadevābhvaṃ nānuprajāyeta yannā tannābhibhavediti |............iṃdrasya yonirasītīṃdrasya haiṣā yonirato vā haināṃ pranitanpraviśatyato vā jāyamāno jāyate tasmādāheṃdrasya yonirasīti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-1-25 to 29)

The sacrifice desired to establish a connection with speech. Indra, knowing this, understood that a great power would certainly arise from the union of the two, and fearing that this power might become greater than his own, he himself entered them in the form of an embryo. After a year he was born in the form of a great power and himself became the sacrificer. Therefore it is well known that sacrifice and speech are pleasing to Indra.

### Printed p. 291
देवीः आपः समुद्रे ते मदंति (*devīḥ āpaḥ samudre te madaṃti*) आसु—द्योतमानाः आपः उदकसमुद्रवणापादानभूते अंतरिक्षे प्रजासु निमित्त भूतासु त्वां मादयंति । (*āsu—dyotamānāḥ āpaḥ udakasamudravaṇāpādānabhūte aṃtarikṣe prajāsu nimitta bhūtāsu tvāṃ mādayaṃti |*)—addressing Indra, the general meaning may be that the shining waters make Indra glad, for the sake of creatures, in the atmosphere, the region where waters take liquid form. But Sāyaṇa explains: यदा प्राण्युपकारार्थ० वर्षणाय त्वां प्रेरयंति वृष्ट्युदकानि तदा खलु तव सोमयागाः सुखकरा भवंति (*yadā prāṇyupakārārtha0 varṣaṇāya tvāṃ prerayaṃti vṛṣṭyudakāni tadā khalu tava somayāgāḥ sukhakarā bhavaṃti*)—when the rain-waters urge Indra to rain for the benefit of living beings, the Soma sacrifices become pleasing to Indra; therefore वृष्टिप्रदानेन यागान्निर्वर्तय (*vṛṣṭipradānena yāgānnirvartaya*)—by giving the rain that causes the sacrifice to be accomplished, may Indra accomplish the sacrifices. Thus the sacrificers' aspiration is described here.

समुद्रे (*samudre*)—the word samudra is also read among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). Here Yāska, since in common usage the word samudra denotes the mass of water on the earth, shows a doubt about the derivation of the word, and then explains it: समुद्र इत्येतत् पार्थिवेन समुद्रेण संदिह्यते (*samudra ityetat pārthivena samudreṇa saṃdihyate*).

समुद्रवंत्यस्मादापः, समभिद्रवंत्येनमापः, सम्मोदंते अर्स्मि भूतानि समुदको भवति समुनत्तीति वा (*samudravaṃtyasmādāpaḥ, samabhidravaṃtyenamāpaḥ, sammodaṃte arsmi bhūtāni samudako bhavati samunattīti vā*). The waters assume different forms here as waves, billows and drops; or the waters come together and gather here, in your region; or the creatures of the water rejoice here; since water is denoted by the word udaka, the mass of water is denoted by the word samudaka; or the word samudra is used because it wets everything. So he explains the meaning of the word. And he narrates a story on this subject.

देवापिश्चार्ष्टषेणः शंतनुश्च कौरव्या भ्रातरौ बभूवतुः । स शंतनुः कनीयानभिषेचयां चक्रे । देवापिस्तपः प्रतिपेदे ततश्यंतनो राज्ये द्वादशवर्षाणि देवो न ववर्ष ॥ (*devāpiścārṣṭaṣeṇaḥ śaṃtanuśca kauravyā bhrātarau babhūvatuḥ | sa śaṃtanuḥ kanīyānabhiṣecayāṃ cakre | devāpistapaḥ pratipede tataśyaṃtano rājye dvādaśavarṣāṇi devo na vavarṣa ‖*) (Ni. 2-11)

Of the two princes of the Kuru line, Devāpi and Śantanu, the younger, Śantanu, was consecrated king. When the elder, Devāpi, undertook austerity, there was no rain for twelve years in Śantanu's kingdom.

तमूचुब्रार्ह्मणा अधर्मस्त्वया चरितो ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमंतरित्याभिषेचितं तस्मात्ते देवो न वर्षतीति । स शंतनुर्देदापिं शिशिक्ष राज्येन । तमुवाच देवापिः पुरोहितस्ते असानि याजयानि च त्वेति । (*tamūcubrārhmaṇā adharmastvayā carito jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaramaṃtarityābhiṣecitaṃ tasmātte devo na varṣatīti | sa śaṃtanurdedāpiṃ śiśikṣa rājyena | tamuvāca devāpiḥ purohitaste asāni yājayāni ca tveti |*) (Ni. 2-11)

### Printed p. 292
Then the brāhmaṇas said to King Śantanu: "You have been consecrated after passing over your elder brother, and so you practise unrighteousness; that is why there has been no rain in your kingdom." Hearing this, King Śantanu pressed his elder brother Devāpi to become king. Devāpi, unwilling to be king, said: "I shall be your priest so that rain may fall in your kingdom, and I shall perform the sacrifice for you." And so he had the sacrifice performed with the hymn for desiring rain. Having said this, Yāska cites the Ṛk of the hymn for desiring rain:

अर्ष्टिषेणो होत्रमृषिर्निषीर्द देवापिर्देवसुमतिं चिकित्त्वा । स उत्तरस्मादधरं समुद्रमपो दिव्या असृजद्वर्ष्या अभि ॥ (*arṣṭiṣeṇo hotramṛṣirniṣīrda devāpirdevasumatiṃ cikittvā | sa uttarasmādadharaṃ samudramapo divyā asṛjadvarṣyā abhi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-98-5)

Here, on the sentence सः उत्तरस्मात् अधरं अपो दिव्याः अस्पृजत् (*saḥ uttarasmāt adharaṃ apo divyāḥ aspṛjat*), Yāska says: देवापिः अंतरिक्षाख्यात् समुद्रात् अधरं समुद्रं पार्थिवं प्रति प्रशस्ताः सस्यसंपत्करीः आपः अस्पृजत् (*devāpiḥ aṃtarikṣākhyāt samudrāt adharaṃ samudraṃ pārthivaṃ prati praśastāḥ sasyasaṃpatkarīḥ āpaḥ aspṛjat*)—Devāpi, by the favour of the gods pleased with his praise, created excellent waters that cause the increase of crops, beneficial even to the earthly sea, which is lower than the sea called the atmosphere. Thus he establishes the distinction between the atmospheric and the earthly seas. And the word samudra is also used in another sense:

सविता यंत्रैः पृथिवीमरम्णादस्कंभने सविता द्यामद्यंहत् । अश्वमिनाधुक्षद्दुनिमंतरिक्षमतूर्ते बद्धं सविता समुद्रं ॥ (*savitā yaṃtraiḥ pṛthivīmaramṇādaskaṃbhane savitā dyāmadyaṃhat | aśvaminādhukṣaddunimaṃtarikṣamatūrte baddhaṃ savitā samudraṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-149-1)

Here समुद्रं उदकबंधितारं मेघं (*samudraṃ udakabaṃdhitāraṃ meghaṃ*)—the cloud that holds back the water; thus the word samudra is explained as meaning cloud.

पवित्रवंतः परि वाचमासते पितैषां प्रत्नो अभि रक्षति व्रतं । महस्समुद्रं वरुणस्तिरो दधे धीरा इच्छेकुर्धरुणेष्वारभं ॥ (*pavitravaṃtaḥ pari vācamāsate pitaiṣāṃ pratno abhi rakṣati vrataṃ | mahassamudraṃ varuṇastiro dadhe dhīrā icchekurdharuṇeṣvārabhaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-73-3)

Here समुद्रं आदित्यं (*samudraṃ ādityaṃ*)—the word samudra is explained as meaning the sun.

विश्वा गौः जोष्या (*viśvā gauḥ joṣyā*)—सर्वापि स्तोत्रशस्त्ररूपा वाक् जोषणार्हा प्रीणयित्रि (*sarvāpi stotraśastrarūpā vāk joṣaṇārhā prīṇayitri*). The Nirukta-writers begin with गौरिति पृथिव्या नामधेयं (*gauriti pṛthivyā nāmadheyaṃ*) (Ni. 2-5) and explain for the word go the meanings earth, phlegm, the string tied to a bow, the sun, rays, the sushumnā-nāḍī, and so on. Sāyaṇa explains the meaning as speech, and describes the sense that all the stotras and śastras addressed to Indra are such as to please Indra:

### Printed p. 293
The derivations of the word गौः (*gauḥ*) in the senses earth, animal and so on were given earlier. In the present context the word may also mean the sacrificial offering or the sun's ray that brings rain, and this meaning is fitting to the context. If the meaning is offering, then the oblations and other wealth that Indra may receive are what is intended.

गा दास्यति गोदा गा मे देहित्येवं यं कामं कामयते सोऽस्मै कामः समृध्यते (*gā dāsyati godā gā me dehityevaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate so 'smai kāmaḥ samṛdhyate*) (Śa. Brā. 19-3. 16)

Citing sentences such as this, the exact meaning of the word go was given earlier. It will be explained further later.

सूरींश्चित् धिषा वेषि (*sūrīṃścit dhiṣā veṣi*)—the word sūri is stated among the names of worshippers (Ni. 3-19). Sāyaṇa explains the sense thus: Indra, favourably to the worshippers who urge him with stotras and other rites, bestows प्रज्ञया वृष्टिप्रदानरूपेण कर्मणा वा (*prajñayā vṛṣṭipradānarūpeṇa karmaṇā vā*), that is, wisdom or rain; therefore he is at all times a fit recipient of their praise.

##### Grammar

- एना — निपातस्य च (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
- सवना — सुञ् अभिषवे इति धातुः । अधिकरणार्थे ल्युट् प्रत्ययः । युवोरनाकौ (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति अनादेशः । नपुंसकबहुवचने शेत्छंदसि बहुलं (पा. सू. ६-१-२०) इति शि इत्यस्य लोपः । लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वमुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- मदंति — मद तृप्तियोगे इति धातुः । प्रयोजकव्यापारदर्शनादंतर्भावितण्यर्थको धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । ल सार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- देवीः — सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू ७-१-३९) इति जसि परे पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घो भवति ।
- जोष्या — जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः इति धातुः । अर्हार्थे यत् प्रत्ययः । पुगंतलघूपधस्य च इति लघूपधगुणः । यशोनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- भूत् — भू सत्तायां इति धातुः । छांदसत्वेन वर्तमानार्थे लुज् । गातिस्थाघु (पा. सू. २-४-७७) इति सिचो लुक् । छांदसत्वेन अडागमो न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।

### Printed p. 294
- वेषि — वी गत्यादिषु इति धातुः । अत्र इच्छार्थे प्रयुक्तः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । निपातैर्यद्यदि (पा. सू. ८-१-३०) इति यदि संबंधान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । सिप् पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> असा॑म॒ यथा॑ सुष॒खाय॑ एन स्वभि॒ष्टयो॑ न॒रां न शंसैः॑ ।  
> अस॒द्यथा॑ न॒ इंद्रो॑ वंदने॒ष्ठास्तु॒रो न कर्म॒ नय॑मान उ॒क्था ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असाम । यथा । सुसखायः । एन । सुअभिष्टयः । नरां । न । शंसैः ।  
> असत् । यथा । नः । इंद्रः । वंदने ऽस्थाः । तुरः । न । कर्म । नयमानः । उक्का ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे एनेनेत्वरेंद्र यथा सुसखायः शोभनत्वद्रूपसहायवंतोऽसाम
> भूयास्म किंच स्वभिष्टयः शोभनाभ्येषणाः शोभनाभीष्टाश्चासाम । किमिव । नरां
> न तंसैः । नराणां राजादीनां तंसैः शंसनैरिव । स्तुतिभिर्यथा मनुष्याः शोभनाभीष्टा भवंति तद्वत् । इदानीं परोक्षेणाह । नोऽस्मभ्यमिंद्रो वंदनेष्ठा
> अस्मत्सुतौ वर्तमानः संस्तुरो न त्वरमाण इव नोऽस्माकं कर्मोक्षोक्तैः
> शस्त्रैनयमानः फलं प्रापयन् स्तुत्या तुष्टः सन्नस्मदीयेन कर्मणा फलप्रापयिता
> यथासत् भवेत् । हे ऋत्विजः तथा कुरुतेति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra (addressed as एनेनेत्वरेंद्र (*enenetvareṃdra*)**NOTE**): may we have good companions, that is, helpers of your auspicious form, and may we be well desired, with good aims fulfilled. How? As men become well desired through the praises of men, kings and others; as people attain their wishes through praises, so may we. Now he speaks indirectly: may Indra, abiding in our praise, hurrying as it were, leading our rite along with recited śastras and bringing its fruit, pleased by the praise, become the bringer of fruit through our rite. "O priests, so act" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे एन (*he ena*)—O Indra, the lord
- यथा (*yathā*)—how
- सुसखायः (*susakhāyaḥ*)—those having the help of you, the auspicious one
- नरां (*narāṃ*)—of kings and others
- शंसैः न (*śaṃsaiḥ na*)—as we attain the desired end through praise
- सु अभिष्टयः (*su abhiṣṭayaḥ*)—those having auspicious desired ends
- असाम (*asāma*)—we become (so favour us)
- किंच हे ऋत्विजः (*kiṃca he ṛtvijaḥ*)—and, O priests
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वंदनेष्ठाः (*vaṃdaneṣṭhāḥ*)—being in (our) praise (pleased with our praise)

### Printed p. 295
- …as if hastening
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- कर्म (*karma*)—rites (for the rites), with praises (satisfied)
- नयमानः (*nayamānaḥ*)—one who brings the fruit
- यथा असत् (*yathā asat*)—as he becomes; (so act)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Lord Indra, just as men gain their desired ends by satisfying kings and others with praise and the like, we too wish to gain the fulfilment of our desires through your friendship (through your favour). O Ṛtvijs, so act that Indra, pleased with our rites and our hymns of praise, may quickly become the giver of their fruit.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May we be, as it were, your valued friends, O Lord, and obtain our desires, like those (who gain their objects) by the praise of princes. May Indra, propitiated by our eulogiums, be brought to the sacrifice by our hymns.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the seer of the mantra describes, as it were, the instruction which the sacrificers give to their Ṛtvijs.
By the words हे एन इंद्र (*he ena iṃdra*) Indra is addressed: "O Lord, O Indra."
नरां न शंसैः राजादीनां शंसैः स्तुतिभिः यथा मनुष्याः शोभनाभीष्टा भवंति तद्वत् शोभनत्वद्रूप सखायवंतः शोभनाभीष्टाश्च असाम । (*narāṃ na śaṃsaiḥ rājādīnāṃ śaṃsaiḥ stutibhiḥ yathā manuṣyāḥ śobhanābhīṣṭā bhavaṃti tadvat śobhanatvadrūpa sakhāyavaṃtaḥ śobhanābhīṣṭāśca asāma |*) Here is described the sacrificers' wish: just as men, praising kings and others, accomplish their desires, so may we, by praising Indra through the sacrifice, become his beloved friends and have our desires fulfilled.
तुरो न उक्ता नयमानः कर्म यथा असत् । (*turo na uktā nayamānaḥ karma yathā asat |*) Here is described the instruction the sacrificers give to the Ṛtvijs: "Let Indra, becoming the object of our praises, be like one in haste; hearing our praises, let him favour us so that our sacrifices and other rites yield fruit; perform the sacrificial rites so that, through our rite, he himself becomes the giver of its fruit (अस्मदीयेन कर्मणा फलप्रापयिता (*asmadīyena karmaṇā phalaprāpayitā*)) to us."
By the two similes नरां न (*narāṃ na*) and तुरो न (*turo na*) the comparison with the king and with men is explained. In the phrase तुरो न (*turo na*) the comparison is with one in haste who quickly carries out his own necessary duty.

### Printed p. 296
In the same way the carefulness in performing the rite is made plain: that Indra, hearing our praises, may quickly become the giver of the full fruit of our sacrifices.

##### Grammar

- आसाम — अस भुवि इति धातुः । लोट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । आडागमस्य पित्त्वात् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- सुसखायः — शोभनः सखा येषां ते । नञ् सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) इति उत्तरपदांदोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- स्वभिष्टयः — शोभनाः अभिष्टयः येषांते । पूर्ववत् उत्तरपदोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- नराम् — सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१८) इति षष्ठीबहुवचनस्य उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- शंस्यैः — शंसु स्तुतौ धातुः । घञ् प्रत्ययः । इत्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । तृतीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- असत् — अस भुवि धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । इतश्चलोपः (पा. सू. ३-४-९७) इति इकारलोपः । लेटोडाट् (पा. सू. ३-४-६४) इति अडागमः । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- वंदनेष्ठाः — वंदने तिष्यतीति वंदनेष्ठाः । ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलम् इति सप्तम्या लोपो न भवति । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- तुरः — तुर त्वर्णे धातुः । अगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कॆः (पा. सू. ३-१-१३५) इति क प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् लघूपधगुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- उक्का — वच परिधाषणे धातुः । पात्यतुदिवचि (उ. सू. २-१६४) इति फक् प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. सू. ६-१-१५) इति संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपं च । चोःकुः इति कुत्वम् । सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति तृतीया परे पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घो भवति ।

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विष्प॑र्धसो न॒रां न शंसै॑र॒स्माका॑स॒दिंद्रो॒ वज्र॑हस्तः ।  
> मि॒त्रा॒युवो॒ न पूर्प॑तिं॒ सुशि॑ष्टौ मध्या॒युव॒ उप॑ शिक्षंति य॒ज्ञैः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विस्पर्धसः । नरां । न । शंसैः । न । अस्माक । असत् । इंद्रः । वज्रहस्तः ।  
> मित्रयुवः । न । पूःपतिं । सुशिष्टौ । मध्ययुवः । उप । शिक्षंति यज्ञैः ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नरां नेत्यणां मध्ये सस्पर्धान्नरान्यथा विस्पर्धसः कुर्वंति सखिभूताः
> तद्वद्वयमपींद्रं शंसैः । स्तुतिभिः सखायो वयं तं तथा कुर्मः । स च वज्रहस्तो विरोधिशिक्षणाय सर्वदा वज्रधारींद्रोऽस्माकमसत् । विस्पर्धमनुकूलो भवतु । किंच मित्रायुवो न मित्रेच्छवो हितैषिण इव सुशिष्टौ सुशासने
> वर्तमानं पूर्पतिं पुरः स्वामिनं यथाभिमतदानेन पूजयंति तथा मध्याय
> वोऽस्माकंश्च्रियां यशसां च मध्यॆऽवस्थितिं कामयमाना अध्वर्यादयो यज्ञैर्यज्ञसाधनैर्हविःस्तोत्रादिभिरुप शिक्षंति । उपेत्य यजंते । शिक्षतिर्दानकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: just as, among men who rival one another, friends make the rivals free of rivalry, so we also, as friends of Indra through praises (शंसैः (*śaṃsaiḥ*)), make him so. And may Indra, the thunderbolt-handed, who always bears the thunderbolt to punish his adversaries, be favourable to us, free of rivalry. Further: as well-wishers, desiring friends, honour with gifts of what is desired the lord of the city who abides in good government, so the Adhvaryus and the others, desiring a place for themselves in the midst of our wealth and our fame, approach and sacrifice with the means of sacrifice (यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)), oblations, hymns and the like. The root शिक्ष (*śikṣa*) has the sense of giving.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरां (*narāṃ*)—among men (those who are rivals)
- विस्पर्धसः न (*vispardhasaḥ na*)—(as friends make them) free of rivalry
- शंसैः (*śaṃsaiḥ*)—by hymns and the like (we make Indra so too)
- वज्रहस्तः (*vajrahastaḥ*)—bearing the thunderbolt (to punish adversaries)
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अस्माक असत् (*asmāka asat*)—may he be (favourable) to us
- मित्रायुवः (*mitrāyuvaḥ*)—well-wishers
- सुशिष्टौ (*suśiṣṭau*)—(intent) on governing (the kingdom) well
- पूर्पतिं न (*pūrpatiṃ na*)—as the lord of the city (they satisfy with gifts of what is desired)
- मध्यायुवः (*madhyāyuvaḥ*)—Adhvaryus and others desiring to be in the midst (of our wealth or fame)
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—with oblations and the like, the means of sacrifice
- उप शिक्षंति (*upa śikṣaṃti*)—approach and worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Just as friends set right, by praise and the like, men marked by envy and such faults, so we too make Indra favourable by hymns and the like. Just as well-wishers honour with gifts of what is desired a king who governs well, so our Ṛtvijs, the Adhvaryus and others, who desire wealth and the like, worship with oblations and other means of sacrifice.

### Printed p. 298

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Emulous in commendation, like (those contending for the favour) of men, may Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, be equally (a friend) to us : like those who, desirous of his friendship. (conciliate) the lord of a city (ruling) with good government, so do our intermediate (representatives) propitiate (Indra) with sacrifices.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नरां विस्पर्धासः शंसैः (*narāṃ vispardhāsaḥ śaṃsaiḥ*)—नेतृणां मध्ये सस्पर्धान् नरान् यथा सखिभूताः कुर्वंति तद्वद्वयमपि इंद्रं स्तुतिभिः सखायो वयं तं तथा कुर्मः । (*netṛṇāṃ madhye saspardhān narān yathā sakhibhūtāḥ kurvaṃti tadvadvayamapi iṃdraṃ stutibhiḥ sakhāyo vayaṃ taṃ tathā kurmaḥ |*) Seeing men who carry on worldly affairs rivalling one another, their friends, for their benefit, make them give up the rivalry. In the same way we sacrificers, regarding Indra as a friend, praise him that he may be favourable to us and rival-like in zeal; the wish is expressed that we make his zeal to favour us grow to excess.
वज्रहस्तः (*vajrahastaḥ*)—विरोधिशिक्षणाय सर्वदा वज्रधारी अस्माकं अनुकूलो भवतु (*virodhiśikṣaṇāya sarvadā vajradhārī asmākaṃ anukūlo bhavatu*) The wish is expressed that Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand only to subdue enemies, be favourable to us, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice.
मित्रायुवो न (*mitrāyuvo na*)—Sāyaṇa has explained the word मित्र (*mitra*) in the sense of "beneficial". As a friend desires what is good for his friend, so may Indra be a well-wisher to us; thus the comparison is described.
पूर्वतिं मध्यायुवः यज्ञैः उपशिक्षंति (*pūrvatiṃ madhyāyuvaḥ yajñaiḥ upaśikṣaṃti*)—अस्माकं क्रियां यशसां च मध्ये आवस्थितिं कामयमानाः अध्वर्यादयः यज्ञसाधनैः हविः स्तोत्रादिभिः उपेत्य यजंति । (*asmākaṃ kriyāṃ yaśasāṃ ca madhye āvasthitiṃ kāmayamānāḥ adhvaryādayaḥ yajñasādhanaiḥ haviḥ stotrādibhiḥ upetya yajaṃti |*) The root शिक्ष (*śikṣa*) is read by the Nirukta-author among the ten words for giving, दाति (*dāti*), दाशति (*dāśati*) and so on (Ni. 3-19); here it is used in the sense of giving. As one worships a lord in his very presence by offering what pleases him, so the Adhvaryus and the other Ṛtvijs, who desire for the sacrificers a place between wealth and fame, worship Indra by offering oblations, the means of sacrifice, and by reciting hymns. As one worships a lord in his very presence

### Printed p. 299
by giving what he desires, so Indra is worshipped in his very presence by the offering of oblations; thus the meaning is explained by comparison.

##### Grammar

- विस्वर्धसः — विगतं स्पर्धः येषांते । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- अस्माकॆ — छांदसत्वात् अंत्यलोपो भवति ।
- असत् — अस भुवि धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- वज्रहस्तः — वज्रः हस्ते यस्य सः । व्यधिकरणबहुव्रीहिसमासः । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- मित्रायुवः — मित्राणि आत्मनः इच्छंतः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (पा.सू. ३-१-८) इति क्यच् । छांदसत्वात् संहितायां दीर्घो भवति । क्याच्छंदसि (पा. सू. ३-२-१७०) इति क्यजंतात् उ प्रत्ययः । अतोलोपः (पा. सू. ६-४-४८) इति अकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरो भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- पूर्पतिः — पुरः पतिः पूर्वतिः सत्यावैश्वर्ये (पा. सू. ६-२-१८) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- सुशिष्टौ — शासु अनुशिष्टौ धातुः । स्त्रियांक्तिन् इति भावार्थे क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । शास इदज्हलोः (पा. सू. ९-४-३४) इति धातोरुपधाया इत्वम् । शासिवसिघसीनां च (पा. सू. ८-३-६०) इति धातुसकारस्य षत्वम् । तन्निमित्तीकृत्य प्रत्ययस्य ष्टुत्वम् । तादौचनिति (पा. सू. ६-२-५०) इति गतेः (सु) उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- मध्यायुवः — क्याच्छंदसि (पा.सू. २-२-१७०) इति क्यजंतात् उप्रत्ययः । क्यजस्य अकारस्य लोपः । संहितायां छांदसत्वात् दीर्घः । प्रत्ययस्वरो भवति ।
- शिक्षंति — शिक्ष विद्योपादाने धातुः । अत्र दानार्थे प्रयुक्तः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
