> गच्चन्नेदं प्राप्नोति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । तीर्थे प्रसिद्धे मार्गेऽच्छाभिमुख्येन
> समीपे वर्तमानमोकः पानीयादिकं सदनं ततृषाणं पिपासायुक्तं यथाविलंबेन प्रीणाति । स यथा तत्सदनमागच्छतीत्यर्थः । तद्विद्यज्ञेन कश्चित्पुमानिंद्रमभिगच्छतीति । कुटिलस्य दृष्टांतः । दीर्घो न वक्रत्वेनातिदूरोऽध्वा मार्ग इव । स
> यथा सिद्धं फलं पानीयादिरूपं फलार्थिनं वा पुरुषमा कृणोति अर्वाक्करोति
> नीचैः करोति । वर्जयतीत्यर्थः । तस्माद्यज्ञमार्गमजानानो वक्रो दूरे
> परिभ्रमति नेंद्रं तर्पयति । तद्विलक्षणस्तु वर्जयत्येव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: a certain man who sacrifices, performing the sacrifice, is "increasing" (ऋंधन् (*ṛṃdhan*)), that is, he makes Indra grow by the sacrifice. But a crooked-going man (जुहुराणश्चित् (*juhurāṇaścit*)) goes around (परियन् (*pariyan*)) with the mind alone, going about thinking of worldly objects and the like. Or else परि (*pari*) has the sense of avoidance: going by avoiding, he does not obtain this. An illustration follows. As a dwelling (ओकः (*okaḥ*)) with water and the like, standing near, facing a well-known ford (तीर्थे (*tīrthe*)) on the road, satisfies without delay the man who is thirsty (ततृषाणं (*tatṛṣāṇaṃ*)), so that he comes to that dwelling, in the same way a man goes to Indra by the sacrifice. For the crooked man the illustration is: like a long road (दीर्घो न (*dīrgho na*) अध्वा (*adhvā*)), exceedingly far because of its windings. As that road makes the accomplished fruit, in the form of water and the like, or the man who seeks the fruit, आ कृणोति (*ā kṛṇoti*), he makes him remote, lowers him, that is, avoids him. Therefore one who does not know the way of sacrifice, being crooked, wanders far and does not satisfy Indra; one unlike him only avoids this.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कः चित् यज्ञः (*kaḥ cit yajñaḥ*)—some man who performs sacrifice
- तीर्थे (*tīrthe*)—(some) ford's
- अच्छ (*accha*)—near
- ओकः (*okaḥ*)—dwelling with water and the like
- ततृषाणं न (*tatṛṣāṇaṃ na*)—as it satisfies one tormented by thirst
- ऋंधन् स्म (*ṛṃdhan sma*)—he keeps increasing (Indra); (but)
- जुहुराणः चित् (*juhurāṇaḥ cit*)—a crooked man
- दीर्घः (*dīrghaḥ*)—far
- अध्वा (*adhvā*)—road
- सिध्रं (*sidhraṃ*)—the desired fruit
- आ कृणोति न (*ā kṛṇoti na*)—as it makes it despicable
- सिध्रं (*sidhraṃ*)—the man who seeks fruit
- आ कृणोति न (*ā kṛṇoti na*)—as it keeps (him) far (from the desired fruit)
- मनसा (*manasā*)—in the mind alone
- परि यन् (*pari yan*)—he goes around (thinking of worldly objects and the like); that is, he does not worship Indra at all

### Printed p. 301

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Just as the water of a sacred place quenches the thirst of a man who stands near some holy site, the performer of the sacrifice gratifies Indra with sacrifices and the like. Just as a long road keeps a man who seeks a result away from that result, a crooked man wanders about without worshipping Indra, thinking in his mind of worldly matters.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Oue man propitiates Indra, augmenting (his vigour) by sacrifice; another, who is insincere, worships (him), with mind averted, (to worldly thoughts): (to the first he is) like a lake to a thirsty (pilgrim) near a sacred spot: (to the other) like a long road, which retards the end (of the journey).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कश्चित् यज्ञः ऋंधर् (*kaścit yajñaḥ ṛṃdhar*)—Here the word यज्ञ (*yajña*) is used in the sense of the yajamāna, the householder who performs the sacrifice. By यज्ञर्वा यज्ञानुष्ठाया इंद्रं यज्ञेन वर्धयति (*yajñarvā yajñānuṣṭhāyā iṃdraṃ yajñena vardhayati*) the meaning is explained: the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice gratifies Indra by sacrificing.

जुहुराणश्चित् मनसा परि र्य (*juhurāṇaścit manasā pari rya*) (one who goes astray): one who moves along a crooked path, परिशो गच्छन् लौकिक विषयादिकं धार्य वर्तते (*pariśo gacchan laukika viṣayādikaṃ dhārya vartate*): he goes on meditating with his mind only on the enjoyable things of the world. Or else, यद्वा वर्जयित्वा गच्छन्नेदं प्राप्नोति (*yadvā varjayitvā gacchannedaṃ prāpnoti*): he abandons the path of performing sacrifices and the like and winning the favour of Indra and the other deities. Thus the meaning is explained by taking the prefix परि (*pari*) in the sense of avoidance, following usage.

तीर्थे अच्छ ओकः ततृषाणं (*tīrthe accha okaḥ tatṛṣāṇaṃ*)—The Nirukta authors explain the word ओकस् (*okas*) as meaning a dwelling-place (Ni. 3-3).

To show that a man has complete attachment to his own house, the Nirukta authors gave a charming example:

नहि ग्रधायारणः सुशेवोऽन्योदरो मनसा मंतवा उ । अधा चिदोकः पुनरित्स एत्या नो वाज्येभीषाळेतु नव्यः ॥ (*nahi gradhāyāraṇaḥ suśevo 'nyodaro manasā maṃtavā u | adhā cidokaḥ punaritsa etyā no vājyebhīṣāḷetu navyaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-4-8).

### Printed p. 302
They cite and explain the above Ṛk to show that the word ओक (*oka*) suggests that one's own house is the object of complete attachment: an adopted son, whatever happens, has his attachment in his own house and returns there.

As a house that has prepared drink along a well-known road (a water-shed) quickly delights a thirsty man, so a man who performs the sacrificial rites famed in the Śruti delights Indra; thus it is explained.

दीर्घो न अध्वा सिद्धं आकृणोति (*dīrgho na adhvā siddhaṃ ākṛṇoti*)—वक्रत्वेन अतिदूरः मार्ग इव (*vakratvena atidūraḥ mārga iva*). The Nirukta authors explain the word सिद्ध (*siddha*) as meaning a means (Ni. 9-39). Sāyaṇa explains it as the result, and पानीयादिरूपं फलार्थिनं वा पुरुषं (*pānīyādirūpaṃ phalārthinaṃ vā puruṣaṃ*): a thirsty man, travelling by a crooked or very long road, forsakes the place where the drink-like result beneficial to him is to be had. Thus the course of the crooked man who goes by the crooked path is described.

तस्माद्यज्ञमार्गमजानानो वक्रो दूरे परिभ्रमति नेंद्रं तर्पयति तद्विलक्षणस्तु वर्जयत्येव । (*tasmādyajñamārgamajānāno vakro dūre paribhramati neṃdraṃ tarpayati tadvilakṣaṇastu varjayatyeva |*) The crooked man, not knowing the way of performing sacrifice and delighting Indra, goes on circling in the ordinary worldly course and does not bring about Indra's delight. The performer of sacrifice, performing it in the order stated in the Śruti and delighting Indra, abandons the crooked path of worldly conduct. Thus, showing the fruit arising from following the worldly and the Vedic paths, the difference between the crooked man who follows worldly practice and the Vedic man who performs sacrifice is explained.

##### Grammar

- यज्ञः—यज्ञः अस्य अस्ति इति यज्ञः । आर्तआदिभ्योच् (पा. सू. ५-२-१२७) इति मत्त्वर्थे अच् प्रत्ययः । यस्येति च (पा. सू. ६-४-१४८) इति पूर्वस्य आकारस्य लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- ऋंधन्—ऋधु वृद्धौ धातुः । दिवादिः । लटि शत्रादेशः । व्यत्ययेन श्नम् विकरणम् । मित्त्वात् अंत्याचः परः आगच्छति । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- जुहुराणः—हुर्छा कौटिल्ये धातुः । हुर्छेःसनो लुक् छलोपश्च (उ. सू. २-२४८) इति सन्नंतात् आनट् प्रत्ययः । सनो लोपः । धातोः छकारस्य लोपः । प्रत्ययलोपे (सन्) अपि प्रत्ययलक्षणेन धातो र्द्वित्वम् । रेफनिमित्तं प्रत्ययनकारस्य णत्वम् । चित्त्वात् चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

- परियन्—इण् गतौ धातुः । लटि शत्रादेशः । इषोयण् (पा. सू. ६-४-८१) इति यणादेशः । गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९) इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, in these battles now at hand, battles for rain, that is, victories over the clouds, do not abandon us, together with the gods, the Maruts and others; this is the understood supplement. The meaning: fight together with the Maruts. O mighty Indra, there is for you अवयाः (*avayāḥ*), that is, a separate sacrifice, a share of the oblation apart. A separate share of oblation exists also for the Maruts. One should not think, "The oblation is given only to the Maruts, not to us; how then shall I fight?" Or else अवयाः (*avayāḥ*) is the thunderbolt that goes to ward off enemies; it is yours. Further, the two words हविष्मतः (*haviṣmataḥ*) and माळ्हुषः (*māḷhuṣaḥ*) (the giver of oblations, the sprinkler) are epithets of the Maruts, possessed of the oblation to be offered. The speech of the praise and recitation kind, mingling with the fruit or with Indra, of me, the worshipper, praises the Maruts, great as they are, who shed rain and possess the oblation given.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हविष्मतः (*haviṣmataḥ*)—endowed with the oblation (to be offered to you)
- मीळ्हुषः (*mīḷhuṣaḥ*)—the giver of the oblation (to you)
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of whom, of me (us)
- यव्या (*yavyā*)—accompanied by the fruit
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the speech in the form of praise
- महः चित् (*mahaḥ cit*)—though very great. [Or हविष्मतः (*haviṣmataḥ*)—possessed of the oblation (given by us); मीळ्हुषः (*mīḷhuṣaḥ*)—showerers (rain-shedders).]
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- वंदते (*vaṃdate*)—praises
- नः (*naḥ*)—us (such)
- (हे (*he*)) इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अत्र पृत्सु (*atra pṛtsu*)—in the battles now present (the means of conquering the clouds)
- देवैः (*devaiḥ*)—with the Maruts (accompanied by them, you)
- मो षु (*mo ṣu*)—do not abandon at all
- (हे (*he*)) शुष्मि ९ (*śuṣmi 9*)—O mighty Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- अवयाः (*avayāḥ*)—share of the sacrifice, or the thunderbolt that destroys enemies
- अस्ति हि स्म (*asti hi sma*)—it is indeed there.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

My praise, I who am the giver of oblations and am now furnished with the oblation to be offered, gratifies the Maruts, the very great gods. The share of the sacrifice due to you is ready. Therefore, O mighty Indra, in the battles that are the means of conquering the clouds, do not leave our hand, you who are accompanied by the Maruts.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, associated with the Maruts in battles (with the clouds), abandon us not; for a share of tLe offering is set apart, mighty one, tor you, for whom, the shedder of rain and accepter of oblations, the worship is offered with oblations, whilst the hymn glorifies the Maruts.

### Printed p. 305

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पृत्सु देवैः नः मो षु (*pṛtsu devaiḥ naḥ mo ṣu*)—The word पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*) is read among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Here, addressing Indra, संग्रामेषु उपस्थितेषु (*saṃgrāmeṣu upasthiteṣu*), when the circumstances for fighting have arisen, or वृष्ट्यर्थं मेघजयेषु (*vṛṣṭyarthaṃ meghajayeṣu*), at the time of conquering the clouds in order to pour out rain-water, may Indra fight मरुदादिभिस्सह (*marudādibhissaha*), being together with the Maruts; so the wish is expressed.

Since he fights united with the Maruts, this mantra suggests that Indra and the Maruts each have a separate share of the oblation.

अवयाः—अवयजनं अवकृत्य पृथक्कृत्य यजनं । हे शुष्मिन् बलवन् (*avayāḥ—avayajanaṃ avakṛtya pṛthakkṛtya yajanaṃ | he śuṣmin balavan*). In this sentence addressed to the mighty Indra: मरुद्भ्यः पृथगप्यस्ति हविर्भागः (*marudbhyaḥ pṛthagapyasti havirbhāgaḥ*); since the Maruts have a separate share of oblation, केवलं मरुद्भ्य एव दीयतॆ नास्मभ्यं अतः कथं न योत्स्वामीति न मंतव्यं (*kevalaṃ marudbhya eva dīyatè nāsmabhyaṃ ataḥ kathaṃ na yotsvāmīti na maṃtavyaṃ*). One meaning, in the form of a doubt, is explained: because the oblation is offered to the Maruts, Indra has no share and will not fight. In answer to this, by the sentence अस्ति हि स्म ते (*asti hi sma te*), अस्ति हि स्म तव खलु (*asti hi sma tava khalu*), it is explained that Indra too has a share in the oblation.

In the second meaning: यद्वा अवयाः शत्रूणां वर्जनाय गंता वज्रोस्ति । (*yadvā avayāḥ śatrūṇāṃ varjanāya gaṃtā vajrosti |*) The word अवयाः (*avayāḥ*) is taken to mean one who goes to destroy enemies. The meaning described is that Indra has the thunderbolt that destroys enemies and also natural strength.

यव्या गीः महश्चित् मरुतः वंदते (*yavyā gīḥ mahaścit marutaḥ vaṃdate*)—The word यव्या (*yavyā*) (फलेनेंद्रेण वा मिश्रयंती (*phaleneṃdreṇa vā miśrayaṃtī*)) is used as an epithet of the speech that sets forth the fruit or sets forth Indra's greatness. For the word गीः (*gīḥ*) the meaning given is स्तुतिशस्त्रादिरूपा वाक् (*stutiśastrādirūpā vāk*): speech in the form of a śastra that praises the gods or invokes them. The words हविष्मतः (*haviṣmataḥ*) and माळ्हुषः (*māḷhuṣaḥ*) are used as epithets of the Maruts and of Indra. For these words the meaning given is: on Indra's behalf, one possessed of a share of the oblation offered by the yajamāna to the Maruts, and a giver of food to the worlds. On behalf of the Maruts, the meaning is: those who shower rain abundantly, more plentifully than other gods, and who obtain shares of oblation through Indra from the oblation offered. The speech in the form of praise and śastra, recited by the yajamānas and adhvaryus together, is to be employed in the worship (as praise) of Indra or the Maruts, who possess oblations and bestow rain; thus the yajamāna prays.

### Printed p. 306
The word मीळ्हुषः (*mīḷhuṣaḥ*) is derived from the root मिह् (*mih*), meaning sprinkling. From the sentence यन्मेहति तत्वर्षति (*yanmehati tatvarṣati*) (Bṛ. U. 1-1-1) the meaning of its basic form can be seen.

वाजयन्निव नू रथान्योगा अग्नेरुव स्तुहि । यशस्तमस्य माळ्हुषः ॥ (*vājayanniva nū rathānyogā agneruva stuhi | yaśastamasya māḷhuṣaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-8-1)

In all such Ṛks, फलस्य सेक्तुः (*phalasya sektuḥ*) means one who pours out and gives desired objects. In the present Ṛk it means those who shed rain. The word माळ्हुं (*māḷhuṃ*), formed from this same root, the Nirukta authors read among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9), and the word माळ्ही (*māḷhī*) among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Their special meanings will be explained in their respective contexts.

##### Grammar

- सु—सुणाः (पा. सू. ८-३-१०७) इति सत्वम् । निपातस्य च (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति । **NOTE**
- पृत्सु—पृतना शब्दः । सप्तमीबहुवचने परे मांसपृत्कनासानूनां मान्स् पृत्स्नवः शसादौ वा वाच्याः इति वचनेन पृतादेशः । ऊडिदं पदादि—(पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- स्म—निपातस्य चॆ (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
- शुष्मिन्—शुष्म बलं अस्य अस्ति इति । शुष्मी । इतनितनौ इति मत्त्वर्थे इनि प्रत्ययः । संबुद्धौ आमंत्रितस्य च (पा. सू. ८-१-१९) इति निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- अवयाः—अव पृथक्कृत्य याति इति अवयाः । या प्रापणे धातुः । क्विड् प्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- मीळ्हुषः—मिह सेचने धातुः । दात्वान् साह्वान् मीढ्वांश्च (पा. सू. ६-१-१२) इति क्वसुप्रत्ययांतः निपातितः । शसि जसि वा परे वसोः संप्रसारणं इति संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपं च । प्रत्ययस्वरेण उकार उदात्तो भवति ।
- वंदते—वदि अभिवादनस्तुत्योः धातुः । इदितो नुम् धातोः इति नुमागमः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधो भवति । तास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) सूत्रेण लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 307
#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष स्तोम॑ इंद्र॒ तुभ्य॑म॒स्मे ए॒तेन॑ गा॒तुं ह॑रिवो विदो नः ।  
> आ नो॑ ववृत्याः सुवि॒ताय॑ देव वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । स्तोमः । इंद्र । तुभ्यं । अस्मे इति । एतेन । गातुं । हरिवः । विदः । नः ।  
> आ । नः । ववृत्याः । सुविताय । देव । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरदानुं ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ त्रयोदश्या सूक्तादिमारभ्य कृतां स्तुतिं निगमय्य फलं प्रार्थयते ॥
> हे इंद्र एष स्तोम इदानींकारितप्रकारः स्तोत्रविशेषस्तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं ।
> हे हरिवो हरिभ्यां तद्वन्निंद्र एतेन स्तोत्रेण गमनेन वा नोऽस्मदीयं गातुं
> देवयजनमार्गं विदः । विदस्व । विदित्वा च हे देव सुविताय सुहिताय
> शोभनगमनाय वा नोऽस्माना ववृत्याः । आवर्तस्व । अस्मद्यागं प्रत्यागच्छ ।
> विद्यामेत्यादि व्याख्यातं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that, having concluded the praise begun with the first Ṛk of the sūkta, the seer now prays for the fruit. "O Indra, this stoma", that is, the particular praise just now composed, "is for you", on your account. "O Harivas", Indra, who has the two bay horses (Hari), "by this praise", or by this going, "find out for us the path (gātu) of the sacrifice", that is, the path to the place of worship of the gods. Having found it, "O god, turn towards us for our good (suvitāya)", for our welfare or for a good going: come back to our sacrifice. The words beginning with विद्याम (*vidyāma*) have been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) इंद्र (*(he) iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्मे (*asme*)—our
- एषः स्तोमः (*eṣaḥ stomaḥ*)—this praise (made up to now)
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- (हे) हरिवः (*(he) harivaḥ*)—O Indra, possessor of the horses named Hari
- एतेन (*etena*)—by this praise
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—the path to the sacrificial hall
- विदः (*vidaḥ*)—know (it), (then)
- (हे) देव (*(he) deva*)—O god
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—for our good (for a pleasant coming)
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- आ ववृत्याः (*ā vavṛtyāḥ*)—come, turning towards us
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—strength
- जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*)—long life
- विद्याम (*vidyāma*)—let us obtain (by your grace)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the praise we have made up to now is for the sake of satisfying you. By this praise of ours, knowing the way to our sacrificial hall, come to the sacrificial hall for our good. By the grace of you who have come, may we obtain food, strength and long life.

### Printed p. 308

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This hymn, Indra, is addressed to you. Lord of steeds, learn by it the way to our sacrifice, and come hither for our good, that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हरिवः—हरिभ्यां तद्वन्निंद्र (*harivaḥ—haribhyāṃ tadvanniṃdra*). Because the phrase "Hari of Indra" (हरी इंद्रस्य (*harī iṃdrasya*)) is used for Indra's horses, Sāyaṇa has explained the word हरिवः (*harivaḥ*) as having the sense of the possessor (tadvat). Indra is addressed by this word.

एष स्तोमः (*eṣa stomaḥ*)—The seers, the seers of the mantra, express the wish that this particular praise, "of the kind just now composed" (इदानींकारितप्रकारः स्तोत्रविशेषः (*idānīṃkāritaprakāraḥ stotraviśeṣaḥ*)), spoken in this manner, may reach Indra.

एतेन नः गातुं विदः (*etena naḥ gātuṃ vidaḥ*)—Since the word एतेन (*etena*) is listed among the pronouns and so conveys a meaning that refers to what is present in the mind, it is used in the sense "by the praise"; and since it is formed from the root इण् (*iṇ*) which means going, it is also used in the sense "by going". Addressing Indra, Sāyaṇa has described the meaning thus: अस्मदीयं देवयजनमार्गं स्तोत्रेण गमनेन वा विदस्व (*asmadīyaṃ devayajanamārgaṃ stotreṇa gamanena vā vidasva*)—let him know the way to the sacrificial hall where we offer oblations to the gods, either by our praise or by his own going.

गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—Even when the sense "going" is taken, two kinds of meaning are possible: the path of performance of the rite, or the path of going to the world of the gods. As with the word सुगं (*sugaṃ*), this word too has a physical and a moral sense. In Ṛks such as

ऊर्ध्वो नां गातुरध्वरे अकार्यूर्ध्वा शोचेंषि प्रस्थिता रजांसि । दिवो ना नाभा न्यसादि होता स्तृणीमहि देवव्यचा वि बर्हिः । (*ūrdhvo nāṃ gāturadhvare akāryūrdhvā śoceṃṣi prasthitā rajāṃsi | divo nā nābhā nyasādi hotā stṛṇīmahi devavyacā vi barhiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-4)

it is used in the sense "path"; in places such as

अरमा नो अदितिर्यज्ञॆयासोदब्धानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि । युयोत नो अनपत्यानि गंतोः, प्रजावान्नः पशुमाअस्तु गातुः ॥ (*aramā no aditiryajñèyāsodabdhāni varuṇasya vratāni | yuyota no anapatyāni gaṃtoḥ, prajāvānnaḥ paśumāastu gātuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-18)

it is explained स्तुवंतींद्रादीनत्रेति गातुर्गृहं । (*stuvaṃtīṃdrādīnatreti gāturgṛhaṃ |*), "the house in which Indra and other gods are praised", that is, a house.

### Printed p. 309
In

न्यस्मै देवी स्वधितिर्जिहीत इंद्राय गातुरुशतीव येमे । सं यदोजो युवते विश्वमाभिरनु स्वधान्ने क्षितयो नमंत । (*nyasmai devī svadhitirjihīta iṃdrāya gāturuśatīva yeme | saṃ yadojo yuvate viśvamābhiranu svadhānne kṣitayo namaṃta |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-10)

it means the earth (the word गातु (*gātu*) is read among the names of the earth) (Ni. 9-5). In Ṛks such as

स ते जानाति सुमतिं यविष्ठ य ईवते ब्रह्मणे गातुमैरत् । विश्वान्यस्मै सुदिनानि रायो द्युम्नान्यर्यो वि दुरो अभि द्यौत् । (*sa te jānāti sumatiṃ yaviṣṭha ya īvate brahmaṇe gātumairat | viśvānyasmai sudināni rāyo dyumnānyaryo vi duro abhi dyaut |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-6)

the word is also used as a synonym of praise: गीयते उच्चार्यते इति गातुः स्तोत्रं (*gīyate uccāryate iti gātuḥ stotraṃ*). In the present Ṛk the meaning taken is "going" and "the place of worship of the gods".

जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*)—At 1-165-15 Sāyaṇa has explained this word as जयशीलदानं (*jayaśīladānaṃ*). There is also a variant reading of this, जयशीलं दानं जीवनं वा (*jayaśīlaṃ dānaṃ jīvanaṃ vā*). How the sense "victory" or "bringing victory" arises for the word जीर (*jīra*) here is a matter worth considering. जीरदानु (*jīradānu*) is made of the two words जीर (*jīra*) and दानु (*dānu*). These two words are used separately in many places and give different meanings. Moreover, with the word जीर (*jīra*) other words such as अश्व (*aśva*) and अध्वर (*adhvara*) also combine, giving usages such as जीराश्व (*jīrāśva*) and जीराध्वर (*jīrādhvara*).

In the Ṛk

मनुष्वद्देव धीमहि प्रचेतसं जीर दूतममर्त्यं । (*manuṣvaddeva dhīmahi pracetasaṃ jīra dūtamamartyaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-44-11)

Sāyaṇa, giving the derivation of the word जीर (*jīra*), says that it is formed from the root जु (*ju*) (जोरी च (*jorī ca*), Uṇ. Sū. 2-181) and gives the meaning "(of enemies) causing loss of vigour". Here जीरं (*jīraṃ*) is an epithet of Agni. From this meaning it is understood that the derivation may also be possible from the root ज्ञ वयोहानौ (*jña vayohānau*). The author of the Nirukta has included the word जीर (*jīra*) among the names for "swift" (Ni. 3-9).

In the Ṛk

दिविस्पृशं यज्ञमस्माकमश्विना जीराध्वरं कृणुतं सुम्मनिष्टये । प्राचीनरश्मिमाहुतं धृतेन तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥ (*divispṛśaṃ yajñamasmākamaśvinā jīrādhvaraṃ kṛṇutaṃ summaniṣṭaye | prācīnaraśmimāhutaṃ dhṛtena taddevānāmavo adyā vṛṇīmahe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-36-6)

the Aśvin gods are prayed to make our rite जीराध्वर (*jīrādhvara*). Here जीराध्वर (*jīrādhvara*) means a sacrifice that is not obstructed by hindrances, is free from violence, and is completed swiftly.

### Printed p. 310
In places such as

पृषे ता निश्वा भुवना ववक्षीरे मिश्राय वा सदमा जीरदानवः । पृषदश्वासो अनवभ्रराधस ऋजिप्यासो न वयुनेषु धूर्षदः ॥ (*pṛṣe tā niśvā bhuvanā vavakṣīre miśrāya vā sadamā jīradānavaḥ | pṛṣadaśvāso anavabhrarādhasa ṛjipyāso na vayuneṣu dhūrṣadaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-4)

जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*) is an epithet of the Maruts; it means those who fulfil the sacrificer's wishes very swiftly. In the same way the compounds जीरात्वः (*jīrātvaḥ*) and जीरात्वं (*jīrātvaṃ*) are also epithets of Agni and other gods. Or they are sometimes epithets of their chariot. In Ṛks such as

आ वां रथं पुरुमायं मनोजुवं जीराश्वं यज्ञॆयं जीवसे हुवे । सहस्रकेतुं वनिनं शतद्वसुं श्रुष्टिवानं वरिवोधामभि प्रयः ॥ (*ā vāṃ rathaṃ purumāyaṃ manojuvaṃ jīrāśvaṃ yajñèyaṃ jīvase huve | sahasraketuṃ vaninaṃ śatadvasuṃ śruṣṭivānaṃ varivodhāmabhi prayaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-119-1)

the chariot of the Aśvin gods is described as having swiftly running horses.

In the same way the word दानु (*dānu*) also, used separately and as a compound, सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*), जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*), gives a meaning according to the context. From the context in which the author of the Nirukta cites it, it is understood that the word दानु (*dānu*) gives the meaning either "giver" or "demon". In explaining the Ṛk

स्टुपेय्यं पुरुवर्णसमृभ्यमिनतमपाप्त्य मास्तानां । आ दर्शते शवसा सप्त दासून् प्र साक्षते प्रतिमानानि भूरि ॥ (*sṭupeyyaṃ puruvarṇasamṛbhyaminatamapāptya māstānāṃ | ā darśate śavasā sapta dāsūn pra sākṣate pratimānāni bhūri ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-120-6)

the author of the Nirukta has said that the phrase सप्त दासून् (*sapta dāsūn*) means सप्तदातृन् इति वा सप्त दानवान् इति वा (*saptadātṛn iti vā sapta dānavān iti vā*), either "seven givers" or "seven Dānavas". But how, in such contexts, the sense "demon" is possible for the word दानु (*dānu*), Max Müller, indicating his own doubt, has said as follows:

It must be confessed that even the meaning of Danu is by no means quite clear. It is clear enough where it means Demon, II. 11. 18; II. 12 11 ; IV. 30.7 ; X. 120.6 ; The seven Demons. In I. 32.9; III. 30.8 Danu, Demon is applied to the mother of Vritra, the dark cloud; From this Danu we have the derivative Danava, meaning again Demon, why the demons conquered by Indra, were called Danu, is not clear, unless they were conceived originally as dark clouds, like Danu, the mother of Indra. Danu might mean wise or even powerful, for this meaning also is ascribed to Danu by the author of Unadi Sutras. [S. B. E. XXXII. P. 114-115]

### Printed p. 311
This scholar asks: दानु (*dānu*) is the name of an Asura woman, that is, of the mother of Vṛtra; her sons should be called दानव (*dānava*), so how did they come to be called दानु (*dānu*)? And it is understood from the Uṇādi sūtra that the meanings "power" and "wise" are also possible for this word. But the meaning "giver" is the more widely known.

Thus, if the word जीर (*jīra*) means "swift" and the word दानु (*dānu*) means "gift", then in the present Ṛk the meaning would have to be "swift gift". But Sāyaṇa has explained it as "victorious gift". Since the word जीर (*jīra*) is used in many places in the sense of "impelling", here it can be explained as "a gift that impels to victory". Commonly, the word जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*) occurs mostly as an epithet of the Maruts.

पृक्षे ता विश्वा भुवना ववक्षिरे मिश्राय ना सदमा जीरदानवः ॥ (*pṛkṣe tā viśvā bhuvanā vavakṣire miśrāya nā sadamā jīradānavaḥ ‖*) (Mi. Sē. 2-34-4) **NOTE**

In Ṛks such as this, जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*) meaning the Maruts is well known. And in

वृषा न क्रुद्धः पतॆयद्रजस्वा यो आर्यपत्नीरकृणोदिमा अपः । स सुन्वते मघवा जीरदानवेऽविंदज्योतिर्मनवे हविष्मते ॥ (*vṛṣā na kruddhaḥ patèyadrajasvā yo āryapatnīrakṛṇodimā apaḥ | sa sunvate maghavā jīradānave 'viṃdajyotirmanave haviṣmate ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-43-8)

and similar Ṛks, this word is also an epithet of the sacrificer who offers oblations and the like.

सुविताय—सुहिताय शोभनगमनाय वा (*suvitāya—suhitāya śobhanagamanāya vā*)—The wish is expressed that Indra's coming to our sacrificial hall may be for producing our welfare and for our having a good going. Yāska, in the Ṛk

आ रुद्रास इंद्रवंतः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गंतन । इयं वो अस्मत्पृति हर्यते मतिस्तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥ (*ā rudrāsa iṃdravaṃtaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gaṃtana | iyaṃ vo asmatpṛti haryate matistṛṣṇaje na diva utsā udanyave ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-57-1)

has shown the use of the word सुविताय (*suvitāya*) in the sense सुगुणाय कर्मणे (*suguṇāya karmaṇe*), "for an excellent rite". In the Ṛk

पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुविता कल्पयावहै । य एष स्वप्ननंतनोऽस्तमेषि पथा पुनर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः । (*punarehi vṛṣākape suvitā kalpayāvahai | ya eṣa svapnanaṃtano 'stameṣi pathā punarviśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-21)

the meaning of the word सुविता (*suvitā*) is explained as सुप्रसूतानि सुप्रवृत्तानि (*suprasūtāni supravṛttāni*).

### Printed p. 312
The meaning is explained thus: by Indra's grace we, the sacrificers, hope to obtain वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*), strength, इषं (*iṣaṃ*), food, and जेशवानुं (*jeśavānuṃ*), abundant capacity for drinking. **NOTE**

##### Grammar

- अस्मे — सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति विभक्तेः (षष्ठीबहुवचनस्य) शे आदेशः ।
- गातुम् — गै शब्दे इति धातुः । कमिमनिजनि (उ. सू. १-७२) इति तुप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति ।
- हरिवः — छंदसीरः (पा. सू. ८-२-१५) इति मतुपः मकारस्य वत्वम् । मतोरुः संबुष्टौ (पा. सू ८-३-१) इति संबुद्धौ रुत्वम् । आमंत्रितस्य च (पा. सू. ८-१-१९) इति निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- विदः — विद ज्ञाने इति धातुः । लेट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । इतश्चलोपः (पा. सू. ३-४-९७) इति इकारलोपः । लेटोडाटौ (पा. सू. ३-४ ९४) इति तस्य अडागमः । प्रत्ययसकारस्य रत्वविसर्गौ । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- ववृत्याः — वृतु वर्तने इति धातुः । लिजि व्यत्ययो बहुलं इति परस्मैपदप्रत्ययः भवति । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपि श्लुविकरणम् । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोः द्वित्वादि । सिपि यासुटागमः । तस्य जित्वविधानात् लघूपधगुणः न भवति । तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. सू. ८-१-२८) इति निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- सुविताय — इण् गत् इति धातुः । क्तप्रत्ययः । तन्वादीनां छंदसि बहुलमुपसंख्यानम् इति वचनेन उवजादेशः । गतिरनंतरः इति सूत्रेण पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते सूपमानात् क्तः (पा. सू. ६-२-१४५) इति उत्तरपदांतोदात्तस्वरः भवति ।

### Printed p. 313
## Sūkta 174 (Maṇḍala 1)

Introduction. The sūkta त्वं राजेति (*tvaṃ rājeti*) has ten Ṛks and is the tenth sūkta, Āgastya's, addressed to Indra, in Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says त्वं राजा दश (*tvaṃ rājā daśa*). In the Pṛṣṭha ṣaḷaha, at the increase of the stomas, the Hotṛ priests are to recite it for the sake of exceeding the stoma. The Āśvalāyana sūtra on this is: ऐंद्राणि त्रैष्टुभान्यमरुच्छज्ञान्यावसेरन् (*aiṃdrāṇi traiṣṭubhānyamarucchajñānyāvaseran*) (Ā. Sū. 7-12).

Anuvāda: This sūkta, "त्वं राजा (*tvaṃ rājā*)", is the tenth sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Agastya is the seer, Indra the deity, Triṣṭubh the metre. The Anukramaṇī says "त्वं राजा दश (*tvaṃ rājā daśa*)". At the Soma sacrifice called Pṛṣṭha, performed over six days, the mantras recited for the increase of the stomas are to be recited as this sūkta by the Ṛtvijs of the Hotṛ group, for the purpose of exceeding the stomas. On this point the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra has the sūtra ऐंद्राणि त्रैष्टुभान्यमरुच्छब्दान्यावपेरन् (*aiṃdrāṇi traiṣṭubhānyamarucchabdānyāvaperan*) (Ā. Śrau. 7-12).

Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 23; Sūkta 174. Aṣṭaka 2; Adhyāya 4; Vargas 16, 17. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Āgastya. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं राजें॑द्र॒ ये च॑ दे॒वा रक्षा॒ नृन्पा॒ह्य॑सुर॒ त्वम॒स्मान् ।  
> त्वं सत्प॑तिर्म॒घवा॑ न॒स्तरु॑त्र॒स्वं स॒त्यो वस॑वानः सहो॒दाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । राजा । इंद्र । ये । च । देवाः । रक्ष । नृन् । शाहि । असुर । त्वं । अस्मान् ।  
> त्वं । सत्पतिः । मघवा । नः । तरुत्रः । त्वं । सत्यः । वसवानः । सहदाः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 314

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं राजाधिपतिः सर्वस्य जगतः । किंच ये देवा मरुदादयः संति
> तेषामपि विशेषेण । अतो हे असुर शत्रुणां निरसितः त्वं नृनस्मान् कर्मनेत्यन्य
> जमानान्रक्ष । पालय । विशेषतोऽस्मानपि रक्ष । त्वं च सत्पतिः सतां सतः कर्मफलस्य
> वा पाता मघवा धनवान्नोऽस्माकं तरुत्रस्तारयिशा पापात् किंच त्वं सत्योऽबाध्यः
> सत्यफलो वा वसवानः स्वतेजसा सर्वं छादयन् वसूनि वा कुर्वन् स्तोतृभ्यः
> सहोदाः सहसो बलस्य दाता भवेति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you are the king, the overlord of the whole world, and especially of those gods, the Maruts and others, who exist. Therefore, O Asura, hurler-down of enemies, protect us, the sacrificers, the leaders of the rite; protect us in particular as well. You are the protector of the good (or of the fruit of the good rite), the wealthy one, our saviour from sin. You are true: unobstructable, or having true fruit. You are *vasavān*: covering all with your own radiance, or making wealth for the singers. You are the giver of might (sahas); "be" is the word to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- राजा (*rājā*)—lord (of the whole world)
- ये देवाः (*ye devāḥ*)—the gods (the Maruts and others) who exist (and especially their sovereign)
- असुर (*asura*)—O Indra, destroyer of enemies (therefore)
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—the sacrificers, leaders of rites
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us also
- रक्ष (*rakṣa*)—guard
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सत्पतिः (*satpatiḥ*)—lord of good men or of the fruit of rites
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—the possessor of wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- तरुत्रः (*tarutraḥ*)—one who carries (us) across (from sins)
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)—one free from obstruction, or one having true fruit
- वसवानः (*vasavānaḥ*)—one who covers everything with his own splendour, or one who provides wealth to the singers
- सहोदाः (*sahodāḥ*)—giver of strength
- (be)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you alone are the lord of the whole world together with the gods, the Maruts and the rest. O Indra, destroyer of enemies, protect the performers of the sacrifice and us. You are the lord of the fruit of rites, rich in wealth, remover of sin; grant (us) true fruit, wealth and strength.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You, Indra, are King: they who are gods (are subject) to you therefore, scatterer (of foes), do yau protect and cherish us men: you are the protector of the good, the possessor of wealth, the extricator of us (from sin): you are true, the invester (of all with your lustre), the giver of strength.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Indra's greatness is set out through a description of his qualities. त्वं राजा (*tvaṃ rājā*): Indra is addressed. Explaining that Indra is सर्वस्य जगतः अधिपतिः (*sarvasya jagataḥ adhipatiḥ*), the lord of the whole world, the text goes on, ये देवाः मरुदादयस्संति तेषामपि विशेषेण (*ye devāḥ marudādayassaṃti teṣāmapi viśeṣeṇa*): he is protector and lord even of the gods, the Maruts and the rest.
### Printed p. 315
*asura nṛn asmān rakṣa*: The word asura is listed among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-22), and is explained in Ni. 3-8: असुरा असुरताः स्थानेष्टस्ताः स्थानेभ्य इति वा अपि वा असुरिति प्राणनाम अस्तः शरीरे भवति तेन तद्वंतः (*asurā asuratāḥ sthāneṣṭastāḥ sthānebhya iti vā api vā asuriti prāṇanāma astaḥ śarīre bhavati tena tadvaṃtaḥ*). Sāyaṇa explains that Indra is an asura because he destroys enemies, and takes the meaning to be: may Indra protect us, the sacrificers who perform the sacrificial rites.

In the Purāṇas and elsewhere the word asura is a synonym of rākṣasa. In the Ṛksaṃhitā, however, the word is used in various senses. Asu means breath, intelligence, throwing, and many other meanings; the word asura is accordingly used according to these meanings, and they are to be applied as the context requires. In the Ṛk बृहच्छ्रवा असुरो बर्हणा कृतः पुरो हरिभ्यां वृषभो रथो हि षः । (*bṛhacchravā asuro barhaṇā kṛtaḥ puro haribhyāṃ vṛṣabho ratho hi ṣaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-3) the word asura is an epithet of Indra, just as in the present Ṛk. Here too, as stated in that Ṛk, one meaning is असुरः शत्रूणां निरसिता (*asuraḥ śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā*), "he who casts down enemies"; and, alternatively, असुः प्राणो बलं वा तद्वान् (*asuḥ prāṇo balaṃ vā tadvān*) with the affix ra in the sense of possession; or asavaḥ are breaths, and by that the waters are indicated: तान् राति ददातीति असुरः (*tān rāti dadātīti asuraḥ*), "he who gives them". (The Kannada also adds "one who looks at enemies".) Or, since asu means breath and strength, "one who has breath" or "one who has strength", or asavaḥ means waters, and so "Indra who gives them". Since Indra has such various powers, the word can be an epithet of Indra in all these meanings. Likewise in the Ṛk क्षयन्नस्मभ्यमसुर प्रचेता राजन्नेनांसि शिश्रथः कृतानि । (*kṣayannasmabhyamasura pracetā rājannenāṃsi śiśrathaḥ kṛtāni |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-14) Varuṇa is called asura, as अनिष्टक्षेपणशीलः (*aniṣṭakṣepaṇaśīlaḥ*), one who destroys what is unwelcome; and in the same sense, in त्वमग्ने रुद्रो असुरो महो दिवस्त्वं शर्धो मारुतं पृक्ष ईशिषे । (*tvamagne rudro asuro maho divastvaṃ śardho mārutaṃ pṛkṣa īśiṣe |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-6) the quality of Agni is described. Likewise, in वि सुपर्णो अंतरिक्षाण्यख्यद्गभीरवेपा असुरः सुनीथः । (*vi suparṇo aṃtarikṣāṇyakhyadgabhīravepā asuraḥ sunīthaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-7) asura means Sūrya, the giver of breath.
### Printed p. 316
In पृषद्योनिः पंचहोशा तृषोत्वतूर्तपंथा असुरो मयोभुः । (*pṛṣadyoniḥ paṃcahośā tṛṣotvatūrtapaṃthā asuro mayobhuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-1) it means Vāyu, the giver of breath. In places such as धृतप्रसत्तो असुरः सुशेवो रायो धर्ता धरुणो वस्तो आग्निः । (*dhṛtaprasatto asuraḥ suśevo rāyo dhartā dharuṇo vasto āgniḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-15-1) and न्यंग्नि सीददसुरो न होता हुवानो अत्र सुभगाय देवान् । (*nyaṃgni sīdadasuro na hotā huvāno atra subhagāya devān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-30-3) it is an epithet of Agni and others, "strong, powerful". In अस्मे वीरो मरुतः तुष्मस्य जनानां यो असुरो विधर्ता । (*asme vīro marutaḥ tuṣmasya janānāṃ yo asuro vidhartā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-24) and the like it means "intelligent"; in शतं कक्षीवा असुरस्य गोनां दिवि श्रवोऽजरमा ततान । (*śataṃ kakṣīvā asurasya gonāṃ divi śravo 'jaramā tatāna |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-2) "munificent"; in त्रिरुत्तमा दूणशा रोचनानि त्रयो राजंत्यसुरस्य वीराः । (*triruttamā dūṇaśā rocanāni trayo rājaṃtyasurasya vīrāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-56-8), अस्यति क्षिपति सर्वमित्यसुरः कालात्मा संवत्सरः (*asyati kṣipati sarvamityasuraḥ kālātmā saṃvatsaraḥ*), that is, time. In places such as यथा रुद्रस्य सूनवो दिवो वशंत्यसुरस्य वेधसः । (*yathā rudrasya sūnavo divo vaśaṃtyasurasya vedhasaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-20-17) it has the sense of cloud; and in Ṛks such as अनायधासो असुरा अदेवाश्चक्रेण ता अप वप ऋजेषिन् । (*anāyadhāso asurā adevāścakreṇa tā apa vapa ṛjeṣin |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-9) the asuras are demons belonging to the company of rākṣasas. In the present Ṛk the meaning is Indra, the one who casts down such rākṣasas.

सत्पतिः (*satpatiḥ*): सशां कर्मफलस्य वा पाता (*saśāṃ karmaphalasya vā pātā*). Sāyaṇa gives two meanings: Indra is the protector of good men, or of the fruit of the rites each has performed. Here *satām* may mean "of the sat", that is, of all beings whose nature is truth; or "of all good people". Explaining the special sense of this word, the scholar Max Muller says:
### Printed p. 317
"Satpati. Lord of men means Lord of real men, of heroes, and should not be translated as good lord (sat) by itself is frequently used in the sense of heroes, of men, physically rather than morally good." [S. B. E. XXXII]

He explains that the word means not merely protector of the people, but protector of people who are powerful and who show their valour in battles, and as examples he cites two Ṛks in which the word is used. First, in त्वमग्न इंद्रो वृषभः सतामसि त्वं विष्णुरुरुगायो नमस्यः । त्वं ब्रह्मा रयिविद्ब्रह्मणस्पते त्वं विधर्तः सचसे पुरंध्या । (*tvamagna iṃdro vṛṣabhaḥ satāmasi tvaṃ viṣṇururugāyo namasyaḥ | tvaṃ brahmā rayividbrahmaṇaspate tvaṃ vidhartaḥ sacase puraṃdhyā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-3), सतां वृषभः असि (*satāṃ vṛṣabhaḥ asi*) means "the hero among heroes". Likewise, in समत्सु त्वा शूर सतामुराणं प्रपथिंतमं परितंसयध्यै । सजोषस इंद्रं मदे क्षोणीः सूरिं चिद्ये अनुमदंति वाजैः ॥ (*samatsu tvā śūra satāmurāṇaṃ prapathiṃtamaṃ paritaṃsayadhyai | sajoṣasa iṃdraṃ made kṣoṇīḥ sūriṃ cidye anumadaṃti vājaiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-173-7), समत्सु शूर सतामुराणं (*samatsu śūra satāmurāṇaṃ*) means one who protects others in battle; and in the same way in the present Ṛk too the meaning can be "protector of heroic people".

मघवा तरुत्रः (*maghavā tarutraḥ*): Sāyaṇa says that Indra is wealthy and is our तारयिता पापात् (*tārayitā pāpāt*), one who protects us from sins.

सत्यः वसवानः सहोदाः (*satyaḥ vasavānaḥ sahodāḥ*): For the word satya the explanation given is अबाध्यः सत्यफलो (*abādhyaḥ satyaphalo*): one not subject to trouble arising from enemies, or one who gives the sacrificers fruit that does not fail. Where the same word satya is an epithet of Indra in some other places, its sense is explained as अबाध्यः सत्सु भवो (*abādhyaḥ satsu bhavo*): beyond obstruction, or one who dwells among good men. To be beyond obstruction he must not be untrue in nature but of the nature of truth and follow the path of truth.

Throughout the Ṛksaṃhitā the word satya is used with the sense of an excellent and moral worth and power. The acts performed by those who have such excellent worth are also of the nature of truth. Expressing this meaning, the Niruktakāra too gives the etymology of satya as follows:
### Printed p. 318
सत्यं कस्मात् सत्सु तायते सत्यभवं भवतीति वा (*satyaṃ kasmāt satsu tāyate satyabhavaṃ bhavatīti vā*) (Ni. 2-13)

According to this etymology, satya is so called because it spreads among good people or because it arises from good people. Since fruit of the nature of truth too must come to the good alone, the Ṛk shows the sense that Indra is the giver of fruit that is fitting to the true acts of the virtuous and is of the nature of the good. Since the word satya is used here with reference both to act and to fruit, one must explain what universal principle this idea reflects in both these contexts.

ते देवा उत्सृज्यान्यतं । सत्यमन्वालेभिरे (*te devā utsṛjyānyataṃ | satyamanvālebhire*) (Śa. Brā. 9-5-1-13)

तद्यत्तत्सत्यं । त्रयीसा विद्या ते देवा अब्रुवन् यज्ञं कृत्वेदं सत्यं तनवामहा इति । (*tadyattatsatyaṃ | trayīsā vidyā te devā abruvan yajñaṃ kṛtvedaṃ satyaṃ tanavāmahā iti |*) (Śa. Brā. 9-5-1-18)

The gods gave up untruth and firmly took hold of truth. Since the Vedas called the Trayī are of the nature of this truth, the gods wished: "Let us perform the rites enjoined by the Veda and spread truth." Beyond showing in this way the essential connection between truth and conduct, it is hoped that through such pure performance of rites one can obtain well-being that is complete and endowed with all prosperity.

नाभिर्युतस्य सप्रथा इति । सत्यं वा ऋतं वा ऋतं सत्यस्य नाभिः सप्रथा इत्येवैतदाह स नो विश्वायुः सप्रथा इति स नः सर्वायुः इत्येवैतदाह। (*nābhiryutasya saprathā iti | satyaṃ vā ṛtaṃ vā ṛtaṃ satyasya nābhiḥ saprathā ityevaitadāha sa no viśvāyuḥ saprathā iti sa naḥ sarvāyuḥ ityevaitadāha|*) (Śa. Brā. 14-3-1-18)

By such explanations the identity of truth with the order of the universe is shown, and, because by following such truth and performing true acts full life is obtained as their fruit, the relation of cause and effect between good fruit and good act is declared. Since even for the performance of acts of the nature of truth it is essential to know the order of the universe and the nature of the gods who cause it, that knowledge too, it is made clear in many contexts, is possible only through truth.

सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरभिज्ञा सत्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन् । सत्यं तदिंद्रो दशभिर्दशग्वैः सूर्यं विवेद तमसि क्षियंतं । (*sakhā ha yatra sakhibhirnavagvairabhijñā satvabhirgā anugman | satyaṃ tadiṃdro daśabhirdaśagvaiḥ sūryaṃ viveda tamasi kṣiyaṃtaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-5)

त इद्देवानां सधमाद आसन् (*ta iddevānāṃ sadhamāda āsan*) … *uṣāsaṃ* **NOTE** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-76-4)

### Printed p. 319
The Ṛks beginning *satyaṃ tadiṃdro* … *kṣiyaṃtaṃ* **NOTE** and the rest contain many sentences pointing to earlier occasions on which all the seers knew the true nature of the deities, who are of the nature of truth, performed rites, and obtained wealth as the fruit of doing so. Along with this goes the prayer that good may come to us through truth alone.

अधा यथा नः पितरः परासः प्रत्नासो आग्न ऋतमाशुषाणाः । शुचीदयन्दीधितिमुक्थशासः क्षामा भिंदंतो आरुणीरप व्रन् ॥ (*adhā yathā naḥ pitaraḥ parāsaḥ pratnāso āgna ṛtamāśuṣāṇāḥ | śucīdayandīdhitimukthaśāsaḥ kṣāmā bhiṃdaṃto āruṇīrapa vran ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2-16)

In prayers of this kind — "as our fathers obtained good fruits through sacrifice of the nature of truth, so now too may all our rites yield true fruits, तत्सत्यमस्तु (*tatsatyamastu*)" — the true nature of Agni and the other deities, whose law is truth, is also described.

अजो न क्षां दाधार पृ, वीं तस्तंभ द्यां मंत्रेभिः सत्यैः । (*ajo na kṣāṃ dādhāra pṛ, vīṃ tastaṃbha dyāṃ maṃtrebhiḥ satyaiḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-67-5)

कविमग्निमुप स्तुहि सत्यधर्माणमध्वरे । देवममीवचातनं ॥ (*kavimagnimupa stuhi satyadharmāṇamadhvare | devamamīvacātanaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-7)

देवो न यः सविता सत्यमन्मा क्रत्वा निपाति वृजनानि विश्वा । पुरुप्रशस्तो अमतिर्न सत्य आत्मेव शेवो दिधिषाय्यो भूत् ॥ (*devo na yaḥ savitā satyamanmā kratvā nipāti vṛjanāni viśvā | purupraśasto amatirna satya ātmeva śevo didhiṣāyyo bhūt ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-73-2)

In these and many other places Agni and the other deities are described as sustaining the earth and the other worlds through truth alone and as carrying out the protection of the worlds; it is also made known that human beings too must follow that same path of truth. In the present Ṛk, from that same point of view, Indra is described as if his identity with truth were being stated.

The word वसवानः (*vasavānaḥ*) is explained as "Indra covers everything with his own splendours", or "he who bestows wealth on those who praise him"; and the word सहोदाः (*sahodāḥ*) is explained as one who bestows strength on the sacrificers and on those who praise him. The word सहः (*sahaḥ*) is read among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of water (Ni. 2-24).

- रक्ष — रक्ष पालने । धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधो भवति । शप् पित्त्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते । द्व्यचोतस्तिजः (पा. सू. ६-३-१३५) इति दीर्घो भवति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, at the time when you split the cities of the asuras connected with Vṛtra, you made their subjects, who were of मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*) (forbearing speech), दनः (*danaḥ*) (tamed) in such a way that there was शर्म (*śarma*) (happiness); दनः (*danaḥ*) means "you tamed", this being a form of the root दमेरिदं रूपं (*dameridaṃ rūpaṃ*). Or else, by transposition of letters, it is नदः (*nadaḥ*): you made the asura subjects utter a most fearful sound. When was this? यत् (*yat*) — when you split the seven cities, शारदीः (*śāradīḥ*) (new, fresh). Or else शारदीः (*śāradīḥ*) indicates a year: cities that had been made firm for a whole year. The change of person is noted: दर्त् (*dart*) stands for "you split", from the root दृ (*dṛ*).

Having done so, O अनवद्य (*anavadya*) (Indra, who has no blame of timidity), you set in motion the flowing waters, that is, the tanks and the like in their fortress-places that had water as their support, and broke them. Having thus split the cities, for Purukutsa, a king of that name, ever young, you रंधीः (*raṃdhīḥ*) — accomplished the end of, that is, slew — the asura named Vṛtra. This is the historical (aitihāsika) account.

According to the Nirukta tradition: O Indra, you made the subjects who are in the form of rain, मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*) (endowed with the sound of forbearing), दनः (*danaḥ*), that is, you made them sound, meaning you made them rain. When? When you split the seven cities, शारदीः (*śāradīḥ*) — the clouds of creeping nature, fresh, which fill the world with rain. Then, O अनवद्य (*anavadya*), you set the waters flowing, of flowing nature, in the form of channels and the like. Afterwards, for the young Purukutsa you slew Vṛtra, the principal cloud. This meaning is well known from other mantras such as त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र सप्त युध्यन् (*tvaṃ ha tyadiṃdra sapta yudhyan*) (Ṛ. 1-63-7). Yāska has explained it thus: दनो दानमनसो नो मनुष्यानिंद्र मृदुवाचः कुरु (*dano dānamanaso no manuṣyāniṃdra mṛduvācaḥ kuru*) (Ni. 6-31) — "make us men of generous mind and gentle speech, O Indra".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- शारदीः (*śāradīḥ*)—new (made firm, bound for one year)
- सप्तपुरः (*saptapuraḥ*)—the seven cities (of the asuras)
- दर्त् (*dart*)—you split
- तदा (*tadā*)—then
- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*)—of gentle speech (praying for forgiveness)
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—the subjects (of those cities)
- शर्म (*śarma*)—so that there is happiness
- दनः (*danaḥ*)—you made humble (you made a most fearful sound)
- अनंतर (*anaṃtara*)—afterwards
- हे अनवद्य (*he anavadya*)—O blameless Indra
- अर्णाः (*arṇāḥ*)—of flowing nature
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters, the tanks and the like situated in their fortresses
- ऋणोः (*ṛṇoḥ*)—you sent forth (you broke them)
- किंच (*kiṃca*)—and
- यूने (*yūne*)—young
- पुरुकुत्साय (*purukutsāya*)—for the king named Purukutsa
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the asura named Vṛtra
- रंधीः (*raṃdhīḥ*)—you destroyed
- [Or: हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra; यत् (*yat*)—when; सप्त (*sapta*)—seven, of creeping nature; शारदीः (*śāradīḥ*)—new; पुरः (*puraḥ*)—the clouds that fill the world (with rain); दर्त् (*dart*)—you split; तदा (*tadā*)—then; मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*)—

### Printed p. 322
- distinguished by a gentle sound; विशः (*viśaḥ*)—the subjects in the form of rain; शर्म दनः (*śarma danaḥ*)—you made them submissive so that there is happiness (for the world), you made it rain; हे अनवद्य (*he anavadya*)—O Indra, unblamed; अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)—of flowing nature; अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters; ऋणोः (*ṛṇoḥ*)—you sent forth (in the form of rivers and the like); afterwards यूने पुरुकुत्साय (*yūne purukutsāya*)—for the youthful Purukutsa; वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the principal cloud; रंधीः (*raṃdhīḥ*)—you destroyed.]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when you destroyed the seven cities of the enemies, you made their subjects, who sued for pardon, humble (or: you split the clouds and brought about rain). O blameless Indra, you sent forth the flowing waters; for the youthful Purukutsa you also destroyed the asura Vṛtra.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You have humbled the people, suing for pardon when you had destroyed their seven new cities: you the irreproachable, have dispersed the flowing waters : you have destroyed Vritra for the sake of the youthful Purukutsa.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa has given one kind of meaning from the historical point of view and another from the Nirukta point of view. The first meaning is the one given here as historical.

मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*) — मर्षणवचनाः (*marṣaṇavacanāḥ*). He has explained that this word is used as an epithet of the word विशः (*viśaḥ*). Addressing Indra, he explains: पुरभेदनसमये मर्षणवचनाः तदीयाः प्रजाः सुखं यथा भवति तथा दनः अदमयः (*purabhedanasamaye marṣaṇavacanāḥ tadīyāḥ prajāḥ sukhaṃ yathā bhavati tathā danaḥ adamayaḥ*) — when he destroyed the towns of the asuras connected with the asura Vṛtra, the inhabitants, the subjects there, spoke gentle words, and he acted in such a way that they lived in happiness. Or else, यद्वावर्णव्यत्ययः अनदः असुरप्रजाः अतिभयंकरशब्दमकरोः (*yadvāvarṇavyatyayaḥ anadaḥ asuraprajāḥ atibhayaṃkaraśabdamakaroḥ*): he explains दॆनः (*dènaḥ*) as a form of the root दमु (*damu*). In the second explanation, for the word नदः (*nadaḥ*) produced by transposing the letters of the word दनः (*danaḥ*), the meaning given is that at the time when Indra destroyed the cities of the subjects of the asura Vṛtra, he made a fearful sound, so that those subjects spoke gentle words, so that happiness came to them, and so that a state of existence (conduct) was brought about among them.**NOTE**

शारदीः सप्तपुरः दर्त् (*śāradīḥ saptapuraḥ dart*) — he explains that the word शारदीः (*śāradīḥ*) is used in the sense of "new" and also in the sense of "year". The meaning is explained thus: Indra split and destroyed

### Printed p. 323
the seven cities of the asuras, newly built, or made so firm that for a year even they could not be broken.

अनवद्य अर्णाः अपः ऋणोः (*anavadya arṇāḥ apaḥ ṛṇoḥ*) — he explains the word अनवद्य (*anavadya*) as one who is free from the blame in the form of timidity (fear), and with this word Indra is addressed. After Indra, fearless, destroyed the cities of the enemies, तदीय दुर्गस्थानानि उदकात्रयाणि तटाकादीन् प्रावर्तयः (*tadīya durgasthānāni udakātrayāṇi taṭākādīn prāvartayaḥ*) — he explains that he made the fortress regions of the asuras filled with flowing waters, and changed them into another form in which there were tanks and the like as supports of the waters.

पुरुकुत्साय वृत्रं रंधीः (*purukutsāya vṛtraṃ raṃdhīḥ*) — he makes clear that Indra killed the asura Vṛtra for the king Purukutsa and so did the king a service.

In the meaning that follows the view of the Nirukta authors: addressing Indra, for the word वितः (*vitaḥ*)**NOTE** वृष्टिरूपाः प्रजाः (*vṛṣṭirūpāḥ prajāḥ*) — the subjects in the form of rain — मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*), मर्षणध्वनि (*marṣaṇadhvani*): he made them endowed with the sound of forbearance, and through them brought about sound and rain-water. For the words in the sentence सप्तपुरः शारदीर्दत् (*saptapuraḥ śāradīrdat*) the meaning given is सर्पणस्वभावान् प्रत्यग्रान् वृष्टा जागरूकान् मेघानदारयः (*sarpaṇasvabhāvān pratyagrān vṛṣṭā jāgarūkān meghānadārayaḥ*): Indra split the clouds, of a wandering nature, new, alert in pouring down the waters of rain. अनवद्य अर्णाः अपः ऋणोः अरणस्वभावा अपः प्रावर्तयः कुल्यादिरूपेण (*anavadya arṇāḥ apaḥ ṛṇoḥ araṇasvabhāvā apaḥ prāvartayaḥ kulyādirūpeṇa*) — for अनवद्य (*anavadya*) the meaning is explained as before. The meaning stated is that Indra poured down the rain-waters so that waters of a nature to move in the form of a flood flow in the form of canals. In the sentence यूने पुरुकुत्साय वृत्रं रंधीः (*yūne purukutsāya vṛtraṃ raṃdhīḥ*) the word वृत्र (*vṛtra*) is given the meaning "cloud": Indra split the cloud for the young king Purukutsa and caused rain to come.

त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र सप्त युध्यन् पुरो वज्रिन् पुरुकुत्साय दर्दः । बर्हि र्न यत्सुदासे वृथा वर्गंडो राजन् वरिवः पूरवे कः ॥ (*tvaṃ ha tyadiṃdra sapta yudhyan puro vajrin purukutsāya dardaḥ | barhi rna yatsudāse vṛthā vargaṃḍo rājan varivaḥ pūrave kaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-7)

He explains that this same meaning is established in this Ṛk.**NOTE**

The Nirukta authors, citing this very Ṛk, have explained the word मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*) by the meaning दानमनसो नो मनुष्यानिंद्र मृदुवाचः कुरु (*dānamanaso no manuṣyāniṃdra mṛduvācaḥ kuru*) (Ni. 6-31). The Nirukta authors have described the petition that Indra may make the sacrificers

### Printed p. 324
gentle in speech and also inclined in mind to the practice of giving.

It is known from the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa that the king Purukutsa belonged to the Aikṣvāku line.

पुरुकुत्सो दौगृहेणेज ऐक्ष्वाको राजा (*purukutso daugṛheṇeja aikṣvāko rājā*)
(Śa. Brā. 13-5-405)**NOTE**

This sentence says that the king Purukutsa, born in the Aikṣvāku line, performed the aśvamedha of the Daurgāha kind. This same matter is indicated in the Ṛk

अस्माकमत्र पितरस्त आसन्तप्त ऋषयो दौर्गृहे बध्यमाने (*asmākamatra pitarasta āsantapta ṛṣayo daurgṛhe badhyamāne*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-42-8)

But in the Ṛk cited, Sāyaṇa has taken the word दौर्गह (*daurgaha*) as a patronymic name and explained it as दुर्गहस्य पुत्रे पुरुकुत्से (*durgahasya putre purukutse*).

त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र सप्त युध्यन्सुरो वज्रन्पुरुकुत्साय दर्दः । बर्हिर्न यत्सुदासे वृथा वर्गंहो राजन्वरिवः पूरवे कः ॥ (*tvaṃ ha tyadiṃdra sapta yudhyansuro vajranpurukutsāya dardaḥ | barhirna yatsudāse vṛthā vargaṃho rājanvarivaḥ pūrave kaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-7)

On the strength of this Ṛk it is known that he was a contemporary of the king Sudāsa.

सनेम तेवसा नव्य इंद्र प्र पूरवः स्तवंत एना यज्ञैः । सप्त यत्पुरः शर्म शारदीर्द्धर्दन् दासीकॆ पुरुकुत्साय शिक्षन् । (*sanema tevasā navya iṃdra pra pūravaḥ stavaṃta enā yajñaiḥ | sapta yatpuraḥ śarma śāradīrddhardan dāsīkè purukutsāya śikṣan |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-10)

Here Purukutsa is said to be a king of the people called Pūru. He is also said to have conquered all the Dāsas. It is also known that he had a son named Trasadasyu. But it appears that this son may have been born after the death of Purukutsa.

पुरुकुत्सानी हि वामदाशद्धव्येभिरिंद्रावरुणा नमोभिः । अथा राजानं त्रसदस्युमस्या वृत्रहणं ददथुरर्धदेवं ॥ (*purukutsānī hi vāmadāśaddhavyebhiriṃdrāvaruṇā namobhiḥ | athā rājānaṃ trasadasyumasyā vṛtrahaṇaṃ dadathurardhadevaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-42-9)

In this it is said that when the wife of Purukutsa satisfied Indra and Varuṇa with oblations and praises, they granted that she should bear a son named Trasadasyu. On this basis there is a story that after Purukutsa died in battle, his wife prayed to Indra and Varuṇa and bore a son named Trasadasyu.

#### Ṛk 2 (continued)

##### Grammar

- दनः — दमु उपशमे इति धातुः । लज् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थको धातुः । बहुलं छंदस्य (पा. सू. ६-४-७५) इति अडागमो न भवति । अथवा णद अव्यक्ते शब्दे इति धातुः । छांदसो वर्णव्यत्ययः जातः । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । शप् अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- मृध्रवाचः — मृध्रा वाक् येषां ते । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- दर्त् — द्य विदारणे इति धातुः । लज् । व्यत्ययो बहुलं इति सिपः तिप् भवति । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः इति धातोः इकः गुणः । र परः भवति । रात् सस्य (पा. सू. ८-२-२४) इति संयोगांतलोपो न भवति । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्‌योगेऽपि इति अडागमो न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- ऋणोः — ऋणु गतौ इति धातुः । तनादिः । लज् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । इकारलोपः । तनादिकृञ्भ्यउः (पा. सू. ३-१-७९) इति उ विकरणम् । सिप्निमित्तं तस्य गुणः । छांदसत्वात् अडागमो न भवति । विकरणस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- अपः — द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् । ऊडिदं पदादि (पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- यूने — युवन् शब्दः । चतुर्थ्येकवचने परे श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धिते (पा. सू. ६-४-१३३) इति संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपं च ।
- रंधीः — रध हिंसा संराद्योः इति धातुः । लुज् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । इकारलोपः । छ्लेः सिचादेशः । अर्धधातुक— (पा. सू. ७-२-३५) इति तस्य इडागमः । अस्तिसिचोऽपृक्ते (पा. सू. ७-३-६६) इति प्रत्ययस्य ईडागमः । इटईटि (पा. सू. ८-२-२८) इति सूत्रेण सिचो लोपः । रधिजभोरचि (पा. सू. ७-१-६१) इति धातोः नुमागमः । छांदसत्वात् अडागमो न भवति । अतिजंतपरत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अजा॒ वृत॑ इंद्र॒ शूर॑पत्नी॒र्द्यां च॒ येभिः॑ पुरुहूत नू॒नं ।  
> रक्षो॑ अ॒ग्निम॒शुषं॒ तूर्व॑याणं सिं॒हो न दमे॒ अपां॑सि॒ वस्तोः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अज । वृतः । इंद्र । शूरपत्नीः । द्यां । च । येभिः । पुरुहूत । नूनं ।  
> रक्षो इति । अग्निं । अशुषं । तूर्वयाणं । सिंहः । न । दमे । अपांसि । वस्तोः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र शूरपत्नीः शूरै रक्षोभिः पालिता वृतः । वर्तंत आस्तिति वृतोऽसुरपुरीः । यद्वा । शूरा यजमानाः । तैः पालिता वृतो वेदिभूमाः । अज ।
> गच्छ जेतुं । तथा कृत्वा द्यां च नूनमवश्यमज । किं त्वमेक एव न । हे पुरुहूत
> बहुभिर्बहुधा वाहूतेंद्र येभिर्मरुदादिभिरनुगतोऽसि तैः सहितः सन् । तथा
> कृत्वाशुषमाशोषयितारमशांतं वा तूर्वयाणं तूर्णगमनमग्निं वैद्युतं
> होमाधारं वाग्निं रक्षो । रक्षस्यॆव । किमर्थं रक्षणमिति उच्यते । दमे गृहेऽपांसि कर्माणि कुर्वन् वस्तोर्वस्तुं । यद्वा । वासयितुं स्थापयितुं ।
> कारयितुमित्यर्थः । यज्ञद्विट्टु हतेश्वग्नौ सुस्थिरे सति यागाद्यनुष्ठानपरः
> स्थास्सामीत्यर्थः । रक्षणे दृष्टांतः । सिंह इव । स यथा स्वात्रयभूतं वनं
> गजाद्युपद्रवपरिहारेण रक्षति तद्वत् । असुरपुरभंगगमने वा दृष्टांतः । सिंहो
> यथा निर्भयो विरोधिमृगान् हंतुं धावति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, go to the वृतः (*vṛtaḥ*), the शूरपत्नीः (*śūrapatnīḥ*)": that is, the cities of the Asuras, which are protected by heroic demons and in which they dwell (वर्तंत (*vartaṃta*)). Or else: शूरा (*śūrā*) are the sacrificers; the वृतः (*vṛtaḥ*) protected by them are the sacrificial altar-grounds. अज (*aja*) means "go in order to conquer", and having done so, go also to heaven without fail. Indra is not to go alone: he is पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*), called by many or in many ways, and he is to go together with the Maruts and others by whom he is followed. Having so gone, he is to protect Agni (the lightning fire, or the fire that is the support of the oblation), who is अशुषं (*aśuṣaṃ*) (a drier-up, or unappeased) and तूर्वयाणं (*tūrvayāṇaṃ*) (swift in going). दमे (*dame*) is "in the house"; अपांसि (*apāṃsi*) is "rites"; so Agni is to be protected so that, performing rites in the house, he may be वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*), to dwell; or else to be established, to be made to act. The meaning is: when the foes of the sacrifice are slain and Agni is firmly settled, the sacrificer says he will be intent on performing sacrifices and the like. The example for protecting is the lion: as he protects the forest that is his own refuge by warding off the harassment of elephants and others. Or else, for the going to break the cities of the Asuras, the example is: as a lion fearlessly runs to kill hostile beasts.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) इंद्र (*(he) iṃdra*)—O Indra
- शूरपत्नीः (*śūrapatnīḥ*)—protected by heroic demons
- वृतः (*vṛtaḥ*)—their dwelling-places, the cities of the Asuras
- सिंहः न (*siṃhaḥ na*)—as a lion fearlessly confronts other animals
- अज (*aja*)—set out (in order to conquer). [Or else शूरपत्नीः (*śūrapatnīḥ*)—protected by the sacrificers; वृतः (*vṛtaḥ*)—(toward) the altar-grounds; अज (*aja*)—go] (afterwards)
- द्यां च (*dyāṃ ca*)—to the world of heaven also
- नूनं (अज) (*nūnaṃ (aja)*)—(go) without fail
- हे पुरुहूत (*he puruhūta*)—O Indra, called by many or in many ways
- येभिः (*yebhiḥ*)—accompanied by those followers of yours, the Maruts and others, who are with you
- (अज) (*(aja)*)—go to both the places mentioned above; afterwards
- अशुषं (*aśuṣaṃ*)—the drier-up, or unappeased
- तूर्वयाणं (*tūrvayāṇaṃ*)—swift in going
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—the lightning fire or the sacrificial fire
- दमे (*dame*)—in the house
- अपांसि (*apāṃsi*)—performing rites
- वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)—in order to dwell. [Or else अपांसि (*apāṃsi*)—rites; वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)—in order to establish]
- सिंहः न (*siṃhaḥ na*)—as a lion protects the forest that is his own refuge by removing harassment and the like
- रक्षो (*rakṣo*)—protect

### Printed p. 327

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, called in many ways or by many, accompanied by your followers the Maruts and others, set out to conquer the cities of the Asuras protected by demons, as a lion boldly rushes in among other animals; from there go to the world of heaven also; and establish and protect the swift and unappeased sacrificial fire so that it may be favourable for the performance of rites in the houses.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Go to the cities inhabited by the Rakshasas, and thence to heaven (attended), receiver of many sacrifices, by those who (attend you). Defend, like a lion, the untamed, quick-moving Agni, that he may abide in his dwelling, fulfilling his functions.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शूरपत्निः (*śūrapatniḥ*)—The meaning of this word is explained as used in two senses. In the first, शूरैः रक्षोभिः पालिताः (*śūraiḥ rakṣobhiḥ pālitāḥ*): those protected by heroic demons; and वर्तंते आस्थिति वृतः (*vartaṃte āsthiti vṛtaḥ*): the Asura cities, the places where the demons dwell. In the second, शूराः यजमानाः तैः पालिताः वृतः वेदिभूमिः (*śūrāḥ yajamānāḥ taiḥ pālitāḥ vṛtaḥ vedibhūmiḥ*): शूर (*śūra*) is taken to mean the sacrificers, and the sacrificial altars protected by them are meant. It is explained that Indra should journey toward the cities protected by Asuras, or toward the altar protected by the sacrificers.
Indra is addressed by the word पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*), explained as पुरुभिः बहुधा ना आहूत (*purubhiḥ bahudhā nā āhūta*): Indra is called in many ways by many sacrificers. येभिः द्यां च नूनं अज (*yebhiḥ dyāṃ ca nūnaṃ aja*): since Indra is always with the Maruts, the sacrificers' wish is expressed that with them he conquer the Asura cities, or come to the sacrificial hall, accept the oblation and reach द्यां (*dyāṃ*), heaven.
अशुषं (*aśuṣaṃ*) and तूर्वयाणं (*tūrvayāṇaṃ*) are both used as epithets of the word अग्निं (*agniṃ*). With अशोषयितारं अशांतं वा (*aśoṣayitāraṃ aśāṃtaṃ vā*) the quality of Agni is described: he dries up everything completely and does not grow calm; and he is swift and pervading in his going. It is explained that अग्निं (*agniṃ*), possessed of such qualities, may be the lightning fire or the terrestrial fire that is the support of the sacrifice in which oblations are offered; and the wish is expressed that Indra protect this Agni.

### Printed p. 328
दमे अपांसि वस्तोः (*dame apāṃsi vastoḥ*)—गृहे कर्माणि कुर्वन् वस्तुं । यज्ञा वासयितुं स्थापयितुं कारयितुं (*gṛhe karmāṇi kurvan vastuṃ | yajñā vāsayituṃ sthāpayituṃ kārayituṃ*) **NOTE**. The word दमे (*dame*) is stated among the names of the house (Ni. 3-13). The word अपः (*apaḥ*) is read among the names of rites (Ni. 3-2). The word वस्तो (*vasto*) explains the sense of dwelling, of obtaining a settled state. The meaning described here is: while Agni is comfortably in the sacrificial altar, Indra's protection is indispensable so that sacrifices and other rites may be performed by the sacrificers; and the sacrificer's hope is made plain: यज्ञद्विट्टु हतेषु अग्नौ सुस्थिरे यागाद्यनुष्ठानपरः स्थास्यामि (*yajñadviṭṭu hateṣu agnau susthire yāgādyanuṣṭhānaparaḥ sthāsyāmi*).
The sentence सिंहः इव (*siṃhaḥ iva*) is stated as the comparison for the protection given by Indra. In the protection given by the lion, the forest, the lion's dwelling, serves to ward off the harassment caused by elephants and others. Likewise the protection of the sacrifice performed by the sacrificers serves to destroy the harassment of the Asuras, the obstructers of sacrifice; this meaning is described by way of an example.
In the second sense this sentence is, as he says, असुर भंगगमने वा दृष्टांतः (*asura bhaṃgagamane vā dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ*): an example of Indra's going in a fierce mood to destroy the Asuras; and सिंहो यथा निर्भयो विरोधिमृगान् हंतुं धावति तद्वत् (*siṃho yathā nirbhayo virodhimṛgān haṃtuṃ dhāvati tadvat*)—as a lion, without any fear, goes to destroy the beasts that are its enemies, so Indra, fearless, travels to subdue the Asuras; so the meaning is explained.

##### Grammar

- अजा — अज गतिक्षेपणयोः इति धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । द्वचोतस्तिजः (पा. सू. ६-३-१३५) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
- वृतः — क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- येभिः — यच्छब्दः । भिस् परे बहुलं छंदसि इति ऐस्भावस्य विकल्पत्वात् एत्वम् ।
- पुरुहूत — पुरुभिः हूतः पुरुहूतः । संबुद्धौ आमंत्रितनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- रक्षो — रक्ष पालने इति धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- तूर्वयाणम् — तूर्वं यानं यस्य । तम् । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
