- अपांसि — आषः कर्माख्यायाम् (उ सू. ४-६४७) इति असुन् प्रत्ययः । ह्रस्वः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- वस्तोः — वस निवासे इति धातुः । बहुलग्रहणात् तुमर्थे तोसुन् प्रत्ययः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१६९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । कृन्मेजंतः इति एजंतत्वात् अव्ययसंज्ञा भवति ।

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शेष॒न्नु त इं॑द्र॒ सस्मि॒न्नोनौ॒ प्रश॑स्तये॒ पवी॑रवस्य म॒ह्ना ।  
> सृ॒जदर्णां॒स्यव॒ यद्यु॒धा गास्तिष्ठ॒द्धरी॑ धृष॒ता मृ॑ष्ट॒ वाजा॑न् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शेषन् । नु । ते । इंद्र । सस्मिन् । योन् । प्रशस्तये । पवीरवस्य । मह्ना ।  
> सृजन् । अर्णांसि । अव । यत् । युधा । गाः । तिष्ठत् । हरी इति । धृषता । मृष्ट ।  
> वाजान् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते शत्रवः सस्मिन् सर्वस्मिन् समाने वा योन् स्वकीये
> स्थाने०तरिक्षे वा । योनिरंतरिक्षं । नु क्षिप्रं शेषन् । शेरतां ॥ शीजतो लेट्यडागमः।
> व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥ किमर्थ० । प्रशस्तये प्रशंसनाय
> त्वत्सुतये । त्वन्महिमज्ञापनायेत्यर्थः । किं सेवनादिसाधनेनेति आह । पवीरवस्य
> कुलिशस्य कुलिशशब्दस्य वा मह्ना महिम्ना । त्वद्वज्रप्रहारेण हता मेघाः शत्रवो
> वा तत्रैव शेरते निपातेन पलायंत इत्यर्थः । किंच यद्यदा युधा प्रहरणसाधनेनायुधेन युद्धेन वा गाः गच्छसि तदाणांस्युदकान्यव सृजत् । अवासृजः ।
> अवाङ्मुखमपातयः ॥ पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ तदर्थ० हरी अश्व तिष्ठत् । अध्यतिष्ठः ॥
> अत्रापि पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ यद्वा । यदा हरी अधितिष्ठसि तदावासृजः । अथैवं कृत्वा
> वाजानन्नानि सस्यादिलक्षणानि धृषता धर्षकेण सामर्थ्येन मृष्ट । शोधय ।
> प्रवर्धयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, let your foes (the clouds) lie down quickly सस्मिन् योन् (*sasmin yon*), in their own place or in the sky." सस्मिन् (*sasmin*) is "in all" or "in the same"; योनि (*yoni*) is the sky. शेषन् (*śeṣan*) is "let them lie"; the imperfect-like form is a Vedic variation of person and parasmaipada, with सिप् (*sip*) by the rule on its variable occurrence. For what purpose? प्रशस्तये (*praśastaye*): for praising you, to make known your greatness; not by service and other means. पवीरवस्य (*pavīravasya*) is of the thunderbolt, or of the word कुलिश (*kuliśa*); मह्ना (*mahnā*) is "by the greatness". The clouds or foes struck down by the blow of your thunderbolt lie there, or flee at its fall. Moreover, when you go with a weapon or in battle, you send the waters down (अवासृजः (*avāsṛjaḥ*), made to fall downward; a change of person). For that purpose you mount your two bay horses (तिष्ठत् (*tiṣṭhat*) for अध्यतिष्ठः (*adhyatiṣṭhaḥ*); again a change of person). Or else: when you mount the two bays, then you send the waters down. Having done so, मृष्ट (*mṛṣṭa*): cleanse, that is, increase, the foods (वाजान् (*vājān*)), such as grain and the like, by your daring power (धृषता (*dhṛṣatā*)).

### Printed p. 330

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) इंद्र (*(he) iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—those foes of yours (the clouds)
- सस्मिन् (*sasmin*)—all, or the same
- योन् (*yon*)—in their own place, or (in the cloud) in the sky
- पवीरवस्य (*pavīravasya*)—of the thunderbolt weapon, or of the sound of the thunderbolt weapon
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by the greatness
- प्रशस्तये (*praśastaye*)—in order to praise (your greatness)
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- शेषन् (*śeṣan*)—let them fall. (Moreover)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- युधा (*yudhā*)—(distinguished) by the weapon that is the means of striking, or by battle
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—you go. (then)
- अर्णांसि (*arṇāṃsi*)—the waters
- अव सृजत् (*ava sṛjat*)—you make fall downward. (for that purpose)
- हरी (*harī*)—the two horses named Hari
- तिष्ठत् (*tiṣṭhat*)—you mount (having done so)
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—food in the form of grain and the like
- धृषता (*dhṛṣatā*)—by your power
- मृष्ट (*mṛṣṭa*)—cleanse (increase)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let your foes, overcome by the power of your thunderbolt, lie in their own places, so as to proclaim your greatness (let the clouds, other than the thunderbolt, remain in their own place, the sky, proclaiming your greatness); mounting your horses named Hari, eager for battle (bearing a weapon), you go and make the waters fall downward. By this power of yours food in the form of grain and the like increases.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Let (your foes, Indra,) humbled by the might of your thunderbolt, rest in their own station, for your glory : when you move, (armed) with your weapon, you send down the waters : arresting your horses, increase, by your power, ( the abundance of ) food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सस्मिन् योन् ते नु शेषन् (*sasmin yon te nu śeṣan*)—In this sentence Indra is addressed. The word ते (*te*) is explained as meaning Indra's foes. The word सस्मिन् (*sasmin*) is used as an epithet of the word योन्नौ (*yonnau*) (योन्‌नौ (*yonnau*)). The authors of the Nirukta read the word योनि (*yoni*) among the names of the house (Ni. 3-13). And—
इहं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा । यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवाय एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥ (*ihaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā | yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya evā rātryuṣase yonimāraik ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-1)

### Printed p. 331
In this Ṛk the word योनि (*yoni*) is described as used in the sense of "place". And further—
य ईं चकार न सो अस्य वेद य ईं ददर्श हिरुगिन्नु तस्मात् । स मातुर्योना परिवीतो अंतर्बहुप्रजा निर्ऋतिमा विवेश ॥ (*ya īṃ cakāra na so asya veda ya īṃ dadarśa hiruginnu tasmāt | sa māturyonā parivīto aṃtarbahuprajā nirṛtimā viveśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-32 **NOTE**)
Here the explanation is योनिरंतरिक्षं महानवयवः परिवीतो वायुना आयमपीतरो योनिरेतस्मादेव परियुतो भवति । (*yoniraṃtarikṣaṃ mahānavayavaḥ parivīto vāyunā āyamapītaro yoniretasmādeva pariyuto bhavati |*) (Ni. 2-8). As the embryo comes into being in the womb through the wind, so the firmament, pervaded by the wind and joined with the water-bearing cloud, is here referred to by the word योनि (*yoni*). This is how the meaning is explained.

Besides being used in the senses of cause, place of origin and dwelling-place, the word योनि (*yoni*) is also read by the Nirukta-author among the names of water, अणः (*aṇaḥ*), क्षोदः (*kṣodaḥ*) and so on (Ni. 2-24).

In the Ṛk
ऋतस्य देवा अनु व्रता गुर्भुवत्परिष्टिर्द्यौर्न भूम । वर्धंतीमापः पन्वा सुशिश्मिमृतस्य योना गर्भे सुजातं । (*ṛtasya devā anu vratā gurbhuvatpariṣṭirdyaurna bhūma | vardhaṃtīmāpaḥ panvā suśiśmimṛtasya yonā garbhe sujātaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-65-2)
the word means "in the water that is the cause of the sacrifice or of something else", that is, in the water that is the cause of sacrifice and of food.

In
देवं वो देवयज्ययाग्निमीळीत मर्त्यः । समिद्दः शुक्र दीदिह्यृतस्य योनिमासदः (*devaṃ vo devayajyayāgnimīḷīta martyaḥ | samiddaḥ śukra dīdihyṛtasya yonimāsadaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-21-4)
योनिं कारणं स्वर्गसाधनं (*yoniṃ kāraṇaṃ svargasādhanaṃ*): the means that helps in conveying one to heaven.

In
दुरोकशोचिः क्रतुर्न नित्यो जायेव योनावरं विश्वस्मै । चित्रो यदभ्राट् चैतो न विक्षु रथो न रुक्मी त्वेषः समत्तु । (*durokaśociḥ kraturna nityo jāyeva yonāvaraṃ viśvasmai | citro yadabhrāṭ caito na vikṣu ratho na rukmī tveṣaḥ samattu |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-66-3)
it means "house".

In
यमीं द्वा सवयसा सपर्यतः समाने योना मिथुना समोकसा । दिवा न नक्तं पलितो युवाजनि पुरू चरन्नजरो मानुषा युगा । (*yamīṃ dvā savayasā saparyataḥ samāne yonā mithunā samokasā | divā na naktaṃ palito yuvājani purū carannajaro mānuṣā yugā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-144-4)
it means the place of origin of the fruit. Likewise in
वेदिषदे प्रियधामाय सुद्युते धासिमिव प्र भरा योनिमग्नये । वस्त्रेणेव वासया मन्मना शुचिं ज्योतीरथं शुक्रवर्णं तमोहनं । (*vediṣade priyadhāmāya sudyute dhāsimiva pra bharā yonimagnaye | vastreṇeva vāsayā manmanā śuciṃ jyotīrathaṃ śukravarṇaṃ tamohanaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-1)

### Printed p. 332
and in other such Ṛks it means the place called the altar (vedi). Thus the word has uses in various senses. In the present Ṛk the meaning "in the firmament, which is the support of all things" is stated.

Addressing Indra, the meaning is explained thus: let Indra's enemies lie hidden in their own places, as they were before, or else let them lie hidden in the firmament, which is the support of all beings.

पवीरवस्य मह्ना प्रकस्तये (*pavīravasya mahnā prakastaye*)—the word पविः (*paviḥ*) is stated among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 3-11). It is also read among the names of speech (Ni. 2-13). And Yāska, citing the Ṛk
पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिंधुरापस्समुद्रियः । विश्वे देवासः शृणवन् वचांसि मे सरस्वती सह धीभिः पुरंध्या ॥ (*pāvīravī tanyaturekapādajo divo dhartā siṃdhurāpassamudriyaḥ | viśve devāsaḥ śṛṇavan vacāṃsi me sarasvatī saha dhībhiḥ puraṃdhyā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-13)
explains: पविः शल्यो भवति यद्विपुनाति कायं, तद्वत् पवीरमायुधं तद्वानिंद्रः पवीरवान् (*paviḥ śalyo bhavati yadvipunāti kāyaṃ, tadvat pavīramāyudhaṃ tadvāniṃdraḥ pavīravān*). The word पवि (*pavi*) may mean a thorn. Because a thorn pierces the body, the weapon, being furnished with a thorn, is denoted by the word पवीर (*pavīra*); Indra, who possesses this weapon, is spoken of by the word पवीरवान् (*pavīravān*). Here Sāyaṇa explains पवीरवस्य (*pavīravasya*) as कुलिशस्य (*kuliśasya*), "of the thunderbolt", or of the word कुलिश (*kuliśa*) meaning the thunderbolt, and he describes the meaning thus: through the greatness of the thunderbolt, and त्वद्वज्रप्रहारेण हताः मेघाः शत्रवो वा तत्त्रैव शेरते निपातेन पलायंते (*tvadvajraprahāreṇa hatāḥ meghāḥ śatravo vā tattraiva śerate nipātena palāyaṃte*): struck by the blow of Indra's thunderbolt, the clouds or the enemies lie hidden there (in the firmament) or flee. This is प्रशंसनाय त्वत्तुतये त्वन्महिमज्ञापनाय (*praśaṃsanāya tvattutaye tvanmahimajñāpanāya*): for making known Indra's greatness.

यत् युधा गाः अर्णांसि अवसृजत् (*yat yudhā gāḥ arṇāṃsi avasṛjat*)—यदा प्रहरणसाधनेन आयुधेन युद्धेन वा गच्छसि तदा उदकानि अवासृजः (*yadā praharaṇasādhanena āyudhena yuddhena vā gacchasi tadā udakāni avāsṛjaḥ*). The word यत् (*yat*) is used in the sense of यदा (*yadā*) ("when"). The word युधा (*yudhā*) may mean the weapon, the instrument of striking, or else battle. Thus the meaning is that whether Indra moves in battle or is with his weapon, he makes the waters fall to the earth (he sends rain). The worldly way, that a hero bearing his weapon fights with enemies and fells them to the ground face downwards, is here described of Indra, as the word अवाज्मुखमपातयः (*avājmukhamapātayaḥ*) indicates.

### Printed p. 333
हरी तिष्ठत् (*harī tiṣṭhat*)—Since the Nirukta-author says हरी इंद्रस्य (*harī iṃdrasya*) (Ni. 2-28), that the horses of Indra are known as हरी (*harī*), the meaning is explained: as soon as Indra, in order to win in battle, mounts his vehicle, the horses called हरी (*harī*), यदा हरी अधितिष्ठसि तदा अवासृजः (*yadā harī adhitiṣṭhasi tadā avāsṛjaḥ*): he sends rain. By the sentence वाजान् धृषता मृष्ट (*vājān dhṛṣatā mṛṣṭa*) Sāyaṇa explains: let Indra increase सस्यादि लक्षणानि अन्नानि (*sasyādi lakṣaṇāni annāni*), food in the form of crops, by his power that overwhelms others (धर्षकेण सामर्थ्यीन (*dharṣakeṇa sāmarthyīna*)).

Although the word वाज (*vāja*) is used in many senses, here its use is fixed in the sense of food alone.

##### Grammar

- शेषन्—शीज् स्वप्ने धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने व्यत्ययो बहुलं इति झि प्रत्ययः आगच्छति । इतश्चलोपः (पा. सू. ३-४-९७) इत्यनेन अंत्यइकारस्य लोपः । झोंतः इत्यनेन अंतादेशः । लेटोडाटौ (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) इत्यनेन तस्य अडागमः । अंत्यलोपः । सिब्बहुलं लेटि (पा. सू. ३-१-३४) इत्यनेन सिप् । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोरिकः गुणः । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न आगच्छति । धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- सस्मिन्—सर्वस्मिन् इति रूपे सिद्धे छांदसत्वात् वर्णलोपः आगच्छति ।
- प्रशस्तये—शंसु स्तुतौ धातुः । भावार्थे क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । तादौ च निति (पा. सू. ६-२-५०) इत्यनेन गतेः (प्र) उदात्तस्वरः आगच्छति । चतुर्थ्येकवचनांतं रूपम् ।
- सृजत्—सृज विसर्गे धातुः । व्यत्ययो बहुलं इत्यनेन लज् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने तिबादेशः । इकारलोपः । श विकरणम् । तस्य चित्त्वात् लघूपधगुणः न आगच्छति । बहुलं छंदस्यमा इत्यनेन अडागमः न आगच्छति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न आगच्छति । विकरणस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- युधा—युध संप्रहारे धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । तृतीयैकवचनांतं रूपम् । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) इत्यनेन विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- शिष्ठत्—स्था गतिनिवृत्तौ धातुः । पूर्ववत् पुरुषव्यत्ययः । लज् । यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इत्यनेन निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधः आगच्छति । शप् अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

### Printed p. 334
- धृषता—इद्धृषा प्रागल्भ्ये धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । नुम्रहिते शतृप्रत्यये परे तृतीयैकवचनस्य आगतत्वात् शतुरनुमोनद्य- (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३) इत्यनेन तस्य उदात्तस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- मृष्ट—मृजू शुद्धौ धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनस्य व्यत्ययेन तादेशः । विकरणस्य लुक् । व्रश्चभृस्थ- (पा. सू. ८-२-३६) इत्यनेन जकारस्य षत्वम् । तं निमित्तीकृत्य प्रत्ययस्य ष्टुत्वम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः आगच्छति ।

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वह॒ कुत्स॑मिंद्र॒ यस्मि॑ञ्चा॒कन्तून्य॑म॒न्यू ऋ॒ज्रा वात॒स्याश्वा॑ ।  
> प्र सूर॑श॒क्रं वृ॑हताद॒भीके॒ऽभि स्पृधो॑ यासिष॒द्वज ॑बाहुः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वह । कुत्सं । इंद्र । यस्मिन् । चाकन् । स्यूमन्यू इति । ऋज्रा । वातस्य । अश्वा ।  
> प्र । सूरः । चक्रं । वृहतात् । अभीके । अभि । स्पृधः । यासिषत् । वज्रबाहुः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र कुत्समेतन्नामानमृषिं प्राप्तं स्यूमन्यू । स्यूमकमिति सुखनाम । तदिचंतौ सततगामिनौ वा ऋज्रा ऋजुगामिनौ वातस्य वायोः समानवेगावश्वा तदीयावश्च वह । प्रस्थापय । यस्मिन् हविषि निमित्तभूते सति
> कुत्सं जाकन् कामयसे तर्पयसे वा हविरादिकं । तदर्थं सूरः प्रेरकः
> सूर्यश्चक्रं स्वमंडलं स्वरथचक्रं वाभीक आसन्ने देशे वृहतात् । ऊर्ध्वं
> गमयतु । प्रकाशयतु । अथ परोक्षेणाह । वज्रबाहुरयमिंद्रः स्पृधः
> संग्रामं कुर्वतः शत्रूनभि यासिषत् । अभियातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, convey the sage Kutsa, who has come to you, with your two horses, which are स्यूमन्यू (*syūmanyū*) (स्यूमकमिति सुखनाम (*syūmakamiti sukhanāma*): desirous of comfort, or else constantly moving), ऋज्रा (*ṛjrā*) (moving straight) and equal in speed to the wind, and also those that belong to the wind. Send them forth to the offering on account of which you desire Kutsa or gratify him. For that purpose let Sūrya, the impeller, lift his disc or the wheel of his chariot upward in the near region and make it shine. Then he speaks in the third person: let this Indra, वज्रबाहुः (*vajrabāhuḥ*) (thunderbolt-armed), advance against the enemies who wage battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—when which oblations and the like are the occasion
- कुत्सं (*kutsaṃ*)—the sage Kutsya
- जाकन् (*jākan*)—you desire or you satisfy
- कुत्सं (*kutsaṃ*)—that sage Kutsa
- स्यूमन्यू (*syūmanyū*)—desirous of comfort, or constantly moving
- ऋज्रा (*ṛjrā*)—moving straight
- वातस्य (*vātasya*)—of the wind (having speed equal to it)
- अश्वा (*aśvā*)—your horses (by means of the horses)
- वह (*vaha*)—bring together (for that same purpose)
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—Sūrya, the impeller
- चक्रं (*cakraṃ*)—his disc or his wheel
- अभीके (*abhīke*)—in the near region
- प्र वृहतात् (*pra vṛhatāt*)—let him lift upward (let him make shine)
- वज्रबाहुः (*vajrabāhuḥ*)—the bearer of the thunderbolt (this Indra)
- स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)—the enemies who fight
- अभि यासिषत् (*abhi yāsiṣat*)—let him go against them

### Printed p. 335

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, to the place where are the oblations and the like that you wish to reach Kutsya, let your horses, which are desirous of comfort (constantly moving), straight-going and swift as the wind, carry that Kutsya; let Sūrya also shine for the same purpose; and you, bearing the thunderbolt, advance against them for the destruction of the enemies (for the conquest of the cloud).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Bear, Indra, with your obedient horses as swift as the wind, (the sage) Kutsa, to that ceremony (to which) you desire (to convey him) let the sun bring near the wheel of his chariot, and let the thunder-armed advance against his opponents.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Two points must be noted in this mantra. First, Indra goes mounted on his horses to help Kutsa; and on this occasion the sun's wheel shines and helps Indra by supporting him. Of these, if we first examine the matter of Kutsa, it is learned that on some occasions Kutsa, as Indra's friend, received help from Indra, and on other occasions he fell out with Indra and was defeated by him.
तत्र कुत्स इत्येतत् कृंततेः । ऋषिः कुत्सो भवति कर्ता स्तोमानां इत्यौपमन्यवः । तत्सख इंद्रः तुष्णं जघान इति ॥ (*tatra kutsa ityetat kṛṃtateḥ | ṛṣiḥ kutso bhavati kartā stomānāṃ ityaupamanyavaḥ | tatsakha iṃdraḥ tuṣṇaṃ jaghāna iti ‖*) (Ni. 3-11)
By this explanation the Nirukta-author has shown Kutsa to be Indra's friend.

Examining certain contexts, there is room also for the conjecture that Kutsa may be Indra's son. How? The epithet अर्जुनेय (*arjuneya*) is applied to Kutsa in many places. And in all the places where it is said that Indra helped Kutsa Ārjuneya, it is stated clearly that the sun too helped Indra.

### Printed p. 336
In such contexts one must consider what the epithet अर्जुनेय (*arjuneya*) means.
अहं मनुरभवं सूर्यश्चाहं कक्षीवा ऋषिरस्मि विप्रः । अहं कुत्समार्जुनेयं न्यृंजेऽहं कविरुशना पश्यता मा ॥ (*ahaṃ manurabhavaṃ sūryaścāhaṃ kakṣīvā ṛṣirasmi vipraḥ | ahaṃ kutsamārjuneyaṃ nyṛṃje 'haṃ kaviruśanā paśyatā mā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-1)
त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र कुत्समावः शुक्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये । दासं यच्छुष्णं कुवयं न्यस्मा आरंधय आर्जुनेयाय शिक्षन् ॥ (*tvaṃ ha tyadiṃdra kutsamāvaḥ śukrūṣamāṇastanvā samarye | dāsaṃ yacchuṣṇaṃ kuvayaṃ nyasmā āraṃdhaya ārjuneyāya śikṣan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-2)
यत्तुदत्तूर एतशं वज्गू वातस्य पर्णिना । वहत्कुत्समार्जुनेयं शतक्रतुः त्सरद्गंधर्वमस्तृतं ॥ (*yattudattūra etaśaṃ vajgū vātasya parṇinā | vahatkutsamārjuneyaṃ śatakratuḥ tsaradgaṃdharvamastṛtaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-11)
For the words occurring in such Ṛks Sāyaṇa in some contexts explains *arjunyāḥ putraṃ kutsaṃ*: Kutsa, the son of a woman named Arjunī; in other contexts, अर्जुन इतींद्रस्य नाम । तस्य पुत्रं (*arjuna itīṃdrasya nāma | tasya putraṃ*): Indra's name is Arjuna, and since Kutsa is his son, he has the epithet Ārjuneya. Where he speaks of him as Indra's son, he cites the Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā mantra
एतद्वा इंद्रस्य गुह्यं नाम यदर्जुनः । (*etadvā iṃdrasya guhyaṃ nāma yadarjunaḥ |*)
and shows that the name Arjuna for Indra is well known in the Śruti and elsewhere. It may also be noted that other Śruti passages too say that the words Arjuna and Arjunī are connected with Indra. For example—
फल्गुनीष्वग्नी आदधीत । एता वा इंद्रनक्षत्रं यत्फल्गुन्नोऽप्यस्य प्रतिनाम्योऽर्जुनो ह वै नामेंद्रो यदस्य गुह्यं नाम (*phalgunīṣvagnī ādadhīta | etā vā iṃdranakṣatraṃ yatphalgunno 'pyasya pratināmyo 'rjuno ha vai nāmeṃdro yadasya guhyaṃ nāma*) (Śa. Brā. 21-2-11)
इंद्रो भवति यच्च क्षत्रियो यदु च यजमानस्तस्मादाहारिष्टोर्जुन इति । (*iṃdro bhavati yacca kṣatriyo yadu ca yajamānastasmādāhāriṣṭorjuna iti |*) (Śa. Brā. 5-4-3-7)
The Phalgunīs are Indra's constellations, and there is agreement in the name: Indra is called Arjuna, and the Phalgunīs are called Arjunīs. Since the Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa and other places say this, it is understood that Kutsa may be called in two ways, son of Indra or son of Arjunī.

### Printed p. 337
In the passage

कुत्साय यत्र पुरुहूत वन्वङ्ष्ण मनंतैः परियासि वध्यैः । (*kutsāya yatra puruhūta vanvaṅṣṇa manaṃtaiḥ pariyāsi vadhyaiḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-121-9)

and likewise in Ṛk verses such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-3 and 1-175-4, it is said that Indra helped Kutsa and killed Kṛṣṇa. And further:

अहं पितेव वेतसूरभिष्टये तुग्रं कुत्साय स्मदिभं च रंधयं ॥ (*ahaṃ piteva vetasūrabhiṣṭaye tugraṃ kutsāya smadibhaṃ ca raṃdhayaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-49-4)

In such places Indra declares of himself: "For Kutsa's sake I overcame many enemies — Vetasu, Tugra, Smadibha and others." But in

त्वमस्मै कुत्समतिथिग्वमायुं महे राज्ञे यूने आरंधनायः । (*tvamasmai kutsamatithigvamāyuṃ mahe rājñe yūne āraṃdhanāyaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-10)

य आयुं कुत्समतिथिग्वमर्दयो वावृधानो दिवे दिवे ॥ (*ya āyuṃ kutsamatithigvamardayo vāvṛdhāno dive dive ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-53-2)

and similar Ṛk verses, Indra is also described as having defeated Kutsa and others. Concerning this person, the scholar Keith has said in his book *Religion and Philosophy of the Vedas*:

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
His chief rival is Kutsa, who appears as battling against him, and as victor by the aid of Indra, who. for his sake tore from the Sun a wheel, prolonging the daylight and thus enabling, it may be assumed, Kutsa to turn the issue of battle. The feat of Indra is several times mentioned and the fact that Kutsa is a real hero is suggested, though not proved, by the fact that elsewhere he appears in hostile relation to Indra, just as Athithigva, who is normally the protege of Indra, in one or two places appears in the reverse relation. It is true that it is not to be expected that a God, or a hero of divine dimensions, would be thus placed in opposition to the God, though,as the God is the uncertain Indra, the argument is by no means conclusive. Kutsa, in the case of his real personality must be a king, and this is not inconsistent with his being called a seer : royal seers are not unknown :
(Harward Oriental Series. Vol. 31. p. 130),

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

These sentences tell both that Indra acted against Kutsa and that he helped Kutsa. It is also suggested that, to help Kutsa, he took the Sun's wheel in his hand and secured victory for Kutsa.

### Printed p. 338
There is a story about Indra defeating an enemy by using the Sun's wheel.

केचन असुराः इंद्रस्य वज्रायुधेन अस्माकं वधो मा भूदिति ब्रह्मणा वरं लब्ध्वा इंद्रं अगणय्य उद्वृत्ताः स्थिताः । तान् हंतुमिंद्रः सूररथस्य चक्रं आदाय अवधीत् । (*kecana asurāḥ iṃdrasya vajrāyudhena asmākaṃ vadho mā bhūditi brahmaṇā varaṃ labdhvā iṃdraṃ agaṇayya udvṛttāḥ sthitāḥ | tān haṃtumiṃdraḥ sūrarathasya cakraṃ ādāya avadhīt |*)

Some Asuras, having obtained from Brahmā the boon that they should not die by Indra's thunderbolt, disregarded Indra and behaved wickedly. Then Indra made the wheel of the Sun's chariot itself his weapon and destroyed them all — such is the tradition.

अथवा इंद्र एव द्युःस्थानस्सन् आदित्यात्मना स्तूयते (*athavā iṃdra eva dyuḥsthānassan ādityātmanā stūyate*) — it may also be said that Indra himself, dwelling in the heavenly region, is praised in the form of the Āditya (Sun). Sāyaṇa, stating this same point elsewhere, says:

सूरः सूर्यः जातः उदितःसन् ओजसा स्वकीयेन तेजसा युक्तः तमोनिवारणार्थं असुरजयाय वा चक्रोपलक्षितं रथं प्रकर्षेण उद्यतं करोति । ततः पूर्वमरुणः तद्रथयंता मंदेहाद्यसुराणां समीपे वाचं तेषां जहि, भिंदि इत्यादि ध्वनिं मुषायति । (*sūraḥ sūryaḥ jātaḥ uditaḥsan ojasā svakīyena tejasā yuktaḥ tamonivāraṇārthaṃ asurajayāya vā cakropalakṣitaṃ rathaṃ prakarṣeṇa udyataṃ karoti | tataḥ pūrvamaruṇaḥ tadrathayaṃtā maṃdehādyasurāṇāṃ samīpe vācaṃ teṣāṃ jahi, bhiṃdi ityādi dhvaniṃ muṣāyati |*)
(Sā. Bhā.)

As soon as the Sun has risen, endowed with his own radiance, he sets his chariot, marked by the wheel-weapon, moving vigorously, in order to dispel the darkness or to conquer the Asuras. Before this, Aruṇa, the charioteer who drives this chariot, brings the Sun's chariot near the host of demons known as Mandeha and silences them, so that the words they might utter in battle, such as "cut" and "strike", do not come out of their mouths. The Nirukta-author, quoting the Ṛk

यदुदंचो वृषाकपे गृहमिंद्राजगंतन । क्वंस्य पुल्वघो मृगः कमगञ्जनयोपनो विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ (*yadudaṃco vṛṣākape gṛhamiṃdrājagaṃtana | kvaṃsya pulvagho mṛgaḥ kamagañjanayopano viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-22)

says तमगमद्देशं जनयोपनः सर्वस्माद्य उत्तरत्तमेतद्रूम आदित्यं । (*tamagamaddeśaṃ janayopanaḥ sarvasmādya uttarattametadrūma ādityaṃ |*) Indra is invisible. People, through the knowledge of the Āditya's rising and setting, are deluded into thinking Indra and Āditya are different. But this is not true knowledge. Among the gods

### Printed p. 339
Indra is the greatest; it is explained that Indra himself is the one who exists in the form of Āditya. This same identity of Indra and Āditya, and their unity of action, are described in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā and in the Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas (Śa. Brā. 3-4-2-15 etc.).

स्यूमन्यू (*syūmanyū*)—this word is used as an epithet of the word अश्नौ (*aśnau*). The Nirukta-author explains that the word स्यूमकम् (*syūmakam*) is read among the names of happiness (Ni. 2-13). Sāyaṇa comments तदिच्छंतौ सततगामिनौ वा (*tadicchaṃtau satatagāminau vā*), giving the meaning "those desiring happiness, or those constantly moving". The horses of the seer Kutsa, being ऋज्रा (*ṛjrā*) (moving by a straight path) and वातस्य (*vātasya*) (equal in speed to the wind's speed), he explains thus: कुत्सं वह (*kutsaṃ vaha*) — convey the seer renowned as Kutsa, make him set out and send him; the seer's command (or request) is thus described as addressed to Indra. But since this meaning does not fit well, and the meaning of the following sentences too is not clear:

यस्मिन् चाकन् (*yasmin cākan*)—हविसि निमित्तभूते सति कुत्सं कामयसे तर्पयसे वा । (*havisi nimittabhūte sati kutsaṃ kāmayase tarpayase vā |*) The meaning is given as: Indra desires Kutsa because he offers oblations to him, or Indra satisfies the seer Kutsa so that the oblations may reach him.

Yāska:

वने न वा यो न्यधायि चाकञ्चुचिर्वा स्तोमो भुरणावजीगः । यस्येदिंद्रः पुरुदिनेषु होता नृणां नर्यो नृतमः क्षपावान् ॥ (*vane na vā yo nyadhāyi cākañcucirvā stomo bhuraṇāvajīgaḥ | yasyediṃdraḥ purudineṣu hotā nṛṇāṃ naryo nṛtamaḥ kṣapāvān ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-29-1).

Having quoted this Ṛk, he explains चाकन् जायन्निति वा, कामयमान इति वा (*cākan jāyanniti vā, kāmayamāna iti vā*). Durgācārya gives the meaning चायन् पश्यन्, भूयात् दिशो निरीक्षमाणः, अथवा तदुत्सुकमनाः (*cāyan paśyan, bhūyāt diśo nirīkṣamāṇaḥ, athavā tadutsukamanāḥ*).

सूरः अभीके चक्रं बृहतात् (*sūraḥ abhīke cakraṃ bṛhatāt*)—the word अभीकॆ (*abhīkè*) is not read among the names of "near" (āsanna/antika), yet it is used in the sense "near" in प्रपित्वे अभीक इत्यासन्नस्य अभीकॆ अभ्यक्ते (*prapitve abhīka ityāsannasya abhīkè abhyakte*) (Ni. 3-20). Sāyaṇa gives the meaning अभीकॆ आसन्न देशे (*abhīkè āsanna deśe*). The word सूर (*sūra*) is explained as the Sun, the impeller. It is described that here the seer's words, spoken to Indra, are cited: "For the coming of the seer Kutsa, let the Sun make either his disc or the wheel of his chariot shine near, close to the sacrificial hall (in the upper region)."

### Printed p. 340
वज्रबाहुः स्पृधः अभियासिषत् (*vajrabāhuḥ spṛdhaḥ abhiyāsiṣat*)—the word स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*) is read among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). The wish is expressed that Indra, bearing the thunderbolt, may fight against the enemies in battles.

वज्रः कस्मात् वर्जयतीति सतः । (*vajraḥ kasmāt varjayatīti sataḥ |*) Because it separates living beings from their breaths, it is called vajra (Ni. 3-11). The greatness of this weapon, and how Indra obtained it, are described in various ways in various places.

अस्मा इदु त्वष्टा तक्षद्वज्रं स्वपस्तमं स्वयं १ रसाय । (*asmā idu tvaṣṭā takṣadvajraṃ svapastamaṃ svayaṃ 1 rasāya |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-6)

अनवस्ते रथमश्वाय तक्षन्त्वष्टा वज्रं पुरुहूत द्युमंतं । (*anavaste rathamaśvāya takṣantvaṣṭā vajraṃ puruhūta dyumaṃtaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-31-4)

In many Ṛk verses like these it is described that Tvaṣṭṛ prepared a radiant thunderbolt for Indra. Moreover:

यं ते काव्य उतना मंदिनं दाद्वृत्रहणं पार्यं ततक्ष वज्रं । (*yaṃ te kāvya utanā maṃdinaṃ dādvṛtrahaṇaṃ pāryaṃ tatakṣa vajraṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-12)

In such Ṛk verses it is said that this was given to Indra by Kāvya Uśanas.

समुद्रे अंतः तयत उद्ना वज्रो अभीवृतः । भरंत्यस्मै संयतः पुरःप्रस्रवणा बलिं ॥ (*samudre aṃtaḥ tayata udnā vajro abhīvṛtaḥ | bharaṃtyasmai saṃyataḥ puraḥprasravaṇā baliṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-100-9)

In these and similar places the nature and power of the thunderbolt are described. The power of the thunderbolt is told thus: it lies within the sea, covered with water and dormant, and as soon as it comes to the battlefield, enemies offer their very lives to it as tribute on the field.

##### Grammar

- वह—वह प्रापणे । धातुः । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थकः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । पादादित्वान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- चाकन्—चक तृप्तौ । धातुः णिजंतात् लटः शत्रादेशः । छंदस्युभयथा (पा. सू. ३-४-११७) इति तस्यार्धधातुकसंज्ञात्वात् शेरनिटि इति णिचो लोपः । शप् विकरणमपि न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- स्यूमन्यू—स्यूमकं आत्मनः इच्छंतौ । इच्छार्थे क्यच् आगते क्याच्छंदसि (पा. सू. ३-२-१७०) इति उ प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।

- ऋज्रा—ऋज गतिस्थानादिषु । धातुः । ऋज्रेंद्र— (उ. सू. २-१८६) इति र गंतत्वेन निपातितः । सुपां सुलुक्—(पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति द्विवचनस्य (औ) आकारादेशो भवति । अश्वा इत्यत्रापि एवमेव आकारादेशः ।
- वृहताक्—वृहू उद्यमने । धातुः । तुदादिः । लोट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । विकरणस्य जित्वातिदेशत्वात् लघोपधगुणो न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- स्पृधः—स्पर्ध संघर्षे । स्पर्धंते इति स्पृधः क्विप् च (पा. सू. ३-२-७६) इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । बहुलं छंदसि इति धातो रेफस्य संप्रसारणं । ऋकारः । अकारलोपः । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपं ।
- यासिषत्—या प्रापणे । धातुः । छंदसिलुज् लज्—(पा. सू. ३-४-६) इति लोडर्थे लुज् । प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । च्लेः सिचादेशः । यमरमनमातां सक् च (पा. सू. ७-२-७३) इति धातोः सकागमः, परस्य सिचः इडागमः । व्यत्ययेन प्रत्ययस्य अडागमः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति । **NOTE**

> वर्णिता अपत्यं पुत्रं वहमाना ये संति तान् जघन्वान्भवेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, हरिवः (*harivaḥ*), possessing the two bay horses, you, grown strong through our urging praises, have slain the non-giving अदाशून् (*adāśūn*) and the मित्रेरून् (*mitrerūn*) — those who injure the sacrificers, who are friends, or who bring about friendship with their enemies." Further: those men who look upon you, अर्यमणं (*aryamaṇaṃ*) (the giver), as a friend, together with the आयोः (*āyoḥ*) (the man, the adhvaryu and others) or with the sacrificial food, शूर्ताः (*śūrtāḥ*) (quickly, by offering oblations), through you obtain a son, a preserver of the family (अपत्यं (*apatyaṃ*)) — they look upon you with favour. Alternatively: those who look upon you as the giver, they become thus. Or again: those men who, seeing some other giver, do not worship you, being helpers of a man, and are cast down (शूर्ताः (*śūrtāḥ*)) by you and are bearing a son — be the slayer of those. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—you who have the two horses named Hari
- चोदप्रवृद्धः (*codapravṛddhaḥ*)—grown strong by our praise
- अदाशून् (*adāśūn*)—those who make no gifts of oblations and the like (and)
- मित्रेरून् (*mitrerūn*)—those who injure the sacrificers who are friends, or those who have fostered friendship with the sacrificers' enemies
- जघन्वान् (*jaghanvān*)—you slay
- (Kiñca—and)
- ये (*ye*)—who
- अर्यमणं (*aryamaṇaṃ*)—you, the giver
- प्र पश्यन् (*pra paśyan*)—look upon (as a friend; regard)
- ते (*te*)—those men
- आयोः सचा (*āyoḥ sacā*)—together with the man (the adhvaryu and others) or with the sacrificial food
- तूर्ताः (*tūrtāḥ*)—quickly (through oblation-offering and so on)
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—by you
- अपत्यं (*apatyaṃ*)—a son
- वहमानाः (संति) (*vahamānāḥ (saṃti)*)—become obtainers
- [Or ये (*ye*)—which men; अर्यमणं (*aryamaṇaṃ*)—some giver; प्र पश्यन् (*pra paśyan*)—having seen (and not worshipping you); आयोः सचा (*āyoḥ sacā*)—being helpers of a man; त्वया (*tvayā*)—by you; शूर्ताः (*śūrtāḥ*)—cast down (driven away); अपत्यं (*apatyaṃ*)—a son; वहमानाः (संति) (*vahamānāḥ (saṃti)*)—who become obtainers. (तान् जघन्वान् भव (*tān jaghanvān bhava*)—be the slayer of such)]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who possess the horses named Hari, pleased by our praise, be the slayer of those who do not offer oblations and the like and of those who injure the sacrificers; and, to those who regard you, the giver, alone as protector, who, accompanied by the adhvaryu and others, offer oblations and the like to you, grant offspring. (Or: destroy those who, relying on some other giver, are helpers of men, do not worship you, and are endowed with sons and the like.)

### Printed p. 343

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, lord of steeds. invigorated by our animating praise, you have slain those who make you no offerings and disturb your worshippers; but they who look upon you as (their) protector, and are associated for (the presentation of sacrificial) food, obtain from you posterity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अदाशून् मित्रेरून् जघन्वान् (*adāśūn mitrerūn jaghanvān*)—The word अदाशून् (*adāśūn*) is explained as "those who give no gifts". Here the word मित्र (*mitra*) is explained as "sacrificers", and for the word मित्रेरु (*mitreru*) two kinds of meaning are given: those who cause trouble to the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, or those who incite the enemies of the sacrificers to trouble them. The sense that Indra destroys people who give no gifts and who trouble the sacrificers is explained by the sentence मित्राणां यजमानानां ईरयित्थान् बाधकान्, तद्वैरिणां मित्रत्वं गच्छतो ना हतवानसि (*mitrāṇāṃ yajamānānāṃ īrayitthān bādhakān, tadvairiṇāṃ mitratvaṃ gacchato nā hatavānasi*).

आर्यमणं (*āryamaṇaṃ*)—Sāyaṇa explains the meaning as दातारं (*dātāraṃ*), "the giver". Yāska quotes the Ṛk दक्षस्य वादिके जन्मनि व्रते राजाना मित्रावरुणा विवाससि । अतूर्त्तपंथाः पुरुरथो अर्यमा सप्तहोता विषुरूपेषु जन्मसु ॥ (*dakṣasya vādike janmani vrate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā vivāsasi | atūrttapaṃthāḥ pururatho aryamā saptahotā viṣurūpeṣu janmasu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-64-5) and explains that the Āditya who restrains enemies is denoted by the word अर्यमन् (*aryaman*): आर्यमा आदित्यो अरीन् नियच्छति (*āryamā ādityo arīn niyacchati*). Durgācārya explains it as अरीणां तमसां नियंता (*arīṇāṃ tamasāṃ niyaṃtā*), "one who destroys the darkness that is like an enemy".

आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—आयोः-मनुष्यस्याध्वय्यादे॥ हविर्लक्षणान्नस्य वा । (*āyoḥ-manuṣyasyādhvayyāde‖ havirlakṣaṇānnasya vā |*) The word आयुः (*āyuḥ*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa gives two meanings for this word: the officiating priests such as the Adhvaryu, or the food in the form of the oblation. For the word आयोः (*āyoḥ*) the sense is given in some places as "enemy" and in others as "friend". It is clear from Sāyaṇa's own explanation that it is difficult to say that this or that is the exact meaning of the word. The commentator has shown his own doubt: "human beings such as the Adhvaryu, or the food that is the oblation". The word आयुः (*āyuḥ*) is a proper name

### Printed p. 344

and also may indicate the name of a lineage. Even in these contexts it is described in some places as a friend of Indra and others, in others as an enemy. It is therefore necessary to understand as far as possible the variety in the use of this word. In the present context, Śruti passages that indicate the relation between Āyu and Indra and the other deities are cited; it is shown that there are many persons named Āyu; that the Āyu who was an enemy of the gods and of sacrificers is one, the Āyu who was a friend of Indra another, and the Āyu who was a friend of Agni another; and that there was a lineage famous by the name Āyu.

In . उर्वश्यसीत्यथोत्तरारण्याज्य विलापनीमुपस्पृश्यायुरसीति तामभिनिदधाति पुरूरवा असीत्युर्वशी वाप्सराः पुरूरवाः पतिरथ यत्तस्मान्मिथुनादजायत तदायुरेवमेवैष एतस्मिन्मिथुनाद्यज्ञं जनयति । (*. urvaśyasītyathottarāraṇyājya vilāpanīmupaspṛśyāyurasīti tāmabhinidadhāti purūravā asītyurvaśī vāpsarāḥ purūravāḥ patiratha yattasmānmithunādajāyata tadāyurevamevaiṣa etasminmithunādyajñaṃ janayati |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-4-1-20), it is said that Āyu was born of Urvaśī and Purūravas, and the identity of Agni and Āyu is stated. Likewise in the sentence आयुषो न मध्यादित्यग्निर्वा आयुः (*āyuṣo na madhyādityagnirvā āyuḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-15) the identity of Agni and Āyu is stated. But there, one view is that the word आयु (*āyu*) is a proper name; another view is that it is not. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa cites the Ṛk of the Saṃhitā मा नो मित्रो वरुणो आर्यमायुरिंद्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतः परि ख्यन् । (*mā no mitro varuṇo āryamāyuriṃdra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-1) (Śa. Brā. 13-5-1-18) and thereby indicates a prayer addressed to Āyu along with the other deities.

In the Ṛk passage स पूर्वया निविदा कव्यतायोरिमाः प्रजा अजनयन्मनूनां । (*sa pūrvayā nividā kavyatāyorimāḥ prajā ajanayanmanūnāṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-2), since the word आयोः (*āyoḥ*) is explained as "Manu", it can be understood as Manu, one of the creator Prajāpatis. Likewise in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-10; 8-15-5; 8-53-2; 2-32-2 and others, it has been explained earlier what person the proper name Āyu indicates. (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part 8, p. 77.)

In many places the words आयुः (*āyuḥ*) and आयोः (*āyoḥ*) are used as alternatives for "human beings who are sacrificers".

### Printed p. 345

होत्राभिरग्निर्मनुषः स्वध्वरो राजा विशामतिथिश्चारुरायवे । (*hotrābhiragnirmanuṣaḥ svadhvaro rājā viśāmatithiścārurāyave |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-2-8).
इमं विधंतो अपां सदस्ये द्वितादधुर्भृगवो विक्षातियोः । (*imaṃ vidhaṃto apāṃ sadasye dvitādadhurbhṛgavo vikṣātiyoḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-4-2).
प्र स्वादनं पितूनामस्ततातिं टिदायवे (*pra svādanaṃ pitūnāmastatātiṃ ṭidāyave*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-7-6).
In these and many other Ṛks the commentator has said that the word आयु (*āyu*) means the sacrificer. In the present Ṛk also he indicates the same view and explains it as human beings such as the Adhvaryu.

शूर्ताः (*śūrtāḥ*)—क्षिप्राः (*kṣiprāḥ*). The word शूर्ताः (*śūrtāḥ*) is stated among the names of "swift" (kṣipra). Here it is used in the sense "quickly".

अपत्यं (*apatyaṃ*)—कुलस्यापातयिताशं पुत्रं । (*kulasyāpātayitāśaṃ putraṃ |*) The word अपत्य (*apatya*) is stated among the fifteen names of offspring beginning तुक् (*tuk*), तोकं (*tokaṃ*) (Ni. 3-2). Durgācārya explains the meaning of the word: अपत्यं कस्मात् अपततं भवति (*apatyaṃ kasmāt apatataṃ bhavati*)—because it is extended, separate from the begetter, the father; or नानेन पततीति वा (*nānena patatīti vā*)—because the begetter does not fall into hell through this son who is born. Sāyaṇa explains that the offspring born is called अपत्य (*apatya*) because he increases the lineage.

For the second sense of this Ṛk Sāyaṇa gives three kinds of meaning. In the first meaning: knowing Indra to be the best giver, the sacrificers, together with human priests such as the Adhvaryu, quickly offer food in the form of the oblation; satisfied by this, Indra (grants) them a son who increases the lineage, and having obtained him, they see Indra, the best of givers.

Secondly, यद्वा—अर्यमणं त्वां पश्यंति ते एवं भवंति । (*yadvā—aryamaṇaṃ tvāṃ paśyaṃti te evaṃ bhavaṃti |*): knowing Indra to be the destroyer of darkness, those who realise him obtain a son who increases the lineage and again see Indra face to face (enjoyment of happiness in this world and the next is described).

Thirdly, यद्वा ये नरा आर्यमणं यं कंचिद्दातारं पश्यन् पश्यंतस्त्वामयजंत आयोर्मनुष्यस्य सचा सहायभूताः त्वया तूर्ताः क्षिप्तावर्जिता असत्यं पुत्रं वहमाना ये संति तान् जघन्वान् भव । (*yadvā ye narā āryamaṇaṃ yaṃ kaṃciddātāraṃ paśyan paśyaṃtastvāmayajaṃta āyormanuṣyasya sacā sahāyabhūtāḥ tvayā tūrtāḥ kṣiptāvarjitā asatyaṃ putraṃ vahamānā ye saṃti tān jaghanvān bhava |*).

### Printed p. 346

Those who, thinking that some one (god) is a giver, worship Indra with indifference, are helpers of men; therefore you, Indra, quickly destroy their wealth in the form of sons and grandsons and destroy them too—thus the meaning is described. (On the whole the meaning of this Ṛk is difficult and not easy to follow, and has therefore been explained to a limited extent.)

##### Grammar

- जघन्वान् — हन हिंसागत्योः धातुः । क्वसुश्च (पा. सू. ३-२-१०७) इति लिटि क्वसुरादेशः । धातोर्द्वित्वम् । कुहोश्चुः (पा. सू. ६-४-६२) इत्यभ्यासस्य कुत्वं जस्वत् । अभ्यासाच्च (पा. सू. ७-३-५५) इत्यभ्यासात् परस्य हकारस्य कुत्वम् । वसोः स्वरः शिष्यते । प्रथमाविभक्त्येकवचने नुम् दीर्घः सलोपः ।
- मित्रेरून् — ईर गतिहिंसादर्शनेषु धातुः । औणादिक उ प्रत्ययः । मित्राणि ईरयंति इति मित्रेरवः तान् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- चोदप्रवृद्धः — चोद्यैः प्रवृद्धः । तृतीया कर्मणि (पा. सू. ६-२-४८) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- हरिवः — हरयः अस्य संति इति हरिवान् । संबुद्धौ रुत्वम् । आमंत्रितनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- अदाशून् — दाश्य दाने धातुः औणादिक उ प्रत्ययः । न दाशवः अदाशवः तान् । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ (पा. सू. ६-२-२) इति नञ्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- पश्यन् — दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे धातुः । छांदसत्वात् वर्तमानार्थे लज् । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । छांदसत्वात् अडागमः न भवति । यद्वृत्तान्तित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधः भवति । ल सार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- आयोः — इण् गतौ धातुः । छंदसीणः इति उण् प्रत्ययः । अचोञ्णिति इति धातोः वृद्धिः आयादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- वहमाना — वह प्रापणे धातुः । लटः शानचादेशः । शप् विकरणः । आनेमुक् इति मुकागमः । ल सार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- अपत्यम् — न पतंति पितरः येन । पत्‌ल्य गतौ धातुः । यत् प्रत्ययः । नञ्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।

> रप॑त्क॒विरिं॑द्रा॒र्कसा॑तौ॒ क्षां दा॒सायो॑प॒बर्ह॑णीं कः ।  
> कर॑त्ति॒स्रो म॒घवा॒ दानु॑चित्रा॒ नि दु॑र्यो॒णे कुय॑वाचं मृ॒धि  ॑
> श्रेत् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रपत् । कविः । इंद्र । अर्कसात् । क्षां । दासाय । उपबर्हणीं । करिति कः ।  
> करत् । शिस्रः । मघवा । दान्चित्राः । दुर्योणे । कुयवाचं । मृधि । श्रेत् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वां कविः क्रांतदर्शनूचानो वा होतार्कसातावर्चनीयस्यान्नस्य लाभे निमित्तभूते पति रपत् । स्तौति । यद्वा । एतन्नामर्षि रपत्
> अस्तौत् अन्नार्थं । तस्यातिप्रभूतमन्नं प्रादा इत्यर्थः । तथा च दासाय प्राण्युपक्षपयित्रॆसुराय क्षां भूमिमुपबर्हणीं शय्यां कः । अकरोः । हत्वा

> क्षित्यंतरिक्षद्युरूपा ना भूमिदार्ानुचित्रा दानेन देयैर्धनैर्वा चायनीयाः
> करत् । करोति । यद्वा । तिस्रोऽयोरजतहिरण्यमयाः पुरीर्दानुचित्रा खंडनेन

> चित्रा अकरोत् । तथा दुर्योणे दुष्टयोन् स्थाने एतन्नामकस्य राज्ञः
> प्रीत्यर्थं वा कुयवाचं कुत्सितं शब्दायंतमेतन्नामानमसुरं मृधि संग्रामे
> नि श्रेत् । हिंसितवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, the कविः (*kaviḥ*)—one who sees beyond, or the one who knows (अनूचानो वा (*anūcāno vā*)) the tradition—the Hotṛ, praises you (रपत् (*rapat*)) in अर्कसातौ (*arkasātau*), that is, in the winning of worshipful food, which is the occasion." **NOTE**. Or else a seer of this name praised Indra for food, and Indra gave him very abundant food. Further: for the दास (*dāsa*), an asura who destroys living beings, you made (कः (*kaḥ*) = अकरोः (*akaroḥ*)) the earth a bed; the meaning is that you killed him and laid him low on the ground.

Then, in the third person: this wealthy Indra (मघवा (*maghavā*)) made the three earths (तिस्रो भूमीः (*tisro bhūmīḥ*))—the earths in the form of the Darśa, Paśu and Soma sacrifices, or the three worlds, earth, atmosphere and heaven—दानुचित्रा (*dānucitrā*), marvellous or to be gathered by gift, by the wealth to be given; करत् (*karat*) is करोति (*karoti*). Or else he made the three cities of iron, silver and gold दानुचित्रा (*dānucitrā*) by breaking them. Likewise in दुर्योणे (*duryoṇe*)—in an evil place, or for the pleasure of a king of that name—he struck down in battle (मृधि (*mṛdhi*)) the asura named Kuyavāca, who sounds evilly, (नि श्रेत् (*ni śret*), he injured).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—(O) Indra
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the wise Hotṛ, or the seer named Kavi
- अर्कसातौ (*arkasātau*)—for the gaining of food
- रपत् (*rapat*)—(he) praises (you)
- दासाय (*dāsāya*)—for the asura who harms living beings
- क्षां (*kṣāṃ*)—the earth
- उपबर्हणीं (*upabarhaṇīṃ*)—as a bed
- कः (*kaḥ*)—you made
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—this Indra, possessed of wealth
- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—the three rites in the form of Darśika, Pāśuka and Saumika, or the three worlds, earth, atmosphere and heaven
- दानु चित्राः (*dānu citrāḥ*)—marvellous by gifts or by wealth to be given
- करत् (*karat*)—makes

- [or तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—the three asura cities of iron, silver and gold; दानु चित्राः (*dānu citrāḥ*)—breaking them so as to look wonderful; करत् (*karat*)—made]
- तथा (*tathā*)—likewise
- दुर्योणे (*duryoṇe*)—in an evil place, or for the pleasure of the king named Duryoṇa
- कुयवाचं (*kuyavācaṃ*)—the asura (named Kuyavāca) who sounded evilly
- मृधि (*mṛdhi*)—in battle
- निश्रेत् (*niśret*)—he injured

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Hotṛ who desires food (the seer named Kavi) praises you; you have laid the asura who harms living beings on the bed of the earth; you, the lord of wealth, have filled earth, sky and heaven with wealth and the like (made the rites in the form of Darśika, Pāśuka and Saumika marvellous by wealth fit to be given); and for the pleasure of the king named Duryoṇa you destroyed the asura named Kuyavāca in battle.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sage praises you Indra, for the grant of desirable (food), since you have made the earth the bed of the Asura : Maghavan has made the three (regions) marvellous by his gifts, and has destroyed for (the prince) Duryoni (the Asura), Kuyavacha, in combat.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कविः (*kaviḥ*)—This word is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning: क्रांतदर्शि (*krāṃtadarśi*), one who has understood the far shore of knowledge, or अनू चानो वा (*anū cāno vā*), one who knows the tradition of performing sacrificial rites. Thus the Hotṛ priest, learned and excellent in the performance of rites, praises Indra in अर्कसातौ (*arkasātau*), in order to obtain the oblation, which is the means of invoking and worshipping the gods—one kind of meaning. Sāyaṇa then explains for this same sentence कविः अर्कसात् रपत् (*kaviḥ arkasāt rapat*) a second meaning: यद्वा एतन्नामर्षि अन्नार्थमस्तौत् इंद्रं ? तस्यातिप्रभूतमन्नं प्रादाः (*yadvā etannāmarṣi annārthamastaut iṃdraṃ ? tasyātiprabhūtamannaṃ prādāḥ*): since the seer named Kavi praised Indra in order to obtain food, Indra has granted him food.

अर्कसात् (*arkasāt*)—अर्जनीयस्यान्नस्य लाभे (*arjanīyasyānnasya lābhe*). Yāska reads the word अर्क (*arka*) both among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 3-11), and says अर्को नेवो भवति यषेनमर्चति (*arko nevo bhavati yaṣenamarcati*)

### Printed p. 349
The Kannada commentary continues: all deities who are to be worshipped are denoted by the word अर्क (*arka*). Also अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चति (*arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcati*): the mantra that is the means of worshipping deities or others is also spoken of by the word अर्क (*arka*). And अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि (*arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtāni*): the food that satisfies living beings and makes them objects of worship is likewise understood by the word अर्क (*arka*). For the word अर्क (*arka*) he shows three kinds of etymology: अर्च्यते, इति अर्कः (*arcyate, iti arkaḥ*), अर्चनसाधनमर्कः (*arcanasādhanamarkaḥ*), अर्चननिमित्तमपि अर्कः (*arcananimittamapi arkaḥ*). Then, अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्मा (*arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimmā*): because of its pungent quality, the tree too is denoted by the word अर्क (*arka*); this sense is described. Further, he cites the Ṛk
गायंति त्वा गायत्रिणोऽर्चंत्यर्कमकिणः । ब्रह्माणस्त्वा शतक्रत उद्यंशमिव येमिरॆ ॥ (*gāyaṃti tvā gāyatriṇo 'rcaṃtyarkamakiṇaḥ | brahmāṇastvā śatakrata udyaṃśamiva yemirè ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-1)
and explains अर्क (*arka*) and आर्कि (*ārki*) as "the worshipful one" and "those who worship". Thus Sāyaṇa's two kinds of explanation are set out here.

दासाय क्षां उपबर्हणीं कः (*dāsāya kṣāṃ upabarhaṇīṃ kaḥ*)—The word दास (*dāsa*) is stated as दासो दस्यतेरुपदासयति कर्माणि (*dāso dasyaterupadāsayati karmāṇi*) (Ni. 2-18): one who performs works abundantly, a worker, is a dāsa. Accordingly Sāyaṇa explains: Indra made the earth a bed for the Asura who destroys living beings greatly; हत्वा भूमावपातयः (*hatvā bhūmāvapātayaḥ*), having slain the Asura, he made him lie fallen on the earth. The word क्षा (*kṣā*) is read among the words for earth (Ni. 2-5); क्षा क्षियतेर्निवासकर्मणः (*kṣā kṣiyaternivāsakarmaṇaḥ*): the word क्षा (*kṣā*), formed from the root क्षि (*kṣi*) meaning "to dwell", is used in the sense of earth, as Yāska explains.

मघवा (*maghavā*)—The word मघ (*magha*) is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). Since it is used in the sense of wealth, Indra, possessing wealth, is called मघवा (*maghavā*).

तिस्रः दानुचित्राः करत् (*tisraḥ dānucitrāḥ karat*)—Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning for the word तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*) and for the word दानु (*dānu*), and so two meanings for this sentence. In the first, rites, when in the form of performance, are knowable by (contemplative) knowledge, pertain to the animal in the animal sacrifice, and pertain to the soma plant in the soma sacrifice; they thus have three forms. Hence the places where their fruit is obtained are also the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven. These rites, when they yield fruit, are acquired दानेन धनैर्देयै वा (*dānena dhanairdeyai vā*), by wealth or by other things fit to be given;

### Printed p. 350
this is the meaning. In this sense the word दानुचित्राः (*dānucitrāḥ*) is explained as "to be gathered by giving".

In the second sense: अयोरजतहिरण्मयाः पुरीः दानुचित्राः खंडनेन चित्राः अकरोत् (*ayorajatahiraṇmayāḥ purīḥ dānucitrāḥ khaṃḍanena citrāḥ akarot*). Because he says अथ परोक्षकृतः (*atha parokṣakṛtaḥ*), the sentence could be explained both historically and in terms of principle, yet only the historical meaning is given: Indra, with his thunderbolt, destroyed the three cities of iron, silver and gold which the Asuras, oppressing the world, had built for their protection, and broke them so that they became variegated. Here the word दानु (*dānu*) is formed from the root दो अवखंडने (*do avakhaṃḍane*) as दातु (*dātu*), used in the sense of breaking. (A meaning in terms of principle was possible — Indra as the knower, the mind's tamasic, rajasic and sattvic modes as the cities, which he destroyed — but it is not given here.)

In the sentence दुर्योणे कुयवाचं मृधि निश्रेत् (*duryoṇe kuyavācaṃ mṛdhi niśret*), one meaning is given: दुष्टयोन् स्थाने कुत्सितं शब्दायंतं असुरं (*duṣṭayon sthāne kutsitaṃ śabdāyaṃtaṃ asuraṃ*): Indra destroyed the Asura who made an evil sound in an evil place. In the second meaning: एतन्नामकस्य राज्यः प्रीत्यर्थं एतन्नामानमसुरं (*etannāmakasya rājyaḥ prītyarthaṃ etannāmānamasuraṃ*): out of regard for the king known by the name Duryoṇa, Indra destroyed in battle the Asura named Kuyava. Sāyaṇa explains the sense of these two sentences with अत्र परोक्षकृतः (*atra parokṣakṛtaḥ*).

##### Grammar

- रपत्—रप शब्दे धातुः । लज् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । बहुलं छंदस्य (पा. सू. ६-४-७५) इति अडागमो न भवति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- अर्कसात्—अर्कस्य सातिः यस्मिन् तस्मिन् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- दासाय—दसि सेवने धातुः । दंसे ष्टटन्ौ नअच (उ. सू. ५-६८८) इति ट, टन्, प्रत्ययः । धातुनकारस्य आकारादेशः । चुटो (पा. सू. १-३-७) इति टकारस्य लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति । **NOTE**
- कः—डुकृञ् करणे धातुः । लुज् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचने सिप् । इकारलोपः । मंत्रेघसह्व (पा. सू. २-४-८०) इति ब्लेः लुक् । प्रत्ययनिमित्तं धातोः इकः गुणः । र परो भवति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, those everlasting heroic deeds of yours, नव्या (*navyā*), are reached by the newer, present-day sages: through their praise they obtain them. Which are they? The many नभः (*nabhaḥ*), "injuries" (नभ (*nabha*) from the root meaning injury, with क्विप् (*kvip*)). For अविरणाय (*aviraṇāya*), the ending of war and the destruction of battle, you endured (सहः (*sahaḥ*), overcame) those injuries. For that purpose you split also the hostile, undivine, Asuric cities; भिनत् (*bhinat*) is a change of person, "you split", and न (*na*) has the sense "also". Likewise you bent (ननमः (*nanamaḥ*), made favourable) the thunderbolt of the unpraiseworthy, injuring Asura.
Or else: O Indra, those ancient waters of yours, ever praised in their times (a change of gender), come anew as praiseworthy. For what? अविरणाय (*aviraṇāya*): for the non-destruction of living beings. For that you subdued the injuring or obstructing clouds; and by their not raining you split the undivine, water-holding enclosures; likewise you bent the thunderbolt of Vṛtra, the undivine, hostile one.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- सना (*sanā*)—everlasting
- नव्याः (*navyāḥ*)—new (recent)
- पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—many
- नभः (*nabhaḥ*)—injuries (suffered by you)
- आ अगुः (*ā aguḥ*)—(the sages, under pretext of praise) experience
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those injuries
- अविरणाय (*aviraṇāya*)—for there to be no wars
- सहः (*sahaḥ*)—you endured
- भिदः (*bhidaḥ*)—destructive
- अदेवीः (*adevīḥ*)—belonging to the Asuras
- पुरः न (*puraḥ na*)—the cities also
- भिनत् (*bhinat*)—you split
- अदेवस्य (*adevasya*)—of the unpraiseworthy
- पीयोः (*pīyoḥ*)—of the injuring Asura
- वधः (*vadhaḥ*)—the thunderbolt
- ननमः (*nanamaḥ*)—(you bent) you turned so as to be favourable

Or: O Indra; सना (*sanā*)—eternally; ते (*te*)—related to you; पूर्विः ताः (*pūrviḥ tāḥ*)—those ancient waters; नव्याः (*navyāḥ*)—as praiseworthy; अविरणाय (*aviraṇāya*)—so that living beings do not perish; आ आगुः (*ā āguḥ*)—come; नभः (*nabhaḥ*)—the injuring or obstructing clouds; सहः (*sahaḥ*)—you made submissive; अदेवीः (*adevīḥ*)—displeasing (not raining); पुरः (*puraḥ*)—water-enclosures; भिनत् (*bhinat*)—you split; अदेवस्य (*adevasya*)—of the one of non-pleasing nature; पीयोः (*pīyoḥ*)—and hostile; Vṛtra's; वधः (*vadhaḥ*)—thunderbolt; ननमः (*nanamaḥ*)—you bent.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you split the destructive cities of the Asuras and broke the thunderbolt of the grievous, injuring Asura, in order to stop war; the sages always praise such daring deeds done by you with this aim, and the hardships you faced.

### Printed p. 353

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sages have celebrated your everlasting (as well as your) recent (exploits, in achieving which) you have endured many injuries in putting an end to war: verily, you have de molished the hostile and undivine cities; you have bowed down the thunderbolt of the undivine Asura.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नव्याः सना आगुः (*navyāḥ sanā āguḥ*)—Two kinds of meaning are given in this Ṛk. In the first, the word नव्य (*navya*) is explained by नव्याः इदानींतनाः ऋषयः (*navyāḥ idānīṃtanāḥ ṛṣayaḥ*), "the present-day sages". Addressing Indra, the present-day sages, not ancient ones, through praising obtain (come to know) his renowned exploits of all times, the displays of valour done with heroism. The Nirukta authors explain that the word नभः (*nabhaḥ*) as a noun denotes water and so on; here Sāyaṇa explains it as "injury". पूर्विः नभः अविरणाय सहः (*pūrviḥ nabhaḥ aviraṇāya sahaḥ*): Indra put aside many injuries so that wars should not occur (so that the world be kept peaceful); and he destroyed also the cities of the Asuras: thus his greatness is set out. This is the first meaning.
In the second meaning, पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*) is explained as पुरातन्यः आपः (*purātanyaḥ āpaḥ*) and नव्याः (*navyāḥ*) as स्तुत्याः (*stutyāḥ*); addressing Indra: the ancient waters, though always existing, are seen in the world as praiseworthy in their respective times; by them the life of living beings arises. And:
तदर्थं नभो हिंसकान्बंधकान्वा मेघान् सहः । मर्षणमकरोः । किंचादेवीः पुरोऽवर्षणेनादेवनशीलानुदकपुटबंधान् भिनत् । भिन्नानकरोः । तथादेवस्यादेवनशीलस्य पीयोः प्रतिकूलस्य । वृतस्य वधर्वज्रं ननमः । अनमयः ॥ (*tadarthaṃ nabho hiṃsakānbaṃdhakānvā meghān sahaḥ | marṣaṇamakaroḥ | kiṃcādevīḥ puro 'varṣaṇenādevanaśīlānudakapuṭabaṃdhān bhinat | bhinnānakaroḥ | tathādevasyādevanaśīlasya pīyoḥ pratikūlasya | vṛtasya vadharvajraṃ nanamaḥ | anamayaḥ ‖*)
For that very reason Indra, by his strength, restrained from doing injury the clouds that harm or cause trouble. By their nature of spreading darkness without releasing rain, the clouds, like cities filled with water, he split as one destroys the cities of enemies. The cloud that, by its nature of lacking light, obstructs the world, he struck with the thunderbolt and made it pour down rain: thus Indra's greatness is set out here.

- ता—तानि इति रूपे शेच्छंदसि बहुलं (पा. सू. ६-१-७०) इति शेः लोपः । अथवा लिंगव्यत्ययः ।
- अगुः—इण् गतौ धातुः । लुज् । प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचने झि प्रत्ययः । लुजीच (पा. सू. २-४-४३) इति धातोः गादेशः । गातिस्थाघुषा (पा. सू. २-४-७७) इति च्लेः सिचि आगते तस्य लुक् । आतः (पा. सू. ३-४-११०) इति झेः जुसादेशः । उस्यपदांतात् (पा. सू. ६-१-९६) इति पररूपं । तस्य अडागमः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- नभः—णभ हिंसायां धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । बहुवचनांतरूपं ।
- भिनत्—भिदिर् विदारणे धातुः । लज् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचने व्यत्ययो बहुलं इति तिप् प्रत्ययो भवति । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । रुधादिभ्यः त्नम् इति त्नम् विकरणं । मित्त्वात् अंत्याचः परो भवति । बहुलं छंदस्य (पा. सू. ६-४-७५) इति अडागमो न भवति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । विकरणस्वरो भवति ।
- भिदः—पूर्वोक्तधातोः क्विप् प्रत्ययः । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपं ।
- अदेवीः—नञ् तत्पुरुषसमासः । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपं । तत्पुरुषे शुल्यार्थ (पा. सू. ६-२-२) इति नञ्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । **NOTE**
- ननमः—णमु प्रह्वत्वे शब्दे च । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थको धातुः । लज् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचने सिप्, इकारलोपः, शप् विकरणं । व्यत्ययेन धातोः द्वित्वं । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- पीयोः—पा पाने धातुः । खरु तंकु पीयु (उ. सू. १-३६) इति कु प्रत्ययांततया निपातितं । षष्ठ्यंतरूपं ॥ ८ ॥ **NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं धुनिः कंपयिता शत्रूणामसि । अतो धुनिमतीः कंपनो
> पेततरंगवतीः । अथवा । धुनिर्नाम जलप्रतिरोधकार्यसुरः । स एव प्रतिबंधकतयो यासां तादृशीः । अप ऋणोः । अगमयः । भूमावपातयः । तत
> दृष्टांतः । स्रवंतीः प्रवहंतीः सीरा न । नदीनामैतत् । सरणवशीर्नदीरिव ।
> तद्वत्संतता इत्यर्थः । एवं कृत्वा हे शूर यद्यदा समुद्रमति पर्षि अतिक्रम्य
> पूरयस्युदकं तदानीं तुर्वशं यदुमुभावपि राजर्षी स्वस्त्रविनातं पारय ।
> अपालयः संपूर्णजलवर्षेन । तथा च मंत्रांतरं । त्वमपो यदवे
> तुर्वशायारमयः । ऋ ५-३१.८. । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is addressed as धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*), the one who makes his enemies tremble. So he has made the waters धुनिमतीः (*dhunimatīḥ*), "possessed of waves that shake". Alternatively, धुनि (*dhuni*) is the name of an Asura who obstructed the waters. The waters are then those that had him as their hindrance, and Indra made them fall on the earth (ऋणोः (*ṛṇoḥ*), "you sent"). The simile follows: the waters are like flowing rivers (सीरा न (*sīrā na*) is said of rivers). They flow like rivers in continuous streams. Then, "O hero, when you overflow the ocean and fill it with water, you have protected both royal sages, Turvaśa and Yadu, so that they come to no harm (स्वस्ति (*svasti*))", that is, you have kept them safe by sending down abundant rain. Sāyaṇa cites another mantra to the same effect: त्वमपो यदवे तुर्वशायारमयः (*tvamapo yadave turvaśāyāramayaḥ*) (Ṛ. 5-31.8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*)—one who makes (enemies) tremble with fear; you are such (therefore)
- धुनिमतीः (*dhunimatīḥ*)—wave-possessing, or having the Asura named Dhuni as their obstructor
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- स्रवंतीः (*sravaṃtīḥ*)—flowing
- सीराः न (*sīrāḥ na*)—like rivers (continuously)
- ऋणोः (*ṛṇoḥ*)—you sent forth (made them fall on the earth); having done so
- शूर (*śūra*)—O hero
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—the ocean
- प्र अति पर्षि (*pra ati parṣi*)—you overflow and fill (then)
- तुर्वशं (*turvaśaṃ*)—Turvaśa
- यदुं (*yaduṃ*)—and Yadu (the kings)
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—so that they do not perish
- पारय (*pāraya*)—you protected

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you cause trembling in your enemies. Such as you are, you slew the Asura named Dhuni, who had been holding back the waters. You sent the waters forth as streams and so filled the ocean, and you brought well-being to the two kings Turvaśa and Yadu.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You, Indra, are the terrorier (of your foes); you have made the trembling waters overspread (the earth) like flowing rivers : but, hero, when you fill the ocean, you have protected in their well-being Turvasha and Yadu.

### Printed p. 356

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*)—the one who causes trembling. Indra is described as the one who makes his enemies tremble. The word धुनि (*dhuni*) is formed from the root धूज् कंपने (*dhūj kaṃpane*) and is explained as धुनिः धुनोतेः (*dhuniḥ dhunoteḥ*) (Ni. 5-12). धुनयः (*dhunayaḥ*) is read among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24).

धुनिमतीः अपः ऋणोः (*dhunimatīḥ apaḥ ṛṇoḥ*): कम्मनोपेततरंगवतीः । अथवा जलप्रतिरोधकारी असुरः स एव प्रतिबंधकतया यासां तादृशीः अपः भूमावपातयः । (*kammanopetataraṃgavatīḥ | athavā jalapratirodhakārī asuraḥ sa eva pratibaṃdhakatayā yāsāṃ tādṛśīḥ apaḥ bhūmāvapātayaḥ |*). When waters flow they shake, and being full of waves they are called धुनिमत्यः (*dhunimatyaḥ*). Or, because the Asura who stops the waters from flowing is named Dhuni, the waters that have that obstructor Dhuni are called ध्युनिमत्यः (*dhyunimatyaḥ*). The meaning explained is that Indra destroyed the obstructing condition of such waters and made them flow on the earth.

स्रवंतीः सीरा न (*sravaṃtīḥ sīrā na*): सरणवतीर्नदीरिव । तद्वत्संगताः (*saraṇavatīrnadīriva | tadvatsaṃgatāḥ*). The word स्रवंत्यः (*sravaṃtyaḥ*) is stated among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24). The word न (*na*) is used here as a particle of comparison. The waters are likened to rivers that flow gathered together.

Indra is addressed by the word शूर (*śūra*): यत् समुद्रमतिपर्षि तुर्वशं यदुं स्वस्ति पारय (*yat samudramatiparṣi turvaśaṃ yaduṃ svasti pāraya*). When Indra filled the ocean with waters so that it overflowed, he protected the two royal sages Yadu and Turvaśa from harm and made them rejoice in the abundant rain. Sāyaṇa quotes the mantra त्वमपो यदवे तुर्वशायारमयः (*tvamapo yadave turvaśāyāramayaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-31-8) for the same sense.

The Nirukta author explains the meaning of the word स्वस्ति (*svasti*) with an example: स नः पितेव सूनवेऽग्ने सूपायनो भव । सचस्वा नः स्वस्तये । (*sa naḥ piteva sūnave 'gne sūpāyano bhava | sacasvā naḥ svastaye |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-9). Here the word स्वस्ति (*svasti*) is explained as स्वस्तीति अविनाशिनाम आस्तिरभिपूजितः सु अस्तीति (*svastīti avināśināma āstirabhipūjitaḥ su astīti*). The word अस्ति (*asti*) is used in the sense "worshipped". The prefix सु (*su*) joins it, giving the form स्वस्ति (*svasti*). Durgācārya comments that its meaning is अविनाशि (*avināśi*), "free from destruction".

### Printed p. 357
Further: स्वस्तिरिद्दि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्णस्वत्यभि या वाममेशि । सा नो अमा सो अरणे नि पातु स्वावेशा भवरु देवगोपा (*svastiriddi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇasvatyabhi yā vāmameśi | sā no amā so araṇe ni pātu svāveśā bhavaru devagopā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-63-16 **NOTE**). A goddess known as Svasti lives in the atmosphere, so she is a deity of the middle region, and her greatness is described in this Ṛk in this way. The Nirukta explains: स्वस्तिरेव हि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्ष्णस्वती धनवत्यभ्येति या वसूनि वननीयानि सा नोऽमा गृहे सा निरमणे सा निर्गमने पातु स्वावेशा भवतु देवी गोप््री देवान् गोपायत्विति देवा एनां गोपायंत्वि वा । (*svastireva hi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṣṇasvatī dhanavatyabhyeti yā vasūni vananīyāni sā no 'mā gṛhe sā niramaṇe sā nirgamane pātu svāveśā bhavatu devī goprī devān gopāyatviti devā enāṃ gopāyaṃtvi vā |*) (Ni. 11-48). On this Durgācārya explains as follows. The goddess Svasti is more praiseworthy than all the gods in the atmosphere. She always moves about, endowed with the water that is indispensable to all, like one who has filled herself with wealth. May that goddess protect us, whether we dwell in the forest or in the house. May she protect us so that we travel in comfort. May she protect the oblations offered with the gods in view, and the gods, and us. And may the middle-region gods in the sky, or the rays, protect this goddess.

##### Grammar

- धुनिः—धुञ् कंपने इति धातुः । स्वादिः । कर्तरि औणादिकः नि प्रत्ययः ।
- धुनिमतीः—धुनिः आसां संति इति धुनिमत्यः ताः । मतुप् प्रत्यये आगते स्त्रीत्वे उगितश्च इति जेप् ।
- ऋणोः—ऋणु गतौ इति धातुः । तनादिः । लज् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । इकारलोपः । तनादिकृञ्छ्यउः (पा. सू. ३-१-७९) इति उ विकरणः । सिप् निमित्तं कृत्वा तस्य गुणः । प्रत्ययस्य रुत्वं विसर्गः । छांदसत्वात् अडागमो न भवति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । विकरणस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- अपः—द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् । ऊडिदं पदा—(पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- सीराः—सिञ् बंधने इति धातुः । तुसिचिमीनां दीर्घश्च (उ. सू २-१८३) इति क्रन् प्रत्ययः । धातोः दीर्घः । कित्त्वात् गुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति । शूर इत्यपि अनेन एव सूत्रेण सिध्यति ।

### Printed p. 358
- स्रवंतीः—स्रु गतौ इति धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशे आगते उगितश्च (पा.सू. ४-१-६) इति जीप् । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् । जीप् लसार्वधातुकं च अनुदात्तं तस्मात् धातुस्वरो अवशिष्यते ।
- पर्षि—पृ पालनपूरणयोः इति धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । बहुलंछंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । प्रत्ययनिमित्तं कृत्वा धातोः इकः गुणः । रपरत्वं भवति ।
- पारय—पूर्वोक्तात् धातोः हेतुमति च इति णिच् । अचोञ्ञिति इति ऋकारस्य वृद्धिः । रपरत्वं भवति । णिजंतात् लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिपः हि आदेशः । शप् निमित्तं कृत्वा णिचः गुणः अयादेशः । अतोहेः इति हेः लुक् । तिजंतपरत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । णिच् स्वरो अवशिष्यते ।

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वम॒स्माक॑मिंद्र वि॒श्वध॑ स्या अवृ॒कत॑मो न॒रां नृ॑पा॒ता ।  
> स नो॒ विश्वा॑सां स्पृ॒धां स॑हो॒दा वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । अस्माकं । इंद्र । विश्वध । स्याः । अवृक्ततमः । नरां । नृपाता ।  
> सः । नः । विश्वासां । स्पृधां । सहःदाः । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरदानुं ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वमस्माकं विश्वध विश्वस्मिन्नपि काले विश्वप्रकारैर्वावृकृतमः ।
> यद्वा । दातृतम इत्यर्थः । स्याः । भव । तथा नरां नृपातास्मदीयानां पुत्रभृत्यादिरूपाणां बहूनां मनुष्याणां रक्षको भव । अपरो नृशबोऽनुवादः ।
> किंच स त्वं विश्वासां स्पृधां सर्वासां स्पर्धानिमित्तानामस्मत्सेनानां सहोदास्तासामर्थाय्यबलस्य दाता भव । विद्यामेति गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, be विश्वध (*viśvadha*), at every time or in every manner, our अवृकतमः (*avṛkatamaḥ*)", or, in the alternative, our greatest giver. Likewise be the protector of नरां (*narāṃ*), our many men such as sons and servants. The word नृ (*nṛ*) is a restatement of what नरां (*narāṃ*) already says. Further, be the giver of सहः (*sahaḥ*), strength, for the sake of all स्पृधां (*spṛdhāṃ*), all our armies engaged in rivalry. Of विद्याम (*vidyāma*) he says that it has been explained already.

### Printed p. 359

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—for us
- विश्वध (*viśvadha*)—at all times (in every manner)
- अवृकतमः (*avṛkatamaḥ*)—the best among protectors (among givers)
- स्याः (*syāḥ*)—be
- नरां नृपाता (*narāṃ nṛpātā*)—the protector of our men, sons, servants and the like (be)
- सः (*saḥ*)—such as you are
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- विश्वासां (*viśvāsāṃ*)—all
- स्पृधां (*spṛdhāṃ*)—engaged in rivalry, our army
- सहोदाः (*sahodāḥ*)—be the giver of strength
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—strength
- जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*)—long life
- विद्याम (*vidyāma*)—may we obtain (by your grace)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you alone are the special protector at all times and in every way. Protect also our sons, servants and the rest. Give strength to all our armies. Grant us food, strength and long life.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Be Indra, at all times our especial defender, the preserver of our people, the bestower of strength upon all these our emulous (followers); that we may obtain food, strength, and long life.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विश्वध अवृकतमः स्याः (*viśvadha avṛkatamaḥ syāḥ*): विश्वस्मिर्काले विश्वप्रकारैर्वा दातृतमः भव (*viśvasmirkāle viśvaprakārairvā dātṛtamaḥ bhava*). Addressing Indra, the poet wishes that at all times and in every way he may be gentle towards us, the sacrificers, knowing our true nature and understanding our sacrifice aright, or showing favour towards us. The Nirukta author quotes the Ṛk उदीरतामवर उत्परास उन्मध्यमाः पितरः सोम्यासः । असुं य ईयुरवृक्कायतज्ञास्तेनोऽवंतु पितरो हवेषु ॥ (*udīratāmavara utparāsa unmadhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ | asuṃ ya īyuravṛkkāyatajñāsteno 'vaṃtu pitaro haveṣu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-15-1), and explains: अवृका अनमित्राः सत्यज्ञा वा, यज्ञज्ञा ना (*avṛkā anamitrāḥ satyajñā vā, yajñajñā nā*).**NOTE** Durgācārya explains the word अवृक (*avṛka*) thus: अनमित्राः (*anamitrāḥ*) are those who have reached equality, who behave in one and the same manner towards those who have taken refuge in them; and also those who know the truth and the sacrifice. The wish is that Indra be अवृकतम (*avṛkatama*).

### Printed p. 360
नरां नृपाता (*narāṃ nṛpātā*): अस्मदीयानां पुत्रभृत्यादिरूपाणां बहूनां मनुष्यणां सर्वदा रक्षको भव (*asmadīyānāṃ putrabhṛtyādirūpāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ manuṣyaṇāṃ sarvadā rakṣako bhava*). The prayer is that Indra should always protect our people, who belong to us the sacrificers, in the form of children, servants and so on.

विश्वासां स्पृधां सहोदाः (*viśvāsāṃ spṛdhāṃ sahodāḥ*): सर्वसां स्पर्धानिमित्तानां अस्मत्सेनानां अर्थाय बलस्य दाता भव (*sarvasāṃ spardhānimittānāṃ asmatsenānāṃ arthāya balasya dātā bhava*). The wish is that Indra should produce strength in abundance, so that the prosperity of our helpers, the sacrificers who are rivals growing in competition with one another, may increase.

The sentence विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं (*vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānuṃ*) has been explained earlier in two or three places in the sense: "by Indra's grace may we obtain food, strength and the power of giving".

##### Grammar

- विश्वध—विश्व शब्दः । अस्मात् तसिल् प्रत्ययः । पृषोदरादीनि यथोपदिष्टम् इति प्रत्ययसकारस्य लोपः । तकारस्य धकारादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य लित्त्वात् लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इति प्रत्ययात् पूर्वस्य उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- अवृकतमः—नास्ति वृकः अस्मिन् इति अवृकः । बहुव्रीहौ नञ् सुभ्याम् इति उत्तरपदांतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । तस्मात् अतिशायनेतमबिष्ठनौ इति तमप् प्रत्ययः । स पित्त्वात् अनुदात्तो भवति ।
- नृपाता—अत्र नृ शब्दः पूर्वार्थं अनुवदति । पा रक्षणे इति धातुः । कर्तरि तृच् प्रत्ययः । चित्त्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- स्पृधाम्—स्पर्ध संघर्षे इति धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । छांदसत्वात् ऋकारस्य संप्रसारणं अकारलोपश्च भवतः । षष्ठीबहुवचनांतरूपम् । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

### Printed p. 361
## Sūkta 175 (Maṇḍala 1)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

The sūkta मत्स्यपायीति (*matsyapāyīti*) has six Ṛks and is the eleventh sūkta of the twenty-third anuvāka. Its seer is Agastya and its deity is Indra. Metres: the first Ṛk is a Skandhogrīvī Bṛhatī, because its second pāda has twelve syllables and the other three have eight. If the second pāda is the twelve-syllable one, the Ṛk is Nyaṅkusāriṇī, Urobṛhatī or Skandhogrīvī (Anukramaṇī 7.3). The last Ṛk is a Triṣṭubh. The remaining ones are Anuṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: मत्सि षळानुष्टुभं तु त्रिष्टुबंतं त्वाद्या स्कंधोग्रीवी (*matsi ṣaḷānuṣṭubhaṃ tu triṣṭubaṃtaṃ tvādyā skaṃdhogrīvī*). Use: in the second Svarasāman day the first three Ṛks are Stotriya verses; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section अभिजिद्दृहत्पृष्ट (*abhijiddṛhatpṛṣṭa*), prescribes this with the sūtra मत्स्यपायि ते मह एमेनं प्रत्येतन (*matsyapāyi te maha emenaṃ pratyetana*) (Ā. 8-5).

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta मत्स्यपायि ते (*matsyapāyi te*) is the eleventh sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka; it has six Ṛks. Agastya is the seer and Indra the deity. The Anukramaṇī statement (Anukra. 7-3) means: in the first Ṛk the first pāda has 12 syllables and the other three pādas eight each, so by the science of metre such a Ṛk is called Skandhogrīvī Bṛhatī or Urobṛhatī. If the second pāda has 12 syllables and the others eight each, it is called Nyaṅkusāriṇī Bṛhatī. The last Ṛk of the sūkta is Triṣṭubh; the other Ṛks are Anuṣṭubh. In the second Svarasāman, the first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as Stotriya mantras, as explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section Abhijid-bṛhat-pṛṣṭha, by the sūtra मत्स्यपायि ते मह एमेनं प्रत्येतन (*matsyapāyi te maha emenaṃ pratyetana*) (Ā. 8-5).

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 23; Sūkta 175
- Aṣṭaka 2; Adhyāya 4; Varga 18
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6
- Ṛṣi: Agastya
- Devatā: Indra
- Chandas: 1. Skandhogrīvī Bṛhatī; 2–5. Anuṣṭubh; 6. Triṣṭubh

### Printed p. 362
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मत्स्यपा॑यि ते॒ महः॒ पात्र॑स्येव हरिवो मत्स॒रो मदः॑ ।  
> वृषा॑ ते॒ वृष्ण॒ इंदु॑र्वा॒जी स॑हस्र॒सात॑मः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मत्सि । अपाययि । ते । महः । पात्रस्य इव । हरिः । मत्सरः । मदः ।  
> वृषा । ते । वृष्णे । इंदुः । वाजी । सहस्रसातमः ॥ १ ॥

> हे हरिवो हरिभ्यां तद्वन्निंद्र महो महान् पूज्योऽयं सोमः

> पिबसि अतो मत्सि । माद्यसि मादयस्व वा । पात्रे यथा सोमः पूर्यते
