##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Hari-yoked Indra, this great, venerable Soma has been drunk by you, as it is held by its vessel" — the genitive is in the sense of the instrumental. Or else the construction is: great Soma, as if your own from the vessel. अपायि (*apāyi*) means "is drunk"; the aorist-like form is used because a wish is intended. Because you drink, you rejoice, or cause yourself to rejoice. As Soma fills the vessel, so drink abundantly and, having drunk, be exhilarated. Further: for you, the showerer of desired things (the genitive is in the sense of the dative), it is exhilarating, a means of intoxication, satisfying, showering, moistening (delighting), and वाजी (*vājī*) means "possessed of food" — called so because it gives the satisfaction of food. सहस्रसातमः (*sahasrasātamaḥ*) means a most boundless giver, or one of surpassing power sufficient to serve a thousand men. Such a Soma has been prepared; drink it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, possessed of the pair of horses called Hari
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—to the showerer of desires
- ते (*te*)—for you
- मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—the means of intoxication
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—satisfying
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—granting what is wished
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—moistening (delighting)
- वाजी (*vājī*)—possessed of food (satisfying like food)
- सहस्रसातमः (*sahasrasātamaḥ*)—having the power of giving without measure (the Soma has been prepared)
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—this venerable Soma
- पात्रस्य इव (*pātrasya iva*)—as it is held by the vessel
- ते (*te*)—by you
- अपायि (*apāyi*)—is drunk
- मत्सि (*matsi*)—(therefore) you rejoice

### Printed p. 363

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, possessed of the horses called Hari: the Soma juice, showering desires, giving satisfaction and joy, delighting, satisfying like food, giving boundless bliss, has been made ready for you. Drink this venerable Soma abundantly, as a vessel is filled to the full, and be satisfied by it.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Lord of steeds, you are exhilarated when the sacred (Soma juice) has been imbibed by you as by its (appropriate) vessel ; for to you, showerer (of benefits), it is exhilarating, inebiating, invigorating, the yieldder of delight, (satisfying as) food, and the giver of a thousand (pleasures).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

By द्वितीये स्वरसामि (*dvitīye svarasāmi*) …, Sāyaṇa states the use of the mantras of this sūkta: they are mantras to be recited on Svarasāman days. Svarasāman is the name of certain sacrificial days. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra and its commentary explain the term thus:
अभिप्लवत्र्यहः पूर्वः स्वरसामाना । स्वराणि श्विह पृष्टानि । शेषां स्तोत्रिया यज्जायथा अपूर्वमत्स्यपायि ते मह......... (*abhiplavatryahaḥ pūrvaḥ svarasāmānā | svarāṇi śviha pṛṣṭāni | śeṣāṃ stotriyā yajjāyathā apūrvamatsyapāyi te maha.........*) (Aś. Śrau. 8-5)
The commentary gives a fuller explanation of what the sūtras say:
अभिप्लवस्य यः पूर्वस्त्र्यहस्तेनातिदिष्टानि वक्ष्यमाणगुणविशिष्टानि त्रीण्यहानि स्वरसामसंज्ञानि भवंति। स्वरसंज्ञकानि सामानि एतेष्वहस्सु पृष्टानि भवंति । एतदेवैषु स्वरसामशब्दस्य प्रवृत्तिनिमित्तं । यथासंख्येन शेषामेते स्तोत्रिया भवंति । (*abhiplavasya yaḥ pūrvastryahastenātidiṣṭāni vakṣyamāṇaguṇaviśiṣṭāni trīṇyahāni svarasāmasaṃjñāni bhavaṃti| svarasaṃjñakāni sāmāni eteṣvahassu pṛṣṭāni bhavaṃti | etadevaiṣu svarasāmaśabdasya pravṛttinimittaṃ | yathāsaṃkhyena śeṣāmete stotriyā bhavaṃti |*) (Nārāyaṇa's Vṛtti).
In connection with the Abhiplava sacrifice, the first three days are called Svarasāman. The sāmans called Svara become Pṛṣṭha on these days. That is the reason for the use of the word Svarasāman. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa explains the same and states the importance of Svarasāman thus:
स्वरसाम्न उपयंतीमे वै लोकाः स्वरसामान इमान्वै लोकान् स्वरसामभिरस्वण्वंस्तत्स्वरसाम्नां स्वरसामत्वं तद्यत्स्वरसाम्न उपयंतेष्टेवैनं कल्लोकेष्वाभजंति । (*svarasāmna upayaṃtīme vai lokāḥ svarasāmāna imānvai lokān svarasāmabhirasvaṇvaṃstatsvarasāmnāṃ svarasāmatvaṃ tadyatsvarasāmna upayaṃteṣṭevainaṃ kallokeṣvābhajaṃti |*) (Ai. Brā. 4-19)

### Printed p. 364
These three worlds are the Svarasāman days. Because the sacrificers satisfy these three worlds with the Svarasāmans, these days became famous as Svarasāman days. By performing the rites to be done on these days, the sacrificers impel Āditya to be the agent of the activities of the three worlds. The scholar Haug criticises this explanation thus:
This etymology is certainly fanciful. Swara cannot be traced to the root स्वृण् (*svṛṇ*), a modification of प्री (*prī*) to love. The name literally means "The samans of the tones" This appears to refer to some peculiarities in their intonations. These Samans being required only for great सत्त (*satta*) which have been out of use for at least a thousand years. it is difficult now to ascertain the exact nature of the Samans. (Aiteraya Brahmana. P. 290 Translation by Haug.)
That is: the derivation that shows the root प्री (*prī*), in the altered form स्वण् (*svaṇ*), to be the source of this word is not very apt. The name must belong to sāmans that have a peculiarity in their arrangement of tones and are to be recited at sattras and the like. Since sacrifices performed thousands of years ago are no longer practised, the nature and the tone-rules of the sāmans recited then cannot be known exactly; so the scholar gives his opinion. The book also explains the reasons for the days' arrangement and for the rites done on them, before and after them, in relation to Āditya's revolution and so on:
तस्य वै देवा अदित्यस्य स्वर्गाल्लोकादव पातादबिभयुस्तं त्रिभिः स्वर्गैर्लोकैरवस्तात्पत्युत्तभ्नुवन् स्तोमा वै त्रयो लोकास्तस्य पराचोऽतिपाताद बिभयुस्तं त्रिभिः स्वर्गैर्लोकैः परस्तात्पत्युत्तभ्नुवन् स्तोमा वै त्रयः स्वर्गा लोकास्तत्रयोऽवस्तात्सप्तदशा भवंति त्रयः परस्तान्मध्य एष एकविंश उभयतः स्वरसामभिर्धृत उभयतो हि वा एष स्वरसामभिर्धृतस्तस्मादेषो०तरेमालोकान्यन्न व्यथते । (*tasya vai devā adityasya svargāllokādava pātādabibhayustaṃ tribhiḥ svargairlokairavastātpatyuttabhnuvan stomā vai trayo lokāstasya parāco 'tipātāda bibhayustaṃ tribhiḥ svargairlokaiḥ parastātpatyuttabhnuvan stomā vai trayaḥ svargā lokāstatrayo 'vastātsaptadaśā bhavaṃti trayaḥ parastānmadhya eṣa ekaviṃśa ubhayataḥ svarasāmabhirdhṛta ubhayato hi vā eṣa svarasāmabhirdhṛtastasmādeṣo0taremālokānyanna vyathate |*) (Ai. Brā. 4-81)
The gods, fearing Āditya's fall, placed a supporting pillar for Āditya beneath the three worlds. The Svarasāmans are these pillars. Then, fearing a fall again, they set up a pillar in the form of Svarasāman above the three worlds as well. These are in the form of these three

### Printed p. 365
worlds. The three stomas before the Viṣuvat day and the three after it together make the group of seventeen stomas. In the middle of these stands the Ekaviṃśa day, which rests on the Svarasāman days and reflects Āditya. Because he is held by the Svarasāmans, Āditya's revolution meets no hindrance in the three worlds.
तेषां वै देवाः सप्तदशानां प्रव्लयादबिभयुः समा इव वै स्तोमा अविगूह्ला इवेमे ह न प्रव्लियेरन्निति तान् सर्वैः स्तोमैरवस्तात्पर्यार्षन् सर्वैः पृष्टैः परस्तात्तद्यदभिजित्सर्वस्तोमोऽवस्ताद्भवति विश्वजित्सर्वपृष्ठः परस्तात्तत्सप्तदशानुभयतः पर्यषंति धृत्या अप्रव्लयाय । (*teṣāṃ vai devāḥ saptadaśānāṃ pravlayādabibhayuḥ samā iva vai stomā avigūhlā iveme ha na pravliyeranniti tān sarvaiḥ stomairavastātparyārṣan sarvaiḥ pṛṣṭaiḥ parastāttadyadabhijitsarvastomo 'vastādbhavati viśvajitsarvapṛṣṭhaḥ parastāttatsaptadaśānubhayataḥ paryaṣaṃti dhṛtyā apravlayāya |*) (Ai. Brā. 4-19)
Fearing that these seventeen stomas, in the form of Svarasāmans, might fall without support, the gods covered them below with all the stomas and above with the pṛṣṭhas. Therefore on the Abhijit day, before the Svarasāman days, they recite with all the stomas, and on the Viśvajit day after them, with the pṛṣṭha. These save the seventeenfold stoma from falling; thus the distinctive character of the Svarasāmans and of their related stotras is praised. And in telling their origin, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says:
त्रिष्टुभं छंदो ग्रीष्मादृतोर्निरमिमीत त्रिष्टुभः स्वारमिति त्रिष्टुभश्चंदसः स्वारग्‌ंसाम निरमिमीत स्वारादंतर्याम इति । (*triṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdo grīṣmādṛtorniramimīta triṣṭubhaḥ svāramiti triṣṭubhaścaṃdasaḥ svāragṃsāma niramimīta svārādaṃtaryāma iti |*) (Śa. Brā. 8-1-1-8)
Viśvakarman fashioned the Triṣṭubh metre from the summer season, from the Triṣṭubh the Svarasāman, and from the Svarasāman the Antaryāma cup. Further, in the sacrifice called गवां अयनं (*gavāṃ ayanaṃ*), performed over one year, the Svarasāman days are very important. The division of time for this performance is:
1. The Prāyaṇīya Atirātra: the opening day.
2. The Caturviṃśa day: made of the twenty-four stoma.
3. Five months, each containing four Abhiplava ṣaḍahas and one Pṛṣṭya ṣaḍaha.
4. The (sixth) month containing the Abhijit day and the three Svarasāman days.
5. The Viṣuvat day, with the Ekaviṃśa stoma.
6. The seventh month containing the Viśvajit day and again three Svarasāman days; and so on.
Thus the order of origin of the Svarasāman days, which are an essential part of the year of the Gavāmayana, is explained as follows.

सवंत्सराच्चतुर्विग्०तमहः । ब्रह्मणोऽभिप्लवं क्षत्रात्पृश्यमग्नेरभिजितमद्भ्यः स्वरनाम्न आदित्याद्विषुवंतमुक्ताः स्वरसामान्यः ॥ (*savaṃtsarāccaturvig0tamahaḥ | brahmaṇo 'bhiplavaṃ kṣatrātpṛśyamagnerabhijitamadbhyaḥ svaranāmna ādityādviṣuvaṃtamuktāḥ svarasāmānyaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 12-1-2-2)
From the year came the Caturviṃśa day, from Brahman the Abhiplava, from the kṣatra the Pṛṣṭha, from Agni the Abhijit, from water the Svarasāman, from Āditya the Viṣuvat day. This states the order of the Svarasāman days. The connection between water and Āditya is also stated above. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa explains the same:
अथ यत्स्वरसाम्न उपयंति । अप एव देवतां यजंत अपो देवता भवंतपाग्ं सायुज्यग्ं सलोकतां जयति। अथ यद्विषुवंतमुपयंति। आदित्यमेव देवताग्ंयजंत आदित्यो देवता भवंत्यादित्यस्य सायुज्यग्ं सलोकतां जयत्युक्ताः स्वरसामान्यः । ( (*atha yatsvarasāmna upayaṃti | apa eva devatāṃ yajaṃta apo devatā bhavaṃtapāgṃ sāyujyagṃ salokatāṃ jayati| atha yadviṣuvaṃtamupayaṃti| ādityameva devatāgṃyajaṃta ādityo devatā bhavaṃtyādityasya sāyujyagṃ salokatāṃ jayatyuktāḥ svarasāmānyaḥ | (*) (Śa. Brā. 12-1-2-13)
All who perform rites on the Svarasāman days worship water, the cause and presiding deity of the Svarasāman; as the fruit of that worship they attain sāyujya with water. Likewise those who offer worship on the Viṣuvat day attain sāyujya with Āditya, who is related to it. This is the distinctive character of the Svarasāmans. Further, stating the identity of the Puruṣa with the year of the Gavāmayana:
पुरुषो वै संवत्सरः । तस्य पादादेव प्रायणीयोऽतिरात्रः पादाभ्याग्ंहि प्रयंति................ ॥ १ ॥ (*puruṣo vai saṃvatsaraḥ | tasya pādādeva prāyaṇīyo 'tirātraḥ pādābhyāgṃhi prayaṃti................ ‖ 1 ‖*)
अयमेव दक्षिणो बाहुरभिजित् । इम एव दक्षिणो त्रयः प्राणाः स्वरसामानो मूर्धा विषुवानिम एवोत्तरे त्रयः प्राणाः स्वरसामानः ॥ २ ॥ (*ayameva dakṣiṇo bāhurabhijit | ima eva dakṣiṇo trayaḥ prāṇāḥ svarasāmāno mūrdhā viṣuvānima evottare trayaḥ prāṇāḥ svarasāmānaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 12-1-4-2)
The year is the Puruṣa; the Prāyaṇīya Atirātra, the opening day of the Gavāmayana, is his foot. As the foot is the means of movement, this Atirātra is the means of the movement that is the carrying out of rites ........ The Abhijit day is his right arm; the Svarasāmans of the Abhijit day are the three chief breaths of his right side. The Viṣuvat day is the head; the Svarasāmans related to it are the three chief breaths of the left side. So it is praised. Discussing the distinctive character of the Svarasāmans to be sung on these days and the manner of singing, the English scholar Eggling says as follows.

### Printed p. 367
"स्वारसामन् (*svārasāman*)" is the name of a chanted verse which has no special concluding nidhana or finale, but in which the svarita (circumflex), the first rising and then falling pitch of the final vowel, takes the place of the finale; whence svara is often explained as svaranidhana, i.e. having the svarita for its nidhana. In the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa (IX. 3. 11) the Svārasāman is prescribed in case the Udgātṛs have previously committed an excess in their chanting............In the Lāṭyāyana Śrauta Sūtra (VI. 9. 6) Svara-sāmans thus treated are called पदानुस्वाराणि (*padānusvārāṇi*), whilst those with which the musical syllables "हा इ (*hā i*)" are used with a similar effect are called हायिकारस्वराणि (*hāyikārasvarāṇi*).................................
(Sacred Books of the East, Vol. XLIII, pp. 6-7)

Āśvalāyana, in the sūtra मत्स्यपायि ते मह एमेनं प्रत्येतन (*matsyapāyi te maha emenaṃ pratyetana*) (Āśva. Śrau. 8-5), has stated that the present sūkta, which contains the mantra "मत्स्यपायि (*matsyapāyi*)", is to be recited on the Svarasāma days belonging to the Niṣuvat day (the second part).

हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—With this word Indra is addressed. The reading हरी इंद्रस्य (*harī iṃdrasya*) (Ni. 2-28) is given: since Indra's vehicles are named हरी (*harī*), Sāyaṇa has explained it as Indra "possessing them".

पात्रस्येव ते अपायि (*pātrasyeva te apāyi*)—सोमपात्रेण यथा धार्यते सोमः यद्वा पात्रस्येव ते तव स्वभूतो महान् सोम इति वा योजना (*somapātreṇa yathā dhāryate somaḥ yadvā pātrasyeva te tava svabhūto mahān soma iti vā yojanā*). For the word पात्रस्येव (*pātrasyeva*) one meaning is, in the instrumental sense, "as the Soma juice is filled and held by the Soma vessel". Just as महः (*mahaḥ*) conveys the sense "worthy of worship", so, since it is also used in the sense "abundant", the meaning "abundant" is given to महः (*mahaḥ*). For the word पात्र (*pātra*) the meaning "one who is worthy" is stated. Because the abundant Soma juice that is Indra's own, Indra being worthy to drink Soma, has been offered for drinking, the wish is expressed that Indra may drink the Soma.

मत्सि (*matsi*)—माद्यसि मादयस्व ना । पात्रे यथा सोमः पूर्यते तथा अत्यधिकं पिब पीत्वा च मादयस्व । (*mādyasi mādayasva nā | pātre yathā somaḥ pūryate tathā atyadhikaṃ piba pītvā ca mādayasva |*) The wish is described that, as the Soma juice fills the vessel from which Soma is drunk, so Indra may drink it abundantly and become exhilarated.

The Soma juice is मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—an instrument in producing exhilaration; मदः (*madaḥ*)—a producer of delight; वर्षिता (*varṣitā*)—an increaser of strength; इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—an augmenter of refreshment. Thus the qualities of Soma are described.

### Printed p. 368
वाजी (*vājī*)—since food is satisfying, "possessing food"; सहस्रसातमः (*sahasrasātamaḥ*)—one who increases the power of giving without measure, or the abundant power that restrains a thousand heroes. Thus the effect of the Soma juice is explained. The wish is expressed that Indra may drink the Soma juice possessing this effect.

##### Grammar

- मत्सि — मद तृप्तियोगे । धातुः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । खरि च इति दकारस्य चर्त्वम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । सिप् पित्त्वात् धातुस्वरः अवतिष्ठते ।
- अपायि — पा पाने । धातुः । आशंसायां भूतवच्च (पा. सू. ३-३-१३२) इति भूतकालप्रत्ययो लुङ् आगच्छति । (कर्मणि) प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने त प्रत्ययः । चिण् भावकर्मणोः (पा. सू. ३-१-६६) इति च्लेः चिणादेशः । आतोयुक् चिण् कृतोः (पा. सू. ७-३-३३) इति धातोर्युकागमः । चिणो लुक् (पा. सू. ६-४-१०४) इति तशब्दस्य लुक् । अंगस्य अडागमः । पूर्वं तिजंतत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । अडागमस्य उदात्तत्वात् आद्युदात्तो भवति ।
- पात्रस्य इव — सुपां सुपो भवंति इति वाक्येन तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी आगता ।
- मत्सरः — मदी हर्षे । धातुः । कृधूमदिभ्यः कित् (उ. सू. ३-३५३) इति सरप्रत्ययः । खरि च सूत्रेण धातुदकारस्य तकारादेशः । चित् इति पूर्वसूत्रात् अनुवृत्तत्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- मदः — पूर्वोक्ताय धातवे बहुलग्रहणेन कर्तरि मदोनुपसर्गे (पा. सू. ३-३-६७) इति अप् प्रत्ययः । अयं पित्त्वात् अनुदात्तो भवति ।
- इंदुः — उंदी क्लेदने । धातुः । उंदेरिच्चादेः (उ. सू. १-२) उन् प्रत्ययः । धातोरादेः इकारादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- सहस्रसातमः — सहस्रं सनुते ददाति इति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने । धातुः । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् (पा. सू. ३-२-६७) इति विट् प्रत्ययः । निड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् (पा. सू. ९-४-४१) इति धातोर्नकारस्य आत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । तदुपरि अतिशयार्थे तमस् प्रत्ययः । अयं पित्त्वात् अनुदात्तो भवति । **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ न॑स्ते गंतु मत्स॒रो वृषा॒ मदो॒ वरे॑ण्यः ।  
> स॒हावा॑ इंद्र सान॒सिः पृ॑तना॒षाळम॑र्त्यः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । ते । गंतु । मत्सरः । वृषा । मदः । वरेण्यः ।  
> सहवान् । इंद्र । सानसिः । पृतनाषाट् । अमर्त्यः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते त्वां नोऽस्मदीयो मत्सरो मर्षणसाधनः सोम आ गंतु ।
> आगच्छतु । कीदृशोऽयं । वृषा वर्षकः मदस्तर्पयिता वरेण्यो वरणेयः
> सहावान् सहायवान् सहसा बलेन तद्वान्वा सानसिः संभजनीयः पृतनाषाट्
> शत्रुसेनाया अभिभविता अमर्तोऽविनाशी । ईदृशः सोमस्त्वामागच्छतु । यद्वा ।
> उत्तरार्ध इंद्रपरतया व्याख्येयः । हे इंद्र सहानानस्मद्दत्तसोमसहायवान्
> बलवान्वा सानसिरस्माभिः संभजनीयः पृतनाषाडमर्त्यश्च भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, may our Soma, the instrument of exhilaration (मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*), from "bearing/overcoming"), come to you. What kind is it? वृषा (*vṛṣā*) a showerer; मदः (*madaḥ*) a satisfier; वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*) choice-worthy; सहावान् (*sahāvān*) helpful, or possessing strength (सहसा (*sahasā*)); सानसिः (*sānasiḥ*) to be shared in; पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*) an overpowerer of the enemy's army; अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*) imperishable. Such a Soma, may it come to you. Or else: the latter half is to be explained as referring to Indra: O Indra, you are सहावान् (*sahāvān*), helped by the Soma given by us, or strong; सानसिः (*sānasiḥ*), to be shared in by us; and पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*) and immortal.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) इंद्र (*(he) iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—showerer of desires
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—satisfying
- वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—desirable
- सहावान् (*sahāvān*)—possessed of help (strength)
- सानसिः (*sānasiḥ*)—to be enjoyed
- पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*)—destroyer of enemies
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—imperishable
- मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—the Soma juice that is the instrument of exhilaration
- ते (*te*)—to you
- आ गंतु (*ā gaṃtu*)—may it reach
- [Or: नः वृषा, मदः, वरेण्यः (*naḥ vṛṣā, madaḥ, vareṇyaḥ*)—showerer of desires, satisfying, choice-worthy; मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—the Soma juice offered by us, the instrument of exhilaration; ते आ गंतु (*te ā gaṃtu*)—may it reach you (and having drunk it you); सहावान् (*sahāvān*)—strong; सानसिः (*sānasiḥ*)—attainable by us; पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*)—destroyer of enemies; अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—imperishable (you become).]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Soma juice, showerer of desires, satisfying, desirable, the instrument of exhilaration, offered by us, reaches you; having drunk it, become strong, attainable by us, destroyer of enemies, imperishable.

### Printed p. 370

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May our Soma libation reach you, (for it is) exhilarating, invigorating, inebriating, most precious : it is companionable, Indra, enjoyable, the overthrower of hosts, immortal.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the words मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*), वृषा (*vṛṣā*), मदः (*madaḥ*), वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*), सहावान् (*sahāvān*), सानसिः (*sānasiḥ*), पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*), अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*) are described as being used as epithets of the Soma juice. Since the meanings of these words were explained in the previous Ṛk, they are not explained again here.

पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*)—The word पृतनाः (*pṛtanāḥ*) is stated among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Since those who fight in battles are the people of armies, the meaning "enemy army" is explained here. The explanation शत्रुसेनायाः अभिभविता (*śatrusenāyāḥ abhibhavitā*) is given, meaning that Soma produces the ability to conquer the enemy army.

By established usage this word is an epithet of Indra, describing Indra's distinction. But in the Ṛksaṃhitā it is not an epithet of Indra alone; it is an epithet also of Agni and other deities and indicates their prowess. For example—
कृणोत धूमं वृषणं सखायोऽस्रेधंत इतन वाजमच्छ । अयमग्निः पृतनाषाट् सुवीरो येन देवासो असहंत दस्यून् ॥ (*kṛṇota dhūmaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ sakhāyo 'sredhaṃta itana vājamaccha | ayamagniḥ pṛtanāṣāṭ suvīro yena devāso asahaṃta dasyūn ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29 9)
Here, with पृतनोपलक्षितं युद्धं सहमानः (*pṛtanopalakṣitaṃ yuddhaṃ sahamānaḥ*), it indicates Agni's prowess. And व्याप्रियंते अत्र योद्धारः इति पृतनाः संग्रामाः (*vyāpriyaṃte atra yoddhāraḥ iti pṛtanāḥ saṃgrāmāḥ*): since it is the place where warriors gather and form groups, battle is named पृतना (*pṛtanā*), so in one place (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-49-2); and also in
इमं नरो मरुतः सच्चता वृधं यस्मिन्रायः शेवृथासः । अभि ये संति पृतनासु दूढ्यो विश्वाहा शत्रुमादभुः ॥ (*imaṃ naro marutaḥ saccatā vṛdhaṃ yasminrāyaḥ śevṛthāsaḥ | abhi ye saṃti pṛtanāsu dūḍhyo viśvāhā śatrumādabhuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-16-2)
Sāyaṇa gives, in another place, पृतनासु सेनासु तदुपलक्षितेषु संग्रामेषु (*pṛtanāsu senāsu tadupalakṣiteṣu saṃgrāmeṣu*) as the derivation of this word. The Nirukta authors have included this word among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Since he shows his strength in battles consisting of such enemy armies and withstands the enemy's force, it is natural for this epithet to belong either to Indra or to Agni. In the present Ṛk, however, it is an epithet of Soma.

### Printed p. 371
मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—For this word one meaning is "cause of exhilaration", and another is "possessing jealousy". The Nirukta author too has given both meanings for this word.
मत्सर सोमो मंदशेस्तृप्तिकर्मणः (*matsara somo maṃdaśestṛptikarmaṇaḥ*)
(Ni. 9-25)
It is formed from the root मंद् (*maṃd*), which gives the sense "produce satisfaction", and is used as a synonym of the Soma juice; and मत्सर इति लोभ नाम (*matsara iti lobha nāma*): since it shows excessive desire and self-assertion, it is named मत्सर (*matsara*); such is the Nirukta author's derivation of this word. In the present Ṛk it means either "cause of exhilaration" or "excelling, in rivalry with the Soma juices of other sacrifices".

Having thus explained these words in the bhāṣya, he explains उत्तरार्धः इंद्रपरतया व्याख्येयः (*uttarārdhaḥ iṃdraparatayā vyākhyeyaḥ*): it is appropriate to interpret the latter half as referring to Indra. Hence, addressing Indra as हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*), Indra is अस्मद्दत्तसोमसहायवान् (*asmaddattasomasahāyavān*), helped by the Soma juice offered by the sacrificers; or बलवान् (*balavān*), possessed of strength; सानसिः (*sānasiḥ*), worthy of being attained by the sacrificers; पृतनाषाधमर्त्यश्च (*pṛtanāṣādhamartyaśca*), one who has the power to carry on battles and overcome enemy armies, and one who is free of the nature of death. Thus Indra's abundant power is described here.

##### Grammar

- गंतु — गम्‌ल्य गतौ धातुः । लोट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । एरुः इति उत्वम् । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । धातुमकारस्य अनुस्वारः परसवर्णः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- वरेण्यः — वृञ् वरणे धातुः । वृञ् एण्यः (उ. सू. ३-३७८) इति एण्यप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययनिमित्तत्वेन धातोरिको गुणः । र परत्वेन आगच्छति । वृषादौ संगृहीतत्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- सहवान् — मतुप् आगते माधुपधायात्थ इति मकारस्य वत्वम् । अन्येषामपि दृश्यते इति पूर्वस्य संहितायां दीर्घो भवति । अस्य इंद्र इति परतो दीर्घादट समानपादे (पा. सू. ८-३-९) इति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । आशोटिनित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-३-३) इति आकारस्य अनुनासिकभावो भवति । **NOTE**
- सानसि — षण संभक्तौ । धातुः । अस्मात् सानसिधर्णसि (उ. सू. ४-५४७) इति असि प्रत्ययः वृद्धिः अंतोदात्तस्वरश्च निपातितः ।

### Printed p. 372

##### Grammar

- पृतनाषाट् — षह मर्षणे । धातुः । छंदसिसहः (पा. सू. ७-२-११६) इति ण्व प्रत्ययः । आत उपधायाः (पा. सू. ८-३-५६) इति उपधावृद्धिः । सहेः साडः सः (पा. सू. ८-३-५६) इति पदांते धातुसकारस्य षत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं हि शूरः॒ सनि॑ता चो॒दयो॒ मनु॑षो॒ रथं॑ ।  
> स॒हावा॒न्दस्यु॑मव्र॒तमोषः॒ पात्रं॒ न शो॒चिषा॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । हि । शूरः । सनिता । चोदयः । मनुषः । रथं ।  
> सह्यवान् । दस्युं । अव्रतं । ओषः । पात्रं । न । शोचिषा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं खलु शूरः शौर्योपेतः सनिता दातासि । अतो मनुषो
> मानुष्यस्य मे रथं रंहणं स्पंदनं मनोरथं वा स्वर्गगमनसाधनं यज्ञाख्यं
> रथं वा चोदयः । प्रेरय । किंच त्वं सहावान् सोमसहायवान् बलवान्वा
> भूत्वा दस्युमुपक्षपयितारमव्रतमकर्माणमननुष्ठायिनमोषः । दह । किमिव ।
> शोचिषा दीप्या ज्वालयाग्निः पात्रं न स्वाधारं पात्रविशेषमिव । यागाधिकारी
> सन्नो न यजते तं दहेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you are heroic, endowed with valour, and a giver. Therefore impel the chariot (रथं (*rathaṃ*)) of me, a man (मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)): the chariot meaning speed or motion, or my desire, or the chariot called sacrifice, the means of going to heaven. Further, being सहावान् (*sahāvān*), helped by Soma or strong, burn (ओषः (*oṣaḥ*)) the दस्युं (*dasyuṃ*), the destroyer, who is अव्रतं (*avrataṃ*), without rites and not performing them. Like what? As fire with its flame (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)) burns a vessel (पात्रं न (*pātraṃ na*)), a particular vessel of its own support. The meaning is: burn him who, being qualified for the sacrifice, does not sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- *(he iṃdra)*—O Indra
- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—heroic
- त्वं हि (*tvaṃ hi*)—are you not
- सनिता (*sanitā*)—the giver (to us)
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—of me, a man (therefore)
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the desire (the chariot of sacrifice, the means of going to heaven)
- चोदयः (*codayaḥ*)—impel
- *(kiṃca tvaṃ)*—and further, you
- सहावान् (*sahāvān*)—endowed with the help of Soma (strong)
- दस्युं (*dasyuṃ*)—the destroyer
- अव्रतं (*avrataṃ*)—one without rites
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with the flame (as fire)
- पात्रं न (*pātraṃ na*)—as it burns a vessel of its own support
- ओषः (*oṣaḥ*)—burn

### Printed p. 373

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are a hero and a giver to us. Impel the chariot of me, a mortal, that is, my heart's desire or my sacrifice, so that it prospers. And you, the mighty one (as the one empowered for the rite), burn the man who performs no rites and is a destroyer, as fire with its flame burns the vessel that is its own support.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You are a hero, a benefactor, accelerate the vehicle of man (that bears him to heaven); consume, mighty one, the irreligious Dasyu, as a (wooden) vessel is burnt by fire.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सनिता (*sanitā*)—giver. The word is explained as used in the sense of "one who is given to giving". Indra is asked to impel the chariot of the sacrificing sacrificer, taken as रथं (*rathaṃ*) ("speed", "motion"), or the heart's desire, or else the chariot called sacrifice, which is the means of going to heaven. The meaning given is: may he impel it so that wishes are fulfilled, or so that the chariot of sacrifice, the sacrificer's means of reaching heaven, is brought to completion.

रथः (*rathaḥ*): this word is derived from the root रंह् (*raṃh*), which means going: रथो रंहतेर्गतिकर्मणः (*ratho raṃhatergatikarmaṇaḥ*). Or: स्थिरतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य (*sthiratervā syādviparītasya*), that is, the word स्थिर (*sthira*) used inverted yields the word रथ (*ratha*). Or: रममाणोऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति वा रपतेर्वा रसतेर्वा (*ramamāṇo 'smiṃstiṣṭhatīti vā rapatervā rasatervā*) (Ni. 9-12): the means of a situation in which the fighter stands in comfort, and it is derived from the root रप (*rapa*) or from the root रस (*rasa*).

The author of the Nirukta shows the nature of the chariot by citing the Ṛk वनस्पते वीड्वंगो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः । गोभिः संनद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥ (*vanaspate vīḍvaṃgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ | gobhiḥ saṃnaddho asi vīḷayasvāsthātā te jayatu jetvāni ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-26). But because the word रथ (*ratha*) is derived from the root रंड् (*raṃḍ*) in the sense of motion, in some places it is also used as an epithet of sons who move about. In the present Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains the word रथ (*ratha*) in two ways: as the heart's desire in the form of motion, and as the chariot that is the means of going to heaven and has the form of sacrifice.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सहावान् (*sahāvān*)—सोमसहायवान् बलवान् वा (*somasahāyavān balavān vā*). The word सहः (*sahaḥ*) is read among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). The author of the Nirukta explains the word सहवान् (*sahavān*) in the Ṛk त्यमू षु वाजिनं देवजूतं सहावानं तरुतारं रथानाम् । अरिष्टनेमिं पृतनाजमाशुं स्वस्तये तार्क्ष्यमिहा हुवेम ॥ (*tyamū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtaṃ sahāvānaṃ tarutāraṃ rathānām | ariṣṭanemiṃ pṛtanājamāśuṃ svastaye tārkṣyamihā huvema ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-178-1) as सहस्वंतं (*sahasvaṃtaṃ*). Durgācārya explains the meaning as: सहावानं सहः बलं तेन तद्वंतं (*sahāvānaṃ sahaḥ balaṃ tena tadvaṃtaṃ*), that is, the word सह (*saha*) means strength and the word means one who possesses it. Here Sāyaṇa describes Indra as one who has the help of Soma, or one who has strength.

दस्युं (*dasyuṃ*)—उपक्षपयितारं (*upakṣapayitāraṃ*). Yāska says दस्युदर्स्यतेः क्षयार्थादुपदस्यंत्यस्मिन् रसाः उपदासॆयति कर्माणि (*dasyudarsyateḥ kṣayārthādupadasyaṃtyasmin rasāḥ upadāsèyati karmāṇi*) (Ni. 7-23). He explains that the word दस्यु (*dasyu*) is derived from the root दसु (*dasu*), meaning to injure or destroy, and is used in the sense that waters are dried up and rites are destroyed. Sāyaṇa describes the meaning as "the destroyer".

The word दस्युं (*dasyuṃ*) is used as an epithet of the word अव्रतं (*avrataṃ*). For अव्रतं (*avrataṃ*) the gloss is अकर्माणं अननुष्ठायिनं (*akarmāṇaṃ ananuṣṭhāyinaṃ*): one who performs none of the sacrificial rites and destroys everything. The injunction here is that Indra should दह (*daha*) (destroy) such a man. Further, in this matter, शोचिषा पात्रंन ज्वालया अग्निः स्वाधारं पात्रविशेषमिव (*śociṣā pātraṃna jvālayā agniḥ svādhāraṃ pātraviśeṣamiva*): as fire burns with its flame the fuel and the like that are its own support, so यागाधिकारी यो न यजते तं दह (*yāgādhikārī yo na yajate taṃ daha*): if a man is qualified to perform the sacrifice yet remains indifferent and does not perform it, Indra should destroy him too. This is explained with the simile stated.

The meaning that the word देव (*deva*) shows (Ni. 7-15), whether expansion, shining or giving, is opposed throughout by the meaning that the word दस्यु (*dasyu*) shows: decay, darkness and violence. Vṛtra and the other asuras all belong to the class of dasyus. Their deeds are to hold back the waters, as if stopping a flow, and to cover the light. Since Indra destroyed them, made the waters flow and spread the light, the epithet दस्युहा (*dasyuhā*) is applied to him in many places.

Although the word दस्यु (*dasyu*) is used in many places as a synonym of rākṣasas and the like, in some places it is also used of human beings who neglect rites. For example:

### Printed p. 375
त्वं ह नु त्यवदमायो दस्यू रेकः कृष्णीरवनोरार्याय । (*tvaṃ ha nu tyavadamāyo dasyū rekaḥ kṛṣṇīravanorāryāya |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-3)

In Ṛks such as this, दस्यून् (*dasyūn*) is explained as कर्महीनान् जनान् (*karmahīnān janān*). Since Indra destroyed both dasyus of the form of Vṛtra and the rest, and dasyus of human form who neglect rites, the epithet दस्युहा (*dasyuhā*) is natural for him.

कुवित्सस्य प्र हि व्रजं गोमंतं दस्युहा गमत् । (*kuvitsasya pra hi vrajaṃ gomaṃtaṃ dasyuhā gamat |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-45-24)

In this and many other Ṛks the epithet shows Indra's extreme power and the protection of the world brought about by slaying dasyus. And:

It is the opinion of some that the two words ārya and dasyu are conventional terms pointing to two different groups of people. Historians have discussed the difference between the two groups, showing the āryas as cultured and the dasyus as uncultured people with a change of complexion. This subject will be dealt with later, with examples.

##### Grammar

- सनिता—षणु दाने इति धातुः । धात्वादेः षः सः इति आदेः सत्वम् । कर्तरि तृन् प्रत्ययः । अर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः इति तस्य इडागमः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- चोडॆयुः—चुद प्रेरणे इति धातुः । छंदसि लुज्— (पा. सू. ३-४-६) इति लोडर्थे लज् । सत्यापपाक— (पा. सू. ३-१-२५) इति स्वार्थे णिच् । सिप् शप् निमित्तं णिचः गुणः अयादेशः । णिच् निमित्तं धातोः लघोपधस्य गुणः । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । णिच्स्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- दस्युम्—दसु उपक्षये इति धातुः । यजिमनि शुंधि— (उ. सू. ३-३००) इति युच् प्रत्ययः । वृषादिषु अंतर्भूतत्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । उकारः इत् यस्य युवः तस्य अनादेशविधानात् अत्र अनादेशः न भवति ।
- अप्रतम्—न विद्यते व्रतम् यस्य सः तम् । नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू: ६-२-१७२) इति उत्तरपदांतोदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- ओषः—उष दाहे इति धातुः । भ्वादिः । लोट् अर्थे प्रतीयमाने छांदसः लज् । मध्यम पुरुषः एकवचनांतरूपम् । छांदसत्वात् अहागमः न भवति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । शप् अनुदात्तः भवति इति धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

> शुत्साय शुष्नमशुषं । ऋ. ४-१६-१२ । इत्यादीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O wise Indra, far-seeing, being able, you robbed by your might one wheel belonging to the sun." Sāyaṇa takes सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*) as the genitive सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*), the accusative ending being substituted for the genitive singular by the rule सुपां सुपो भवंतीति (*supāṃ supo bhavaṃtīti*). मुषाय (*muṣāya*) is अमुष्णाः (*amuṣṇāḥ*) ("you stole"), the form *śāyaj* being substituted in the Veda. The sun's chariot formerly had two wheels, and Indra stole one; so the itihāsa says. He cites another mantra: प्रान्यच्चक्रमवृहः सूर्यस्य कुत्सायान्यत् (*prānyaccakramavṛhaḥ sūryasya kutsāyānyat*) (Ṛ. 5. 29. 10).

Further, शुष्णाय (*śuṣṇāya*) means for the asura of that name, for his slaying; or the dative stands for the accusative, meaning "to slay Śuṣṇa". कुत्सं (*kutsaṃ*) is the cutting instrument, वधं (*vadhaṃ*) is the thunderbolt. वह (*vaha*) is अवहः (*avahaḥ*): yoked with the horses of the wind, that is, with horses of the wind's speed, you bore the thunderbolt to slay Śuṣṇa. Or else: you bore the thunderbolt for Śuṣṇa's slaying; and having slain him, you went to the great seer Kutsa with Śuṣṇa's horses of wind-like speed, which stand here for his wealth marked by horses. The meaning is that you gave the asura Śuṣṇa's wealth to Kutsa. He cites elsewhere: त्वं कुत्सं शुष्नहत्येष्याविथ (*tvaṃ kutsaṃ śuṣnahatyeṣyāvitha*) (Ṛ. 1. 51. 6) and शुत्साय शुष्नमशुषं (*śutsāya śuṣnamaśuṣaṃ*) (Ṛ. 4-16-12), and so on.
