##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कवे (*kave*)—O Indra, the wise one
- ईशानः (*īśānaḥ*)—you, who are able
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—of the sun
- चक्रं (*cakraṃ*)—one wheel of the chariot
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by excess of might
- मुषाय (*muṣāya*)—you carried off
- शुष्णाय (*śuṣṇāya*)—for the slaying of the asura named Śuṣṇa
- कुत्सं (*kutsaṃ*)—the cutting instrument
- वधं (*vadhaṃ*)—the thunderbolt
- वातस्य (*vātasya*)—having the speed of the wind
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—yoked with horses
- वह (*vaha*)—you bore
- (Alternatively) शुष्णाय (*śuṣṇāya*)—for the slaying of the asura named Śuṣṇa; वधं (*vadhaṃ*)—the thunderbolt; वह (*vaha*)—you bore (having slain him); वातस्य (*vātasya*)—having speed equal to the wind; अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—yoked with the horses of that Śuṣṇa (with wealth marked by horses); कुत्सं (*kutsaṃ*)—the seer named Kutsa (you reached).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are able, by your excess of might you carried off one wheel of the sun's chariot; and, bearing the thunderbolt, you slew the asura Śuṣṇa, reached the seer Kutsa together with the wind-swift horses and wealth of that asura, and gave that wealth to the seer.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Sage Indra, who are the lord, you have carried off by your strength one wheel of (the chariot of) the sun. Take up your bolt for the death of Shushna, and proceed with your horses, swift as the wind, to Kutsa.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कवे (*kave*)—Sāyaṇa gives the meaning of this word as क्रांतदर्शिन्निंद्र (*krāṃtadarśinniṃdra*). In some other places Sāyaṇa explains the word in two ways. First, following the śruti sentence “ये वा अनूचानास्ते कवयः (*ye vā anūcānāste kavayaḥ*)”, as scholars of the śāstras who have studied the Veda together with the Vedāṅgas. Second, following the Nirukta sentence कविः, मनीषी (*kaviḥ, manīṣī*) (Ni. 3-15), as one endowed with intelligence.

The author of the Nirukta gives the derivation of the word कवि (*kavi*) thus: मेधावी कविः क्रांतदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्वा (*medhāvī kaviḥ krāṃtadarśano bhavati kavatervā*) (Ni. 12-13). The derivation shows that, formed from the root क्रम् (*kram*), it can mean one whose vision is far-reaching; or, formed from the root कम् (*kam*), it can mean a praiser who offers praise. What is the nature of the kavi? What is his power? It is necessary to know what nature and power the use of the word कवि (*kavi*) in the Ṛksaṃhitā is meant to convey.

### Printed p. 378
It may be said that the word कवि (*kavi*) is useful for conveying the same particular nature that the words ऋषि (*ṛṣi*), सुमेध (*sumedha*), धीर (*dhīra*) and रेभ (*rebha*) show. He who has the extraordinary, supernatural power of knowing all the affairs of past, future and present times is the dhīra; he is the ṛṣi, and he is the kavi. One who has this power is also fit for the creation of poetry in the form of hymns of praise. Therefore the praiser too has such names as kavi and rebha. In worldly literature and in treatises on poetics also, the words कवि (*kavi*) and काव्य (*kāvya*) are terms indicating a similar extraordinary power, though their derivation there differs somewhat from this; that point will be explained later as occasion arises. To show the true nature of the kavi the author of the Nirukta cites the Ṛk विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । नि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योऽनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥ (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catuṣpade | ni nākamakhyatsavitā vareṇyo 'nu prayāṇamuṣaso vi rājati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-2), and explains what nature of Savitṛ the word कवि (*kavi*), an epithet of Savitṛ here, shows. It is understood that Savitṛ has this epithet because he makes all the forms of the universe shine. That is, he has the power by his might to make visible to the world those matters that lie hidden and do not meet its sight. In this same sense the name kavi is well known also for the praiser who offers praise. This idea is suggested in the Ṛk of the Ṛksaṃhitā ब्रह्मा कृशोति वरुणो गातुविदं तमीमहे । व्यूर्णोति हृदा मतिं नव्यो जायतामृतं नित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥ (*brahmā kṛśoti varuṇo gātuvidaṃ tamīmahe | vyūrṇoti hṛdā matiṃ navyo jāyatāmṛtaṃ nittaṃ me asya rodasī ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-15), and likewise in other Ṛks. In this cited Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains the word वॊर्णोति (*vòrṇoti*) as उच्चारयति (*uccārayati*), प्रकाशयति (*prakāśayati*).**NOTE**

ऊर्णुञ् (*ūrṇuñ*)—अच्छादने (*acchādane*). The root ऊर्णु (*ūrṇu*), meaning to hide or cover, becomes ऊर्णोति (*ūrṇoti*). Joined here with the prefix वि (*vi*) it gives the sense of removed covering, that is, removal of concealment; the purport is to make manifest. From this it is understood that the power of creation, in the form of making manifest a feeling hidden in the mind, and the power of making manifest and showing what is hidden, are the special quality of the kavi or praiser. Therefore the word कवि (*kavi*) is an epithet that shows to both Savitṛ and the praiser their common property. Describing this same characteristic and the kavi's work, the Ṛksaṃhitā says:

समानं नीळं वृषणो वसानाः सं जग्मिरे महिषा अर्वतीभिः । ऋतस्य पदं कवयो नि पांति गुहा नामानि दधिरे पराणि । (*samānaṃ nīḷaṃ vṛṣaṇo vasānāḥ saṃ jagmire mahiṣā arvatībhiḥ | ṛtasya padaṃ kavayo ni pāṃti guhā nāmāni dadhire parāṇi |*)

### Printed p. 379
बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं यत्प्रैरत नामधेयं दधानाः । यदेषां श्रेष्ठं यदरिप्रमासीत्प्रेणा तदेषां निहितं गुहाविः ॥ (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ yatprairata nāmadheyaṃ dadhānāḥ | yadeṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yadaripramāsītpreṇā tadeṣāṃ nihitaṃ guhāviḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-1). In this and similar Ṛks this idea is expressed. The poets (kavis) enter the path of Ṛta and bear the names of the highest secret in the most hidden heart. It is described that they then make these names manifest and let the world know them. Seeing of this kind (the poet's vision) is possible only through a means whose form is the act of making manifest:

यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन् तामन्वविंदन्नृषिसु प्रविष्टां । तामाभृत्या व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा तां सप्त रेभा अभि सं नवंते ॥ (*yajñena vācaḥ padavīyamāyan tāmanvaviṃdannṛṣisu praviṣṭāṃ | tāmābhṛtyā vyadadhuḥ purutrā tāṃ sapta rebhā abhi saṃ navaṃte ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-3).

The poets obtained, by the means whose form is sacrifice, the Word that lay dormant in the seers, who see things beyond the senses. Afterwards, for the benefit of the people of the world, they gave instruction to them also. The metres such as Gāyatrī serve this Word, whose form is the principle of the universe. Thus in some places identity (tādātmya) is stated between creation, which is the manifestation of the Word, and the rite, whose form is sacrifice; in other places a relation of effect and cause. The same idea is stated in the Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas in this way:

अयुरेतज्योतिः प्रविशति य एतमनु ना ब्रूते भक्षयति वा तस्य व्रतचर्या यो सृष्टौ ॥ (*ayuretajyotiḥ praviśati ya etamanu nā brūte bhakṣayati vā tasya vratacaryā yo sṛṣṭau ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 14-1-2-26).

Here identity is stated between the rite performed with recitation of mantras and new creation. In the Ṛk at hand, the word is an epithet declaring the unique quality of Indra, who is endowed with knowledge of matters beyond the senses and is all-knowing. Since this epithet is used in many places, it must be understood according to each context.

ईशानः सूर्यं चक्रं ओजसा मुषाय (*īśānaḥ sūryaṃ cakraṃ ojasā muṣāya*)—सवर्थः सन् सूर्यस्य एकं चक्रं सामथ्यातिशयेन अमुष्णाः (*savarthaḥ san sūryasya ekaṃ cakraṃ sāmathyātiśayena amuṣṇāḥ*). Indra, by his power, stole one of the two wheels of Sūrya's chariot. Having so explained, and describing that this meaning is well known in the Itihāsa as पूर्वं सूर्यरथस्य चक्रद्वय—मस्ति एकमिंद्रो मुमुष इतीतिहासः (*pūrvaṃ sūryarathasya cakradvaya—masti ekamiṃdro mumuṣa itītihāsaḥ*), he quotes the Ṛk

प्रान्यच्चक्रमवृहः सूर्यस्य कुत्सायान्यद्वरिवो यातवेऽकः (*prānyaccakramavṛhaḥ sūryasya kutsāyānyadvarivo yātave 'kaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-29-10).

शुष्णाय (*śuṣṇāya*)—एतन्नामकाय असुराय शुष्णं हंतुं (*etannāmakāya asurāya śuṣṇaṃ haṃtuṃ*): in order to destroy the asura famed by the name Śuṣṇa; वातस्य अश्वैः (*vātasya aśvaiḥ*): endowed with the speed of the wind, or with horses,
### Printed p. 380
Indra bears the cutting thunderbolt (कुत्सं वधं वहः (*kutsaṃ vadhaṃ vahaḥ*)). Or, having slain him, अथवा तं च हत्वा तदुपलक्षितैस्तदीयधनैः कुत्सं महर्षिमगमः (*athavā taṃ ca hatvā tadupalakṣitaistadīyadhanaiḥ kutsaṃ maharṣimagamaḥ*). In the first way the word Kutsa is used as an epithet of the thunderbolt, with the meaning "instrument of cutting". In the second sense it is explained that Indra gave Kutsa, a great seer, all the wealth of the asura Śuṣṇa after killing Śuṣṇa. And further—

त्वं कुत्सं शुष्णहत्येष्वाविधारंधयोऽतिथिग्वाय शंबरं । महांतं चिदर्बुदं नि क्रमीः पदा सनादेव दस्युहत्याय जज्ञिषे ॥ (*tvaṃ kutsaṃ śuṣṇahatyeṣvāvidhāraṃdhayo 'tithigvāya śaṃbaraṃ | mahāṃtaṃ cidarbudaṃ ni kramīḥ padā sanādeva dasyuhatyāya jajñiṣe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-6)

कुत्साय शुष्णमशुषं नि बर्हिः प्रपित्वे अह्नः कुयवं सहसा (*kutsāya śuṣṇamaśuṣaṃ ni barhiḥ prapitve ahnaḥ kuyavaṃ sahasā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-12)

Sāyaṇa cites these Ṛks as stating this meaning, and explains that the same idea is stated in other mantras too. The word śuṣka is stated by Yāska among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). And further—

नियद्वृणक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि कुष्णस्य चित् व्रन्दिनो रोरुवद्वना । प्राचीनेन मनसा बर्हणावता यदद्या चित्कृणवः कस्त्वा परि ॥ (*niyadvṛṇakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani kuṣṇasya cit vrandino roruvadvanā | prācīnena manasā barhaṇāvatā yadadyā citkṛṇavaḥ kastvā pari ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54--5)

In this Ṛk the meaning is explained as शुष्णस्य शोषयितुरादित्यस्य (*śuṣṇasya śoṣayiturādityasya*).

न्याविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दृह्ला वि शृङ्गणमभिनच्छुष्णमिन्द्रः । यावत्तरो मघवन् यावदोजो वज्रेण शत्रुमवधीः पृतन्युं ॥ (*nyāvidhyadilībiśasya dṛhlā vi śṛṅgaṇamabhinacchuṣṇamindraḥ | yāvattaro maghavan yāvadojo vajreṇa śatrumavadhīḥ pṛtanyuṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-12)

Here the word śuṣka is used in the sense शुष्णं बलवंतं मेघं (*śuṣṇaṃ balavaṃtaṃ meghaṃ*).

कुत्सं (*kutsaṃ*)—Sāyaṇa's explanation shows that two kinds of meaning can be given to the word Kutsa here. First, कुत्सं-कर्तन साधनं (*kutsaṃ-kartana sādhanaṃ*), "the instrument of cutting", as an epithet of the thunderbolt; second, कुत्सं कुत्सनामानं ऋषिं (*kutsaṃ kutsanāmānaṃ ṛṣiṃ*), the seer named Kutsa. If it is taken as the seer, Indra is praised as having helped Kutsa by killing the asura Śuṣṇa.

From the descriptions in the Ṛksaṃhitā it is known that the relation between Kutsa and Indra is very close. The epithet Ārjuneya occurs for Kutsa in many places. The word Ārjuneya can mean "son of a woman named Arjunī"; or else अर्जुन इतींद्रस्य नाम । तस्य पुत्रः (*arjuna itīṃdrasya nāma | tasya putraḥ*): Arjuna is a name of Indra, and since Kutsa is his son the epithet Ārjuneya is natural—this is another way of explaining it. To support that Indra has the name Arjuna, Sāyaṇa in some places
### Printed p. 381
quotes the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā mantra एतद्वा इंद्रस्य गुह्यं नाम यदर्जुनः (*etadvā iṃdrasya guhyaṃ nāma yadarjunaḥ*). But in the Ṛks

अहं कुत्समार्जुनेयं न्यंजेऽहं कविरुशना पश्यता मा (*ahaṃ kutsamārjuneyaṃ nyaṃje 'haṃ kaviruśanā paśyatā mā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-1)

दासं यच्चुष्णं कुयवं न्यस्मा अरंधय आर्जुनेयाय शिक्षन् (*dāsaṃ yaccuṣṇaṃ kuyavaṃ nyasmā araṃdhaya ārjuneyāya śikṣan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-2)

वहत्कुत्समार्जुनेयं शतक्रतुः त्वरद्धंधर्वमस्तृतं (*vahatkutsamārjuneyaṃ śatakratuḥ tvaraddhaṃdharvamastṛtaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-11)

for all the Ārjuneya words occurring there Sāyaṇa too has explained अर्जुन्याः पुत्रं कुत्सं (*arjunyāḥ putraṃ kutsaṃ*), Kutsa, the son of the woman Arjunī. Since other Śrutis say that both the words Arjuna and Arjunī are related to Indra, it can be said that the two explanations above give one meaning. For example—

फल्गुनीष्वग्नी आदधीत । एता ना इंद्रनक्षत्रं यत्फलुन्नोऽप्यस्य प्रतिनाम्मोऽर्जुनो ह वै नानेंद्रो यदस्य गुह्यं नाम (*phalgunīṣvagnī ādadhīta | etā nā iṃdranakṣatraṃ yatphalunno 'pyasya pratināmmo 'rjuno ha vai nāneṃdro yadasya guhyaṃ nāma*) (Śa. Brā. 2-1-2-11)

इंद्रो भवति यच्च क्षत्रियो यदु च यजमानस्तस्मादाहारिष्टोर्जुन इति । (*iṃdro bhavati yacca kṣatriyo yadu ca yajamānastasmādāhāriṣṭorjuna iti |*) (Śa. Brā. 5-4-3-7)

The Phalgunīs are Indra's constellations; there is agreement in the name also. Indra has the name Arjuna; the Phalgunīs also have the name Arjunīs. Since this is stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and elsewhere, it can be said that Kutsa may be called in two ways, son of Indra and son of Arjunī. In many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā the relation of Indra and Kutsa is shown thus: Kutsa conquers his enemies only with Indra's help.

त्वं शुष्णं वृजने पृक्ष अणौ यूने कुत्साय द्युमते सचाहन् (*tvaṃ śuṣṇaṃ vṛjane pṛkṣa aṇau yūne kutsāya dyumate sacāhan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-3)

कुत्साय यत्र पुरुहूत वन्वइष्णु मनंतैः परियासि वधैः (*kutsāya yatra puruhūta vanvaiṣṇu manaṃtaiḥ pariyāsi vadhaiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-121-9)

In these Ṛks, and likewise in many other places, there is the description that Indra killed Śuṣṇa in order to help Kutsa. And further,
### Printed p. 382
अहं पितेव वेशसूरभिष्टये शुग्रं कुत्साय स्मदिभं च रंधयं (*ahaṃ piteva veśasūrabhiṣṭaye śugraṃ kutsāya smadibhaṃ ca raṃdhayaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-49-4).

Indra himself declares: "For Kutsa I defeated all enemies such as Vetasu, Tugra and Smadibha, and helped my friend." But in

त्वमस्मै कुत्समतिथिग्वमायुं महे राज्ञे यूने अरंधनायः (*tvamasmai kutsamatithigvamāyuṃ mahe rājñe yūne araṃdhanāyaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-10)

य आयुं कुत्समतिथिग्वमर्दयो वावृधानो दिवेदिवे (*ya āyuṃ kutsamatithigvamardayo vāvṛdhāno divedive*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-53-2)

and similar Ṛks it is also described that Indra defeated Kutsa and others.

वधं (*vadhaṃ*)—the authors of the Nirukta have read the name vadha among the names of strength. When this word is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā, it is mostly an epithet of the thunderbolt, which is to be wielded with force and is the instrument of killing. For example,

स्वयं सो अस्मदा निदो वधैरजेत दुर्मतिं (*svayaṃ so asmadā nido vadhairajeta durmatiṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-6).

In such Ṛks (1-133-6; 2-28-7; 6-20-4 etc.) the words वधैः (*vadhaiḥ*), वधं (*vadhaṃ*) are used precisely in the sense of weapons such as the thunderbolt, the instruments of killing. There is no rule that this instrument of killing must be Indra's thunderbolt; it can be a synonym for any weapon wielded with force. For example,

आरे गोहा नृहा वधो वो अस्तु सुम्नेभिरस्मे वसवो नमध्वं (*āre gohā nṛhā vadho vo astu sumnebhirasme vasavo namadhvaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-17)

Here, addressing the Maruts, it is prayed that their weapon may not harm the sacrificers. In the Ṛk at hand the meaning is Indra's thunderbolt.

##### Grammar

- मुषाय — मुष स्तेये इति धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । तस्य हि आदेशः । छंदसि शायजपि (पा. सू. ३-१-८४) इति विकरणस्य शायजादेशः । सार्वधातुकमपित् इति चित्त्वात् लघूपथगुणो न भवति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य चित्त्वात् चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- कवे — कु शब्दे इति धातुः । अचॆइः इति इ प्रत्ययः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य गुण अवादेशः । संबुध्यंतरूपं । आमंत्रितनिघातस्वरो भवति ।**NOTE**
### Printed p. 383
- ईशानः — ईश ऐश्वर्ये इति धातुः । लडर्थे शानचादेशः । अनुदात्तेत्तिन परत्वात् स अनुदात्तो भवति इति धातुस्वरो अवशिष्यते ।
- वह — वह प्रापणे इति धातुः । व्यत्ययेन लडः स्थाने लोट् । मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपं । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । शप् अनुदात्तो भवति इति धातुस्वरो अवशिष्यते ।**NOTE**
- सूर्यम् — सृ गत् इति धातुः । राजसूय सूर्य इति क्यबंतत्वेन निपातितं । सुपां सुपो भवंति इति वचनात् षष्ठीएकवचनस्य द्वितीयाएकवचनादेशः ।
- वधम् — हन हिंसागत्योः धातुः । हनश्च वधः (पा. सू. ३-३-७६) इति भावार्थे अप् प्रत्ययः । तेन सह अंतोदात्तस्वरविशिष्टो वधादेशः । अतो लोपः (पा. सू. ६-४-४८) इति अकारलोपः । अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६१) इति अप् उदात्तो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒ष्मिंत॑मो॒ हि ते॒ मदो॑ द्यु॒म्निंत॑म उ॒त क्रतुः॑ ।  
> वृत्रघ्ना वरिवोविदा मंसीष्ठा अश्वसातमः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुष्मिन्तमः । हि । ते । मदः । द्युम्निन्तमः । उत । क्रतुः ।  
> वृत्रघ्ना । वरिवःसविदा । मंसीष्ठाः । अश्वसातमः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव मदः सोमपानजनितः शुष्मिंतमो बलवत्तमः । उतापि च
> ते क्रतुः कर्म व्यापारोऽस्मदर्थो द्युम्निंतमोऽतिशयेनान्नवान् यशोवान्वा ॥
> उभयत्रायस्मयादीनि छंदसीति भसंज्ञाया बाधितत्वान्न लोपः ॥ हे इंद्र
> अश्वसातमोऽश्वोपलक्षितबहुधनदास्त्वं वृत्रघ्ना वृत्रघातिनौ वरिवोविदा धनस्य
> परिचरणस्य वा वेदयितारौ लंभयितारौ तव मदक्रतू मंसीष्ठाः । अनुज्ञातवानसि।
> शत्रुघातिनौ धनदातारौ च स्यातामित्यनुग्रहमकरोरित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, your intoxication (मदः (*madaḥ*)), born of drinking Soma, is the most powerful (शुष्मिंतमः (*śuṣmiṃtamaḥ*)); and your action (क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*)), your work done for our sake, is most rich in food or in fame (द्युम्निंतमः (*dyumniṃtamaḥ*)). In both words the loss of the ending is not made, since the designation bha is set aside by the rule *āyasmayādīni chaṃdasi*. O Indra, you who are अश्वसातमः (*aśvasātamaḥ*), giver of much wealth marked by horses, you have permitted (मंसीष्ठाः (*maṃsīṣṭhāḥ*)) that your intoxication and action, the two slayers of Vṛtra (वृत्रघ्ना (*vṛtraghnā*)) and the two finders (वरिवोविदा (*varivovidā*)) of wealth or of service, be slayers of enemies and givers of wealth; the meaning is that you have shown favour.
### Printed p. 384

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the joy (born of Soma-drinking)
- शुष्मिंतमः (*śuṣmiṃtamaḥ*)—exceedingly mighty
- उत (*uta*)—and
- ते (*te*)—your
- क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*)—action (done for us)
- द्युम्निंतमः (*dyumniṃtamaḥ*)—endowed with exceeding food (strength)
- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अश्वसातमः (*aśvasātamaḥ*)—you, the giver of much wealth marked by horses (of both your joy and your deeds)
- वृतघ्ना (*vṛtaghnā*)—slayers of Vṛtra (enemies)
- वरिवोविदा (*varivovidā*)—bringers of wealth (having become so)
- मंसीष्ठाः (*maṃsīṣṭhāḥ*)—you have given permission

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, your joy born of Soma-drinking is exceedingly great, and your deeds directed towards us are most beneficial. O Indra, to this joy and these deeds of yours the powers of slaying enemies and of giving wealth have been granted by you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Your inebriety is most intense; nevertheless, Your acts (for our good) are most beneficent. You desire, bountiful giver of horses, that (both your inebriety and your beneficence should be the means of) destroying enemies and distributing riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Addressing Indra, it is described by the sentence मदः शुष्मिंतमः बलवत्तमः (*madaḥ śuṣmiṃtamaḥ balavattamaḥ*) that the intoxication arisen in Indra is produced by Soma-drinking and that it is far more abundant than other intoxicating things.

क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*)—कर्म (*karma*). Yāska has explained the word kratu as कर्म वा प्रज्ञावा (*karma vā prajñāvā*) (Ni. 2.28), "action or intelligence". And he has quoted the Ṛk of the Ṛksaṃhitā

यो जात एव प्रथमो मनस्वान्देवो देवान्कतुना पर्यभूषत् । यस्य शुष्माद्रोदसी अभ्यसेतां नृण्मस्य मह्ना स जनास इंद्रः ॥ (*yo jāta eva prathamo manasvāndevo devānkatunā paryabhūṣat | yasya śuṣmādrodasī abhyasetāṃ nṛṇmasya mahnā sa janāsa iṃdraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-1)

and thereby shown the special meaning of the word kratu there (Ni. 10-10). Even though the word kratu is generally given the meaning "action", wherever this word is used it is understood that this action has an exceedingly great distinctiveness. And the chief meaning of this word is a resolve that urges to action. This meaning is known from the Ṛk quoted below.

### Printed p. 385
In this Ṛk,

सुप्रवाचनं तव वीर वीर्यं यदेकेन क्रतुना विंदसे वसु । जातूष्ठिरस्य प्र वयः सहस्वतो या चकर्थ सेंद्र विश्वास्युक्थः ॥ (*supravācanaṃ tava vīra vīryaṃ yadekena kratunā viṃdase vasu | jātūṣṭhirasya pra vayaḥ sahasvato yā cakartha seṃdra viśvāsyukthaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-13-11)

Sāyaṇa has explained the word क्रतुना (*kratunā*) as कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*). Here it would be more fitting to say "resolve" (saṅkalpa) than "action". The scholar Monier Williams, explaining this very example (Sanskrit–English Dictionary), has rendered एकेन कर्मणा (*ekena karmaṇā*) as "Through the mere will", that is, "by mere resolve alone". This is the natural sense in this context. For here Indra's valour is described; rather than saying that Indra destroyed his enemies by a single action, it is natural to say that Indra "destroyed the enemies by mere resolve alone".

Whenever the word क्रतु (*kratu*) is used as a synonym of action, the resolve that underlies that action and the aim towards which the action is directed are both implied, and the word points to the spiritual existence of the person (puruṣa) and to that same aim. For example—

त्वं सोम क्रतुभिः सुक्रतुर्भूस्त्वं दक्षैः सुदक्षो विश्ववेदाः । त्वं वृषा वृषत्वेभिर्महित्वा द्युम्नेभिर्द्युम्न्यभवो नृचक्षाः ॥ (*tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ sukraturbhūstvaṃ dakṣaiḥ sudakṣo viśvavedāḥ | tvaṃ vṛṣā vṛṣatvebhirmahitvā dyumnebhirdyumnyabhavo nṛcakṣāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-2)

In this Ṛk the two words क्रतु (*kratu*) and दक्ष (*dakṣa*) indicate the extraordinary qualities of the god Soma. Soma is addressed as one endowed with the most excellent knowledge. Likewise,

ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः स्वेन युक्तासः क्रतुना वहंति । इंद्रवायू वीरवाहं रथं वामीशानयोरभि पृक्षः सचंते ॥ (*te satyena manasā dīdhyānāḥ svena yuktāsaḥ kratunā vahaṃti | iṃdravāyū vīravāhaṃ rathaṃ vāmīśānayorabhi pṛkṣaḥ sacaṃte ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-90-5)

Here the knowledge and the resolve that are the root of human activity, which is of the nature of sacrifice, are indicated by the word क्रतुना (*kratunā*). Since all worldly activity is sacrifice-like, the root of this sacrifice, which is both universal and carried out through individual actions, is the resolve of the person. The personality of the person must be complete through this resolve and aim. That is why the person is described as consisting of क्रतु (*kratu*). The Upaniṣads and other texts describe this same point thus:

सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शांत उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिलोके पुरुषो भवति कथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत । (*sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śāṃta upāsīta | atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākraturasmiloke puruṣo bhavati kathetaḥ pretya bhavati sa kratuṃ kurvīta |*) (Chā. U. 3-14-1)

### Printed p. 386
Here the person is said to consist of क्रतु (*kratu*). Explaining what क्रतु (*kratu*) is here, Śaṅkarācārya gave this commentary:

क्रतुं कुर्वीत क्रतुर्निश्चयोऽध्यवसाय एवमेव नान्यथेत्यविचलः प्रत्ययस्तं क्रतुं कुर्वीतोपासीतेत्यनेन व्यवहितेन संबंधः । किं पुनः क्रतुकरणेन कर्तव्यं प्रयोजनं ! कथं वा क्रतुः कर्तव्यः । क्रतुकरणं जाभिप्रेतार्थसिद्धिसाधनं कथं ? इत्यस्यार्थस्य प्रतिपादनार्थमथेत्यादिग्रंथः !............यस्मात्कृतुमयः क्रतुप्रायोऽध्यवसायात्मकः पुरुषो जीवः । यथाक्रतुर्यादृशः क्रतुः अस्य सोऽयं यथाक्रतुयथाध्यव सायः यादृज् निश्चयः अस्मिन्निह पुरुषो भवति तथेतोऽस्माद्देहात्पेत्य मृत्वा भवति । क्रत्वनुरूपफलात्मको भवतीत्यर्थः ॥ (*kratuṃ kurvīta kraturniścayo 'dhyavasāya evameva nānyathetyavicalaḥ pratyayastaṃ kratuṃ kurvītopāsītetyanena vyavahitena saṃbaṃdhaḥ | kiṃ punaḥ kratukaraṇena kartavyaṃ prayojanaṃ ! kathaṃ vā kratuḥ kartavyaḥ | kratukaraṇaṃ jābhipretārthasiddhisādhanaṃ kathaṃ ? ityasyārthasya pratipādanārthamathetyādigraṃthaḥ !............yasmātkṛtumayaḥ kratuprāyo 'dhyavasāyātmakaḥ puruṣo jīvaḥ | yathākraturyādṛśaḥ kratuḥ asya so 'yaṃ yathākratuyathādhyava sāyaḥ yādṛj niścayaḥ asminniha puruṣo bhavati tatheto 'smāddehātpetya mṛtvā bhavati | kratvanurūpaphalātmako bhavatītyarthaḥ ‖*) (Śāṅkara-bhāṣya, Chā. U. 3-14-1)

क्रतु (*kratu*) means mental determination, mental resolve and unwavering faith. Thus the person must necessarily practise the meditation on this क्रतु (*kratu*), which is of the nature of resolve and full of faith. Whether in this world or after the abandonment of the earthly body, the existence of the person follows the nature of his क्रतु (*kratu*), and is the fruit of that meditation on क्रतु (*kratu*). It is also established that without meditation on क्रतु (*kratu*) there is no excellent fruit. Such is the explanation of the Śāṅkara-bhāṣya.

Discussing whether the word क्रतु (*kratu*) here means resolve or aim (purpose), the English scholar Edgerton quotes the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa passage and the passage cited above, and explains the meaning of the word as follows:

The word क्रतु (*kratu*) is not easy to define. Eggeling translates it "understanding" but with an alternative " will; purpose " which is more in accord with the Hindu commentator on the passage who says that क्रतु (*kratu*) means निश्चय (*niścaya*), अध्यवसाय (*adhyavasāya*), i.e, " fixed determination." It seems to mean man's mental constitution as a whole, the " total frame of mind," but with a strong flavour of will, Conscious purpose, or determination..................Man's क्रतु (*kratu*) therefore would be his mental make up in general, but particularly any fixed determination he may entertain with regard to his future life. And his क्रतु (*kratu*) at the moment of death decides his destiny after death.
(Annals of Bhandarkar Institute. Vol. VIII. p. 223)

The gist of this: for the word क्रतु (*kratu*) in the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa (10-6-3-1) and in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (3-14-1), the translator Eggeling first gives the meaning "knowledge" and then the alternative meanings "resolve" and "aim".

### Printed p. 387
In sum, the word means the mental resolve of the person that determines his lasting condition and fortunes.

In many parts of the Ṛk-saṃhitā, even where the word means "sacrifice", this same import is implied, so that it is understood as a sacrifice of the nature of resolve. For example—

साकं हि शुचिना शुचिः प्रशास्ता क्रतुनाजनि । विद्वा अस्य व्रता ध्रुवा वया इनानु रोहते । (*sākaṃ hi śucinā śuciḥ praśāstā kratunājani | vidvā asya vratā dhruvā vayā inānu rohate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-5-4)

In Ṛks of this kind this sense is evident. Since the existence of the person and his future fortunes depend on this action in the form of क्रतु (*kratu*), the Upaniṣads and other texts repeatedly give man a warning on this matter.

ओं क्रतो स्मर कृतग्स्मर क्रतो स्मर कृतग्स्मर । (*oṃ krato smara kṛtagsmara krato smara kṛtagsmara |*) (Īśa. 18)

Thus in the Īśa and Bṛhadāraṇyaka and other Upaniṣads (Bṛ. U. 5-15-1) the instruction is addressed to the self, which is of the nature of resolve. Śaṅkarācārya has explained the word क्रतो (*krato*) as "O you who are of the nature of resolve". But in the Aitareya Upaniṣad, when the nature of the spirit is described—

संज्ञानमाज्ञानं विज्ञानं प्रज्ञानं............स्मृतिः संकल्पः क्रतुः । (*saṃjñānamājñānaṃ vijñānaṃ prajñānaṃ............smṛtiḥ saṃkalpaḥ kratuḥ |*) (Ai. U. 3-2)

resolve and क्रतु (*kratu*) are mentioned as separate qualities of the self.

The word is used not only when such spiritual qualities are being described but also when the physical actions of the person are described. For example—

न हि नु यादधीमसींद्रं को वीर्या परः । तस्मिन्नृम्मुत क्रतुं देवा ओजांसि सं दधुरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं । (*na hi nu yādadhīmasīṃdraṃ ko vīryā paraḥ | tasminnṛmmuta kratuṃ devā ojāṃsi saṃ dadhurarcannanu svarājyaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-15)

In Ṛks of this kind the word क्रतु (*kratu*) is understood as a deed of valour, and in

यस्याजस्रं शवसा मानमुक्थं परिभुजद्रोदसी विश्वतः सीं । स पारिषत्कुभिर्मंदसानो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्त्विंद्र ऊती । (*yasyājasraṃ śavasā mānamukthaṃ paribhujadrodasī viśvataḥ sīṃ | sa pāriṣatkubhirmaṃdasāno marutvānno bhavattviṃdra ūtī |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-14)

and the like, as sacrificial action. Likewise the word is used in the senses of power, wealth, influence and so on.

### Printed p. 388
Here the sense is made clear: the action of Indra performed for us, the sacrificers, is द्युम्निंतमः (*dyumniṃtamaḥ*)—exceedingly possessed of food or of fame—that is, it is meant to produce abundant food or fame. Yāska, quoting the Ṛk

शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु । जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥ (*śataṃ te śiprinnūtayaḥ sudāse sahasraṃ śaṃsā uta rātirastu | jahi vadharvanuṣo martyasyāsme dyumnamadhi ratnaṃ ca dhehi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-25-3)

explains द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वा अन्नं वा (*dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vā annaṃ vā*): the word द्युम्न (*dyumna*), formed from the root द्युत (*dyuta*) meaning "to shine with lustre", means fame or food.

अश्वसातमः (*aśvasātamaḥ*)—अश्वोपलक्षितबहुधनदाः (*aśvopalakṣitabahudhanadāḥ*): Indra bestows abundant wealth together with horses.

वरिवोविदा (*varivovidā*)—धनस्य परिचरणस्य वा वेदयितारौ लंभयितारौ (*dhanasya paricaraṇasya vā vedayitārau laṃbhayitārau*). The word वरिवः (*varivaḥ*) is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa describes Indra's exhilaration and action as वृत्रघ्नौ (*vṛtraghnau*): in the historical sense they suppressed the demon Vṛtra, and from the standpoint of principle they strike the cloud and make rain come. Since they give wealth and suppress the enemy, the sense made clear is: "Indra has granted this favour: शत्रुघातिनौ धनदातारौ च स्यातामित्यनुग्रहमकरोः (*śatrughātinau dhanadātārau ca syātāmityanugrahamakaroḥ*)—may this exhilaration and this action be destroyers of enemies and givers of wealth for us, the sacrificers."

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā**

- शुष्मिंतमः— शुष्म बलमस्य अस्ति इति शुष्मी । अतिशयेन शुष्मी शुष्मिंतमः । आत इनिठना इति मत्त्वर्थे इनिप्रत्यये सति तदुपरि अतिशयार्थे तमप् प्रत्ययः । आयस्मयादीनि छंदसि (पा. सू. १-४-२०) इति तमपः पूर्वस्य भ संज्ञा भवति । तस्मात् पदसंज्ञानिमित्तो न लोपो न भवति । तमप् पित्त्वादनुदात्तो भवति । इनिप्रत्ययस्वरः शिष्यते । द्युम्निंतमः इत्यत्रापि एवमेव कार्याणि भवंति ।
- मदः—मद तृप्तियोगे इति धातुः । मदोऽनुपसर्गे (पा. सू. ३-३-६७) इति अप् प्रत्ययः । पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- वृत्रघ्ना—हन हिंसागत्योः इति धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । छांदसत्वात् भ संज्ञात्वात् अल्लोपः भवति । सुपां सुलुक् - (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति द्विवचनस्य आकारादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । **NOTE**

### Printed p. 389
- वरिवोविदा — विद ज्ञाने इति धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः पूर्ववत् । विभक्तेः आकारादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- मंसीष्ठाः—मन ज्ञाने इति धातुः । लिज् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने थास् आदेशः । लिजिः सीयुट् इति सीयुट् । सुट् तिथोः इति थासः सुटागमः । धातुनकारस्य आनुस्वारः । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण आंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- अश्वसातमः—षणु दाने इति धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । जनसनखनां सन्‌झलोः (पा. सू. ६-४-४२) इति धातोरात्वं भवति । तदुपरि अतिशयार्थे तमप् प्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॒ पूर्वे॑भ्यो जरि॒तृभ्य॑ इंद्र॒ मय॑ इ॒वापो॒ न तृष्य॑ते ब॒भूथ॑ ।  
> तामनु॑ त्वा नि॒विदं॑ जोहवीमि वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । पूर्वेभ्यः । जरितृभ्यः । इंद्र । मयःइव । आपः । न । तृष्यते । बभूथ ।  
> शां । अनु । त्वा । निऽविदं । जोहवीमि । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरदानुं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पूर्वभ्यो जरितृभ्यः पुरातनेभ्यो गरितृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो मय इव
> बभूथ । मयः सुखं । सुखस्वरूपमिनाभवः । तद्वत् स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं सुखो
> भव । तत्र दृष्टांतः । तृष्यत आपो न तृषार्तस्योदकानि यथा सुखकराणीति तद्वत् ।
> तस्मात्तां निविदं, त्वत्प्रीतिकरीं प्रसिद्धां स्तुतिं त्वा तुभ्यमनु जोहवीमि । पुनः पुनः
> करोमि । यद्वा । तां निविदमनु ॥ तृतीयार्थे । पा १-४-८५ । इत्यनोः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं ॥ तया स्तुत्या त्वां जोहवीमि । पुनःपुनराह्वयामि । विद्यामेति व्याख्यात॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, you have been like मयः (*mayaḥ*) (happiness) to the ancient praisers (जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*) = स्तोतृभ्यो (*stotṛbhyo*)). मयः (*mayaḥ*) is happiness; you have been of the very nature of happiness. In the same way be happy for us, your praisers." The illustration: as waters are comforting to one tormented by thirst (तृष्यत आपो न (*tṛṣyata āpo na*)). Therefore I invoke you again and again by that well-known निविदं (*nividaṃ*), a praise that pleases you; that is, I do so repeatedly. Alternatively: तां निविदमनु (*tāṃ nividamanu*)—the word अनु (*anu*) is a karmapravacanīya in the sense of the instrumental (Pā. 1-4-85); so "with that praise I call you, I summon you again and again." विद्याम (*vidyāma*) has been explained already.

### Printed p. 390

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पूर्वेभ्यः (*pūrvebhyaḥ*)—to the ancient
- जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)—praisers
- कृष्यते (*kṛṣyate*)—to one tormented by thirst
- आपः न (*āpaḥ na*)—as waters become satisfying
- मयः इव (*mayaḥ iva*)—like one of the nature of happiness
- यथा (*yathā*)—as
- बभूथ (*babhūtha*)—you have been (so be of the nature of happiness to us also)
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that well-known
- निविदं अनु (*nividaṃ anu*)—following (your) praise
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- जोहवीमि (*johavīmi*)—I invoke again and again
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—strength
- जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*)—long life
- विद्याम (*vidyāma*)—let us obtain (by your favour)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as you have been pleasing to the ancient praisers, as waters give satisfaction to one tormented by thirst, so be a giver of happiness to us also; I too praise you again and again with your well-known words of praise; grant us food, strength and long life.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Inasmuch, Indra, as you have been the-(giver of) happiness to your ancient encomiasts, like water to one who is thirsty, therefore I constantly repeat this your praise, that I may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The joy that Indra produces in his praisers is described, and the satisfaction arising from that joy is compared to the satisfaction that a thirsty person gets from drinking water. The seer of this sūkta too has resolved that, as the earlier praisers praised such a satisfying Indra with निविद् (*nivid*) mantras, he too will praise him.

निविदं जोहवीमि (*nividaṃ johavīmi*)—the resolve is that he will recite निविद् (*nivid*) mantras. Earlier, when giving the special topics of Ṛk 1-96-2 of the Ṛ. Saṃ., the importance of the निविद् (*nivid*) mantras indicated by the mantra स पूर्वया निविदा (*sa pūrvayā nividā*) was explained (Ṛgveda-saṃhitā Part 8, pp. 74-76). But that mantra was addressed to Agni, and the निविद् (*nivid*) mantras specified there being addressed to Agni, only the mantras with Agni as deity were mentioned in that context. Since the present Ṛk is addressed to Indra, the power and the uses of the निविद् (*nivid*) mantras are explained here in a manner suited to this context.

The name निविद् (*nivid*) mantra is well known for mantras that address a deity or a group of deities, describe their extraordinary qualities and invoke them. The Bṛhaddevatā states this, saying,

### Printed p. 391
The Brāhmaṇa-type passage and Bṛhaddevatā verse on the Nivid mantras continue here.

कर्मैव तावत्सावित्र्यां निविदि स्तौति कर्मणा । यद्भेनुः सप्त्यनड्वाहौ वोळ्हा दोग्धाशुरेव ना ॥ (*karmaiva tāvatsāvitryāṃ nividi stauti karmaṇā | yadbhenuḥ saptyanaḍvāhau voḷhā dogdhāśureva nā ‖*) (Bṛhaddevatā 3-50)

By the words दोग्नि (*dogni*) the milch cow is meant; by आशु (*āśu*) (swift-going), and by वोळ्हा (*voḷhā*) (the bearer of a load), the ox is meant. Just as the particular character of each is understood from its particular epithet, so through the Nivid mantras the personal qualities of each deity can be understood from the description of that deity's actions. For example:

अभि त्वा देव सनितरीशानं वार्याणां । सदावन्भागमीमहे । (*abhi tvā deva sanitarīśānaṃ vāryāṇāṃ | sadāvanbhāgamīmahe |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3 **NOTE**)

In this Ṛk, the Nivid mantra addressed to the deity Savitṛ makes known Savitṛ's distinctive character through the description of his extraordinary action. The greatness of the Nivid mantras, and their relation of cause and effect to the creation of the world, is recorded in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

प्रजापतिर्वा इदमेक एवाग्र आस सोऽकामयत प्रजायेय भूयन्तामिति स तपोऽतप्यत स वाचमयच्छत्स संवत्सरस्य परस्ताद्वाहरद्वादशकृत्तो द्वादशपदा वा एषा निविदेतां वाव तां निविदं व्याहरत्तां सर्वाणि भूतान्यन्नसृज्यंत । (*prajāpatirvā idameka evāgra āsa so 'kāmayata prajāyeya bhūyantāmiti sa tapo 'tapyata sa vācamayacchatsa saṃvatsarasya parastādvāharadvādaśakṛtto dvādaśapadā vā eṣā nividetāṃ vāva tāṃ nividaṃ vyāharattāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyannasṛjyaṃta |*) (Ai. Brā. 10-1)

In the beginning Prajāpati was alone; he desired to create offspring and to become many, and practised austerity, keeping silence for a year. Then he recited twelve times the Nivid mantras, which contain twelve great sentences, and after that all beings in the world were created. Having thus declared the power of these mantras, the text then states their distinctive character at the times of the rites and the order of their use:

गर्भा वा एत उक्तानां यन्निविदस्तद्यत्पुरस्तादुक्थानां प्रातःसवने धीयंते तस्मात्परांचो गर्भा धीयंते परांचः संभवति। यन्मध्यतो मध्यंदिने धीयंते तस्मान्मध्ये गर्भा धृताः । यदंततस्यतीयसवने धीयंते तस्मादमुतोऽर्वांचो गर्भाः प्रजायंते प्रजात्यै । प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद । पेशा वा एत उक्तानां यन्निविदस्तद्यत्पुरस्तादुक्थानां प्रातःसवने धीयंते यथैव प्रवणयतः पेशः कुर्यात्तादृक्तद्यन्मध्यतो मध्यंदिने धीयंते यथैव मध्यतः पेशः कुर्यात्ताह- (*garbhā vā eta uktānāṃ yannividastadyatpurastādukthānāṃ prātaḥsavane dhīyaṃte tasmātparāṃco garbhā dhīyaṃte parāṃcaḥ saṃbhavati| yanmadhyato madhyaṃdine dhīyaṃte tasmānmadhye garbhā dhṛtāḥ | yadaṃtatasyatīyasavane dhīyaṃte tasmādamuto 'rvāṃco garbhāḥ prajāyaṃte prajātyai | prajāyate prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda | peśā vā eta uktānāṃ yannividastadyatpurastādukthānāṃ prātaḥsavane dhīyaṃte yathaiva pravaṇayataḥ peśaḥ kuryāttādṛktadyanmadhyato madhyaṃdine dhīyaṃte yathaiva madhyataḥ peśaḥ kuryāttāha-*)

### Printed p. 392
क्तद्यदंततस्तृतीयसवने धीयंते यथैवावप्रज्जनतः पेशः कुर्यात्तादृक्तत् । सर्वतो यज्ञस्य पेशसा शोभते य एवं वेद ॥ (*ktadyadaṃtatastṛtīyasavane dhīyaṃte yathaivāvaprajjanataḥ peśaḥ kuryāttādṛktat | sarvato yajñasya peśasā śobhate ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 11-10)

The Nivid mantras stand to the ukthas as embryos: that is, in the morning libation they are recited before the ukthas. Therefore the embryos too are set in place facing forward. At the midday libation these mantras are recited in the middle; therefore the embryos are held in the middle. At the third libation the Nivid mantras are recited at the end; therefore the child in the womb is born turned downward (?). He who knows these principles is endowed with offspring and with cattle. The Nivid mantras are also like ornaments to the ukthas, increasing their beauty and splendour. The mantras recited at the morning libation are like ornaments of the upper part of a slope, those at the midday time like ornaments of the middle region, those of the third libation like ornaments of the lower part. He who knows this adorns the sacrifice and shines himself. And further:

सौर्या वा एता देवता यन्निविदस्तद्यत्पुरस्तादुक्थानां प्रातःसवने धीयंते मध्यतो मध्यंदिने ततस्तृतीयसवन आदित्यस्यैव तद्व्रतमनु पर्यावर्तंते । पच्चो वै देवा यज्ञं समभरंस्तस्मात्पच्चो निविदः शस्यंते । यद्वै तद्देवा यज्ञं समभरंस्तस्मादत्वः समभवत्तस्मादाहुरश्वं निविदां शंस्त्रे दद्यादिति तदु खलु वरमेव ददति । न निविदः पदमतीयाद्यद्यन्निदवः पदमतीयाद्यज्ञस्य तच्छिद्रं कुर्याद्यज्ञस्य वै छिद्रं स्रवद्यजमानोऽनु पापीयान् भवति (*sauryā vā etā devatā yannividastadyatpurastādukthānāṃ prātaḥsavane dhīyaṃte madhyato madhyaṃdine tatastṛtīyasavana ādityasyaiva tadvratamanu paryāvartaṃte | pacco vai devā yajñaṃ samabharaṃstasmātpacco nividaḥ śasyaṃte | yadvai taddevā yajñaṃ samabharaṃstasmādatvaḥ samabhavattasmādāhuraśvaṃ nividāṃ śaṃstre dadyāditi tadu khalu varameva dadati | na nividaḥ padamatīyādyadyannidavaḥ padamatīyādyajñasya tacchidraṃ kuryādyajñasya vai chidraṃ sravadyajamāno 'nu pāpīyān bhavati*) (Ai. Brā. 11-11)

All the Nivid deities belong to the sun. The mantras of the morning, midday and third libations follow the course of the sun from rising to setting. The gods gathered the sacrifice together by means of limits consisting of metrical feet (pādas); therefore the Nivid mantras are in the form of sentences made of pādas.

### Printed p. 393
As a result of the gods gathering all the portions of the sacrifice together, the horse came into being. Therefore there is an injunction to give a horse to the ṛtvij who recites these mantras. One must not skip over any word in the Nivid mantras. If a word is not recited, it makes a breach in the sacrifice itself, and that brings harm to the sacrificer. Two sentences in these mantras must not be joined together, nor may the earlier be joined to what follows, or the later to what precedes, in reciting. If one does so, uncertainty arises in the sacrificial act itself, and the sacrificer too becomes bewildered. If two sentences are joined together, contraction arises in the sacrificial act, and thereby the sacrificer's life is contracted and he may die. Therefore one must not mix the sentences and so cause contraction in the recitation of the mantra. Only the pair of mantras, sacred and of divine nature, प्रेदं ब्रह्म (*predaṃ brahma*) and प्रेदं क्षत्रं (*predaṃ kṣatraṃ*), may be mixed; therefore priestly splendour and warrior splendour become mixed. The Nivid mantras should stay within three or four mantras, and one must not go beyond them. By the Nivid the recitation of the praise becomes extended.

एकां परिशिष्य तृतीयसवने निविदं दध्यात् । यद्वे परिशिष्य दध्यात्पजननं तदुपहन्याद्गर्भैस्तत्रजा व्यर्धयेत्तस्मादेकामेव परिशिष्य तृतीयसवने निविदं दध्यात् । न सूक्तेन निविदमतिपद्येत; येन सूक्तेन निविदमति पद्येत न तत्पुनरुपनिवर्तेत वास्तुहमेव तत् । अन्यत्तद्दैवतं तच्छंदसं सूक्तमाहृत्य तस्मिन्निविदं दध्यात् । मा प्र गाम पथो वयमिति पुरस्तातूक्तस्य शंसति । पथो वा एष प्रैति यो यज्ञे मुह्यति मा यज्ञादिंद्र सोमिन इति यज्ञादेव तन्न प्रच्यवते । मांतस्सुर्नो अरातय इत्यरातीयत एव तदपहंति । यो यज्ञस्य प्रसाधनस्तंतुर्देवेष्वाततः । तमाहुतं नशीमहीति । प्रजा वै तंतुः प्रजामेवास्मा एतत्संतनोति । मनो न्याहुवामहे नाराशंसेन सोमेनेति । मनसा वै यज्ञ स्वायते मनसा क्रियते । सैव तत्र पायश्चित्तिः प्रायश्चित्तिः ॥ (*ekāṃ pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt | yadve pariśiṣya dadhyātpajananaṃ tadupahanyādgarbhaistatrajā vyardhayettasmādekāmeva pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt | na sūktena nividamatipadyeta; yena sūktena nividamati padyeta na tatpunarupanivarteta vāstuhameva tat | anyattaddaivataṃ tacchaṃdasaṃ sūktamāhṛtya tasminnividaṃ dadhyāt | mā pra gāma patho vayamiti purastātūktasya śaṃsati | patho vā eṣa praiti yo yajñe muhyati mā yajñādiṃdra somina iti yajñādeva tanna pracyavate | māṃtassurno arātaya ityarātīyata eva tadapahaṃti | yo yajñasya prasādhanastaṃturdeveṣvātataḥ | tamāhutaṃ naśīmahīti | prajā vai taṃtuḥ prajāmevāsmā etatsaṃtanoti | mano nyāhuvāmahe nārāśaṃsena someneti | manasā vai yajña svāyate manasā kriyate | saiva tatra pāyaścittiḥ prāyaścittiḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 11-11)

At the third libation the Nivid is to be inserted leaving out one Ṛk. If it is inserted leaving out two, powerlessness results, and then barrenness arises. Therefore it is to be inserted leaving out one only; then the sacrificial act is complete. One must not leave out two: that would destroy the power of procreation, the power of conception would go and people would become childless. In a sūkta fit for the Nivid, the sūkta must not be recited without inserting the Nivid mantras;

### Printed p. 394
once it has been recited, the Nivid is no longer fit to be inserted again. If such a lapse occurs, one should choose another sūkta of the same deity and the same metre and insert these Nivid mantras in it. At such a time:

मा प्र गाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिंद्र सोमिनः । (*mā pra gāma patho vayaṃ mā yajñādiṃdra sominaḥ |*) मांतः स्थुर्नो अराशयः ॥ (*māṃtaḥ sthurno arāśayaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-1)

"May we not go astray from the path; may we not fall outside the sacrifice; may evil powers not assail us." Having first prayed thus, one should then recite that sūkta furnished with the Nivid mantras. Then, with no confusion of any kind, the sacrificial work proceeds without obstacle and the evil powers are destroyed. "The thread, the fruit of the sacrifice, that is stretched out among the gods, may that same thread extend among us the sacrificers" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-2): so the sacrificer recites. The thread is the line of offspring; to the sacrificer this thread, in the form of progeny, comes in unbroken succession.

तद्यदेशां पुरस्तात् सूक्तस्य निविदं दधाति प्रजात्यै । प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद ॥ (*tadyadeśāṃ purastāt sūktasya nividaṃ dadhāti prajātyai | prajāyate prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 10-2)

For this reason the Hotṛ, by reciting the Nivid mantra at the beginning of the sūkta, obtains offspring. To sacrificers who know this, all wealth, beginning with good progeny, accrues; so it is said elsewhere too. In the Ṛksaṃhitā it is seen in many places that it is traditional, with faith that the recitation of mantras gives the highest fruit, to praise the form, power and great deeds of each deity when invoking it, and to recite these. For example:

शान्पूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्रिधं । (*śānpūrvayā nividā hūmahe vayaṃ bhagaṃ mitramaditiṃ dakṣamasridhaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-3)
जुषेथां यज्ञं बोधतं हवस्य मे सत्तो होता निविदः पूर्व्या अनु । (*juṣethāṃ yajñaṃ bodhataṃ havasya me satto hotā nividaḥ pūrvyā anu |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-6)
किमु ष्टिदस्मै निविदो भनंतेंद्रस्यावद्यं दिधिषंत आपः । (*kimu ṣṭidasmai nivido bhanaṃteṃdrasyāvadyaṃ didhiṣaṃta āpaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-18-7)
वि यद्वाचं कीस्तासो भरंते शंसंति के चिन्निविदो मनानाः । (*vi yadvācaṃ kīstāso bharaṃte śaṃsaṃti ke cinnivido manānāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-67-10)

In these and similar contexts the greatness of the Nivid mantras is praised.

### Printed p. 395
In the present Ṛk (1-176-6 **NOTE**) the Nivid mantra addressed to Indra is indicated by the sentence तामनु त्वा निविदं जोहवीमि (*tāmanu tvā nividaṃ johavīmi*). There is some difference of opinion in determining which sūkta is furnished with Nivids addressed to the deity Indra. For example:

जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुरायेति निविद्धानमैकाहिकं । (*janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāyeti nividdhānamaikāhikaṃ |*) (Ai. Ā. 1-2-2)

The Aitareya text says that Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-73, beginning with the Ṛk जनिष्ठा उग्रः (*janiṣṭhā ugraḥ*), is furnished with Nivid mantras. But the Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka (1-3) says that Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9 (read: sūkta beginning with the Ṛk महा इंद्रो न्नवदा (*mahā iṃdro nnavadā*)) is furnished with these mantras. In the present Ṛk the seer of the sūkta declares his resolve: "I praise Indra with Nivid mantras that extol Indra's nature, prowess and distinctive character."

##### Grammar

- जरितृभ्यः—जृष् वयोहानौ धातुः । इह स्तुत्यर्थे प्रयुक्तः । कर्तरि तृच् प्रत्ययः । इडागमः । प्रत्ययनिमित्तेन धातोः ऋकारस्य गुणः । चित्त्वादंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति । चतुर्थीबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- तृष्यते—इतृषा पिपासायां धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (पा. सू. ३.१-६९) इति श्यन् विकरणम् । तास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इति शतृ अनुदात्तं भवति । विकरणस्य नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
- बभूथ—भू सत्तायां धातुः । लिट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचने बभूथ ततंथ—(पा. सू. ७-२-६४) इति इडभावेन निपातितम् । निपातैर्यद्यदि—(पा. सू. ८-१-३०) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधः भवति । थल् लित्त्वात् लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति प्रत्ययपूर्वस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- जोहवीमि—हु दानादनयोः धातुः । यज्लुगंतात् लट् । उत्तमपुरुष एकवचने मिप् । यजो वा (पा. सू. ७-३-९४) इति मिसः ईडागमः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वान्निघातस्वरः भवति । ॥ ६ ॥ **NOTE**

Here ends the one hundred and seventy-fifth sūkta.

### Printed p. 396
## Sūkta 176 (Maṇḍala 1)

The one hundred and seventy-sixth sūkta.

*Sāyaṇa's introduction:* मत्सि न इति षडृचं द्वादशं सूक्तमागस्त्यमैंद्रमानुष्टुभं । पूर्वत्र तुशब्दाक् त्रिष्टुबंतं त्वित्युक्तत्वादंत्या त्रिष्टुप् । मत्सि न इत्यनुक्रांतं । विशेषविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ (*matsi na iti ṣaḍṛcaṃ dvādaśaṃ sūktamāgastyamaiṃdramānuṣṭubhaṃ | pūrvatra tuśabdāk triṣṭubaṃtaṃ tvityuktatvādaṃtyā triṣṭup | matsi na ityanukrāṃtaṃ | viśeṣaviniyogo laiṃgikaḥ ‖*)

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning मत्सि न (*matsi na*) is the twelfth sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Agastya; the deity is Indra; the metre is Anuṣṭubh; the last Ṛk is in Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is listed as beginning मत्सि न (*matsi na*). The special application is by indication (liṅga).

Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 23; Sūkta 176; Aṣṭaka 2; Adhyāya 4; Varga 19. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Ṛṣi: Āgastya. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1–5 Anuṣṭubh; 6 Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मत्सि॑ नो॒ वस्य॑ इष्टय॒ इंद्र॑मिंदो॒ वृषा वि॑श ।  
> ऋ॒घा॒यमा॑ण इन्वसि॒ शत्रु॒मंति॒ न विं॑दसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मत्सि । नः । वस्यः इष्टये । इंद्रं । इंदो इति । वृषा । आ । विश ।  
> ऋघायमाणः । इन्वसि । शत्रुं । अंति । न । विंदसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो क्लेदयितः सोम त्वं नो वस्य इष्टये वसीयसो धनस्य
> प्राप्तय उक्तलक्षणाय यागाय वेंद्रं मत्सि । मादयस्व । तदर्थं त्वमेवेंद्रं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indu, moistening Soma, for the attainment of better wealth for us, that is, for the sacrifice of the kind described, delight Indra, make him rejoice; for that purpose you yourself …".

### Printed p. 397

> वृषा कामानां वर्षिता आ विश । अथ तथा पीतः सन्नृघायमाणः शत्रुन् हिंसयन्निन्वसि । व्याप्प्नोषि । अत्योऽंत्यंतिके शत्रुं न विंदसि । न लभसे । यतः शत्रवस्त्वत्सामर्थ्येन पलयिताः अतो न विंदसि । यद्वा । उत्तरार्ध इंद्रपरतया व्याख्येयः ।
> हे इंद्र त्वं तं सोमं पीत्र्घायमाणः सन्निन्वसि । अंतिके शत्रुं न विंदसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वृषा (*vṛṣā*) means the showerer of desires, and आ विश (*ā viśa*) means "enter him". Then, having been drunk, he pervades (इन्वसि (*invasi*)) while harming enemies, who are ऋघायमाणः (*ṛghāyamāṇaḥ*) ("enemy-smiting"). Close at hand (अंतिके (*aṃtike*)) he does not find (न विंदसि (*na viṃdasi*)) an enemy, that is, does not obtain one, because the enemies have been put to flight by his power, and so he does not find them. Alternatively, the second half of the verse is to be explained as referring to Indra: "O Indra, you, drinking that Soma, pervade while harming the enemy, and you find no enemy near you." **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-juice
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- वस्य इष्टये (*vasya iṣṭaye*)—for the obtaining of wealth
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- मत्सि (*matsi*)—make glad
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—as the showerer of desires
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter well (pervade) (Indra)
- ऋघायमाणः (*ṛghāyamāṇaḥ*)—becoming a harmer of enemies (when thus drunk)
- इन्वसि (*invasi*)—you pervade
- अंति (*aṃti*)—near
- शत्रुं (*śatruṃ*)—an enemy
- न विंदसि (*na viṃdasi*)—you do not get. [Or: O Indra, you, having drunk that Soma, harm enemies and pervade; hence you do not get an enemy near.]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-juice, for the gain of wealth and the like for us, gladden Indra. O Soma-juice, the showerer of desires, pervade him well. O Indra, having drunk the Soma you strike the enemies down thoroughly; for that very reason they cannot come near you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Soma, exhilarate Indra (at the sacrifice we offer). for the sake of obtaining wealth : pervade him, showerer (of benefits), for when imbibed you are the annihilator (of enemies), and suffer not a foe to be nigh.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sūkta 176 was composed by the sage Agastya and is addressed to Indra. In its first Ṛk, मत्सि नः (*matsi naḥ*), Soma, who gives Indra satisfaction, is addressed with a prayer. It is suggested that from the drinking of the Soma-juice there come: (1) the exceeding joy that Indra obtains; (2) the growth of strength that enables him to subdue enemies; and (3) the gift of wealth that Indra, in this joy, bestows on the sacrificer.

1. मत्सि—मादयस्व (*matsi—mādayasva*): the prayer is "give satisfaction". It is well known that in many places Indra is described as fond of Soma. And the happiness obtained from drinking this Soma-juice

### Printed p. 398
is described as extremely great, as can be known from the account in the Ṛks below. The prayer is also that such happiness-giving Soma-juice may be prepared for Indra's drinking.

यत्र ज्योतिरजस्रं यस्मिन् लोके स्वर्हितं । तस्मिन्मां धेहि पवमानामृते लोके अक्षित इंद्रायॆंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra jyotirajasraṃ yasmin loke svarhitaṃ | tasminmāṃ dhehi pavamānāmṛte loke akṣita iṃdrāyèṃdo pari srava ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-7)

यत्र कामा निकामाश्च यत्र ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपं । स्वधा च यत्र तृप्तिश्च तत्र माममृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra kāmā nikāmāśca yatra bradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ | svadhā ca yatra tṛptiśca tatra māmamṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-10)

यत्रानंदाश्च मोदाश्च मुदः प्रमुद आसते । कामस्य यत्राप्ताः कामास्तत्र माममृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatrānaṃdāśca modāśca mudaḥ pramuda āsate | kāmasya yatrāptāḥ kāmāstatra māmamṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-11)

The nature of the happiness described in these and similar Ṛks surpasses even the heavenly happiness commonly described. Bliss, joy and delight free of desire are obtained through the favour of Soma. In the present Ṛk, with the word मत्सि (*matsi*), the prayer is that such happiness-giving satisfaction be produced for Indra.

2. Second, शत्रुमंति न विंदसि (*śatrumaṃti na viṃdasi*); अंतिके शत्रुं न विंदसि (*aṃtike śatruṃ na viṃdasi*). The power of the Soma-juice is described thus: by your influence you do not bring enemies near but drive them far away. Sāyaṇa has indicated that this sentence can have two senses: either the Soma drunk by Indra, by its power, does not let enemies come near; or, हे इंद्र त्वं सोमं पीत्वा अंतिके शत्रुं न विंदसि (*he iṃdra tvaṃ somaṃ pītvā aṃtike śatruṃ na viṃdasi*), "O Indra, you, having drunk the Soma-juice and increased your strength, drive the enemies away", a sense that refers to Indra. The purport of both constructions is one and the same: Soma-juice gives Indra vigour, and by drinking it Indra can subdue his enemies. The same idea is stated in many other places too. For example:

त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्र मदाय सोमं परमे व्योमन् । यद्ध द्यावापृथिवी अविवेशीरथाभवः पूर्व्यः कारुधायाः ॥ (*tvaṃ sadyo apibo jāta iṃdra madāya somaṃ parame vyoman | yaddha dyāvāpṛthivī aviveśīrathābhavaḥ pūrvyaḥ kārudhāyāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-32-10)

In such Ṛks it is described how Indra's mother, as soon as Indra was born, had him drink the Soma-juice, and how his greatness grew by it. And as a result of this,

### Printed p. 399
अवंशे द्यामस्तभायद्बृहंतमा रोदसी अपृणदंतरिक्षं । स धारयत्पृथिवीं पप्रथच्च सोमस्य ता मद इंद्रश्चकार ॥ (*avaṃśe dyāmastabhāyadbṛhaṃtamā rodasī apṛṇadaṃtarikṣaṃ | sa dhārayatpṛthivīṃ paprathacca somasya tā mada iṃdraścakāra ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-2)

Indra is described as having grown powerful and war-intoxicated, and as having gained the strength to support even heaven and earth. The meaning is that by this very strength Indra drives his enemies far off and wins victory.

3. Indra's growth benefits the sacrificers in many ways and increases their wealth. Therefore the prayer is made: वस्य इष्टय वृषा विश (*vasya iṣṭaya vṛṣā viśa*). वस्य इष्टये । वसीयसो धनस्य प्राप्तये उक्तलक्षणाय यागाय वा । (*vasya iṣṭaye | vasīyaso dhanasya prāptaye uktalakṣaṇāya yāgāya vā |*) It means either "for the gaining of wealth" or "for the sacrifice that brings wealth". Qualifications such as वसुवत् (*vasuvat*) are used of Soma in many places. For example:

गोवित्पवस्य वसुविद्धिरण्यविद्रॆतोधा इंदो भुवनेष्वर्पितः । त्वं सुवीरो असि सोम विश्ववित्तं त्वा विप्रा उप गिरेम आसते ॥ (*govitpavasya vasuviddhiraṇyavidrètodhā iṃdo bhuvaneṣvarpitaḥ | tvaṃ suvīro asi soma viśvavittaṃ tvā viprā upa girema āsate ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-26-39)

In this Ṛk the three epithets वसुवित् (*vasuvit*), हिरण्यवित् (*hiraṇyavit*) and गोवित् (*govit*) all belong to Soma. Since it has such qualities, Indra too, having drunk the Soma-juice, becomes able to supply wealth.

इंदो—इंदुरिंधेरुनत्तीर्वा (*iṃdo—iṃduriṃdherunattīrvā*): this word can be formed either from the root इंथ् (*iṃth*), which gives the sense "blaze", or from the root उद् (*ud*), which gives the sense "flow so as to wet". (Ni. 10-42.) The Nirukta-writers have quoted the Ṛk

प्र तद्वोचेयं भव्यायेंदवे हव्यो न य इषवान्‌मन्म रेजति रक्षोहा मन्म रेजति ॥ (*pra tadvoceyaṃ bhavyāyeṃdave havyo na ya iṣavānmanma rejati rakṣohā manma rejati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-6)

and so shown both senses of the word इंदु (*iṃdu*). In the present Ṛk too, this word praises in Soma both the quality of shining and the quality of flowing in liquid form and making everything moist.

ऋघायमाणः— शत्रुन् हिंसयन् (*ṛghāyamāṇaḥ— śatrun hiṃsayan*): "harming enemies". Monier Williams's Dictionary gives "Violence, Passion", that is, intense fervour, wrath. This word is used in some other Ṛks as well. For example,

### Printed p. 400
इंद्रः सुशिप्रो मघवा तरुत्रो महाव्रातस्तुविकूर्मिर्यघवान् । यदुग्रो धा बाधितो मर्त्येषु क्व १ त्या ते वृषभ वीर्याणि ॥ (*iṃdraḥ suśipro maghavā tarutro mahāvrātastuvikūrmiryaghavān | yadugro dhā bādhito martyeṣu kva 1 tyā te vṛṣabha vīryāṇi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-3)

In such Ṛks too, as in the present Ṛk, the purport stated is शत्रुविषयहिंसावान् (*śatruviṣayahiṃsāvān*), "one who has gained the power to harm enemies". Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛk

नहि त्वा रोदसी उभे ऋघायमाणमिन्वतः । जेषः स्वर्वतीरपः सं गा अस्मभ्यं धूनुहि ॥ (*nahi tvā rodasī ubhe ṛghāyamāṇaminvataḥ | jeṣaḥ svarvatīrapaḥ saṃ gā asmabhyaṃ dhūnuhi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-8)

explaining this word, said न्यन् हंतीति ऋघा । शत्रुवधं कुर्वाणं । (*nyan haṃtīti ṛghā | śatruvadhaṃ kurvāṇaṃ |*) that is, the epithet is used because he is a slayer of men. In the present Ṛk this word is an epithet either of Soma or of Indra.

इन्वसि (*invasi*): since this word is read among the roots denoting the action of pervading, such as इन्वति (*invati*) and नक्षति (*nakṣati*) (Ni. 3-10), इन्वसि (*invasi*) means "you pervade". The meaning is: you pervade Indra and increase his strength.

##### Grammar

- मत्सि—मदी स्तुतिमोदमदस्वप्नकांतिगतिषु इति धातुः । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थकः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । खरिच इति धातुदकारस्य तकारादेशः । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न आगच्छति । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- वस्य इष्टये—वसीयसः इष्टिः प्राप्तिः तस्यै । वसुशब्दात् मतुप् । तदुत्तरं ईयसुन् प्रत्यये आगते विन्‌मतोर्लुक् (पा. सू. ५-३-६५) इति मतुपो लुक् । टेः इति टिलोपः । छांदसत्वेन यकारस्यापि लोपः आगच्छति । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- विश—विश प्रवेशने इति धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- ऋघायमाणि—हन हिंसागत्योः इति धातुः । अन्येभ्योपि दृश्यंते (पा. सू. ३-२-७५) इति विट् प्रत्ययः । दृशिग्रहणसामर्थ्यात् नकारस्य अलोपः । हकारस्य घकारादेशः । अनृघा ऋघा भवति इति अर्थविवक्षायां लोहितादि डाज्यः क्यष् (पा. सू. ३-१-१३) इति क्यष् प्रत्ययः । वाक्यषः (पा. सू. १-३-९०) इति आत्मनेपदप्रत्ययः आगच्छति । लटः शानचादेशः । लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् क्यष्स्वरः अवशिष्यते । **NOTE**

### Printed p. 401
- इन्वसि—इवि व्याप्तौ इति धातुः । इदित्त्वात् नुमागमः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । तिणंतनिघातस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- अंति—अंतिके इत्यत्र छांदसत्वेन कादेः लोपः आगतः ।
- विंदसि—विद्‌ल्य लाभे इति धातुः । तुदादिः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने शेमुचादीनाम् (पा. सू. ७-१-५९) इति नुमागमः । तस्य अनुस्वारपरसवर्णौ । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः आगच्छति । **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तस्मि॒न्ना वे॑शया॒ गिरो॒ य एक॑श्चर्षणी॒नां ।  
> अनु॑ स्व॒धा यमु॒प्यते॒ यवं॒ न चर्कृ॑ष॒द्वृषा॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शस्मिन् । आ । वेशय । गिरः । यः । एकः । चर्षणीनां ।  
> अनु । स्वधा । यं । उप्यते । यवं । न । चर्कृषत् । वृषा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अंतरात्मन् होतर्वा तस्मिन्नसिद्ध इंद्रे गिरः स्तुतिरूपा वाच आवेशय ।
> स्थापय । तं स्तुहीत्यर्थः । य इंद्रश्चर्षणीनां ज्ञानवतां मनुष्याणामेक एक
> एव स्थानीयः । यमनु यमेवेंद्रमनु स्वधा हनिर्लक्षणमन्नमुप्यते । दीयत
> इत्यर्थः । स चेंद्रो वृषा वर्षकः सन्यवं न यवमिव पक्वं यवं यथा
> चर्कृषत् क्रमेणाददते कर्षकाः तद्वदादत्ते । यद्वा । अनु स्वधान्नसाधनं व्रीह्यादिक
> मुप्यते भूम् यस्येंद्रस्य वृष्टिरूपमनुग्रहमपेक्ष्योप्यत इत्यर्थः । स च
> वृषा वृष्टेर्वर्षिता स इंद्रो यवं न यवमिव सर्वबीजमपि चर्कृषत् ।
> पुनःपुनः करोति । अंकुरयति । हविःसाधनत्वप्राशस्त्रमपेक्ष्य यवशब्दः प्रयुक्तः ।
> एवंमहानुभाव इंद्रे गिर आ वेशयेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O inner self, or O Hotṛ, cause your praises, speech in the form of hymns, to enter (आवेशय (*āveśaya*)) into that Indra, who is well known." आवेशय (*āveśaya*) means "establish": the sense is "praise him". This Indra is the one (एकः (*ekaḥ*)) sole स्थानीयः (*sthānīyaḥ*) ("support") of the चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*), the knowing men. After whom, that is, after Indra himself (अनु (*anu*)), the स्वधा (*svadhā*), food in the form of the oblation, is offered (उप्यते (*upyate*), "is given"). And that Indra, being वृषा (*vṛṣā*), the shower, takes it, as ripe barley (यवं न (*yavaṃ na*)), as farmers harvest it by turns (चर्कृषत् (*carkṛṣat*)), so he takes it.

Alternatively: after (अनु (*anu*)) whose rain-form favour the स्वधा (*svadhā*), rice and the like, the means of food, is sown (उप्यते (*upyate*)) in the earth, that Indra, the वृषा (*vṛṣā*), the sender of rain, makes all seed, like barley (यवं न (*yavaṃ na*)), sprout again and again (चर्कृषत् (*carkṛṣat*)). The word यव (*yava*) is used with regard to barley's pre-eminence as a means of oblation. "Into Indra, of such great power, cause your praises to enter."
