##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- चर्क्षणीनां (*carkṣaṇīnāṃ*)—of all the knowing
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the one sole refuge
- यं अनु (*yaṃ anu*)—after which Indra
- स्वधा (*svadhā*)—food in the form of oblation
- उप्यते (*upyate*)—is given
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Indra
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—as the shower of desired things
- यवं न (*yavaṃ na*)—as farmers reap ripe barley grain
- चर्कृषत् (*carkṛṣat*)—he accepts. [Or: यं अनु (*yaṃ anu*), after which Indra (the rain given by Indra); स्वधा (*svadhā*), rice and the like, means of food; उप्यते (*upyate*), are sown in the earth; सः (*saḥ*), that; वृषा (*vṛṣā*), Indra, the rain-maker; यवं न (*yavaṃ na*), like barley; चर्कृषत् (*carkṛṣat*), makes (all seeds) sprout again and again.]
- तस्मिन् (*tasmin*)—in such an Indra
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—praises in the form of words
- आ वेशय (*ā veśaya*)—establish (praise Indra)
(Addressed to the self or the Hotṛ.) **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O self (O Hotṛ), praise Indra, the sole refuge of all the knowing, the sender of the rain needed for the growth of rice and the like that are the means of food, and the cause of the sprouting of barley and all other grains.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Pervade with our praise him who is the sole sustainer of men, to whom the oblation is presented. and who, the showerer (of benefits), causes (every desire) to bud like barley.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

एकः चर्षणीनां-ज्ञानवतां मनुष्याणां एक एव स्थानीयः । (*ekaḥ carṣaṇīnāṃ-jñānavatāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ eka eva sthānīyaḥ |*) Indra is the one support for all men endowed with wisdom, that is, their sole bearer and nourisher; thus Indra's greatness is praised.

चर्षणि (*carṣaṇi*): this word is read among the names of man (Ni. 3-7). The word is much used in the sense "man". For example:

अ याहि पूर्वीरति चर्षणीरा अर्य आशिष उप नो हरिभ्यां । इमा हि त्वा मतयः स्तोमतष्वा इंद्र हवंते सख्यं जुषाणाः ॥ (*a yāhi pūrvīrati carṣaṇīrā arya āśiṣa upa no haribhyāṃ | imā hi tvā matayaḥ stomataṣvā iṃdra havaṃte sakhyaṃ juṣāṇāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-43-2)

विश्वा यश्चर्षणीरभ्या ३ सा वाजेषु सासहत् । (*viśvā yaścarṣaṇīrabhyā 3 sā vājeṣu sāsahat |*) (Śa. Brā. 5-23-1)

### Printed p. 403
In many such places the word चर्षणि (*carṣaṇi*) is explained as "subjects, people". This epithet points to a distinctive quality of human beings. But when the component meaning of the word is stated, there is a difference of opinion. The scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit–English Dictionary, gives for this word "cultivating, agile, active", and shows that humans have the epithet चर्षणि (*carṣaṇi*) because they are active in agriculture and the like. He also shows that the root कृष् (*kṛṣ*) is the origin of this word. The Nirukta authors, quoting the Ṛk
हविषा जारो असां पिपर्ति पॆपुरिर्नरा । पिता कुटस्य चर्षणिः । (*haviṣā jāro asāṃ piparti pèpurirnarā | pitā kuṭasya carṣaṇiḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-46-4)
explain the word चर्षणि (*carṣaṇi*), an epithet of the word आदित्य (*āditya*), as "the one who sees, the seer, the one who looks on". In the present Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains it as ज्ञानवतां मनुष्याणां (*jñānavatāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ*), so the meaning is: those who have a sight consisting of knowledge, those who have the power of vision. The word is not an epithet of human beings alone; it is also used as an epithet of Indra and others. Just as in the Ṛk (1-46-4) quoted above by the Nirukta authors the seeing power of Āditya is stated, so in
युवामिंद्राग्नी वसुनो विभागे तवस्तमा शुश्रव वृत्रहत्ये । तावासद्या बर्हिषि यज्ञे अस्मिन्न चर्षणी मादयेथां सुतस्य ॥ (*yuvāmiṃdrāgnī vasuno vibhāge tavastamā śuśrava vṛtrahatye | tāvāsadyā barhiṣi yajñe asminna carṣaṇī mādayethāṃ sutasya ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-109-5)
and similar Ṛks, it is an epithet of Indra and Agni and describes their power of vision. Sāyaṇa explains सर्वस्य द्रष्टारौ इंद्राग्नी (*sarvasya draṣṭārau iṃdrāgnī*): those having the power to see everything. In the present Ṛk too the purport is: of human beings who possess a sight consisting of knowledge. Indra is the one and only protector of such people: this is the meaning of the sentence चर्षणीनां एकः (*carṣaṇīnāṃ ekaḥ*).

अनु स्वधा यमुप्यते (*anu svadhā yamupyate*)—the injunctive sentence that स्वधा (*svadhā*) is to be offered to Indra, the protector of all, indicates the duty of man. स्वधा-हनिर्लक्षणमन्नं । (*svadhā-hanirlakṣaṇamannaṃ |*) In the present context it means food in the form of oblation. The Nirukta authors included this word among the names of water (Ni. 2-23) and among the names of food (Ni. 3-F). But in many contexts स्वधा (*svadhā*) means one's own greatness, one's own brilliance or self-support. For example—
शश्वत्पुरोषा व्युवास देव्यथो अद्येदं व्यावो मघोनी । अथो व्युच्छादुत्तरा अनु द्यूनजरामृता चरति स्वधाभिः ॥ (*śaśvatpuroṣā vyuvāsa devyatho adyedaṃ vyāvo maghonī | atho vyucchāduttarā anu dyūnajarāmṛtā carati svadhābhiḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-13)

### Printed p. 404
In this Ṛk the word, used of Uṣas, is explained as आत्मीयैस्तेजोभिः ! (*ātmīyaistejobhiḥ !*), "by her own brilliances". Likewise,
यदंतरिक्षे पतथः पुरुभुजा यद्वेमे रोदसी अनु । यद्वा स्वधाभिरधितिस्थघो रथमत आ यातमश्विना ॥ (*yadaṃtarikṣe patathaḥ purubhujā yadveme rodasī anu | yadvā svadhābhiradhitisthagho rathamata ā yātamaśvinā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-10-6)
Here, describing the nature of the Aśvin deities, it is explained as आत्मीयैस्तेजोभिर्बलैर्वा सार्धं । (*ātmīyaistejobhirbalairvā sārdhaṃ |*): with your own brilliances, or with your own powers.
न मृत्युरासीदमृतं न तर्हि न रात्र्या अह्न असीत्प्रकेशः । आनीदवातं स्वधया तदेकं तस्माद्धान्नन्य परः किं चनास ॥ (*na mṛtyurāsīdamṛtaṃ na tarhi na rātryā ahna asītprakeśaḥ | ānīdavātaṃ svadhayā tadekaṃ tasmāddhānnanya paraḥ kiṃ canāsa ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-ऎ (*è*))
In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains स्वस्मिन् धीयते द्रियते आश्रित्य वर्तते इति स्वधा । (*svasmin dhīyate driyate āśritya vartate iti svadhā |*) Because it depends on itself, स्वधा (*svadhā*) is an epithet of Māyā, the wonderful power of Īśvara (the Supreme Brahman). Thus the word is used in various senses. In the present Ṛk it means food in the form of oblation.

Speaking of this word, the scholar Max Müller says that its use is ancient and that, from the standpoint of philology, it indicates many special meanings:

स्वधा (*svadhā*), literally one's own place, afterwards, one's own nature. It was a great triumph for the science of comparative philology that, long before the existence of such a word as स्वधा (*svadhā*) in sanskrit was known, it should have been postulated by professor Benfey in 1839. स्वधा (*svadhā*) was known, it is true, in the ordinary Sanskrit but there it only occured as an exclamation used on presenting an oblation to the manes. It was also explained to mean food offered to deceased ancestors, or to be the name of a personification of माया (*māyā*) or worldly illusion or of a nymph. The expressions अनु स्वधां (*anu svadhāṃ*) and स्वधां अनु (*svadhāṃ anu*) are of frequent occurance. They mean, according to the nature or character of the person spoken of and may be translated by as usual or accordig to a person's wont.

The word स्वधा (*svadhā*) has the gross meaning "one's own place, nature"; it also shows the meaning of food offered to the Pitṛs. Besides these, the word is known to be used in other senses. For example—

### Printed p. 405
प्र सु ष विभ्यो मरुतो विरस्तु प्र श्येनः श्येनेभ्य आशुपत्वा । अचक्रया यत्स्वधया सुपर्णो हव्यं भरन्मनवे देवजुष्टं ॥ (*pra su ṣa vibhyo maruto virastu pra śyenaḥ śyenebhya āśupatvā | acakrayā yatsvadhayā suparṇo havyaṃ bharanmanave devajuṣṭaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-4)
In this Ṛk, giving the meaning of the word, Sāyaṇa says that here स्वधा (*svadhā*) means "sap", and to support this meaning quotes
अपश्यं ग्रामं वहमानमारादचक्रया स्वधया वर्तमानं । सिषक्त्यर्यः प्र युगा जनानां सद्यः शिश्ना प्रमिनानो नवीयान् ॥ (*apaśyaṃ grāmaṃ vahamānamārādacakrayā svadhayā vartamānaṃ | siṣaktyaryaḥ pra yugā janānāṃ sadyaḥ śiśnā pramināno navīyān ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-27-19)
and says अत्र स्वधाशब्दो रथवाची, १०-२७-१९ इत्यादौ दर्शनात् (*atra svadhāśabdo rathavācī, 10-27-19 ityādau darśanāt*); he thus indicates that, as in the Ṛk quoted, in this Ṛk too (4-26-4) the word स्वधा (*svadhā*) means "chariot". But again, when explaining the Ṛk 10-27-19, he explains आचक्रया चक्रवर्जितया रथहीनया, स्वधया-स्वयमाश्मानं धारयंत्या सेनया (*ācakrayā cakravarjitayā rathahīnayā, svadhayā-svayamāśmānaṃ dhārayaṃtyā senayā*), giving स्वधा (*svadhā*) the meaning "army". Although he indicates in this context that the word has various meanings, he seems to have forgotten here the statement of the bhāṣya made earlier.

When the expressions स्वधां अनु (*svadhāṃ anu*) and अनु स्वधां (*anu svadhāṃ*) occur, the meanings naturally are "by nature" or "according to custom". For example,
स्वधामनु श्रियं नरो महि त्वेषा अमवंतो वृषप्सवः । वहंते अह्रुतप्सवः ॥ (*svadhāmanu śriyaṃ naro mahi tveṣā amavaṃto vṛṣapsavaḥ | vahaṃte ahrutapsavaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-20-7)
In such Ṛks the meaning is "by nature". In places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-13 the meaning is known to be "water".

##### Grammar

- वेशय—विश प्रवेशने धातुः । प्रयोजकव्यापारे द्योत्ये हेतुमति च इति णिच् । णिजंतात् लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः प्राप्नोति । छांदसत्वात् संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
- चर्षणीनाम्—कृष विलेखने धातुः । कृषेरादेश चः (उ. सू. २-२६१) इति अनि प्रत्ययः । आदेः चकारादेशः । पुगंतलघूपधस्य च इति धातोर्लघूपधस्य गुणः । षष्ठीबहुवचनांतरूपम् । नामन्यतरस्याम् (पा. सू. ६-१-११७) इति नाम उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

### Printed p. 406
- उप्यते—डुवप् बीजसंताने धातुः । कर्मणि लट् । प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । ल सार्वधातुकम् तास्यनुदात्तेत् इति सूत्रेण अनुदात्तत्वात् यक्स्वरः शिष्यते ।
- चर्कृषत्—कृष विलेखने धातुः । यज् लुकि धातोर्द्वित्वम् । आदिहल्‌शेषः । चर्त्वम् । रुग्रिक् च लुकि (पा. सू ७-४-९१) इति अभ्यासस्य रुगागमः । लेटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने तिप् । इतश्चलोपः पर—(पा. सू. ३-४-९७) इति इकारस्य लोपः । लेटोडाटौ (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) इति तस्य अडागमः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः तपः (पा. सू. २-४-७२) इति शपो लुक् । नाभ्यस्तस्याचि पिति—(पा. सू. ७-३-८७) इति लघूपधगुणस्य निषेधः प्राप्नोति । अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१८९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्य॒ विश्वा॑नि॒ हस्त॑योः॒ पंच॑ क्षिती॒नां वसु॑ ।  
> स्पा॒शय॑स्व॒ यो अ॑स्म॒ध्रुग्दि॒ व्येवा॒शनि॑र्जहि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्य । विश्वानि । हस्तयोः । पंच । क्षितीनां । वसु ।  
> स्नाशयस्व । यः । अस्मध्रुक् । दिव्याइव । अशनिः । जहि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्येंद्रस्य हस्तयोः पंच क्षितीनां । क्षियंति निवसंति गच्छंति ना क्षितयो
> मनुष्याः । पंचानां मनुष्याणां प्रीणयित्यणि विश्वानि सर्वाणि वसु वसूनि धृतानि
> भवंति । देवा मनुष्याः पितरः पशवः पक्षिणश्चति पंच जनाः । चत्वारो वर्णा
> विषादपंचमाः पंच जना इत्यन्ये । स तादृशेंद्र त्वं स्पाशयस्व । बाधस्व ।
> योऽस्मधृक् अस्मभ्यं द्रुह्यति तं । केन प्रकारेणीति स उच्यते । दिव्या दिवि
> भवातनिरिवातनिर्भूत्वास्मद्द्वैष्टाज्ञहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of whom, Indra, in whose hands are all treasures of the five क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*). क्षितयो (*kṣitayo*) are human beings, because they dwell, abide or move about. The treasures of the five kinds of people are held (in his hands). The five classes are: gods, humans, Pitṛs, animals and birds. Others say the five peoples are the four castes with the Niṣāda as fifth. Such as you are, Indra: स्पाशयस्व (*spāśayasva*), afflict him who is hostile to us (अस्मध्रुक् (*asmadhruk*)). In what manner? Being like the heavenly thunderbolt, slay him who hates us.

### Printed p. 407

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Indra
- हस्तयोः (*hastayoḥ*)—in both hands
- पंच क्षितीनां (*paṃca kṣitīnāṃ*)—dear to the five classes of living beings: gods, humans, Pitṛs, animals, birds
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—of all kinds
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth (is held)
- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सः (*saḥ*)—such you
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- अस्मध्रुक् (*asmadhruk*)—is hostile to us
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- स्वाशयस्व (*svāśayasva*)—afflict
- दिव्या (*divyā*)—belonging to the heavenly world
- अशनिः इव (*aśaniḥ iva*)—like a thunderbolt
- जहि (*jahi*)—slay (our enemies)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All kinds of wealth dear to the five classes of living beings (gods, humans, Pitṛs, animals, birds) are in your hands. O Indra, such as you are, afflict him who is our enemy; as if you were the heavenly thunderbolt, slay our enemies.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
In whose hands are all the treasures (that are desired by) the five classes of beings : destroy, Indra, him who oppresses us ; slay him, . (as if you were yourself) the heavenly thunderbolt.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Indra is described as the lord of all wealth, which is the cause of the prosperity of all beings, gods, humans and the rest; and Indra, endowed with such greatness, is prayed to destroy the enemies of the sacrificers. यस्य हस्तयोः पंच क्षितीनां विश्वानि वसु (*yasya hastayoḥ paṃca kṣitīnāṃ viśvāni vasu*)—Indra in whose control are the riches of the five क्षिति (*kṣiti*): thus Indra's wealth is described. As to what is meant here by पंचक्षिति (*paṃcakṣiti*), Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning. First,
1. देवा मनुष्याः पितरः पशवः पक्षिणश्चति पंच जनाः । (*devā manuṣyāḥ pitaraḥ paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaścati paṃca janāḥ |*) the five kinds: gods, humans, Pitṛs, animals and birds; and second,
2. चत्वारो वर्णाः निषाद पंचमाः पंच जना इत्यन्ये (*catvāro varṇāḥ niṣāda paṃcamāḥ paṃca janā ityanye*)—he explains in another way as the people of the four castes together with the Niṣādas. For both meanings authorities of Śruti sentences can be shown. First the derivation of the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*) may be examined, and afterwards what meaning of पंचक्षिति (*paṃcakṣiti*) may be taken in the present context may be considered.
क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)—क्षियंति निवसंति गच्छंति ना क्षितयो मनुष्याः । (*kṣiyaṃti nivasaṃti gacchaṃti nā kṣitayo manuṣyāḥ |*) Sāyaṇa explains that human beings have this epithet because they dwell or move about. The Nirukta authors read the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*) among the 25 names of man beginning with नरः (*naraḥ*) (Ni. 3-7).

### Printed p. 408
अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋतावा । स वृत्रहा सनयो विश्ववेदाः वर्षद्विश्वाति मरिता गृणंतं । (*agnirnetā bhaga iva kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ deva ṛtupā ṛtāvā | sa vṛtrahā sanayo viśvavedāḥ varṣadviśvāti maritā gṛṇaṃtaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-4)
In such Ṛks, when the difference between humans and the divine subjects is shown, the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*) indicates humans, the subjects of the earth. But in the present Ṛk it cannot be definitely said that only earthly humans are meant, because Indra's wealth pervades earth, atmosphere and all.
न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता अपश्चन शवसो अंतमापुः । स प्ररिक्वा त्वक्षसा क्षो दिवश्च मरुत्वान्नो भवत्स्विंद्र ऊती । (*na yasya devā devatā na martā apaścana śavaso aṃtamāpuḥ | sa prarikvā tvakṣasā kṣo divaśca marutvānno bhavatsviṃdra ūtī |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-15)
In such Ṛks the power of Indra, who is divine in nature and endowed with qualities such as generosity, is described as surpassing the power of all others in the world; neither gods nor humans have reached its end; and with his enemy-destroying and majestic power Indra makes earth and heaven shine together. Because of this, and because in the present Ṛk too Indra's wealth is described as all-pervading, पंचक्षितीनां (*paṃcakṣitīnāṃ*) cannot be said to mean merely the four-fold class together with the Niṣāda as fifth. In this matter the Nirukta authors do not state their own view but only report the opinions of others.
पंचजना “मम होत्रं जुषध्वं” गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः । (*paṃcajanā “mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ” gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ |*)
(Ni. 3-8)
They report only the opinions of others: some hold that the five groups are Gandharvas, Pitṛs, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; and Upamanyu and others hold that the four castes, Brāhmaṇa and the rest, together with the Niṣādas as the fifth group, make up the five peoples.
Formerly, when all the gods prayed to Agni to accept the oblation offered in the sacrifice for them and distribute it to all, Agni agreed and said,
तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुरा अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं ॥ (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4)
"Let the five peoples together enjoy this oblation." The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā quoted this sentence containing the answer, and discussed the five peoples, showing differences of opinion.

### Printed p. 409
In the verse

प्रत्युवाचाथ तानग्निर्विश्वेदेवा यदूच मां । तत्करिष्ये जुषंतां तु होत्रं पंचजना मम ॥ (*pratyuvācātha tānagnirviśvedevā yadūca māṃ | tatkariṣye juṣaṃtāṃ tu hotraṃ paṃcajanā mama ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-66)

the answer that Agni gave to the gods is stated, and afterwards the word *pañcajana* is explained:

शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः । उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते पंचजनाः स्मृताः ॥ (*śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇaścāgnirete paṃcajanāḥ smṛtāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-67)

That is, the fire at the entrance of the hall, the consecrated Āhavanīya fire, the Gārhapatya fire that is the son of the sacrificer, and the southern and northern fires: these five kinds of fire are traditionally spoken of as five classes. Besides this view there is also:

मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः । गंधर्वा पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ (*manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ | gaṃdharvā pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-68)

According to the first opinion the serpents and rākṣasas form one group; according to the second opinion the yakṣas and rākṣasas form one group.

यास्कौपमन्यवावेतानाहतुः पंच वै जनान् । निषादपंचमान्वर्णा मन्यते शाकटायनः ॥ (*yāskaupamanyavāvetānāhatuḥ paṃca vai janān | niṣādapaṃcamānvarṇā manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-69)

By this sentence the author of the Bṛhaddevatā says that Yāska's view is the first. But in the Nirukta Yāska states the views of others and has not stated his own view definitively; probably he accepted that one.

ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते (*ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate*) (Bṛ. De. 7-70)

It is the view of Śākapūṇi that the four priests beginning with the Hotṛ, together with the sacrificer, make a group of five.

चक्षुःश्रोत्रं मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः । गंधर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा ॥ सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयंते हैतरेयके ॥ (*cakṣuḥśrotraṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ | gaṃdharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā ‖ sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyaṃte haitareyake ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-71, 72)

The view of the spiritualists is that the eye, ear, mind, speech and breath are the five *pañcajana*. That they are the Gandharvas and others is explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3-31-5). That such five peoples should enjoy the oblation

### Printed p. 410
is the answer Agni gave to the gods; thus the differences of opinion are shown in the Bṛhaddevatā's explanation too.

In the verse under discussion it is described: पंच क्षितीनां विश्वानि वसु इंद्रस्य हस्तयोः । (*paṃca kṣitīnāṃ viśvāni vasu iṃdrasya hastayoḥ |*). Since the entire world comes under Indra's protection, all the above views fit the phrase पंच क्षितीनां (*paṃca kṣitīnāṃ*).

स्पाशयस्व (*spāśayasva*)—बाधस्व (*bādhasva*): harass. स्पश—बाधनस्पर्शनयोः (*spaśa—bādhanasparśanayoḥ*): it is a verb form derived from the root *spaś*, which means touching, or perceiving by other kinds of direct perception, and also harassing. The prayer is: harass and destroy the enemies of the sacrificers. Nominal forms derived from this root are also in use; in those contexts it means hostile enemies who harass, or divine messengers who harass enemies. In the verse

प्रति स्पशो वि सृज तूर्णितमो भवा पायुर्विशो अस्या आदब्धः । यो नो दूरे अघशंसो यो अंत्यग्ने माकिष्टे व्यथिरा दधर्षीत् ॥ (*prati spaśo vi sṛja tūrṇitamo bhavā pāyurviśo asyā ādabdhaḥ | yo no dūre aghaśaṃso yo aṃtyagne mākiṣṭe vyathirā dadharṣīt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-3)

the word स्पशः (*spaśaḥ*) means परबाधकान् रश्मीन् चारान् वा (*parabādhakān raśmīn cārān vā*), that is, either the rays of Agni that harass enemies or Agni's messengers who harass enemies.

When it speaks of matter perceptible to the senses such as the skin, the word is used also in the first sense stated above. For example:

प्रोरोर्मित्रावरुणा पृथिव्याः प्र दिव ऋष्टाद्बृहतः सुदानू । स्पतो दधाथे ओषधीषु निष्कृधग्यतो अनिमिषं रक्षमाणा ॥ (*prorormitrāvaruṇā pṛthivyāḥ pra diva ṛṣṭādbṛhataḥ sudānū | spato dadhāthe oṣadhīṣu niṣkṛdhagyato animiṣaṃ rakṣamāṇā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-61-3)

In such verses it means a form perceptible to the senses. In the present verse the root is used in the sense of harassing, as said above, and it means: harass, destroy the enemies.

##### Grammar

- क्षितीनाम् — क्षि निवासगत्योः धातुः । क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । षष्ठीबहुवचनांतरूपं । नामन्यतरस्याम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१७) इति नामिन उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- स्पाशयत्व — स्पश बाधनस्पर्शनयोः धातुः । हेतुमति च (पा. सू. ३-१-२६) इति णिच् । अत उपधायाः (पा. सू. ७-२-११६) इति उपधावृद्धिः । णिजंतात् लोट् । मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने थासः से इति से आदेशः । सवाभ्यां नामा इति एकारस्य वत्वं । शप् निमित्तं कृत्वा णिचे गुणः अयादेशः । पादादौ स्थितत्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । णिच् स्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

### Printed p. 411
- अस्मध्रुक् — ध्रुह जिघांसायाम् धातुः । सत्तूद्विष—(पा. सू. ३-२-६१) इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । दादेर्धातोर्घः (पा. सू. ८-२-३२) इति सु परे हकारस्य घत्वं । एकाचो बशो—(पा. सू. ८-२-३७) इति आदेः दकारस्य धकारादेशः । पदांतस्य जस्त्वं चर्त्वं । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- दिव्या — दिवि भवा दिव्या । दंडादिभ्यो यः (पा.सू ५-१-६६) इति य प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्ता भवति । स्त्रीत्वे अदंतत्वात् टाप् ।
- जहि — हन हिंसागत्योः धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिपः हि आदेशः । हंतेर्जीः (पा.सू. ६-४-३६) इति धातोः जादेशः । असिद्धवत्राभात् (पा.सू. ६-४-२२) इति असिद्धत्वात् अतोहेः इति हेः लोपः न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति । ॥ ३ ॥

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> असु॑न्वंतं समं जहि दू॒णाशं॒ यो न ते॒ मयः॑ ।  
> अ॒स्मभ्य॑मस्य॒ वेद॑नं द॒द्धि सू॒रिश्चि॑दोहते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असुन्वंतं । समं । जहि । दुःखनशं । यः । न । ते । मयः ।  
> अस्मभ्यं । अस्य । वेदनं । दद्धि । सूरिः । चित् । ओहते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र असुन्वंतं सोमाभिषवमकुर्वाणं । त्वामयजंतमित्यर्थः ।
> दूणाशं दुःखेन नाशनीयं समं । आयं सर्वानुदात्तः सर्वशब्द पर्यायः ।
> अयष्टन् सर्वान् । यद्वा । सममेकोद्योगेनाविशेषेण वा जहि । तेन
> किमपराद्धमिति आत अह । यस्ते तव मयः । मय इति सुखनाम । तव सुखहेतुर्न
> भवति । यो होमेन स्तुत्या ना न प्रीणाति तं जहि । किंचास्य वेदनं धनमस्मभ्यं
> दद्दि । देहि ॥ दद दान इत्यस्माद्व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । छांदसः शपो लुक् ॥
> सूरिश्चिदोहते । चिदेवार्थे । सूरिस्थव स्तोतैवौहते । वहति । पाप्नोति धनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, slay the one who does not press Soma (असुन्वंतं (*asunvaṃtaṃ*)), that is, who does not sacrifice to you. दूणाशं (*dūṇāśaṃ*) means one to be destroyed only with difficulty. समं (*samaṃ*) is आयं (*āyaṃ*), with every syllable unaccented, a synonym of the word "all"; the sense is "all who do not sacrifice". Or else: slay with a single effort, or without distinction. If asked what offence they have committed, he answers: the one who is not मयः (*mayaḥ*) to you; मय (*maya*) is a name for happiness, so he is not a cause of happiness to you. Slay the one who does not please you with offering and praise. Further, give us his wealth (वेदनं (*vedanaṃ*)); दद्दि (*daddi*) is "give", from the root दद (*dada*) in the sense of giving, with parasmaipada by irregularity and elision of शप् (*śap*) in the Veda. सूरिश्चिदोहते (*sūriścidohate*): चित् (*cit*) has the sense of "only"; the सूरिः (*sūriḥ*) is your praiser, and he alone carries off (वहति (*vahati*)), obtains, the wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which man
- ते (*te*)—to you
- मयः न (*mayaḥ na*)—is not a cause of happiness (through offering and gifts)
- असुन्वंतं (*asunvaṃtaṃ*)—one who does not press Soma (who gives you no Soma offering)
- दूणाशं (*dūṇāśaṃ*)—though destroyable only with great difficulty
- समं (*samaṃ*)—with a single blow (all such persons)
- जहि (*jahi*)—slay
- अस्य (*asya*)—his
- वेदनं (*vedanaṃ*)—wealth
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- दद्धि (*daddhi*)—give
- सूरिः चित् (*sūriḥ cit*)—the one who praises you alone
- ओहते (*ohate*)—carries (obtains) the wealth

### Printed p. 412

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the one who does not press Soma for you, the one who does not bring you happiness through offerings and the like: slay all of these with a single blow; and give us their wealth. For your praisers alone are worthy to obtain wealth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Slay every one who offers not libations, however difficult to be destroyed : slay every one who is no delight to you : bestow upon us his wealth, for the pious (worshipper) deserves it.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दूणाशं (*dūṇāśaṃ*)—दुःखेन नाशनीयं (*duḥkhena nāśanīyaṃ*). The meaning is one who is destroyed with difficulty. The prowess of some enemies is so great that destroying them takes great effort. The word दूणाश (*dūṇāśa*) is used to convey this point.

सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)—सूरिस्तव स्तोता (*sūristava stotā*). It means a praiser. Since it is read among the 13 names of praisers beginning with रेभः (*rebhaḥ*), जरिता (*jaritā*), कारुः (*kāruḥ*) (Ni. 3-19), सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) means praisers, devotees who recite hymns. The word सूरि (*sūri*) is also used in many places in contexts where it gives the sense of the wise, the discerning, the intelligent. When it is used of the seers, who possess the supernatural power of vision, both of the eye and of the mind, by which they grasp the true nature of the gods and the secret principles of the universe, this epithet gives a special meaning.

तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः । दिवीव चक्षुराततं ॥ (*tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣurātataṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-20)

In such contexts it denotes not merely those who praise but also the extraordinary power of vision of the seers. And it is used not only of seers but also as an epithet of gods such as Indra.

##### Grammar

- असुन्वंतम् — षुञ् अभिषवे धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । नञ् तत्पुरुषसमासे तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ—सूत्रेण नञ् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।

### Printed p. 413
मंहिष्ठ मच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं नावृधध्यै ॥ (*maṃhiṣṭha macchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ nāvṛdhadhyai ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61 3)

In such verses, with विपश्चितमिंद्रं (*vipaścitamiṃdraṃ*), it also shows the wisdom of gods such as Indra. Besides this, the word सूरि (*sūri*) is also used when it denotes a lord, an impeller, one who leads along the good path. For example:

जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवाश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः । (*jano yaḥ pajrebhyo vājinīvāśvāvato rathino mahyaṃ sūriḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-8)

असद्यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिंद्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता । (*asadyathā jaritra uta sūririṃdro rāyo viśvavārasya dātā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-23-10)

मुह्यंत्वन्ने अभिषेको जनास इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु ॥ (*muhyaṃtvanne abhiṣeko janāsa ihāsmākaṃ maghavā sūrirastu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-81-6)

In these and similar contexts, with reference to gods who are lords and leaders along the good path, this epithet also describes the qualities of Indra and others.

आदस्य ते कृष्णासो दक्षि सूरयः शूरस्येव त्वेषथादीषते वयः । (*ādasya te kṛṣṇāso dakṣi sūrayaḥ śūrasyeva tveṣathādīṣate vayaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-141-8)

In such places only here and there does it mean "way".

##### Grammar

- असुन्वंतम् — षुञ् अभिषवे धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । नञ् तत्पुरुषसमासे तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ—सूत्रेण नञ् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- समम् — सर्वार्थकः अयं समशब्दः सर्वानुदात्तः भवति ।
- वेदनम् — विद्‌ल्य लाभे धातुः । ल्युट् प्रत्ययः । युवोरनाकौ इति तस्य अनादेशः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य लघोपधगुणः । लिशि (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति प्रत्ययस्य पूर्वस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- दद्दि — दद दाने धातुः । भ्वादिः । व्यत्ययो बहुलं इति परस्मैपदी भवति । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिपः हि आदेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपः लुक् । झलंतपरत्वात् हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिः (पा सू. ६-४ १०१) इति हेः धि आदेशः । पादादौ स्थितत्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । हेः अपित्वविधानात् अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति ।

- ओहते — वह प्रापणे धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपं । बहुलं छंदसि इति संप्रसारणं भवति । अतिजं-द परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति । ॥ ४ ॥ **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आवो॒ यस्य॑ द्वि॒बर्ह॑सो॒ऽर्केषु॑ सानु॒षगस॑त् ।  
> आ॒जाविंद्र॑स्येंदो॒ प्रावो॒ वाजे॑षु वा॒जिनं॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आवः । यस्य । द्विबर्हसः । अर्केषु । सानुषक् । असत् ।  
> अजौ । इंद्रस्य । इंदो इति । प्र । आवः । वाजेषु । वाजिनं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम तव यस्य द्विबर्हसः स्तोत्रहवीरूपद्विविधपरिवृढकर्मवतो यजमानस्यार्केषु मंत्रेषु सानुषक् सानुषंगः सातत्यमसत् भवेत्
> तमावः । तं यजमानं रक्षसि तर्पयसि वा । यद्वा ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ यं द्वयोः
> स्थानयोः परिवृढं यमिंद्रं हे इंदो यदार्केषु सानुषगसत् भवेः तदावः ।
> अरक्षः । अतर्पयो वा । तस्यैवेंद्रस्याज् संग्रामे हे सोम वाजिनं तथान्नवंतं तमिंद्रं वाजेषु बलेष्वन्नेषु वा निमित्तभूतेषु प्रावः । प्रकर्षणारक्षयः।
> पानसमये तर्पयित्वा संग्रामसमये बलवर्धनेन जयप्राप्तशत्रुधनतर्पणेन
> वारक्ष इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra-Soma (इंदो (*iṃdo*)), the sacrificer who has two-fold परिवृढ (*parivṛḍha*) rites, namely praise and oblation (द्विबर्हसः (*dvibarhasaḥ*)), and in whose अर्केषु (*arkeṣu*) (mantras) there is सानुषक् (*sānuṣak*), continuity, असत् (*asat*) (would be): that sacrificer you protect (आवः (*āvaḥ*)) or satisfy. Or else, with the genitive in the sense of the object: यं (*yaṃ*), the Indra who is परिवृढ (*parivṛḍha*) in two places, whom you, O Soma, protected or satisfied when you were joined with the mantras. Of that same Indra, in battle (अजौ (*ajau*)), O Soma, you प्रावः (*prāvaḥ*), protected excellently, that Indra who is वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*), possessed of food, in the वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*), in the strengths or foods that are the occasion. The sense is: having satisfied him at the time of drinking, you protect him at the time of battle by increasing his strength, or by satisfying him with the wealth of enemies obtained through victory.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) इंदो (*(he) iṃdo*)—O Soma juice
- द्विबर्हसः (*dvibarhasaḥ*)—twofold, in the form of praise and oblation (devoted to Indra)
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which sacrificer
- अर्केषु (*arkeṣu*)—in the mantras
- सानुषक् (*sānuṣak*)—the joining (union of praise and offering)
- असत् (*asat*)—there is
- आवः (*āvaḥ*)—you protect him
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- अर्केषु (*arkeṣu*)—in the mantras
- सानुषक् (*sānuṣak*)—in conjunction
- असत् (*asat*)—you are
- द्विबर्हसः (*dvibarhasaḥ*)—the lord of the two worlds (Heaven and Earth)
- यस्य (*yasya*)—which Indra

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रक्षिसुत्तेयो (*rakṣisutteyo*)—(the sense continues from the previous page) "do you protect (do you satisfy)?"
- तस्य एव (*tasya eva*)—of that very one
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- आजौ (*ājau*)—in battle
- (हे सोम (*he soma*)—O Soma-juice)
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—Indra, who is endowed with food
- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—when strengths or foods are the occasion
- प्र आवः (*pra āvaḥ*)—you have protected especially

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-juice, you protect the sacrificers who worship Indra with both praise and oblations. (When the sacrificer praises Indra, you protect, or satisfy, Indra, the lord of heaven and earth, joining him with the mantras the sacrificer utters.) To that same mighty Indra give help, in battles, to obtain food and the like.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Soma, you protect him in whose prayers, doubly devout, there is the combination (of praise and oblation) : protect, especially, Indra in war ; protect the vigorous Indra in battles.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पानसमये तर्पयित्वा, संग्रामसमये बलवर्धनेन जयप्राप्तशत्रुधन तर्पणेन वा अरक्षः ॥ (*pānasamaye tarpayitvā, saṃgrāmasamaye balavardhanena jayaprāptaśatrudhana tarpaṇena vā arakṣaḥ ‖*) Sāyaṇa has explained that the chief meaning of this mantra is this: describing the satisfaction that comes to Indra after drinking Soma, and, at the time of battle, the growth of strength, the victory over enemies that results from it, and the winning of the enemy's wealth as the consequence, it tells that Soma is a protector to Indra in all circumstances.

द्विबर्हसः (*dvibarhasaḥ*)—स्तोत्रहवीरूपद्विविधपरिवृढकर्मवतः यजमानस्य (*stotrahavīrūpadvividhaparivṛḍhakarmavataḥ yajamānasya*): of the sacrificer who has a rite in the form of praise and oblation, which both increase and are themselves increased; thus it is in one way an epithet of the sacrificer. Or else यं द्वयोः स्थानयोः परिवृढं यं इंद्रं (*yaṃ dvayoḥ sthānayoḥ parivṛḍhaṃ yaṃ iṃdraṃ*) (genitive in the sense of the accusative): Indra, who has grown in both earth and atmosphere (the genitive stands here in the place of the object); in this other way it can be explained, Sāyaṇa says. The second meaning agrees with the explanation of the Nirukta-author. He gives the etymology of the word द्विबर्हाः (*dvibarhāḥ*) thus:
द्विबर्हाः—द्विबर्हा द्वयोः स्थानयोः परिवृढो मध्यमे च स्थान उत्तमे च । (*dvibarhāḥ—dvibarhā dvayoḥ sthānayoḥ parivṛḍho madhyame ca sthāna uttame ca |*) (Ni. 6-17)
The meaning is: one who has grown in the heavenly world and in the atmosphere; and then

### Printed p. 416
he cites the Ṛk
महा इंद्रो नृवदा चर्षणिप्रा उत द्विबर्हा अमिनः सहोभिः । अस्मद्रग्वावृधे वीर्यायोरुः पृथुः सुकृतः कर्तृभिर्भूत् ॥ (*mahā iṃdro nṛvadā carṣaṇiprā uta dvibarhā aminaḥ sahobhiḥ | asmadragvāvṛdhe vīryāyoruḥ pṛthuḥ sukṛtaḥ kartṛbhirbhūt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-19 1)
and shows the use of this word. Here the word द्विबर्हाः (*dvibarhāḥ*) is an epithet of Indra. Sāyaṇa states the purport of the word as द्वयोर्लोकयोः परिवृढः (*dvayorlokayoḥ parivṛḍhaḥ*). Likewise in
आ द्विबर्हा अमिनो याश्विंद्रो वृषा हरिभ्यां परिषिक्तमंधः । गव्या सुतस्य प्रभृतस्य मध्वः सत्रा खेदामरुशहा वृषस्व ॥ (*ā dvibarhā amino yāśviṃdro vṛṣā haribhyāṃ pariṣiktamaṃdhaḥ | gavyā sutasya prabhṛtasya madhvaḥ satrā khedāmaruśahā vṛṣasva ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-116-4)
it is again an epithet of Indra. Here द्वाभ्यां स्तुतिशस्त्राभ्यां वर्धनीयः । वृहेवर्धनार्थस्य कर्मण्यसुन् । (*dvābhyāṃ stutiśastrābhyāṃ vardhanīyaḥ | vṛhevardhanārthasya karmaṇyasun |*) The explanation is given that, formed from the root वृह् (*vṛh*), it gives the sense "one who has grown", and the formation of the word is shown.
[As the usage द्विबर्हाः (*dvibarhāḥ*) occurs, so the usage अद्रिबर्हाः (*adribarhāḥ*) occurs in Ṛks such as 10-63-3: the stones that have grown.]

अर्केषु (*arkeṣu*)—मंत्रेषु (*maṃtreṣu*): explained as "in the mantras that are the means of worship". The Nirukta-author's different meanings are given:
अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चंति । अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चंति । अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि । अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कुटुकिम्ना । (*arko devo bhavati yadenamarcaṃti | arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcaṃti | arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtāni | arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kuṭukimnā |*) (Ni. 5-4)
Since it is the object of worship, arka is a deity; since it is the means of worship, arka is a mantra; since it gives vitality to beings, arka is food; and it is a particular kind of bitter tree. Then the Ṛk
गायंति त्वा गायत्रिणोर्चंत्यर्कमकिणः । ब्रह्माणस्त्वा शतक्रत उद्यंशमिव येमिरे ॥ (*gāyaṃti tvā gāyatriṇorcaṃtyarkamakiṇaḥ | brahmāṇastvā śatakrata udyaṃśamiva yemire ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-1)
is cited, showing the use of the word ārka and its meaning. The power of the ārka is extremely great, and its greatness is praised in many places. In the Aitareya Āraṇyaka:
अथातः शिरः । यद्गायत्रीषु भवत्यग्रं वै छंदसां गायत्र्यग्रमंगानां शिरः । तदर्कवतीषु भवत्यग्निर्वा अर्कः । ता नव भवंति नव कपालं शिरः ॥ (*athātaḥ śiraḥ | yadgāyatrīṣu bhavatyagraṃ vai chaṃdasāṃ gāyatryagramaṃgānāṃ śiraḥ | tadarkavatīṣu bhavatyagnirvā arkaḥ | tā nava bhavaṃti nava kapālaṃ śiraḥ ‖*) (Ai. Ā. 1-4-1)

### Printed p. 417
This passage is cited, and it is said that the next nine Ṛks, beginning with the Ṛk इंद्रमिद्दाथिनो बृहदिंद्रमर्केभिरर्किणः । (*iṃdramiddāthino bṛhadiṃdramarkebhirarkiṇaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-1), are the ārka mantras, that they are the mantras of the nature of the head, and that since the Gāyatra is the principal element and these mantras too are in that Gāyatra form, the ārka mantras hold the principal place above all mantras. In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad, giving the etymology of the word arka:
सोर्चन्न चरत्तस्यार्चच आपोऽजायंतार्चते वै मे कमभूदिति तदेवार्कस्यार्कत्वं कं ह वा अस्मै भवति य एवमेतदर्कस्यार्कत्वं वेद । (*sorcanna carattasyārcaca āpo 'jāyaṃtārcate vai me kamabhūditi tadevārkasyārkatvaṃ kaṃ ha vā asmai bhavati ya evametadarkasyārkatvaṃ veda |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-2-1)
While Death, worshipping, was moving about in search of a body, water came into being; therefore water became known by the name arka. For this very reason:
अपो वा अर्कः तद्यदपां शिर आसीत्तत्समहन्यत । (*apo vā arkaḥ tadyadapāṃ śira āsīttatsamahanyata |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-2-2)
and so on it is described. Here arka reflects the hidden principle of the universe. The greatness of arka, which sets forth the Prajāpati principle, and the account of its nature, are explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, in the context of Āruṇi's instruction, thus:
श्वेतकेतुर्हारुणेयः यक्ष्यमाणा आस तग्०ह पितोवाच कानृत्विजोऽवृथा इति स होवाचायं नेव मे वैश्वावसव्यो होतेति तग्०ह प्रप्रच्छ वेत्थ ब्राह्मणा वैश्वावसव्य ॥ (*śvetaketurhāruṇeyaḥ yakṣyamāṇā āsa tag0ha pitovāca kānṛtvijo 'vṛthā iti sa hovācāyaṃ neva me vaiśvāvasavyo hoteti tag0ha prapraccha vettha brāhmaṇā vaiśvāvasavya ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-4-1)
When Śvetaketu Āruṇi, son of Uddālaka Aruṇi, was engaged in undertaking a sacrifice, his father asked him which priests he had chosen for the rite; Śvetaketu said that Vaiśvāvasavya was his Hotṛ. Then the father said:
चत्वारि महांतीति । वेद भो ३ इति होवाच..................वेत्थ चत्वारि क्यानीति वेद भो ३ इति होवाच वेत्थ चत्वारि क्यानां क्यानी३इति वेद भो ३ इति होवाच वेत्थ चत्वारि अर्कानिति वेद भो इति होवाच वेत्थ चतुरोऽर्काणामर्कानिति वेद भो इति होवा च ॥ (*catvāri mahāṃtīti | veda bho 3 iti hovāca..................vettha catvāri kyānīti veda bho 3 iti hovāca vettha catvāri kyānāṃ kyānī3iti veda bho 3 iti hovāca vettha catvāri arkāniti veda bho iti hovāca vettha caturo 'rkāṇāmarkāniti veda bho iti hovā ca ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-4-2)
"Do you know the four great principles? Do you know the principle connected with Ka (Prajāpati)? And among these, the four most hidden principles — do you know them? Do you know the nature of the four universal lights?

### Printed p. 418
Have you reflected on the principle that is the light-form of the lights?" Asked thus, Śvetaketu replied that he knew all that. Again the father said:
वेत्थार्कमिति । अथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति वेत्थार्कपर्णो इत्यथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति वेत्थार्कपुष्पे इत्यथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति वेत्थार्ककोश्यावित्यथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति वेत्थार्कसमुद्गावित्यथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति वेत्थार्कधाना इत्यथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति वेत्थार्काष्ठीलामित्यथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति वेत्थार्कमूलमित्यथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति ॥ (*vetthārkamiti | atha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti vetthārkaparṇo ityatha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti vetthārkapuṣpe ityatha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti vetthārkakośyāvityatha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti vetthārkasamudgāvityatha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti vetthārkadhānā ityatha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti vetthārkāṣṭhīlāmityatha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti vetthārkamūlamityatha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-4-3)
"Do you know the nature of arka, of the arka-leaves and arka-flowers? Do you know the nature of the arka-capsules and arka-grains? Do you know the root of arka?" Asked this, he said he knew none of these and asked that they be explained to him. Then the father, explaining arka, told also its hidden meaning.
अथ ह वै यत्तदुवाच । वेत्थार्कमिति पुरुषग्ं हैव तदुवाच । वेत्थार्कपर्णे इति कर्णौ हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कपुष्टे इत्यक्षिणी हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्ककोश्याविति नासिके हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कसमुद्गावित्योषौ हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कधाना इति दंतान्हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्काष्ठीलामिति हॆह्वाग्ं हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कमूलमित्यन्नग्ं हैव तदुवाच स एषोऽग्निरर्को यत्पुरुषः स यो हैतमेवमग्निमर्कं पुरुषमुपास्तेयमहमग्निरर्कोऽस्मीति विद्यया हैवास्यैष आत्मन्नग्निरर्कश्चितो भवति ॥ (*atha ha vai yattaduvāca | vetthārkamiti puruṣagṃ haiva taduvāca | vetthārkaparṇe iti karṇau haiva taduvāca vetthārkapuṣṭe ityakṣiṇī haiva taduvāca vetthārkakośyāviti nāsike haiva taduvāca vetthārkasamudgāvityoṣau haiva taduvāca vetthārkadhānā iti daṃtānhaiva taduvāca vetthārkāṣṭhīlāmiti hèhvāgṃ haiva taduvāca vetthārkamūlamityannagṃ haiva taduvāca sa eṣo 'gnirarko yatpuruṣaḥ sa yo haitamevamagnimarkaṃ puruṣamupāsteyamahamagnirarko 'smīti vidyayā haivāsyaiṣa ātmannagnirarkaścito bhavati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-4-5)
Arka means the Puruṣa. The arka-leaves are the Puruṣa's ears; the arka-flowers are the eyes; the arka-capsules are the nostrils; the arka-receptacle means the lips; the arka-grains are the teeth; the arka-stick is the tongue; the arka-root is food; the Puruṣa set forth by this arka is the sacrificial fire. Thus, for one who knows the identity of these three, arka, fire and Puruṣa, the sacrificial fire becomes manifest on the sacrificial altar; so the hidden meaning of the word arka is told. Explaining again that this arka is the Supreme Brahman in the form of the imperishable:
तद्ध्येतत्पश्यन्नृषिरभ्यनूवाद । भूतं भविष्यत्पस्तौमि । महद्ब्रह्मैकमक्षरं बहु ब्रह्मैकमक्षरमित्येतद्द्येवाक्षरग्ं सर्वे देवाः सर्वाणि भूतान्यभि संपद्यंते तदेतद्ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं जाग्निरेव ब्रह्मेंद्रः क्षत्रमिंद्राग्नी वै विश्वे देवा विडु विश्वे देवास्तदेतद्ब्रह्म क्षत्रं विट् ॥ (*taddhyetatpaśyannṛṣirabhyanūvāda | bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyatpastaumi | mahadbrahmaikamakṣaraṃ bahu brahmaikamakṣaramityetaddyevākṣaragṃ sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānyabhi saṃpadyaṃte tadetadbrahma ca kṣatraṃ jāgnireva brahmeṃdraḥ kṣatramiṃdrāgnī vai viśve devā viḍu viśve devāstadetadbrahma kṣatraṃ viṭ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-4-1-9)

### Printed p. 419
The Supreme Brahman, which reflects past, future and present and is all-pervading, is this arka. All the deities are contained in this Supreme Brahman, which is of the form of arka and of the imperishable. It alone reflects both Brahmanical power and Kṣatriya power. All the deities are contained in it. The principle which the seer set forth as such is this arka principle; so it is said. And:
स एष एवार्कः । योऽयमग्निश्चितस्तस्यैतदन्नं क्यमेष सौम्योऽध्वरस्तदर्क्र्य०..................सहोदक्रामदेष चंद्रमाः ॥ (*sa eṣa evārkaḥ | yo 'yamagniścitastasyaitadannaṃ kyameṣa saumyo 'dhvarastadarkrya0..................sahodakrāmadeṣa caṃdramāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-4-1-21)
Arka is this sacrificial altar. The Ka principle, that is, the Soma sacrifice, is its food. The harmony of these two becomes arkya.
स एष एवार्को य एष तपति । तस्यैतदन्नं क्यमेष चंद्रमास्तदर्यं यजुष्ट एष एव महान्............ ॥ इत्यधिदैवतं । (*sa eṣa evārko ya eṣa tapati | tasyaitadannaṃ kyameṣa caṃdramāstadaryaṃ yajuṣṭa eṣa eva mahān............ ‖ ityadhidaivataṃ |*) (Śa. Brā. 10-4-1-22)
The Āditya blazing in the atmosphere is arka; the moon is its food; the harmony of the two becomes arkya. This is the adhidaivata view.
अथाध्यात्मं । प्राणो वा आर्कस्तस्यान्नमेव क्यं............ ॥ (*athādhyātmaṃ | prāṇo vā ārkastasyānnameva kyaṃ............ ‖*)
Breath is arka; the Ka principle is its food; the harmony of this becomes arkya. Thus the arka principle is explained both in the adhidaivata and in the adhyātma view.

सानुषक् (*sānuṣak*)—सानुषंगः सातत्यं । (*sānuṣaṃgaḥ sātatyaṃ |*) It means "continuously threaded"; the purport is that Indra and the mantras of the form of arka have an unbroken connection.

वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—बलेषु; अन्नेषु वा । (*baleṣu; anneṣu vā |*) Two kinds of meaning are given: on account of strength, or on account of food. The word vāja is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9;) and also among the names of battle (3-9). The word is also used in the sense of praise. It also means the most excellent strength. Its special meanings and particular usages have been explained earlier.

##### Grammar

- अवः—अव रक्षणे । धातुः । नांदसवागि लज् । मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । पादादियल्लिरुवुदरिंद निघातस्वरः न भवति । आडागम उदात्तवादुरिंद आद्युदात्तः भवति ।
- द्विबर्हसः—बृह बृहि वृद्धौ । धातुः । द्वयोः स्थानयोः बर्हते प्रवर्धते इति द्विबर्हाः । तस्य । औणादिक असुन् प्रत्ययः । गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-४९) इति । कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । कर्मार्थे षष्ठी आगता ।
- सानुषक्—षंज संगे । धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । अनिदितां हलउ इति उपधानकारस्य लोपः । पदांत जकारस्य कुत्वं । चर्त्वं । कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- असत्—अस भुवि । धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । प्रत्ययस्य इकारस्य लोपे प्राप्ते अडागमः । यद्योगात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । प्रत्ययः पित्तात् अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- अजौ—अज गतिक्षेपणयोः धातुः । अज्यतिभ्यां चॆ (उ सू. ४-५७०) इति इण् प्रत्ययः । अतउपधायाः इति उपधावृद्धिः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । सप्तम्येकवचनांतरूपं ।

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॒ पूर्वे॑भ्यो जरि॒तृभ्य॑ इंद्र॒ मय॑ इ॒वापो॒ न तृष्ण॑ते ब॒भूथ॑  
> तामनु॑ त्वा नि॒विदं॑ जोहवीमि वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । पूर्वेभ्यः । जरितृभ्यः । इंद्र । मयःइव । आपः । न । तृष्यते । बभूथ ।  
> शां । अनु । त्वा । निविदं । जोहवीमि । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरदानुं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पूर्वभ्यो जरितृभ्यः पुरातनेभ्यो गरितृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो मय इव
> बभूथ । मयः सुखं । सुखस्वरूपमिवाभवः । तद्वत् स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं सुखो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, to the ancient praisers (पूर्वभ्यो जरितृभ्यः (*pūrvabhyo jaritṛbhyaḥ*), glossed पुरातनेभ्यो गरितृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो (*purātanebhyo garitṛbhyaḥ stotṛbhyo*)) you were as मय इव (*maya iva*); मयः सुखं (*mayaḥ sukhaṃ*), "you became as if of the nature of happiness". Likewise to us, the praisers, you are happiness…. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 421

> भव । तत्र दृष्टांतः । तृष्यत आपो न तृषार्तस्योदकानि यथा सुखकराणीति तद्वत् ।
> तस्मात्तां निविदं त्वत्प्रीतिकरीं प्रसिद्धां स्तुतिं त्वा तुभ्यमनु जोहवीमि । पुनः पुनः
> करोमि । यद्वा । तां निविदमनु ॥ तृतीयार्थे । पा १-४-८५ । इत्यनोः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं ॥ तया स्तुत्या त्वां जोहवीमि । पुनःपुनराह्वयामि । विद्यामेति व्याख्यातं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his comment on the verse. O Indra, you have been like मयः (*mayaḥ*), that is, happiness itself, to the ancient praisers (जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*), the old reciters of praise). The illustration is तृष्यत आपो न (*tṛṣyata āpo na*): as waters are pleasing to one who is parched with thirst. So the speaker addresses to you that well-known praise (निविदं (*nividaṃ*)), which gives you delight, and he does so again and again (जोहवीमि (*johavīmi*)). Alternatively, तां निविदमनु (*tāṃ nividamanu*) has अनु (*anu*) in the sense of the instrumental, as a karmapravacanīya (Pā. 1-4-85); then the meaning is "with that praise I call you again and again". विद्याम (*vidyāma*) has already been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पूर्वेभ्यः (*pūrvebhyaḥ*)—to the ancient
- जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)—praisers
- तृष्यते (*tṛṣyate*)—to one who is thirsty
- आपः न (*āpaḥ na*)—as waters become satisfying
- मयः इव (*mayaḥ iva*)—like happiness itself
- यथा (*yathā*)—as
- बभूथ (*babhūtha*)—you have been (so be to us also a giver of happiness)
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that well-known
- निविदं अनु (*nividaṃ anu*)—following (your) praise
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- जोहवीमि (*johavīmi*)—I call again and again
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—strength
- जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*)—long life
- विद्याम (*vidyāma*)—may we obtain (by your grace)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as you were a bringer of happiness to the ancient praisers, as waters give satisfaction to one parched with thirst, so be a giver of happiness to us also. I too praise you again and again with your well-known words of praise; grant us food, strength and long life.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Inasmuch, Indra, as you have been the (giver of) happiness to your ancient encomiasts, like water to one who is thirsty, therefore I constantly repeat this your praise, that I may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Having described the joy that Indra produces in the praisers, the verse compares the satisfaction arising from that joy to the satisfaction that those who are thirsty obtain by drinking water. The seer of this sūkta too resolves that he will praise Indra, such a giver of satisfaction, with निविद् (*nivid*) mantras, as the earlier praisers did.

निविदं जोहवीमि (*nividaṃ johavīmi*): he resolves, "I recite the nivid mantras". Earlier, in giving the special topics of Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-2, the importance of the nivid mantras, as indicated by the mantra स पूर्वया निविदा (*sa pūrvayā nividā*), was explained (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 8, pp. 74-76). But that mantra was addressed to Agni, and the nivid mantras indicated there are addressed to Agni; so in that context only the mantras having Agni as deity were described.

### Printed p. 422

Since the present verse is addressed to Indra, the power and the uses of the nivid mantras are explained here in the manner suited to this context.

The name nivid mantra is well known for mantras that address a deity, or a group of deities, describe their extraordinary qualities and invoke them. The Bṛhaddevatā says this:

कर्मैव तावत्सावित्र्यां निविदि स्तौति कर्मणा । यद्धेनुः सप्त्यनड्वाहौ वोळ्हा दोग्धाशुरेव वा ॥ (*karmaiva tāvatsāvitryāṃ nividi stauti karmaṇā | yaddhenuḥ saptyanaḍvāhau voḷhā dogdhāśureva vā ‖*)
(Bṛhaddevatā 3-50)

Just as the particular nature of a milch cow and of an ox is understood from their respective epithets, दोग्धि (*dogdhi*) ("she who is milked"), आतु (*ātu*) ("swift-going"), and वोळ्हा (*voḷhā*) ("the bearer of a load"), so through the nivid mantras the personal qualities of each deity can be understood from the description of that deity's own deeds. For example, in the verse

अभि त्वा देव सवितरीशानं वार्याणां । सदावन्भागमीमहे । (*abhi tvā deva savitarīśānaṃ vāryāṇāṃ | sadāvanbhāgamīmahe |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3)

the nivid mantra addressed to the deity Savitṛ shows Savitṛ's distinctive character by describing his extraordinary deed. The greatness of the nivid mantras, and their relation as cause and effect to the creation of the world, is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

प्रजापतिर्वा इदमेक एवाग्र आस सोऽकामयत प्रजायेय भूयन्त्सामिति स तपोऽतप्यत स वाचमयच्छत्स संवत्सरस्य परस्ताद्वाहरद्वादशकृत्तो द्वादशपदा ना एषा निविदेतां वाव तां निविदं व्याहरत्तां सर्वाणि भूतान्यन्वसृज्यंत । (*prajāpatirvā idameka evāgra āsa so 'kāmayata prajāyeya bhūyantsāmiti sa tapo 'tapyata sa vācamayacchatsa saṃvatsarasya parastādvāharadvādaśakṛtto dvādaśapadā nā eṣā nividetāṃ vāva tāṃ nividaṃ vyāharattāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyanvasṛjyaṃta |*)
(Ai. Brā. 10-1)

In the beginning Prajāpati was alone; desiring to create beings and to become many, he practised austerity, observing silence for a year. Then he recited the nivid mantras, which contain twelve great sentences, twelve times, and after that all beings in the world were created. Having thus stated the power of these mantras, the text then states the special character of the mantra at the times of the rites and the order of its use:

गर्भा ना एत उक्तानां यन्निविदस्तद्यत्पुरस्तादुक्थानां प्रातःसवने धीयंते तस्मात्परांचो गर्भा धीयंते परांचः संभवति। यन्मध्यतो मध्यंदिने (*garbhā nā eta uktānāṃ yannividastadyatpurastādukthānāṃ prātaḥsavane dhīyaṃte tasmātparāṃco garbhā dhīyaṃte parāṃcaḥ saṃbhavati| yanmadhyato madhyaṃdine*)

### Printed p. 423

धीयंते तस्मान्मध्यॆ गर्भा धृताः । यदंततस्तृतीयसवने धीयंते तस्मादमुतोऽर्वांचो गर्भाः प्रजायंते प्रजात्यै । प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद । पेशा वा एत उक्तानां यन्निविदस्तद्यत्पुरस्तादुक्थानां प्रातःसवने धीयंते यथैव प्रवणयतः पेशः कुर्यात्तादृक्तद्यन्मध्यतो मध्यंदिने धीयंते यथैव मध्यतः पेशः कुर्यात्तादक्तद्यदंततस्तृतीयसवने धीयंते यथैवावप्रज्जनतः पेशः कुर्यात्तादृक्तत् । सर्वतो यज्ञस्य पेशसा शोभते य एवं वेद ॥ (*dhīyaṃte tasmānmadhyè garbhā dhṛtāḥ | yadaṃtatastṛtīyasavane dhīyaṃte tasmādamuto 'rvāṃco garbhāḥ prajāyaṃte prajātyai | prajāyate prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda | peśā vā eta uktānāṃ yannividastadyatpurastādukthānāṃ prātaḥsavane dhīyaṃte yathaiva pravaṇayataḥ peśaḥ kuryāttādṛktadyanmadhyato madhyaṃdine dhīyaṃte yathaiva madhyataḥ peśaḥ kuryāttādaktadyadaṃtatastṛtīyasavane dhīyaṃte yathaivāvaprajjanataḥ peśaḥ kuryāttādṛktat | sarvato yajñasya peśasā śobhate ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 11-10)

The nivid mantras are in the form of an embryo (गर्भ (*garbha*)) for the उक्त (*ukta*)s. That is, at the morning libation they are recited before the उक्त (*ukta*)s. For that very reason embryos too are begun with the head turned away. At the midday libation these mantras are recited in the middle; for that very reason embryos too are held in the middle. At the third libation the nivid mantras are recited at the rear, so the child in the womb is born downwards. One who knows these truths is endowed with wealth of offspring and wealth of cattle. The nivid mantras are in the form of ornaments for the उक्त (*ukta*)s and increase their beauty and brilliance. The mantras recited at the morning libation are like ornaments of the upper part, those at the midday time like ornaments of the middle region, and those of the third libation like ornaments of the lower part; they produce adornment. One who knows this adorns the sacrifice and shines himself. And further:

सौर्या वा एता देवता यन्निविदस्तद्यत्पुरस्तादुक्थानां प्रातःसवने धीयंते मध्यतो मध्यंदिने ततस्तृतीयसवन आदित्यस्यैव तद्व्रतमनु पर्यावर्तंते । पच्चो वै देवा यज्ञं समभरंस्तस्मात्पच्चो निविदः शस्यंते । यद्वै तद्देवा यज्ञं समभरंस्तस्मादश्वः समभवत्तस्मादाहुरश्वं निविदां शंस्रे दद्यादिति तदु खलु वरमेव ददति । न निविदः पदमतीयाद्यद्यन्निदवः पदमतीयाद्यज्ञस्य तच्छिद्रं कुर्याद्यज्ञस्य वै छिद्रं स्रवद्यजमानोऽनु पापीयान् भवति तस्मान्न निविदः पदमतीयात् । न निविदः पदे विपरिहरेद्यन्निविदः पदे विपरिहरेन्मोहयेद्यज्ञं मुग्धो यजमानः स्यात्तस्मान्न निविदः पदे विपरिहरेत् । न निविदः पदे समस्येद्यन्निविदः पदे समस्येद्यज्ञस्य तदायुः संहरेत्प्रमायुको यजमानः स्यात्तस्मान्न निविदः पदे समस्येत् । प्रेदं ब्रह्म प्रेदं क्षत्रमित्येते एव समस्यॆद्रह्मक्षत्रयोः संतित्यै तस्माद्ब्रह्म चक्षत्रं च संश्रिते । न तृचं न चतुर्ऋचमतिमन्येत निविद्वानमेकैकं वै निविदः पदमृचं सूक्तं प्रति त (*sauryā vā etā devatā yannividastadyatpurastādukthānāṃ prātaḥsavane dhīyaṃte madhyato madhyaṃdine tatastṛtīyasavana ādityasyaiva tadvratamanu paryāvartaṃte | pacco vai devā yajñaṃ samabharaṃstasmātpacco nividaḥ śasyaṃte | yadvai taddevā yajñaṃ samabharaṃstasmādaśvaḥ samabhavattasmādāhuraśvaṃ nividāṃ śaṃsre dadyāditi tadu khalu varameva dadati | na nividaḥ padamatīyādyadyannidavaḥ padamatīyādyajñasya tacchidraṃ kuryādyajñasya vai chidraṃ sravadyajamāno 'nu pāpīyān bhavati tasmānna nividaḥ padamatīyāt | na nividaḥ pade vipariharedyannividaḥ pade vipariharenmohayedyajñaṃ mugdho yajamānaḥ syāttasmānna nividaḥ pade vipariharet | na nividaḥ pade samasyedyannividaḥ pade samasyedyajñasya tadāyuḥ saṃharetpramāyuko yajamānaḥ syāttasmānna nividaḥ pade samasyet | predaṃ brahma predaṃ kṣatramityete eva samasyèdrahmakṣatrayoḥ saṃtityai tasmādbrahma cakṣatraṃ ca saṃśrite | na tṛcaṃ na caturṛcamatimanyeta nividvānamekaikaṃ vai nividaḥ padamṛcaṃ sūktaṃ prati ta*)

### Printed p. 424

तस्मान्न तृचं न चतुर्यचमतिमन्येत निविद्धानं निविदा ह्येव स्तोत्रमतिशस्तं भवति । (*tasmānna tṛcaṃ na caturyacamatimanyeta nividdhānaṃ nividā hyeva stotramatiśastaṃ bhavati |*)
(Ai. Brā. 11-11)

The nivid deities are all deities related to the sun. The mantras of the morning libation, the midday libation and the third libation follow the course of the sun from rising to setting. The gods gathered the sacrifice by means of limits consisting of पाद (*pāda*)s (metrical quarters); for that very reason the nivid mantras are in the form of sentences made of such pādas. As a result of the gods' gathering all the portions of the sacrifice together, the horse came into being; for that very reason there is a rule that a horse is to be given to the priest who recites these mantras. In the nivid mantras one must not pass beyond any word and go ahead. If any word is not recited, it is as though the sacrifice itself had been made defective; it brings harm to the sacrificer. Two sentences of these mantras must not be joined together, nor must the preceding one be joined to the following, or the following to the preceding, in recitation. If that is done, uncertainty arises in the sacrificial act itself, and the sacrificer too becomes bewildered. If two sentences are joined together, contraction arises in the sacrificial rite itself; thereby the sacrificer's life too is contracted and he may meet death. Therefore one must not mix the sentences and so cause contraction in the pronunciation of the mantra. Only the pair of mantras प्रेदं ब्रह्म (*predaṃ brahma*) and प्रेदं क्षत्रं (*predaṃ kṣatraṃ*), which are sacred and of divine nature, may be mixed. For that very reason the brahmanical radiance and the kṣatriya radiance are the ones to be mixed. The nivid mantras should be included within three or four mantras; they must not be sold. **NOTE** By the nivid alone the recitation of the praise-hymn is extended.

एकां परिशिष्य तृतीयसवने निविदं दध्यात् । यद्वे परिशिष्य दध्यात्पृजननं तदुपहन्याद्दर्भैस्तत्प्राजा व्यर्धयेत्तस्मादेकामेव परिशिष्य तृतीयसवने निविदं दध्यात् । न सूक्तेन निविदमतिपद्येत; येन सूक्तेन निविदमति पद्येत न तत्पुनरुपनिवर्तेत वास्तुहमेव तत् । अन्यत्तद्दैवतं तच्छंदसं सूक्तमाहृत्य तस्मिन्निविदं दध्यात् । मा प्र गाम पथो वयमिति पुरस्तातूक्तस्य शंसति । पथो वा एष प्रैति यो यज्ञे मुह्यति मा यज्ञादिंद्र सोमिन इति यज्ञादेव तन्न प्रच्यवते । मांतस्सुर्नो अरातय इत्यरातीयत एव तदपहंति । यो यज्ञस्य प्रसाधनस्तंतुर्देवेष्वाततः । तमाहुतं नशीमहीति । प्रजा वै तंतुः प्रजामेवास्मा एतत्संतनोति । मनो न्याहुवामहे नाराशंसेन सोमेनेति । मनसा वै यज्ञ स्वायते मनसा क्रियते । सैव तत्र पायश्चित्तिः प्रायश्चित्तिः ॥ (*ekāṃ pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt | yadve pariśiṣya dadhyātpṛjananaṃ tadupahanyāddarbhaistatprājā vyardhayettasmādekāmeva pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt | na sūktena nividamatipadyeta; yena sūktena nividamati padyeta na tatpunarupanivarteta vāstuhameva tat | anyattaddaivataṃ tacchaṃdasaṃ sūktamāhṛtya tasminnividaṃ dadhyāt | mā pra gāma patho vayamiti purastātūktasya śaṃsati | patho vā eṣa praiti yo yajñe muhyati mā yajñādiṃdra somina iti yajñādeva tanna pracyavate | māṃtassurno arātaya ityarātīyata eva tadapahaṃti | yo yajñasya prasādhanastaṃturdeveṣvātataḥ | tamāhutaṃ naśīmahīti | prajā vai taṃtuḥ prajāmevāsmā etatsaṃtanoti | mano nyāhuvāmahe nārāśaṃsena someneti | manasā vai yajña svāyate manasā kriyate | saiva tatra pāyaścittiḥ prāyaścittiḥ ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 11-11)

### Printed p. 425

At the third libation the nivid is to be inserted leaving out one Ṛk. But if it is inserted leaving out two Ṛks, then impotence arises, and then childlessness occurs. Therefore it is to be inserted leaving out one only; then the sacrificial act becomes complete. It must not be inserted leaving out two; if that is done, the power of procreation is destroyed, the power of conceiving goes, and people become childless. In a sūkta that is fit to take a nivid, that sūkta must not be recited without inserting the nivid mantras. Once it has been recited, it is no longer fit for insertion again. If such an omission occurs, another sūkta having the same deity and the same metre is to be chosen and these nivid mantras inserted in it. At such a time, with

मा प्र गाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिंद्र सोमिनः । मांतः स्फुर्नो आरातयः ॥ (*mā pra gāma patho vayaṃ mā yajñādiṃdra sominaḥ | māṃtaḥ sphurno ārātayaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-1)

one first prays, "May we not go astray from the path; may we not be cast out from the sacrificial act; may evil powers not assail us", and afterwards recites that sūkta together with the nivid mantras. Then, without any kind of confusion, the sacrificial work proceeds without hindrance and the evil powers too are destroyed. The sacrificer recites, "May that thread, the fruit of the sacrifice, which is spread out among the gods, extend among us, the sacrificers also" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-2). The thread is the continuance of offspring; to the sacrificer this thread, in the form of offspring, comes in succession.

तद्यदेतां पुरस्तात् सूक्तस्य निविदं दधाति प्रजात्यै । प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद ॥ (*tadyadetāṃ purastāt sūktasya nividaṃ dadhāti prajātyai | prajāyate prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 10-2)

For this reason the hotṛ, by reciting the nivid mantra at the beginning of the sūkta, obtains offspring. To sacrificers who have such knowledge, all wealth, beginning with good offspring, accrues; so it is said elsewhere too. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā it is seen in many places that it is traditional, in the faith that the recitation of mantras gives the most excellent fruit, to praise, when invoking the several deities, the nature, power, great deeds and so on of each deity and so to recite these. For example:

तान्नूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्त्रिधं । (*tānnūrvayā nividā hūmahe vayaṃ bhagaṃ mitramaditiṃ dakṣamastridhaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-3)

जुषेथां यज्ञं बोधतं हवस्य मे सत्तो होता निविदः पूर्व्या अनु । (*juṣethāṃ yajñaṃ bodhataṃ havasya me satto hotā nividaḥ pūrvyā anu |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-6)

### Printed p. 426

किमु ष्विदस्मै निविदो भनंतेंद्रस्यावद्यं दिथिषंत आहः (*kimu ṣvidasmai nivido bhanaṃteṃdrasyāvadyaṃ dithiṣaṃta āhaḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-18-7)

वि यद्वाचं कीस्तासो भरंते तंसंति के चिन्निविदो मनानाः । (*vi yadvācaṃ kīstāso bharaṃte taṃsaṃti ke cinnivido manānāḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-67-10)

In these and similar contexts the greatness of the nivid mantras is praised.

In the present verse (1-176-6) the nivid mantra addressed to Indra is indicated by the sentence तामनु त्वा निविदं जोहवीमि (*tāmanu tvā nividaṃ johavīmi*). There is some difference of opinion in determining which is the sūkta provided with nivids addressed to the deity Indra. For example:

जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुरायेति निविद्धानमैकाहिकं (*janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāyeti nividdhānamaikāhikaṃ*)
(I. Ā. 1-2-2) **NOTE**

The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says that Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 10-73, beginning with the Ṛk जनिष्ठा उग्रः (*janiṣṭhā ugraḥ*), is provided with nivid mantras. But in the Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka (1-3) it is said that Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 6-9, beginning with the Ṛk महा इंद्रो नृवदा (*mahā iṃdro nṛvadā*), is provided with these mantras. In the present verse the seer of the sūkta has declared his resolve: "I shall praise Indra with nivid mantras that extol Indra's nature, valour and distinctive character."

##### Grammar

- जरितृभ्यः—ज्यष् वयोहानौ धातुः । अत्र स्तुत्यर्थे प्रयुक्तः । कर्तरि तृच् प्रत्ययः । इडागमः । प्रत्ययनिमित्तेन धातोः ऋकारस्य गुणः । चित्तात् अंतोदात्तस्वरः आगच्छति । चतुर्थीबहुवचनांतरूपं ।
- तृष्यते—इतृषा पिपासायां धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । दिवादिभ्यः क्यन् (पा. सू. ३.१-६९) इति श्यन् विकरणं । तास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इति शतृ अनुदात्तः भवति । विकरणस्य नित्तात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः आगच्छति । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपं ।
- बभूथ—भू सत्तायां धातुः । लिट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचने बभूथ ततंथ—(पा. सू. ७-२-६४) इति इडभावेन निपातितं । निपात्र्यद्यदि—(पा. सू. ८-१-३०) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधः भवति । थल् लित्तात् लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति प्रत्ययस्य पूर्वस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- जोहवीमि—हु दानादनयोः धातुः यज्लुगंतात् परं लट् । उत्तमपुरुष एकवचने मिप् । यजो वा (पा. सू. ७-३-९४) इति मिपः ईडागमः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति । ॥ ६ ॥

Here ends the one hundred and seventy-sixth sūkta.

### Printed p. 427
## Sūkta 177 (Maṇḍala 1)

The Sūkta "आ चर्षणिप्राः (*ā carṣaṇiprāḥ*)" has five Ṛks. It is the thirteenth Sūkta, and its seer is Agastya. Its deity is Indra, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says "Ā carṣaṇiprāḥ pañca". It has a special use in the Hotṛka Śastras for the increase of the Stoma, as is stated by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: ऐंद्राणि त्रैष्टुभान्यमरुच्छब्दान्यावपेरन् (*aiṃdrāṇi traiṣṭubhānyamarucchabdānyāvaperan*) (Ā. Sū. 7-12).

Anuvāda: this Sūkta, "आ चर्षणिप्राः (*ā carṣaṇiprāḥ*)", is the thirteenth Sūkta in the twenty-third Anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Agastya, its deity is Indra, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā begins with "Ā carṣaṇiprāḥ pañca". When the priests of the Hotṛ group recite Śastra mantras for the increase of the Stoma, this Sūkta has a special use. It is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra ऐंद्राणि त्रैष्टुभान्यमरुच्छब्दान्यावपेरन् (*aiṃdrāṇi traiṣṭubhānyamarucchabdānyāvaperan*) (Ā. 7-12).

Sūkta 177. Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 23; Sūkta 177. Aṣṭaka 2; Adhyāya 4; Varga 20. Number of Ṛks in the Sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Agastya. Devatā: Indra. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ च॑र्षणि॒प्रा वृ॑ष॒भो जना॑नां॒ राजा॑ कृष्णी॒नां पु॑रुहू॒त इंद्रः॑ ।  
> स्तु॒तः श्र॑व॒स्यन्न व॒सोप॑ म॒द्रिग्यु॒क्त्वा हरी॒ वृष॒णा या॑ह्य॒र्वाज् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । चर्षणिप्राः । वृषभः। जनानां । राजा । कृष्णीनां। पुरुहूतः । इंद्रः ।  
> स्तुतः । श्रवस्यन् । अवसा । उपॆ । मद्रिक् । युक्ता । हरी इति । वृषणा । आ । याहि ।  
> अर्वाज् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रश्चर्षणिप्राः । चर्षणयो मनुष्याः । तेषां धनादिना प्रीणयिता । जनानां सर्वॆषां वृषभः कामानां वर्षिता । तथा कृष्णीनां । मनुष्यनामैतत् । मनुष्याणां राजा स्वामी पुरुहूतो बहुभिराहूतः । ईदृत इंद्रोS
> स्मानाजानात्वागच्छतु ना । उत्तरार्धः परोक्षवादः । हे इंड्र स्तुत्योऽस्माभिः
> श्रवस्यन् हविर्लक्षणान्नमिच्छन्नवसास्मद्रक्षणेन तर्पणेन वा युक्तः सन्मद्रिङ्मदभिमुखमंचन् वृषणा वर्षकौ युवानौ हरी अश्वा युक्ता रथे योजयित्वार्वाजिस्मदभिमुखमा याहि । आगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra is चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*). The चर्षणयो (*carṣaṇayo*) are men, and he gratifies them with wealth and the like. He is the वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*) of all people, the showerer of desires. कृष्णीनां (*kṛṣṇīnāṃ*) is a name for men, and he is the king, the lord, of men. He is पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*), called by many. May such an Indra come to us. The latter half is in the third person (परोक्षवादः (*parokṣavādaḥ*)). O Indra, praised by us, desiring the food that is the oblation, and joined with अवसा (*avasā*), our protection or satisfaction, turn towards us. Yoke to the chariot your two vigorous young steeds, the हरी (*harī*), which shower. Then come towards us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*)—he who pleases men (with wealth and the like)
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of all people
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desires
- कृष्णीनां (*kṛṣṇīnāṃ*)—of men
- राजा (*rājā*)—the lord
- पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*)—called by many (in many ways)
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- आ (*ā*)—may he come (may he take notice of us)
- (हे इंद्र (*he iṃdra*)—O Indra)
- स्तुतः (*stutaḥ*)—praised by us
- श्रवस्यन् (*śravasyan*)—desiring the food that is the oblation
- अवसा (*avasā*)—with our protection (joined with satisfaction)
- मद्रिक् (*madrik*)—setting out to face us
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—the young
- हरी (*harī*)—(your) two horses
- युक्ता (*yuktā*)—harnessing (to the chariot)
- अर्वाज् (*arvāj*)—towards us
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you gratify men with wealth and the like. You grant men what they desire, you are the lord of the whole human race, and you are called by many. Praised by us, accept the oblation-food that we offer. For the sake of protecting us, harness to the chariot your horses that are in their youth, set out towards us, and come.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May Indra, who is the cherisher of men, the benefactor of menkind, the lord of men, the adored of many, (come to us). Indra, you who are praised (by us), and are desirous of the oblation, harness your vigorous steeds, and come down to me for (my) preservation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Indra's wealth and generosity are described and his coming towards the sacrificial rite is prayed for. In describing his wealth and lordship the epithets चर्षणिप्रा (*carṣaṇiprā*), वृषभो जननां (*vṛṣabho jananāṃ*) and राजा कृष्टीनां (*rājā kṛṣṭīnāṃ*) are noteworthy. Here
### Printed p. 429
the three words चर्षणि (*carṣaṇi*), जन (*jana*) and कृष्ण (*kṛṣṇa*) are all synonyms for man. But since they are used in different expressions, they should be understood as epithets that show variety in the nature and in the occupation of man.

The word चर्षणि (*carṣaṇi*) is probably used only in the plural. Its derivation and variety of meaning were given earlier under the special topics of the 2nd Ṛk of Sūkta 176. It is formed either from the root चर् (*car*) meaning "to move about", or from the root कृष् (*kṛṣ*) meaning "to cultivate". Although the original meaning is thus, in many places where this word is used Sāyaṇa has explained it as "men endowed with the vision of knowledge". It was also stated earlier that the word is used as an epithet not only of men but also of deities such as Indra who possess extraordinary knowledge. The epithets राजाचर्षणीनां (*rājācarṣaṇīnāṃ*) and चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*) too are used mostly of Indra and Agni (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-10-1; 5-39-4, etc.). The purport is that Indra is the protector of men who are wise, who are seers of Sūktas and who perform sacrifices. The word कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) also has the general meaning "men". The Nirukta-author, explaining the Ṛk
आ दधिक्राः शवसा पंच कृष्टीः सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान । (*ā dadhikrāḥ śavasā paṃca kṛṣṭīḥ sūrya iva jyotiṣāpastatāna |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-38-10)
has explained the phrase पंच कृष्णी (*paṃca kṛṣṇī*) in it as पंच जनान् (*paṃca janān*) (Ni. 10-31), thus including all human beings. About this word the scholar Keith gives the following explanation.

कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) denotes 'people' in general from the Rig-Veda onwards. Its common and regular use in this sense appears to show that the Aryans, when they invaded India, were already Agriculturists, though the employment of the words reffering to ploughing men- tioned under कृषि (*kṛṣi*) indicates that not all of the people devoted themselves equally to that occupation. Indra and Agni are Par exellence the lords of men. the word (कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*)) Sometimes is further defined by the addition of an adjective meaning "belonging to mankind" (मानुषीः (*mānuṣīḥ*) :मानवीः (*mānavīḥ*))
[Vedic Index of Names and Subjects. By Keith anc Maedoneth [Vol. I. P. 183.]

From the above explanation it is indicated that, since they were engaged in occupations such as agriculture, the word कृष्ण (*kṛṣṇa*) shows the way of life of the Āryas.
### Printed p. 430
In Ṛks such as
स युध्मः सत्वा खजकृत्समद्वा तुविम्रक्षो नदनुमा ऋजीषी । बृहद्रेणुश्चवनो मानुषीणामेकः कृष्णीनामभवत्सहावा ॥ (*sa yudhmaḥ satvā khajakṛtsamadvā tuvimrakṣo nadanumā ṛjīṣī | bṛhadreṇuścavano mānuṣīṇāmekaḥ kṛṣṇīnāmabhavatsahāvā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-2)
the expression is used with the qualifying phrase मानुषीणां कृष्णीनां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ kṛṣṇīnāṃ*). Just as the words चर्षणि (*carṣaṇi*) and कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) are synonyms of human subjects, so in such contexts the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*), which gives the meaning "those who have a dwelling, those who are settled", is also used. It is read among the names of man, मनुष्याः नरः (*manuṣyāḥ naraḥ*) and so on (Ni. 3-7).

Indra is described by his extraordinary and universally dear qualities: he is the protector of the people who perform sacrifices, their master, the lord who guards them all. For that very reason the epithet पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*)—बहुभिराहूतः (*bahubhirāhūtaḥ*), "one called by many"—is given. The prayer is that such an Indra may come towards our sacrifice.

श्रवस्यन् (*śravasyan*)—हविर्लक्षणमन्नमिच्छन् (*havirlakṣaṇamannamicchan*), "desiring food in the form of the oblation": this also states Indra's wish. The word श्रवस् (*śravas*) can have two meanings, food or fame. The Nirukta-author, in explaining the Ṛk
आसस्राणासः शवसानमच्छेंद्रं सुचक्रे रथ्यासो अश्वाः । अभि श्रव ऋज्यंतो वहेयुर्नू चिन्नु वायोरमृतं वि दस्येत् ॥ (*āsasrāṇāsaḥ śavasānamaccheṃdraṃ sucakre rathyāso aśvāḥ | abhi śrava ṛjyaṃto vaheyurnū cinnu vāyoramṛtaṃ vi dasyet ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-37-3)
explains the word श्रव (*śrava*) as श्रव इत्यन्ननाम श्रूयत इति सुतः (*śrava ityannanāma śrūyata iti sutaḥ*). Because it is famous everywhere (heard of by all), the word श्रव (*śrava*), formed from the root श्रु (*śru*), means food (Ni. 10-3). And in
इंद्रस्य यस्य सुमखं सहो महि श्रवो नृण्मं च रोदसी सपर्यतः । (*iṃdrasya yasya sumakhaṃ saho mahi śravo nṛṇmaṃ ca rodasī saparyataḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-50-1)
he explains it as श्रवणीयं यशः (*śravaṇīyaṃ yaśaḥ*), that is, fame heard of by all, famous everywhere (Ni. 11-9). Since food brings fame, it may also be explained as food that is the means to fame. As authority for this,
बृहत्या श्रीकामो यशस्वामः कुर्वीत। श्रीर्वैयशश्चंदसां बृहती। श्रियमेव यश आत्मन्धत्ते ॥ (*bṛhatyā śrīkāmo yaśasvāmaḥ kurvīta| śrīrvaiyaśaścaṃdasāṃ bṛhatī| śriyameva yaśa ātmandhatte ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 1-5)
### Printed p. 431
here the identity of श्री (*śrī*), which is wealth in the form of riches and grain, with the fame obtained through it is stated. Wealth such as food is the basis of fame, and where wealth such as food exists, fame comes of itself. So both meanings are possible for the word श्रव (*śrava*). In the present Ṛk it may be explained as the food in the form of the oblation, which is the means to the fame of the sacrificer.

##### Grammar

- चर्षणि प्राः — प्रा पूरणे धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- वृषभः — वृषु सेचने धातुः । औणादिकः अभच् प्रत्ययः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- कृष्णीनाम् — षष्ठीबहुवचनांतरूपम् । नामन्यतरस्याम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१७७) इति नाम उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- श्रवस्यन् — श्रवः अन्नं आत्मनः इच्छन् श्रवस्यन् । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (पा. सू. ३-१-८) इति क्यच् । क्यजंतात् लटि शत्रादेशः । प्रथमाएकवचनांतरूपम् । क्यच्स्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- मद्रिक् — अंचु गतिपूजनयोः धातुः । पृषोदरादीनि यथोपदिष्टम् इति अभिमतरूपं सिद्ध्यति ।
- युक्त्वा — युजिर् योगे धातुः । प्रेरणस्य दर्शनात् अंतर्भावितण्यर्थको धातुः । समानकर्तृकयोः (पा. सू. ३-४-२१) इति क्त्वा प्रत्ययः । चोः कुः इति धातुजकारस्य कुत्वम् । चर्त्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- याहि — या प्रापणे धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये ते॒ वृष॑णो वृष॒भास॑ इंद्र ब्रह्म॒युजो॒ वृष॑रथासो॒ अत्याः॑ ।  
> ता आ ति॑ष्ठ॒ तेभि॒रा या॑ह्य॒र्वाज् हवा॑महे त्वा सु॒त इं॑द्र॒ सोमे॑ ॥

> तान् । आ । तिष्ठ । तेभिः । आ । याहि । अर्वाज् । हवामहे । त्वा । सुते । इंद्र ।  
> सोमे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव संबंधिनो वृषणो वर्षका युवानो वर्षणवंतो
> वा वृषभासः श्रेष्ठा ब्रह्मयुजः परिवृढेन मंत्रेण युज्यमाना वृषरथासो
> वर्षणरथवंतः । तत्र नियुक्ता इत्यर्थः । ईदृशा अत्या अश्वा ये संति ताना तिष्ठ
> आश्रय । आरोह । तेभिस्तैरर्वाजिस्मदभिमुखमा याहि । आगच्छ । वयं च हे
> इंद्र सोमे सुते सति त्वा त्वां हवामहे । आह्वयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, those horses of yours are वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*), showerers, or young, or possessed of vigour. They are वृषभासः (*vṛṣabhāsaḥ*), excellent, and ब्रह्मयुजः (*brahmayujaḥ*), yoked by the mantra called परिवृढ (*parivṛḍha*). They are वृषरथासः (*vṛṣarathāsaḥ*), possessing a chariot that showers; that is, they are appointed to it. Mount the horses of this kind that you have, and with them come towards us. And we, O Indra, when the Soma has been pressed, invoke you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे (*he*)) इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—showerers (of desires), or those in their prime
- वृषभासः (*vṛṣabhāsaḥ*)—excellent
- ब्रह्मयुजः (*brahmayujaḥ*)—to be yoked by the mantra alone
- वृषरथासः (*vṛṣarathāsaḥ*)—yoked to a chariot that showers what is desired
- ते (*te*)—your
- अत्याः (*atyāḥ*)—horses
- ये (*ye*) (संति (*saṃti*))—which are
- तान् (*tān*)—them
- आ तिष्ठ (*ā tiṣṭha*)—resort to (mount)
- तेभिः (*tebhiḥ*)—joined with them
- अर्वाज् (*arvāj*)—facing (us)
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—come
- (वयं च (*vayaṃ ca*)—and we)
- (हे (*he*)) इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सोमे (*some*)—the Soma juice
- सुते (*sute*) (सति (*sati*))—when it has been pressed
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we invoke

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, mount your excellent horses in their prime, which are yoked to your chariot that showers what is desired and are appointed by the mantra alone, set out towards us, and come. We too, having prepared the Soma juice, call you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Mount, Indra, your steeds, who are young and vigorous, tractable to prayer, and harnessed to a bounty-shedding car : come down with them to us. We invoke you, Indra, the libation being poured out.

### Printed p. 433

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The words वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*), वृषभासः (*vṛṣabhāsaḥ*) and वृषरथासः (*vṛṣarathāsaḥ*) are epithets of Indra's horses, and they show the special capabilities of those horses. The differences of meaning among these words, which are all formed from the word वृषन् (*vṛṣan*), and their usages, will be explained in the Special Topics of the next Ṛk. Only the epithets ब्रह्मयुजः (*brahmayujaḥ*) and अत्याः (*atyāḥ*) are explained here.

ब्रह्मयुजः (*brahmayujaḥ*)—परिवृढेन मंत्रेण युज्यमानाः (*parivṛḍhena maṃtreṇa yujyamānāḥ*). It is an epithet of Indra's horses: "yoked with the utterance of a fully developed mantra". The word ब्रह्म (*brahma*) in this context is formed from the root बृहि (*bṛhi*), which means "to grow", and so means a mantra that has grown. Just as ब्रह्मयुजः (*brahmayujaḥ*) is here an epithet of Indra's horses, the word ब्रह्मवाहः (*brahmavāhaḥ*) is used in many places as an epithet of Indra. In all those places the sense is: ब्रह्मणा मंत्ररूपेण स्तोत्रेणोह्यमान प्राप्यमाणेंद्र (*brahmaṇā maṃtrarūpeṇa stotreṇohyamāna prāpyamāṇeṃdra*)—"O Indra, fit to be attained through praise". Here likewise the meaning is horses yoked by means of praise.

ब्रह्मणा ते ब्रह्मयुजा युनज्मि हरी सखाया सधमाद आ शू । स्थिरं रथं सुखमिंद्राधितिष्ठन्रजानन्विद्वा उप याहि सोमं ॥ (*brahmaṇā te brahmayujā yunajmi harī sakhāyā sadhamāda ā śū | sthiraṃ rathaṃ sukhamiṃdrādhitiṣṭhanrajānanvidvā upa yāhi somaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-35-4). As in such Ṛks, which describe how Indra's horses are yoked to his chariot by the power of the mantra, the present Ṛk also states this point.

अत्याः (*atyāḥ*)—आश्वाः (*āśvāḥ*). Indra's horses. अपेक्षितप्रदेशं प्रति आतनशीलाः (*apekṣitapradeśaṃ prati ātanaśīlāḥ*): that is, having the nature and the power to travel to whatever place one wishes. Not only of the horse: this word is also an epithet of Agni and of Āditya.

एष प्र पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिषोऽत्यो न योषामुदयंस्त भुर्वणिः । दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसं ॥ (*eṣa pra pūrvīrava tasya camriṣo 'tyo na yoṣāmudayaṃsta bhurvaṇiḥ | dakṣaṃ mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayaṃ rathamāvṛtyā hariyogamṛbhvasaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-1): here अत्यः (*atyaḥ*) is a synonym of "horse". In
अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्तो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः । मृगाणां न हेतयो यंति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमाया अभि द्यून् ॥ (*asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyāmatto na yaṃsadyakṣabhṛdvicetāḥ | mṛgāṇāṃ na hetayo yaṃti cemā bṛhaspaterahimāyā abhi dyūn ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-4) and similar Ṛks, आतनशीलः आदित्यः (*ātanaśīlaḥ ādityaḥ*) is understood: the travelling Āditya. In the present Ṛk it is a synonym of "horse".

### Printed p. 434

##### Grammar

- ब्रह्मयुजः — ब्रह्मणा युज्यंते इति ब्रह्मयुजः । युजिर् योगे इति धातुः । सत्सूद्विषश्रुणमुहयुज—(पा. सू. ३-२-६१) इति क्विड् प्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- वृषरथासः — बहुह्रीहिसमासः । बहुह्रीहौ प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदं इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । जस् परे अज्जसेरसुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-५०) इति तस्य असुक् आगमः ।
- शान्+आ — दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. सू. ८-३-९) इति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । आतोटनित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-३-३) इति पूर्वाकारस्य नित्यानुनासिकत्वम् ।
- तिष्ठ — ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ इति धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- हवामहे — ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च इति धातुः । बहुलं छंदसि इति लटि संप्रसारणम् । उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । तास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इति लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवतिष्ठते ।
- सुते — षुञ् अभिषवे इति धातुः । निष्ठा इति क्त प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । सप्तम्यंतरूपम् । **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ ति॑ष्ठ॒ रथं॒ वृष॑णं॒ वृषा॑ ते सु॒तः सोमः॒ परि॑षिक्ता॒ मधू॑नि ।  
> यु॒क्त्वा वृष॑भ्यां वृषभ क्षिती॒नां हरि॑भ्यां याहि प्र॒वतोप॑  ॒
> मद्रिक् ॥ ३ ॥
