> कुर्युः । अतो मां किमित्यवमन्यसे । इदानीमपि वा संभावयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Lopāmudrā speaks. "O Agastya, I, Lopāmudrā, for many ancient, countless years, through nights (दोषा (*doṣā*)), days (वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)) and the dawn-times (उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)) that bring decay to the body, have been wearied by serving you with all my effort. The accusative is used throughout because the time is continuous (*atyaṃtakālasaṃyoge dvitīyā*). Now old age (जरिमा (*jarimā*)) destroys the beauty of my limbs; even so you do not favour me." In अप्यू नु (*apyū nu*), अपि (*api*) is used in the sense of possibility, उ (*u*) in emphasis, नु (*nu*) in doubt: "even now, what is thinkable?" In the world, husbands, the sprinklers (of seed), approach their wives and enjoy them. "Why then do you slight me? Or: think of me even now."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे अगस्त्य (*he agastya*)—O Agastya
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I (Lopāmudrā)
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—ancient
- शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)—of many years
- दोषाः (*doṣāḥ*)—of nights
- वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)—of days
- जरयंती (*jarayaṃtī*)—body-wasting
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—of dawn-times (up to)
- शत्रमाणा (*śatramāṇā*)—(serving you with toil) I am wearied
- जरिमा (*jarimā*)—old age (now)
- तनूनां (*tanūnāṃ*)—of the limbs
- श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*)—the beauty
- मिनाति (*mināti*)—injures (destroys)
- अपि ऊ नु (*api ū nu*)—what, then, am I to do now?
- लोके हि (*loke hi*)—in the world
- पत्निः (*patniḥ*)—wives
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—husbands, the sprinklers of seed
- जगम्युः (*jagamyuḥ*)—approach (for enjoyment)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Lopāmudrā says: O Agastya, for many years now, by day, by night and at the dawn-times, I have worn myself out serving you without rest. Now old age is spoiling the beauty of my limbs; what shall I do? In the world, men approach their wives for enjoyment. (Only you still do not favour me.)

### Printed p. 470

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Lopamudra),—Many years have I been serving you diligently, both day and night, and through mornings, bringing on old age : decay now imqairs the beauty of my limbs : what, therefore, is now (to be done) : let husbands approach their wives.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-179 a conversation between Lopāmudrā and Agastya is described. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā presents the episode thus:
ऋत् स्नातामृषिर्भार्यां लोपामुद्रां यशस्सिनीं । उपजल्पितुमारेभे रहःसंयोगकाम्यया ॥ द्वाभ्यां सा त्वब्रवीदृग्भ्यां पूर्विीरिति चिकीर्षितं । रिरंसुस्तामथागस्त्य उत्तराभ्यामतोषयत् ॥ विविश्वा तपसा सर्वं तयोर्भावं रिरंसतोः । श्रुत्त्वैनः कृतवानस्मि ब्रह्मचार्युत्तमे जगौ ॥ (*ṛt snātāmṛṣirbhāryāṃ lopāmudrāṃ yaśassinīṃ | upajalpitumārebhe rahaḥsaṃyogakāmyayā ‖ dvābhyāṃ sā tvabravīdṛgbhyāṃ pūrviīriti cikīrṣitaṃ | riraṃsustāmathāgastya uttarābhyāmatoṣayat ‖ viviśvā tapasā sarvaṃ tayorbhāvaṃ riraṃsatoḥ | śruttvainaḥ kṛtavānasmi brahmacāryuttame jagau ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 4-57 to 59)
After her ritual bath the sage Agastya, desiring union with his wife Lopāmudrā, began to converse with her. She, too, made known her wish with the two Ṛks पूर्विरहं शरदः (*pūrvirahaṃ śaradaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-179-1) and ये जिद्दि पूर्वे (*ye jiddi pūrve*) (1-179-2). Then Agastya made his own desire known to her with the two Ṛks न मृषा श्रांतं (*na mṛṣā śrāṃtaṃ*) (1-179-3) and नहस्य मा रुधतः (*nahasya mā rudhataḥ*) (1-179-4), and satisfied her. On this occasion Agastya's pupil came to know by his ascetic power the conversation revealing their desire for union. Realising that it was a sin to have heard and understood it, he too recited the two Ṛks इमं नु सोमं (*imaṃ nu somaṃ*) (1-179-5) and अगस्त्यः खनमानः (*agastyaḥ khanamānaḥ*) (1-169-6): so the Bṛhaddevatā relates. **NOTE**
Of the two words दोषाः (*doṣāḥ*) and वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*), दोषाः (*doṣāḥ*) is read among the names of night (Ni. 3-9) and वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*) among the names of day. In explaining these two words the Nirukta author quotes the Ṛk of the Saṃhitā
कुहस्विद्दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः । को वां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥ (*kuhasviddoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karataḥ kuhoṣatuḥ | ko vāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ maryaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-40-2)

### Printed p. 471
and explains दोषा (*doṣā*) as night and वस्तो (*vasto*) as day.
शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)—शरच्छृता अस्यामोषधयो भवंति । शीर्षा आप इति ना । (*śaracchṛtā asyāmoṣadhayo bhavaṃti | śīrṣā āpa iti nā |*) (Ni. 4-25). The name autumn is well known either because plants ripen in this season or because the waters dry up. The word is not only a season; in many places it is used as a synonym of "year". For example, in the verse quoted by the Nirukta author (Ni. 4-25) दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जीनाति शरदः शतं । (*dīrghāyurasyā yaḥ patirjīnāti śaradaḥ śataṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-39), शरदशतं (*śaradaśataṃ*) means a hundred years.
वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—The meanings of words formed from वृषन् (*vṛṣan*) and their occurrences in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā were given earlier (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-77-3). Here it means a man capable of sprinkling.

##### Grammar

- पूर्विः — इदे मॊदलाद नाल्कु शब्देषु कालाध्वनोरत्यंतसंयोगे द्वितीया (पा. सू. २-३-५) इति प्रत्येकं संबंधात् द्वितीया आगता ।
- कश्रमाणाः — श्रमु तपसि खेदे च धातुः । व्यत्ययेन लटः शानचादेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति श्लुविकरणम् । तन्निमित्तं धातोर्द्वित्वादि । अट्कुप्वाङ् इति प्रत्ययनकारस्य णत्वम् । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इत्यनेन अंतोदात्तस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- वस्तोः — वस निवासे धातुः । तुमर्थे तोसुन् प्रत्ययः ।
- जरयंतीः — ज्यष् वयोहानौ धातुः । णिजंतात् शतृप्रत्यये स्त्रीत्वे उगित्त्वात् ङीप् । जनीज्यष्क्नसुरंजोमांताश्च इति मित्संज्ञा भवति, ततो मितां ह्रस्वः (पा. सू. ६-४-९२) इति धातोरुपधाया ह्रस्वः । लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वात् णिच्स्वरः अवशिष्यते । **NOTE**
- मिनाति — मीञ् हिंसायां धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः (पा. सू. ७-३-८०) इति धातोर्ह्रस्वः आगच्छति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । विकरणस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

### Printed p. 472
- जतिमा — ज्यष् वयोहानौ धातुः । भावार्थे औणादिक इमनिच् प्रत्ययः । तन्निमित्तं धातोरिकः गुणः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इत्यनेन अंतोदात्तस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- जगम्युः — गमल्य गतौ धातुः । लिज् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनस्य उसादेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति श्लुकीकरणम् । तन्निमित्तं धातोर्द्वित्वादि । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः आगच्छति ।

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये चि॒द्भि पूर्व॑ ऋत॒साप॒ आस॑न्ता॒कं दे॒वेभि॒रव॑दन्नृ॒तानि॑ ।  
> ते चि॒दवा॑सुर्न॒ह्यंत॑मा॒पुः समू॒ नु पत्नी॒र्वृष॑भिर्जगम्युः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । चित् । हि । पूर्वे । ऋतसापः । आसन् । साकं । देवेभिः । अवदन् । ऋतानि ।  
> ते । चित् । अव । असुः । नहि । अंतं । आपुः । सं । ऊं इति । नु । पत्निः । वृषभिः ।  
> जगम्युः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सा तमेवा ॥
> हे पतेऽगस्त्य ये चिद्दि येऽपि तु पूर्व पुरातना ऋतसापः सत्यस्यापयितारो व्याप्नुवाना महर्षय आसन् ते वेवेभिर्देवैः साकं सहर्तानि सत्यवाक्यान्यवदन् । वदंति । ये महत्तपो यज्ञं वानुतिष्ठंति ये च देववाक्यानि
> देवस्कृतिरुवाणि वदंति ते चित् । चिदस्यर्थे । ते चिदवासुः । अवक्षिपंति रेतः ॥
> स्कृतिरुवसृष्टो विमोचने वर्तते ॥ ते नह्यंतमापुः । न हि ब्रह्मचर्यादेरंतं
> प्राप्नुवन् । ब्रह्मचर्यमनिषिद्धर्तुकालगमनमपि कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः । तथा पत्निः
> पत्नश्च तपस्यमाना वृषभिर्भोगवर्षकैः पतिभिः सह समू न जगम्युः । उ न्विति
> पूरणौ । संगच्छेरन् । अतस्त्वं कथं मां नानुभवसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

She says to him: "O husband Agastya, those ancient great sages (ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*), makers of truth pervade), who conversed truths with the gods (साकं देवेभिः (*sākaṃ devebhiḥ*))—those who practise great austerity or sacrifice and speak the words of the gods—even they discharged seed (अवासुः (*avāsuḥ*), चिद (*cida*) being in the sense of चित् (*cit*); अव (*ava*) …*askṛti* is used of discharge). They did not reach the end of their continence (न हि ब्रह्मचर्यादेरंतं प्राप्नुवन् (*na hi brahmacaryāderaṃtaṃ prāpnuvan*)): that is, they also approached their wives in the permitted season. Likewise wives practising austerity (पत्निः (*patniḥ*)) united with their husbands, the showerers of enjoyment (वृषभिः (*vṛṣabhiḥ*)). उ न्विति (*u nviti*) are expletives. So why do you not enjoy me?" **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे अगस्त्य (*he agastya*)—O Agastya
- ये चित् हि (*ye cit hi*)—which
- पूरै (*pūrai*)—ancient
- ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*)—(performers of sacrifice etc.) the great sages who cause truth to pervade

### Printed p. 473
- आसन् (*āsan*)—were
- ये (*ye*)—who
- देवेभिः साकं (*devebhiḥ sākaṃ*)—with the gods
- ऋतानि (*ṛtāni*)—true words (principles)
- अवदन् (*avadan*)—spoke (discussed)
- ते चित् (*te cit*)—even such great sages
- अवासुः (*avāsuḥ*)—discharged seed
- ते (*te*)—they
- अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*)—the end (of their continence)
- न हि आपुः (*na hi āpuḥ*)—did not reach
- तथा (*tathā*)—likewise
- पत्निः (*patniḥ*)—wives (ascetic)
- वृषभिः (*vṛṣabhiḥ*)—with husbands, showerers of enjoyment
- सं ऊ नु जगम्युः (*saṃ ū nu jagamyuḥ*)—enjoyed union

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agastya, even the ancient great sages, who performed sacrifices and the like and discussed matters of truth with the gods, had union for the begetting of progeny; their continence was not lost thereby. Ascetic women, too, have had union with their husbands. (Yet you alone have not favoured me.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The ancient sages, disseminators of truth, who, verily, conversed of truths with the gods, begot (progeny), nor thereby violated (their vow of continence), therefore should wives be approached by their husbands.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk and the one before it, Lopāmudrā prays to Agastya to fulfil her wish. She tells her husband plainly of her desire, but to show that satisfying it brings no lapse in her own dharma or her husband's, she cites the example of the earlier sages: even great sages could not conquer desire; it is a natural wish of man and must be satisfied. ये चेत् ऋतसापः आसन्, ये देवेभिः साकं ऋतानि अवदन्, ते चित् अवासुः (*ye cet ṛtasāpaḥ āsan, ye devebhiḥ sākaṃ ṛtāni avadan, te cit avāsuḥ*)—those who were ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*), who spoke only true words with the gods, even such ancient seers joined their wives for satisfaction of desire. Thus in this Ṛk Lopāmudrā tells her husband and seeks his company. The meaning of the words ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*) and ऋतानि (*ṛtāni*) must be noted here especially. The word ऋत (*ṛta*) denotes the spiritual-physical principle and the moral rule. The essence of the Vedic view is that gods, men and all must understand the path of ṛta and follow its rule. That even such knowers of principle and keepers of the rule obtained satisfaction of desire is Lopāmudrā's argument—

### Printed p. 474
ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*), ऋतानि (*ṛtāni*)—The Nirukta author has included the word ऋत (*ṛta*) among the names of water (Ni. 3-9); yet wherever it occurs in a larger sense he explains it as सत्यं वा यज्ञं वा (*satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā*) (Ni. 4-19), etc. Sāyaṇa too, wherever ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*) occurs, explains it as यज्ञस्पृतः (*yajñaspṛtaḥ*) or सत्यज्ञाः (*satyajñāḥ*). In many places the word ṛta describes the order of the universe. "Standing, as it does inter alia, for impersonal Order or Law, pervading the physical and moral world and sustaining alike the worlds of the gods and nature, the concept of the Rita may be said to have created a land-mark in the history of Vedic thought and culture." In these words the English scholar Eggeling says that the idea denoted by the word ṛta holds a distinction in Vedic culture. It is necessary to examine closely the uses of this word and the ideas it conveys in each context.
The word is used in the very first sūkta of the first Maṇḍala of the Ṛk-Saṃhitā, where the great qualities of Agni are described:
राजंतमध्वराणां गोपामृतस्य दीदिविं । वर्धमानं स्वे दमे । (*rājaṃtamadhvarāṇāṃ gopāmṛtasya dīdiviṃ | vardhamānaṃ sve dame |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-8)
Here Sāyaṇa explains ऋतस्य गोपां (*ṛtasya gopāṃ*) as ऋतस्य सत्यस्यावश्यंभाविनः कर्मफलस्य (*ṛtasya satyasyāvaśyaṃbhāvinaḥ karmaphalasya*). Yāska too gives the meaning "truth" and supports it.
The scholar Max Muller, examining the original meaning of ṛta and its development, says that at first ṛta denoted the course of movement of the sun, moon and the like, and then was used as a synonym of the sacrifices performed according to the seasons and solstices that follow their revolution. By reflecting this rule, the same word finally became a synonym describing the order of nature or dharma. The scholar Keith says of it:
"In the physical world there rules a regular order ऋत (*ṛta*), which is clearly an inheritance from the physical; it is an easy step to the conception of the ऋत (*ṛta*),............ in the moral world".
" The term for Cosmic order, ऋत (*ṛta*) and and its opposite अनृत (*anṛta*) express also moral order as in the dialogue of Yama and Yami. ऋत (*ṛta*) forbids and

### Printed p. 475
(Keith:) "... ऋत (*ṛta*) forbids and doubtless also commands positive action. ऋत (*ṛta*) is more than truth, सत्य (*satya*). Law is denoted by धर्म (*dharma*), which denotes that which supports and that which is supported ; It applies like ऋत (*ṛta*) to all aspects of the world, to the sequence of of events in Nature, to the sacrifice and to man's life."

Whenever the universal order in the physical world is described, that order is indicated by the word ऋत (*ṛta*) itself. In the same way, in man's moral conduct also, the words ऋत (*ṛta*) and its opposite अनृत (*anṛta*) denote man's moral law and immoral conduct. Because man's sacrificial rite is directly related to both physical and moral affairs, ऋत (*ṛta*) has also been used as a synonym of sacrifice. For that reason it is also a word equivalent to सत्य (*satya*) (truth), or rather it gives more meaning than the sense indicated by the word सत्य (*satya*). This is the gist of the sentences above.

The description that all the deities, whether individually or collectively, are presiding over ऋत (*ṛta*) and are engaged in action through ऋत (*ṛta*) itself is stated again and again in the Ṛksaṃhitā. If one mantra that fully conveys this idea is taken as an example, the point becomes clear.

हंसः कुचिषद्वसुरंतरिक्षसद्योता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् । नृषद्वरसदृतसद्योमसदब्बा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं ॥ (*haṃsaḥ kuciṣadvasuraṃtarikṣasadyotā vediṣadatithirduroṇasat | nṛṣadvarasadṛtasadyomasadabbā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-40-5)

In this Ṛk the universal order is stated. In the universe every individual's own fixed place is ordained by ऋत (*ṛta*). How? The Āditya's place is in the sky, the Hotṛ's place is on the sacrificial altar, the guest's place is in the house. But the place of ऋत (*ṛta*) alone is all-pervading. The description of this mantra is that ऋत (*ṛta*) pervades the earth, the atmosphere, men, gods, sacrifices and the like, the Āditya's works and mountains and the like, and so spreads through the whole universe. This is a context that tells of the spiritual and moral principle of the universe. Describing the greatness of this ऋत (*ṛta*), the scholar Bloomfield has said as follows.

"If therefore an ethics of the Rig-veda, rooted in the concept of Ritaf be at all conceded, it is not to be construed as an ethies o, naturalism with its apothesis of la bete humaine. It provides in the stricter sense, an ethics in accordance with the highest human

### Printed p. 476
idual which was destined to realise all its ethical implications in the Law of कर्म (*karma*). Of that there is surely no room for misgivings ; for accredited exponents of the philosophy and history of religion, like Pfleiderer, view the Rita and Karma of the Hindus as more or less hyphenated in their nature, and classify them on grounds of functional similarity, with the Nemesis of the Greeks, the Ashavaista of the Persians and the Tao of the Chinese"

As said above, these sentences too state that ऋत (*ṛta*) is a word that expresses the principle reflecting the universal order, and say that it conveys the same idea as the words Nemesis, Tao and the like, found in the beliefs of other peoples. But another point must be noted here. The word ऋत (*ṛta*) is used in the plural in many contexts. In those contexts it is not proper to interpret it as universal order. Likewise in still other contexts another meaning has to be given, according to the context. Therefore the special meanings of this word will be examined closely along with one or two examples of such contexts.

वि श्रयंतामृतावृधो द्वारो देवीरसश्चतः । अद्या नूनं च यष्टवे ॥ (*vi śrayaṃtāmṛtāvṛdho dvāro devīrasaścataḥ | adyā nūnaṃ ca yaṣṭave ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-6)

Here the deities called the Devī Dvāras are addressed as ऋतावृधरु (*ṛtāvṛdharu*). Here it is understood to mean protection of the sacrifice. ऋत (*ṛta*) must here be a synonym of sacrifice. And,

नमस्यत हव्यदातिं स्वध्वरं दुवस्यत दम्यं जातवेदसं । रथीर्यतस्य बृहतो विचर्षणिरग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोहितः ॥ (*namasyata havyadātiṃ svadhvaraṃ duvasyata damyaṃ jātavedasaṃ | rathīryatasya bṛhato vicarṣaṇiragnirdevānāmabhavatpurohitaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-8)

Here Agni is described as the charioteer of ऋत (*ṛta*); here ऋत (*ṛta*) must mean sacrifice. There is no room for any other meaning. But,

ससस्य यद्वियुता सस्मिन्नूधन्नृतस्य धामन्रणयंत देवाः । महा अग्निर्नमसा रातहव्यो वेरध्वराय सदमिदृतावा ॥ (*sasasya yadviyutā sasminnūdhannṛtasya dhāmanraṇayaṃta devāḥ | mahā agnirnamasā rātahavyo veradhvarāya sadamidṛtāvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-7-7)

In this Ṛk it can be explained in two ways. First, there are two words, ऋतस्य धाम (*ṛtasya dhāma*) and ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*). For the first, ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*), Sāyaṇa gives "water", and for the second, in ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*), he gives for the word ऋत (*ṛta*) the sense "possessor of truth" as the first meaning. As the second, he explains ऋतस्य धाम (*ṛtasya dhāma*) as सत्यस्य योनिः (*satyasya yoniḥ*), that is, the sacrifice, and ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*) as "possessor of truth". Or else, since the sacrifice, which builds up the mutual relation between gods and men, is itself what maintains the universal order whose nature is truth,

### Printed p. 477
ऋत (*ṛta*) is a word that shows the identity of sacrifice and truth. For example—

ऋतमृतेन सपंतेषिरं दक्षमाशाते । अद्रुहा देवौ वर्धेते ॥ (*ṛtamṛtena sapaṃteṣiraṃ dakṣamāśāte | adruhā devau vardhete ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 56-4) **NOTE**

Here Mitra and Varuṇa are praised as those who foster ऋत (*ṛta*) by ऋत (*ṛta*). This sentence describes the sacrifice whose nature is truth and the truth whose nature is sacrifice. The idea in the sentence यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāḥ*) is the same as in this sentence. Since the sacrifice whose nature is truth maintains the universal order, it may be said that ऋत (*ṛta*) is a word reflecting both these principles. (The relation between ऋत (*ṛta*) and the deities such as Mitra and Varuṇa who protect ऋत (*ṛta*), and the point which deities are ऋतावृधरु (*ṛtāvṛdharu*), will be stated later.)

In the present Ṛk, Lopāmudrā, desiring union with her husband Agastya, [states that] all the seers of former times, who were protectors of truth, protectors of sacrifice and who gained relation with the gods through sacrifice, attained the fulfilment of desire. She states that since man's desire is a natural wish of man, and failing to satisfy it would be unnatural conduct, and she desires her husband's company. From a Ṛk of the same sequence, later, at the time of the dialogue of Yama and Yamī, Yamī prays to her brother Yama. Saying that all the seers who walked following the rule of ऋतु (*ṛtu*) obtained the fulfilment of desire,

ये चित्तूर्व ऋतसाप ऋतावान ऋतावृधः । पित्यून् तपस्वतो यम ताश्चिदेवापि गच्छतात् ॥ (*ye cittūrva ṛtasāpa ṛtāvāna ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | pityūn tapasvato yama tāścidevāpi gacchatāt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-154-4)

in this Ṛk she makes a prayer desiring Yama's company. But since the wife's prayer in the present Ṛk is just, her husband Agastya accepts it. The prayer in the Ṛk quoted, being made by the sister Yamī to her brother Yama, becomes immoral conduct.

##### Grammar

- ऋतसापः — आप्‌ल्य व्याप्तौ इति धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । छांदसत्वात् सकारः अधिकः आगच्छति । समासे कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- आसन् — हि च (पा. सू. ८-१-३८) इति निघातस्वर प्रतिषेधः आगच्छति । अतः अद्दुदात्तस्वरः भवति । **NOTE**

### Printed p. 478
- अवडन् — वद व्यक्तायां वाचि इति धातुः । लज् प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वर प्रतिषेधः आगच्छति । अडागमस्वरेण आद्युदात्तः भवति ।
- असुः — षोंतकर्मणि इति धातुः । अव इति उपसर्गसंबंधात् बिडुवुदु इत्यर्थे प्रयुक्तः । छांदसत्वात् वर्तमानार्थे लुज् । प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपम् । अतिहंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः आगच्छति ।
- आपुः — आप्‌ल्य व्याप्तौ इति धातुः । लिट् प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपम् । हिचॆ इति निघातस्वर प्रतिषेधात् प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति ।
- पत्निः — सुपां सुलुक्- (प्रा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति जस् परे पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न मृषा॑ श्रां॒तं यदवं॑ति दे॒वा विश्वा॒ इत्सृधो॑ अ॒भ्य॑श्चवाव ।  
> जया॒वेदत्र॑ श॒तनी॑थमा॒जिं यत्स॒म्यंचा॑ मिथु॒नाव॒भ्यजः ॑व ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । मृषा । श्रांतं । यत् । अवंति । देवाः । विश्वाः । इत् । स्पृधः । अभि । अश्ववाव ।  
> जयाव । इत् । अत्र । शतनीथं । अजिं । यत् । सम्यंचा । मिथुनौ । अभि । अजाव ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आगस्त्यामाह ॥
> भोः पत्नि त्वया मया न मृषा श्रांतं । व्यर्थं नैव खिन्नमावाभ्यां ।
> यद्यस्माद्देवा अवंति रक्षंति तपोभिः प्रीता देवाः । विश्वाः सर्वाः स्पृधोऽभ्यश्चवाव। अभितो व्याप्नुयाव । अत्रास्मिन्संसारे शतनीथमपरिमितभोगप्राप्ति साधनमाजिं
> प्राप्तिं परस्परं जयाव । जयलक्षणं सुरतसंग्रामं वा जयाव । यद्यस्मात्सम्यंचा
> सम्यक्परस्परं गच्छंतौ प्रजयंतौ ना मिथुना मिथुनौ स्त्रीपुरषरूपौ संतावभ्यजाव ।
> त्वं चाहमपि परस्परमभिजयावेत्येवं तयोक्तं संभोगं संभावयामास ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agastya speaks to his wife. "O wife, by you and me effort has not been spent in vain; we two have not laboured fruitlessly. Since the gods, pleased by austerities, protect us, let us two pervade, on all sides, all the longed-for desires (स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)). Here in this world let us win each other, आजिं (*ājiṃ*) being the means of attaining boundless enjoyment; or let us win the battle of love-union (सुरतसंग्रामं (*suratasaṃgrāmaṃ*)), which has conquest as its mark. Since, joining well with each other and conquering, being as man and woman a pair (मिथुनौ (*mithunau*)), we are to win—you and I conquer each other." Thus he gave his assent to the union she had proposed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भोः पत्नि (*bhoḥ patni*)—O wife, Lopāmudrā
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- अवंति (*avaṃti*)—(pleased by our austerity) protect
- (तत् (*tat*)—therefore)

### Printed p. 479
- मृषा (*mṛṣā*)—in vain
- न श्रांतं (*na śrāṃtaṃ*)—(by us two) toil has not been borne
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- स्पृधः इत् (*spṛdhaḥ it*)—desires
- अभि आश्वनाव (*abhi āśvanāva*)—let us obtain
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this world
- मिथुनौ (*mithunau*)—like man and woman
- सम्यंचा (*samyaṃcā*)—well united with each other
- यत् अभि अजाव (*yat abhi ajāva*)—(if we conquer each other) or if we strive well
- शतनीथं (*śatanīthaṃ*)—the means of attaining boundless enjoyment
- आजिं (*ājiṃ*)—mutual attainment
- जयाव (*jayāva*)—we win
- [or आजिं (*ājiṃ*)—the battle in the form of love-union; जयाव इत् (*jayāva it*)—(we two) shall surely win.]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wife, O Lopāmudrā, the gods, pleased by our austerity, protect us, and by their favour we obtain all our desires; so do not say that the toil we have borne is in vain. And in this world, if we two, husband and wife, united with each other, strive well, we can accomplish boundless enjoyments. (Let us two win the victory in the form of enjoyment in the battle of love-union.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Agastya)—Penance has not been practised in vain : since the gods protect us, we may indulge all our desires : in this world we may triumph in many conflicts, if we exert ourselves mutually together.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Agastya gives his reply to his wife Lopāmudrā and gives his consent to union with her as she desired. But here another special point must be noted. In this conversation desire is not presented as the foremost aim of man. Only after the religious works such as sacrifices have all been performed, the gods thereby satisfied and their favour obtained, does Agastya declare this wish. In that, too, another point is to be noted. When he says न मृषा शांतं............ (*na mṛṣā śāṃtaṃ............*), that the toil we have borne to satisfy the gods does not become vain, it is well known that the gods' satisfaction is in turn for the sake of favouring man. Since worldly happiness is one of the rewards befitting this effort, Agastya desires to enjoy the worldly happiness to be acquired through the gods' favour.

स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)—The authors of the Nirukta have read the word स्पृध (*spṛdha*) together with the names of battle. But in the present Ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained it as "desire". From the root स्पर्ध् (*spardh*) the formed word then also means "desire".

### Printed p. 480
Since restraint of desire is an extremely hard discipline, it is here compared to battle.

आजिं (*ājiṃ*)—अजयनस्याजवनस्येति वा (*ajayanasyājavanasyeti vā*) (Ni. 9-23). Battle is called आजि (*āji*) either because it is the place of winning victory or because it is a place of speed. In explaining this word the authors of the Nirukta, citing the Ṛk in the Ṛksaṃhitā,

न्यक्रंदयन्नु पयंत एनममेहयन् वृषभं मध्य आजेः । तेन सूभव० शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः प्रधने जिगाय ॥ (*nyakraṃdayannu payaṃta enamamehayan vṛṣabhaṃ madhya ājeḥ | tena sūbhava0 śatavatsahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pradhane jigāya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-102-5)

have given the above derivation for the word आजेः (*ājeḥ*) occurring there. In the present Ṛk also Sāyaṇa has given both meanings: first, आजिं परस्परप्राप्तिं (*ājiṃ parasparaprāptiṃ*), and second, सुरतरूपसंग्रामं वा (*suratarūpasaṃgrāmaṃ vā*).

##### Grammar

- श्रांतम् — श्रमु तपसि खेदे च इति धातुः । क्त प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति ।
- अवंति — अव रक्षणे इति धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरः न आगच्छति । शास्यदानुत्तेत्-(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इति लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- अक्षवाव — अशू व्याप्तौ इति धातुः । स्वादिः । व्यत्ययो बहुलं (पा. सू. ३-४१-८५) इति परस्मैपदी भवति । लोट् उत्तमपुरुषः । द्विवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः आगच्छति । **NOTE**
- जयाव — जि जये इति धातुः । लोट् उत्तम पुरुष द्विवचनांतरूपम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न आगच्छति । लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- शतनीथम् — णीञ् प्रापणे इति धातुः । हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्धन् (उ. सू. २-१५९) इति क्धन् प्रत्ययः । बहुव्रीहि समासे बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदम् इति पूर्वपदप्रकृति स्वरः आगच्छति । द्वितीया एकवचनांतरूपम् ।
- सम्यंचा — सुपां सुलुक्-(पा. सू. ३-१-३९) इति द्विवचन ओकार विभक्तेः आकारादेशः ।
- अजाव — अज गतिक्षेपणयोः इति धातुः । लोट् उत्तमपुरुष द्विवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरः न आगच्छति । धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते । ॥ ३ ॥

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒दस्य॑ मा रुध॒तः काम॒ आग॑न्नि॒त आजा॑तो अ॒मुतः॒ कुत॑श्चित् ।  
> लोपा॑मुद्रा॒ वृष॑णं॒ नी रि॑णाति॒ धीर॒मधी॑रा धयति श्व॒संतं॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नदस्य । मा । रुधतः । कामः । आ । अगन् । इतः । आजातः । अमुतः । कुतः । चित् ।  
> लोपामुद्रा । वृषणं । निः । रिणाति । धीरं । अधीरा । धयति । श्वसंतं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ चतुर्थ्याप्यगस्य आह ॥
> हे जाये नदस्य नदनस्य जपशब्दयितुर्जपाध्ययनकर्तू रुधतो रेतो
> निरोद्धुब्रह्मचर्यमास्थितस्य ॥ उभे कर्मणि षष्ठौ ॥ उक्तलक्षणं मां काम
> आगन् । आगमत् । नदनस्य मा रुधतः काम आगमदिति निरुक्तं । ५-२ । कस्य हेतोरिति
> उच्यते । इतस्त्वत्संगमनिमित्तात् तथामुतो वसंतादिकालात् कुतश्चित्कारणादाजातः
> सर्वत उत्पन्नः । यद्वा । इत एतल्लोकजनितादमुतो लोकांतरजनिताद्वा
> कुतश्चिन्निमित्तात्कामात् । कथमिति उच्यते । इयं लोपामुद्रा वृषणं रेतसः
> प्रवर्तकं मां नी रिणाति । नितरां गच्छतु । किंच धीरं धीमंतं नियमादविचालिनं
> श्वसंतं महाप्राणं महाबलमधीरा कातरैषा योषिद्धयति । उपभुंक्तां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now, with the fourth Ṛk, Agastya speaks. "O wife, desire has come upon me, who am a नदस्य (*nadasya*), one who utters sound, that is, one who mutters prayers and recites them, and a रुधतः (*rudhataḥ*), one who restrains his seed, one established in celibacy." Both words stand in the genitive in the sense of the object. Sāyaṇa quotes the Nirukta: नदनस्य मा रुधतः काम आगमदिति (*nadanasya mā rudhataḥ kāma āgamaditi*) (5-2). The cause is then stated: desire has arisen from this, namely from union with you, and from that, namely the spring and other seasons, or from some other cause; it is born everywhere. Or else: from a desire produced in this world or in another world, from some cause. How? "Let this Lopāmudrā approach me, the vṛṣan, the impeller of seed." And further: "the unsteady (अधीरा (*adhīrā*)), timid woman enjoys the steady (धीर (*dhīra*)), wise, unshaken by restraint, the one who breathes hard (श्वसंतं (*śvasaṃtaṃ*)), of great breath and great strength."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे जाये (*he jāye*)—O wife
- नदस्य (*nadasya*)—of one making the sound (of prayer and study)
- रुधतः (*rudhataḥ*)—of one practising restraint of seed (celibacy)
- मा (*mā*)—me
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from this cause (union with you)
- आमुतः (*āmutaḥ*)—from that cause (the spring and other seasons)
- कुतश्चित् (*kutaścit*)—or from some other cause. [Or इतः (*itaḥ*)—produced from this world; अमुतः (*amutaḥ*)—produced from the other world; कुतः चित् (*kutaḥ cit*)—from some cause.]
- आजातः (*ājātaḥ*)—arisen
- कामः (*kāmaḥ*)—desire for objects
- आ अगन् (*ā agan*)—has arisen
- लोपामुद्रा (*lopāmudrā*)—this Lopāmudrā
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—me, the impeller of seed
- निः रिणाति (*niḥ riṇāti*)—approaches (let her approach)
- किंच (*kiṃca*)—and
- अधीरा (*adhīrā*)—the timid woman
- धीरं (*dhīraṃ*)—the wise
- श्वसंतं (*śvasaṃtaṃ*)—the greatly strong
- धयति (*dhayati*)—enjoys

### Printed p. 482

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Lopāmudrā, desire has arisen in me, who am devoted to prayer and study and firm in the vow of celibacy, either from nearness to you or from some other cause. Therefore approach me, the sprinkler of seed. However wise and strong a man may be, a timid woman makes him distraught.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Desire, either from this cause or from that, has come upon me whilst engaged in prayer and suppressing (passion) : let Lopamudra approach her husband : the unsteady famale beguiles the firm and resolute man.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Agastya again reassures his wife Lopāmudrā, says he will satisfy her, and makes his desire clear.
The Nirukta author has explained this Ṛk as follows: नदनस्य मा रुधतः काम आगमत् । संरुद्धप्रजननस्य ब्रह्मचारिण इत्यृषिपुत्रा विलपितं वेदयंते ॥ (*nadanasya mā rudhataḥ kāma āgamat | saṃruddhaprajananasya brahmacāriṇa ityṛṣiputrā vilapitaṃ vedayaṃte ‖*) (Ni. 5-2). That is: "Having been married to an ascetic seer, I had to be the object of his passionless love. He has no desire for sexual pleasure; he remains a celibate" — thus the seer's daughter made known her grief. Here a slight conflict appears between the statement of the Bṛhaddevatā and that of the Nirukta. In the Bṛhaddevatā:
रिरंसुस्तामथागस्त्य उत्तराभ्यामतोषयत् । (*riraṃsustāmathāgastya uttarābhyāmatoṣayat |*)
(Bṛ. De. 4-58)
It says Agastya pleased his wife Lopāmudrā with the next two Ṛks, that is, the 3rd and 4th Ṛks of this sūkta, making known his wish. But here, according to the Nirukta, this is Lopāmudrā's statement, and it is understood that Lopāmudrā makes known her mental distress by these words. Durgācārya has commented on the Nirukta passage thus:
*āgastyalopāmudrābrahmacārisūktasaṃvāde lopāmudrayā iyamārṣaṃ |
sā abravīdagastyaṃ bhartāramabhipretya "nadasya nadanasya.........."....| ityevaṃ
vilasamānā kāmārtā lopāmudrā rājarṣiputrikā | ........evaṃ lopā-

### Printed p. 483
mudrāvākye “ nadasya rudhato māmāgamat kāmaḥ ” iti prakaraṇādṛṣirnadaśabdenocyate ityupapadyate ‖*
(Nirukta-vyākhyā 5-2)
The Nirukta author calls Lopāmudrā a seer's daughter, Durgācārya a royal seer's daughter. There is a story that she was Agastya's daughter, and that Agastya himself created her, wishing to obtain a beautiful wife, and left her with the king of Vidarbha. It is described in the Mahābhārata as follows; it is quoted here because it accords with the Bṛhaddevatā statements.
ततः प्रसवसंतानं चिंतयन्भगवानृषिः (*tataḥ prasavasaṃtānaṃ ciṃtayanbhagavānṛṣiḥ*) … मैथुनायाजुहाव तां ॥ (*maithunāyājuhāva tāṃ ‖*) **NOTE**
(Mahābhārata, Vanaparva, 94-95)
Then the seer Agastya wished to obtain the fruit of offspring, but found no wife suited to him. So he himself created a maiden suited to him and left her with the king of Vidarbha, who longed for a son, for her upbringing. The king was delighted to receive her, and all his friends congratulated him on gaining so beautiful a daughter. They named her Lopāmudrā. She grew up happily in the king's palace and reached youth. Then Agastya came and asked the king to give her as his wife. The king was unwilling, but fearing that the angered seer might curse him, he went to consult his wife. Then Lopāmudrā herself came to her father and told him to give her to Agastya. The king then gave her to Agastya in marriage according to the rule. Having received her as wife, Agastya wished to bring her too under a seer's discipline: he had her ornaments removed and told her to wear an ascetic's dress, and at his word she put on bark garments and was in accord with her husband. Having got such a suitable wife, he practised severe austerity with her on the bank of the Gaṅgā. She too served him with love and respect and was his helper. Once, when Lopāmudrā had bathed after her period, Agastya, pleased with her purity of spirit, her bodily beauty and her devotion to her husband, desired union with her; so the story runs in the Mahābhārata.

### Printed p. 484
In the Ṛksaṃhitā, however, it is described that Lopāmudrā, having rested from severe austerity, desired her husband's company; in the Mahābhārata it is Agastya who desires. The rest of the story is the same. In the Bṛhaddevatā, as ऋतुस्नातामृषिर्भार्या० लोपामुद्रां यशस्सिनीं । उपजल्पितुमारेभे रहसंयोगकाम्यया ॥ (*ṛtusnātāmṛṣirbhāryā0 lopāmudrāṃ yaśassinīṃ | upajalpitumārebhe rahasaṃyogakāmyayā ‖*) so also in the Mahābhārata: तपसा द्योतितां स्नातां ददर्श भगवानृषिः (*tapasā dyotitāṃ snātāṃ dadarśa bhagavānṛṣiḥ*). In the sequence of this story there is no great difference between the Veda's description and the Itihāsa's. That very matter the Nirukta author has indicated by "the seer's daughter's lament."

### Printed p. 485
**Special Topics** (continued)
नदस्य (*nadasya*)—Sāyaṇa explains: नदनस्य जपशब्दयितुर्जसाध्ययनकर्तुः (*nadanasya japaśabdayiturjasādhyayanakartuḥ*), that is, the praiser who makes sound by reciting prayers, hymns and so on. In explaining this Ṛk the Nirukta author gives the derivation of the word as: यमिनेर्दो भवति नदतेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (*yaminerdo bhavati nadateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 5-2). The word नद (*nada*), formed from the root नद् (*nad*) meaning "praise", means the seer who praises. The word is used in many places as a synonym of "seer". For example:
रसद्गंधर्वीरप्या च योषणा नदस्य नादे परि पातु मे मनः । (*rasadgaṃdharvīrapyā ca yoṣaṇā nadasya nāde pari pātu me manaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-11-2)
Here there are two words, नदस्य (*nadasya*) and नादे (*nāde*); the former is explained as "of the praiser" (स्तोतुः (*stotuḥ*)) and the latter as a sound in the form of praise. But there is no rule that the meaning "praiser" must hold wherever the word occurs. For example:
उक्षंते आश्वा अत्या इवाजिषु नदस्य कर्णैस्तरयंत आतुभिः । (*ukṣaṃte āśvā atyā ivājiṣu nadasya karṇaistarayaṃta ātubhiḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-3)
Here it is explained as शब्दवतः मेघस्य (*śabdavataḥ meghasya*), "of the cloud that makes sound". **NOTE**
निः रिणाति (*niḥ riṇāti*)—The word रिणाति (*riṇāti*) is read among the roots of motion; here it is explained as "approaches". But the meaning of the word depends on the construction of the whole Ṛk. If, as Sāyaṇa says, the statement is by Agastya, it means "approaches"; if, according to the Nirukta author, it is Lopāmudrā's statement, it means "burns". In general the word is used mostly in the senses "dry up, burn". For example:
पुरूणि दस्मो नि रिणाति जंभैराद्रोचते वन आ विभावा । (*purūṇi dasmo ni riṇāti jaṃbhairādrocate vana ā vibhāvā |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-148-4)
Just as in such Ṛks it gives the sense "burn", so in the present Ṛk too, since there is no room for the satisfaction of desire in the love of an ascetic, it would not be wrong to explain that it burns the body. The words इतः (*itaḥ*) and अमुतः (*amutaḥ*) also differ in meaning accordingly.

##### Grammar

- नदस्य — णद अव्यक्ते शब्दे । धातुः । नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यो (पा. सू. ३-१-१३४) इति अच् प्रत्ययः । चितः इति अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति । कर्मार्थे षष्ठी आगता ।

### Printed p. 486
- रुधत — रुधिर् आवरणे धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । छांदसः विकरणस्य लुक् । षष्ठी एकवचनांतरूपम् । शतुरनुमोनद्यजादी (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३) इति नुम्‌रहितस्य शतृप्रत्ययस्य परस्मिन् विभक्तौ आगतायां तस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- अगन् — गम्‌ल्य गत् । धातुः । लज् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने शिप् । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । हल् ज्याभ्यो दीर्घात् इति तिपः लोपः । मो नो धातोः (पा. सू. ८-२-५४) इति धातुमकारस्य नकारादेशः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति । **NOTE**
- आजातः — गतिरनंतरः (पा. सू. ६-२-४९) इति क्तांतसरे स्थितत्वात् गतेः (आ) उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- रिणाति — री गतिरेषणयोः धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः (पा. सू. ७-३-८०) इति धातोः ह्रस्वः भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- अधीरा — नञ् तत्पुरुषसमासः । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ (पा. सू. ६-२-२) इति अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- धयति — धेट् पाने । धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुषे तिप् परे शप् विकरणम् । तं निमित्तीकृत्य एकारस्य आयादेशः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- श्वसंतम् — श्वस प्राणने । धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । शपः लुक् । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । द्वितीया एकवचनांतरूपम् ।

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं नु सोम॒मंति॑तो हृ॒त्सु पी॒तमुप॑ ब्रुवे ।  
> यत्सी॒माग॑श्चकृ॒मा तत्सु मृ॑ळतु पुलु॒कामो॒ हि मर्त्यः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । नु । सोमं । अंतितः । हृत्सु । पीतं । उप । ब्रुवे ।  
> यत् । सीं । आगः । चकृम । तत् । सु । मृळतु । पुलुकामः । हि । मर्त्यः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 487

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथानयोर्दंपत्योः संभोगसंलापं श्रुत्वा तत्पायश्चित्तं चिकीर्षुरुत्तराभ्यामाह । अनयोर्विनियोगः शौनकेनोक्तेः । इमं नु सोममित्येते
> द्वे ऋचौ प्रयतो जपन् । सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति पापेभ्यश्च प्रमुच्यते ।
> ऋग्वि. १-२६. ॥ इति ॥
> उपेत्य मनसा प्राप्य पार्थयते । किं ब्रवीति उच्यते । यदागो गुर्वोः
> कामप्रलापश्रवणविषयं पापं चक्रम कृतवंतो वयं तत्तस्मादागसः स सोमः
> सु सम्यग्मृळतु । सुखयतु । पापजनितदुःखं मा करोत्वित्यर्थः । महत्पापमनुभुज्यमानं प्रार्थनया कथं लुप्यत इति अत आह । हि यस्मान्मर्त्यो मनुष्यः
> पुलुकामो बहुकामनावान् । अल्वेनैव कर्मणा बहुकामानाकालयति । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्परिहरेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । अयमपवर्जनीयतयॊ प्राप्यत इवेत्याह ।
> पुलुकामो हि खलु मर्त्यः कामहतः सन् कामेन निरुद्ध एव वर्तते । आतस्तयोरुत्सेकोऽयुक्तः । तच्छब्दश्रवणदोषोऽपि प्रावादिकोऽस्माकं प्राप्तेन सोमेन
> परिहर्तव्य इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । आयं मंत्रश्चंद्रपरो व्याख्येयो मनसोऽभिमानित्वाच्च तस्य पापस्यापि मनस्येव संभावितत्वात् । अस्मिन्नक्षे हृत्तु पीतं हृदयस्थितमित्यर्थः । शिष्टं स्पष्टं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Having heard the amorous talk of this couple, and wishing to make atonement for it, the pupil speaks the next two verses. Their use is given by Śaunaka: इमं नु सोममित्येते द्वे ऋचौ प्रयतो जपन् । सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति पापेभ्यश्च प्रमुच्यते । (*imaṃ nu somamityete dve ṛcau prayato japan | sarvānkāmānavāpnoti pāpebhyaśca pramucyate |*) (Ṛgvidhāna 1-26): one who mutters these two verses, self-controlled, obtains all desires and is freed from sins. उप (*upa*) means approaching in mind and attaining; he entreats. What does he say? The sin (आगः (*āgaḥ*)) we have committed, in having listened to the amorous talk of the two teachers: from that sin may Soma gladden us well (सु मृळतु (*su mṛḷatu*)), that is, may he not cause us the suffering born of sin. Since a great sin that is being experienced cannot be removed by prayer alone, he adds: हि (*hi*), because man is पुलुकामः (*pulukāmaḥ*), full of many desires; by a small act he sets many desires in motion. Since this is so, he should therefore be forgiven. Or else: the sin is felt as though it were to be got rid of; man, struck by desire, remains confined by desire; hence the upsurge of the two (teachers' desire) is not improper, and the fault of hearing their words, also a matter of common talk, is to be removed for us by the Soma that has been obtained. Or else: this mantra is to be explained as addressed to the moon, since the moon presides over the mind and the sin too is conceived in the mind; हृत्सु पीतं (*hṛtsu pītaṃ*) then means "abiding in the heart". The rest is clear.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हि (*hi*)—for which reason
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—man
- पुलुकामः (*pulukāmaḥ*)—one who desires much gain (from little action)
- तत् (*tat*)—therefore
- यत् सीं (*yat sīṃ*)—which, this (sin consisting in hearing the amorous talk of the teacher's wife)
- आगः (*āgaḥ*)—sin
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—we have committed
- तत् (*tat*)—that sin
- सु मृळतु (*su mṛḷatu*)—may he make well and pleasant (may he prevent the fault born of sin), thus
- नु (*nu*)—now
- हृत्सु पीतं (*hṛtsu pītaṃ*)—drunk with the heart (drunk by the mind)
- इमं सोमं (*imaṃ somaṃ*)—this Soma juice
- अंतितः (*aṃtitaḥ*)—from near
- उप ब्रुवे (*upa bruve*)—I pray
- Alternatively: हृत्सु पीतं (*hṛtsu pītaṃ*)—dwelling in the heart (presiding over the mind); इमं सोमं (*imaṃ somaṃ*)—this moon; अंतितः उप ब्रुवे (*aṃtitaḥ upa bruve*)—approaching near, I pray.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Men are full of many desires; therefore, approaching this Soma drunk in the mind, I pray that he remove the fault committed by us (the pupil), namely hearing the amorous talk of the teacher and his wife. (I beg the moon, who presides over the mind, to remove the sin.)

### Printed p. 488

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Pupil),—I beseech the Soma juice, which has been drunk in my heart, that it may fully expiate the sin we have committed : man is subject to many desires.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk has been interpreted in two or three ways. Here Agastya's pupil expresses repentance for his sinful act. That repentance may be for the sin arising from having heard the conversation of Agastya and Lopāmudrā concerning amorous desire. Or, since man's natural faults are many and violent desire is one of them, he may be declaring repentance for such a fault. And the means of removing this sin is prayer addressed to Soma. But here there is room for disagreement whether सोमं (*somaṃ*) means the Soma juice or the moon. Hence even Sāyaṇa has not been able to give a definitive meaning to this Ṛk. First: आगः—गुर्वोः कामप्रलापश्रवणविषयं पापं कृतवंतः तस्मादागसः सुखियतु (*āgaḥ—gurvoḥ kāmapralāpaśravaṇaviṣayaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtavaṃtaḥ tasmādāgasaḥ sukhiyatu*): may the sin arising from having heard our teachers' (the couple's) talk of desire be removed. Second: पुरुकामो हि मर्त्यः कामहतःसन् कामेन निरुद्ध एव वर्तते (*purukāmo hi martyaḥ kāmahataḥsan kāmena niruddha eva vartate*): man, afflicted by various desires, is also bound by desire for objects and so earns sin; he prays that such sin be removed. But how is this sin removed? Through prayer addressed to Soma. As to the meaning of the word Soma, it may be the Soma juice or the moon. In the Ṛgveda the word Soma is nowhere explained as the moon; but if one says "the deity Soma", it fits both meanings. Since the identity of the deity Soma and the moon is stated in many places, and since in many places Soma is prayed to for removal of sin, both meanings are possible here.
सोमेनादित्या बलिनः सोमेन पृथिवी मही । अथो नक्षत्राणामेषामुपस्थे सोम आहितः ॥ (*somenādityā balinaḥ somena pṛthivī mahī | atho nakṣatrāṇāmeṣāmupasthe soma āhitaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-2). Where it is described that the gods such as Indra and the worlds such as the earth all grow through Soma, the meaning "Soma juice" also fits. Since the moon is the cause of the nourishment of all worlds, taking it as the moon is also natural. And in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa,

### Printed p. 489
एष वै सोमो राजा देवानामन्नं यच्चंद्रमाः (*eṣa vai somo rājā devānāmannaṃ yaccaṃdramāḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 1-6-4-5), the identity of the moon and Soma is described. Likewise in the following passages there is the same kind of description:
चंद्रमा वै ब्रह्मा सोमो वै चंद्रमाः (*caṃdramā vai brahmā somo vai caṃdramāḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 12-1-1-2); सूर्य एवाग्नेयः । चंद्रमाः सौम्यः (*sūrya evāgneyaḥ | caṃdramāḥ saumyaḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 1-6-3-24).
Thus in many places the moon is called Saumya. Therefore in the present Ṛk, हृत्तु पीतं इमं सोमं (*hṛttu pītaṃ imaṃ somaṃ*) is also given the second meaning, "this moon, dwelling in the heart, that is, presiding over the mind". And for removal of sin, in Ṛks such as उरुष्या नो अभिशस्तेः सोम नि पाह्यंहसः । सखा सुशेव एधि नः । (*uruṣyā no abhiśasteḥ soma ni pāhyaṃhasaḥ | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-15) the prayer is made: "O Soma, protect us from the stigma of slander; protect us completely from sin done or likely to be done." So here too the pupil prays for removal of his sin. In the Atharvaveda: सोमो मा देवो मुंचतु यमाहुश्चंद्रमा इति (*somo mā devo muṃcatu yamāhuścaṃdramā iti*) (Atha. Veda 11-6 7): "May the god Soma, whom all call the moon, free me from sin"; in this prayer the identity of Soma and the moon is plain.
पुलुकामः (*pulukāmaḥ*)—पुलुकामः पुरुकामः पुलुकामो हि मर्त्यः इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*pulukāmaḥ purukāmaḥ pulukāmo hi martyaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati*) (Ni. 6-4). The nature of mortal man is shown as having many kinds of desire. Because of these many desires sin (आगः (*āgaḥ*)) comes naturally to man, so the prayer is made: save us from this sin.
आगः (*āgaḥ*)—आज् पूर्वाद्धमेः (*āj pūrvāddhameḥ*) (Ni. 11-24). The root गम् (*gam*) with the prefix आज् (*āj*) gives the form आगः (*āgaḥ*). The Nirukta author explains that the name आगः (*āgaḥ*) is established because it shows that as a result of sinful acts the impression of sin, and its fruit, must surely come to a man.

##### Grammar

- हृत्सु — ऊडिदंपदादि-(पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- पीतम् — पा पाने इति धातुः । कर्मणि क्त प्रत्ययः । घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि (पा. सू. ६-४-६६) इति आकारस्य ईत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- ब्रुवे — ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि इति धातुः । लट् उत्तमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- आगः — इणौ गतौ इति धातुः । इण आगोपराधे च (उ. सू ४-६५१) इति असुन् प्रत्ययः । धातोः आगादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । **NOTE**
- चकृम — डुकृञ् करणे इति धातुः । लिट् उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- मृळतु — मृड सुखने इति धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंत निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- पुलुकामः — बहुप्रीहौ परादिश्चंदसि बहुलं (पा. सू. ६-२-१९९) इति उत्तरपदाद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

> उ॒भौ वर्णा॒वृषि॑रु॒ग्रः पु॑पोष स॒त्या दे॒वेष्वा॒तिषो॑ जगाम ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ विनियुक्तयोर्मध्ये द्वितीयया सूक्ते षष्ठ्यांतेवास्याह ॥
> अयमगस्तो मद्गुरुः खनित्र्यैः फलस्योत्पादनसाधनैर्यज्ञस्तोत्रादिभिः
> खनमानः फलमभिमतमुत्पादयन् प्रजां प्रकर्षेण पुनःपुनर्जायमानमहत्यं
> कुलस्यापतनसाधनं पुत्रादिकं बलं चेच्छमानः सन् । यद्वा ! प्रजां भृत्यादिरूपां
> चेच्छन् ! ऋषिरतींद्रियद्रष्टा महानुभाव उग्र उद्धूर्णः संसारे संचरन्नप्यपापः सन्नुभौ वर्णौ वर्णनीयावाकारौ कामं च तपश्च पुपोष । सत्या आशिषो
> देवेषु देवेभ्यो जगाम । प्राप्तवान् । यतोऽयं महानुभावस्तस्मादस्मान्पातीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the two verses now applied, with the second (i.e. this sixth verse) he speaks at the close of the sūkta. This Agastya, my teacher, खनित्र्यैः (*khanitryaiḥ*), with the means of producing fruit, sacrifices, praises and the like, "digging" (खनमानः (*khanamānaḥ*)), that is producing the desired fruit; desiring प्रजां (*prajāṃ*), progeny born again and again, अपत्यं (*apatyaṃ*), sons and the like, the means of preventing the family's fall, and बलं (*balaṃ*), strength. Or else: desiring प्रजां (*prajāṃ*) in the form of servants and the like. The seer (ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)), who sees beyond the senses, a man of great power, उग्रः (*ugraḥ*), mighty, though moving in the world of rebirth yet sinless, nourished उभौ वर्णौ (*ubhau varṇau*), the two admirable forms, desire and austerity. He obtained true blessings from the gods (देवेषु (*deveṣu*), i.e. from the gods). Since he is so powerful, he protects us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- खनित्रैः (*khanitraiḥ*)—by sacrifices, praises and the like, the means of producing fruit
- खनमानः (*khanamānaḥ*)—one who produces the desired fruit
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—progeny in the form of servants and the like (offspring)
- अपत्यं (*apatyaṃ*)—sons, grandsons and the like, who uplift the family
- बलं (च) (*balaṃ (ca)*)—and strength
- इच्छमानः (*icchamānaḥ*)—desiring
- ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—seer beyond the senses
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—(though sunk in worldly life) free from sin
- अगस्त्यः (*agastyaḥ*)—our teacher Agastya
- उभौ वर्णौ (*ubhau varṇau*)—the two kinds of action, desire and austerity
- पुपोष (*pupoṣa*)—increased
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods (from the gods)
- सत्याः (*satyāḥ*)—true-fruited
- आशिषः (*āśiṣaḥ*)—blessings
- जगाम (*jagāma*)—obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agastya the seer, who achieves his desires by means such as sacrifice and praise, who desires sons, servants, strength and so on, who sees beyond the senses and, though sunk in worldly life, is free from sin, has cultivated both desire and austerity; therefore he has obtained from the gods blessings of true fruit (the favour of the gods).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agastya, a venerable sage, working with (fit) implements, desiring progeny, offspring, and strength, practised both classes (of obligations), and received true benedictions from the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उभौ वर्णौ ऋषिरुग्रः पुपोष (*ubhau varṇau ṛṣirugraḥ pupoṣa*): the sage Agastya increased two kinds of वर्ण (*varṇa*). For उभौ वर्णौ (*ubhau varṇau*) Sāyaṇa has explained कामं च तपश्च (*kāmaṃ ca tapaśca*)

### Printed p. 492
as desire and austerity. Or it may be explained as the wealth of this world and of the next. All earthly wealth is the fruit of desire; all wealth of the next world is the fruit of austerity. It may be explained that Agastya increased both fruits. To win by his own power the wealth of both worlds, Agastya must have had extraordinary strength; its greatness is shown by the manner of his birth.
Since Agastya was the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, the individual powers of Mitra and Varuṇa combined to produce a special power in Agastya. How and why Agastya became known as Maitrāvaruṇi is told by the author of the Bṛhaddevatā thus:
तयोरादित्ययोः सत्रे दृष्ट्वाप्सरसमुर्वशीं । रेतश्चस्कंद तत्कुंभे न्यपतद्वासतीवरे ॥ (*tayorādityayoḥ satre dṛṣṭvāpsarasamurvaśīṃ | retaścaskaṃda tatkuṃbhe nyapatadvāsatīvare ‖*)
तेनैव तु मुहूर्तेन वीर्यवंतौ तपस्विनौ । अगस्त्यश्च वसिष्ठश्च तत्रर्षि संबभूवतुः ॥ (*tenaiva tu muhūrtena vīryavaṃtau tapasvinau | agastyaśca vasiṣṭhaśca tatrarṣi saṃbabhūvatuḥ ‖*)
बहुधा पतितं रेतः कलशे च जले स्थले । स्थले वसिष्ठस्तु मुनिः संभूत ऋषिसत्तमः ॥ (*bahudhā patitaṃ retaḥ kalaśe ca jale sthale | sthale vasiṣṭhastu muniḥ saṃbhūta ṛṣisattamaḥ ‖*)
कुंभे त्वगस्त्यः संभूतो जले मत्तो महाद्युतिः उदियाय ततोऽगस्त्यः शम्यामात्रो महातपाः ॥ (*kuṃbhe tvagastyaḥ saṃbhūto jale matto mahādyutiḥ udiyāya tato 'gastyaḥ śamyāmātro mahātapāḥ ‖*)
मानेन संमितो यस्मात्तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते । यद्वा कुंभादृषिर्जातः कुंभेनापि हि मीयते ॥ (*mānena saṃmito yasmāttasmānmānya ihocyate | yadvā kuṃbhādṛṣirjātaḥ kuṃbhenāpi hi mīyate ‖*)
कुंभ इत्यभिधानं च परिमाणस्य लक्ष्यते (*kuṃbha ityabhidhānaṃ ca parimāṇasya lakṣyate*) (Bṛ. De. 5-149 to 154).
Of these Ādityas, Mitra and Varuṇa, at the sacrificial session, seeing the apsaras Urvaśī, were infatuated. Then their seed fell and dropped into the pitcher that held the water of the dwelling. तस्या दर्शनान्नित्रावरुणयो रेतच्चस्कंद (*tasyā darśanānnitrāvaruṇayo retaccaskaṃda*) (Ni. 5-13). Immediately two ascetic and virile seers, Vasiṣṭha and Agastya, came into being. That is, the seed fell in the pitcher, in the water, and on the ground. From the seed that fell on the ground, Vasiṣṭha, best of seers, was born. Agastya was born from the pitcher, and the fish from the water. The great ascetic Agastya was only of the measure of a शम्या (*śamyā*) (a peg). Because he was of a definite measure he also got the name Mānya. Such is the story of Agastya's origin. Born of Mitra and Varuṇa, Agastya must have received the extraordinary powers of both. Their individual powers are thus described in the Śruti:
इमां वां मित्रावरणा सुवृक्तिमिषं न कृण्वे असुरा नवीयः । इनो वामन्यः पदवीरदब्बो जनं च मित्रो यतति ब्रुवाणः ॥ (*imāṃ vāṃ mitrāvaraṇā suvṛktimiṣaṃ na kṛṇve asurā navīyaḥ | ino vāmanyaḥ padavīradabbo janaṃ ca mitro yatati bruvāṇaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-36-2).

### Printed p. 493
In the Ṛk beginning *imāṃ vāṃ* the individual nature and function of Mitrāvaruṇa are described. In it Varuṇa is said to preside over dharma and adharma and to lead the people to worldly affairs. In the present Ṛk too these two powers of Agastya are described. And, as described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, it is understood that the individual qualities of Mitra and Varuṇa are the source of these two kinds of power. For example: वागेवाग्निः प्राणोदानौ मित्रावरुणौ । (*vāgevāgniḥ prāṇodānau mitrāvaruṇau |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-2-13). Mitra is of the nature of prāṇa and Varuṇa of the nature of udāna. As described in the Chāndogya: स प्राणः तच्चक्षुः स आदित्यस्तदेतत्तेजोऽन्नाद्यमित्युपासीत तेजस्वन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद (*sa prāṇaḥ taccakṣuḥ sa ādityastadetattejo 'nnādyamityupāsīta tejasvannādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda*) (Chā. U. 3-13-1).

Prāṇa is of the form of Āditya. One should meditate on it as food and as radiance. One who knows this truth becomes radiant and an eater of food; thus prāṇa is praised. This is a quality of worldly wealth. To increase this worldly wealth Agastya had acquired the quality of Mitra. And the quality of Varuṇa, udāna, is praised thus: स उदानः स वायुः स आकाशस्तदेशदोजश्च महश्चेत्युपासीतौजस्वी महस्वान्भवति य एवं वेद (*sa udānaḥ sa vāyuḥ sa ākāśastadeśadojaśca mahaścetyupāsītaujasvī mahasvānbhavati ya evaṃ veda*) (Chā. U. 3-13-5).

Udāna is of the nature of air and space. One should meditate on it as vigour and as greatness. One who knows this truth becomes vigorous and possessed of greatness; thus the matter of spiritual wealth is praised. This is the quality of Varuṇa. The present Ṛk describes that Agastya acquired this and fully obtained spiritual wealth as well.

क्रतूदक्षौ ह वा अस्य मित्रावरुणौ । एतन्नध्यात्मं स यदेव मनसा कामयत इदं मे स्यादिदं कुर्वीयेति स एव क्रतुरथ यदस्मै तत्समृध्यते स दक्षो मित्र एव क्रतुर्वरुणो दक्षो ब्रह्मैव मित्रः क्षत्रं वरुणोऽभिगंतैव ब्रह्म कर्ता क्षत्रियः ॥ (*kratūdakṣau ha vā asya mitrāvaruṇau | etannadhyātmaṃ sa yadeva manasā kāmayata idaṃ me syādidaṃ kurvīyeti sa eva kraturatha yadasmai tatsamṛdhyate sa dakṣo mitra eva kraturvaruṇo dakṣo brahmaiva mitraḥ kṣatraṃ varuṇo 'bhigaṃtaiva brahma kartā kṣatriyaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 4-1-4-1)

Of Mitra and Varuṇa, Mitra is of the form of resolve and Varuṇa of the form of spiritual power. To resolve for the accomplishment of a task is Mitra's function; to accomplish it is Varuṇa's. Further, Mitra is of the form of Brahma and Varuṇa of the form of Kṣatra; Brahma is of the form of kratu, and Varuṇa is dakṣa for everything. And: अयं वै लोको मित्रः आस् वरुणः । (*ayaṃ vai loko mitraḥ ās varuṇaḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 12-9-2-12)

### Printed p. 494
Mitra is of the form of this world and Varuṇa of the form of the divine world; this is praised in many places. Since these same elements were in their son Agastya, he became able to acquire together worldly wealth in the form of sons and so on, and moral and spiritual wealth in the form of dharma. In the present Ṛk the disciple thus praises the great qualities of the teacher.

Ṛṣi: Agastya, being the foremost among ascetics, is praised as a ṛṣi. The derivation of the word ṛṣi is given in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as follows; along with it the relation between creation and the ṛṣis is also shown:
असद्वा इदमग्र आसीत् । तदाहुः किं तदसदासीदित्यषयो वाव तेऽग्रेऽसदासीत्तदाहुः के त ऋषय इति प्राणा वा ऋषयस्ते यत्पुरास्मात्सर्व स्मादिदमिच्छंतः क्रमेण तपसारिषंस्तस्मादृषयः (*asadvā idamagra āsīt | tadāhuḥ kiṃ tadasadāsīdityaṣayo vāva te 'gre 'sadāsīttadāhuḥ ke ta ṛṣaya iti prāṇā vā ṛṣayaste yatpurāsmātsarva smādidamicchaṃtaḥ krameṇa tapasāriṣaṃstasmādṛṣayaḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-1-1)

Before creation only the non-existent was there. These very ṛṣis existed in that form. Who are the ṛṣis? They are the chief prāṇas. Before creation, desiring the creation of the world, they performed austerity and toiled for it; therefore they are called ṛṣis. Thus the derivation of the word ṛṣi is given (तपसारिषंस्तस्मादृषयः (*tapasāriṣaṃstasmādṛṣayaḥ*)). And: त्वयि तंतुमेशमिति योऽसावृषिभिस्तंतुस्ततस्तमेशदाह (*tvayi taṃtumeśamiti yo 'sāvṛṣibhistaṃtustatastameśadāha*) (Śa. Brā. 8-6-3-22).

They spun the sacrificial thread that is the universe; they became the cause of the world's expansion: thus the ṛṣi's power is praised. Therefore they are also said to be of the nature of Brahma, the root of creation: प्राणा वा ऋषयः प्रथमजास्तद्धि ब्रह्म प्रथमजं (*prāṇā vā ṛṣayaḥ prathamajāstaddhi brahma prathamajaṃ*) (Śa. Brā. 8-6-1-5). Thus the identity of the ṛṣis with Brahma is shown. If this is one kind of derivation, another derivation is possible in contrast to it. As stated in the Vācaspatya: यमति ज्ञानेन संसारपारं. (*yamati jñānena saṃsārapāraṃ.*)

Because one crosses to the far shore of saṃsāra through knowledge, the word ṛṣi formed from the root ṛṣ means "the knowers". Thus according to one derivation the ṛṣis are the root cause of the world's creation, and according to the other they are the cause of the cessation of saṃsāra. The description in the present Ṛk is that Agastya had both these powers. In उभौ वर्णौ पुपोष (*ubhau varṇau pupoṣa*) the capacity for creation is described, through the satisfaction of desire, and the power that is the means to the cessation of saṃsāra, through the acquisition of spiritual knowledge.

### Printed p. 495
The derivation above shows that the word ṛṣi is formed from the root ऋषी (ऋष्) गत् । (*ṛṣī (ṛṣ) gat |*), of the meaning "to go". Moreover, the scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit-English Dictionary, states that the word ṛṣi may also be formed from the root dṛś, and, in giving the meaning of the word ṛṣikṛt, cites two authorities and gives the meaning "Causing to see, enlightening". Of these examples, first:
इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरात् । आपिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भ्रमिरस्यृषिकृन्मर्त्यानां ॥ (*imāmagne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imamadhvānaṃ yamagāma dūrāt | āpiḥ pitā pramatiḥ somyānāṃ bhramirasyṛṣikṛnmartyānāṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-16)

In this Ṛk the word ṛṣikṛt is an epithet of Agni. Sāyaṇa gives this word the meaning दर्शनकारी (*darśanakārī*). Likewise in the Ṛk
ऋषिमना य ऋषिकृत्स्वर्णाः सहस्रणीथः पदवीः कवीनां । तृतीतियं धाम महिषः सिषासन्त्सोमो विराजमनु राजति ष्टुप् ॥ (*ṛṣimanā ya ṛṣikṛtsvarṇāḥ sahasraṇīthaḥ padavīḥ kavīnāṃ | tṛtītiyaṃ dhāma mahiṣaḥ siṣāsantsomo virājamanu rājati ṣṭup ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-96-18)

the word ṛṣimanāḥ is explained as सर्वदर्शनशील मनस्यः (*sarvadarśanaśīla manasyaḥ*) and ṛṣikṛt as सर्वस्य दर्शनकर्ता (*sarvasya darśanakartā*). In ordinary usage too, darśana is a synonym for knowledge of truth, and this conveys these ideas. It may be said that Agastya is praised as a ṛṣi because he obtained darśana in the form of knowledge of truth.

Satyāḥ: means "(blessings) whose fruit is true". The derivation of this word and its special meaning will be explained under Ṛk 1-180-7.
इमं नु सोममित्येते द्वे ऋचौ प्रयतो जपन् । सर्वान् कामानवाप्नोति पापेभ्यश्च प्रमुच्यते ॥ (*imaṃ nu somamityete dve ṛcau prayato japan | sarvān kāmānavāpnoti pāpebhyaśca pramucyate ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna 1-147)

The Ṛgvidhāna praises these mantras thus: if a man, with restraint of mind, recites the two Ṛks "Imaṃ somam" and "अगस्त्यः खनमानः (*agastyaḥ khanamānaḥ*)", all his desired ends are accomplished and he is freed from sin. **NOTE**

##### Grammar

- खनमानः—खनु अवधारणे । धातुः । लटि शानचादेशः । हास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इति ल सार्वधातुकमनुदात्तं भवति । ततो धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

### Printed p. 496
- खनित्रैः—पूर्वोक्तो धातुः । उषिखनिथ्यां कित्—(उ. सू. ४-६०१) इति स्प्रन् प्रत्ययः । इडागमः । व्यत्ययेन मध्योदात्तं भवति ।
- इच्छमानः—इषु इच्छायां धातुः । व्यत्ययेन लटि शानचादेशः । इषुगमियमां छः (पा. सू. ७-३-७७) इति धातोश्छकारांतादेशः । आनेमुक् इति मुकागमः । तास्यनुदात्तेत्—इति सूत्रेण ल सार्वधातुकमनुदात्तं भवति । ततः श विकरणस्वरो अवशिष्यते ।
- पुपोष—पुष पुष्टौ धातुः । लिट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः आगच्छति ।

Here ends the hundred and seventy-ninth sūkta.

## Sūkta 180 (Maṇḍala 1)
[[b-intro-none]]

The Sanskrit introduction (not set as a block in kn.md) says: Now in the twenty-fourth anuvāka there are twelve sūktas. Among them the first sūkta, "युवो रजांसि (*yuvo rajāṃsi*)", of ten Ṛks, is by Agastya, in the Triṣṭubh metre. By the Anukramaṇikā's technical usage (tu, hi etc.) this and the next four sūktas are addressed to the Aśvins; the Anukramaṇikā says "युवोर्दशाश्विनं (*yuvordaśāśvinaṃ*)". Five sūktas beginning with this, excluding the third, are employed in the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvinaśastra, for the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Aśvina section (Āśvalāyana) it is aphorised: "Yuvo rajāṃsīti pañcānāṃ tṛtīyam uddharet" (Ā. 4-15).

Anuvāda: With this sūkta the twenty-fourth anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala begins. In this anuvāka there are twelve sūktas. Of them this sūkta "युवो रजांसि (*yuvo rajāṃsi*)" is the first. It has ten Ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi; the metre is Triṣṭubh. Because the Anukramaṇikā uses technical words like "tu hi", the five sūktas from this one onward have the Aśvins as deity; the Anukramaṇikā says "युवोर्दशाश्विनं (*yuvordaśāśvinaṃ*)". Of these five Aśvin sūktas, excluding the third (sūkta 182), for the remaining four, namely sūktas 180, 181, 183, 184, there is application, for Triṣṭubh Ṛks, at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras and the Āśvinaśastra mantras; this is explained by the sūtra "Yuvo rajāṃsīti pañcānāṃ tṛtīyam uddharet" in the Āthāśvina section of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 4-15).

### Printed p. 497
Sūkta 180: Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 24; Sūkta 180; Aṣṭaka 2; Adhyāya 4; Varga 23-24. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Ṛṣi: Āgastya. Deity: Āśvinau. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वो रजां॑सि सु॒यमा॑सो॒ अश्वा॒ रथो॒ यद्वां॒ पर्यर्णां॑सि॒  ॑
> दीयत् ।  
> हि॒र॒ण्यया॑ नां प॒वयः॑ प्रषाय॒न्मध्वः॒ पिबं॑ता उ॒षसः॑ सचेथे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवोः । रजांसि । सुयमासः । अश्वाः । रथः । यत् । वां । परि । अर्णांसि ।  
> दीयत् ।  
> हिरण्ययाः । नां । पवयः । प्रषायन् । मध्वः । पिबंत् । उषसः । सचेथे इति ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवोर्युवयोरश्वा रथवोढारो रजांसि रंजकाल्लोकान्
> सुयमासः शोभननियमनाः । लोकत्रयसंचारिण इत्यर्थः । कदेति आह ।
> यद्यदा वां रथोर्णांस्यरणीयानभिमतदेशान् परि दीयत् परिगच्छेत् परिशो
> गच्छति वा । तदेत्यर्थः । दीयतिर्गतिकर्मा दीयति तकतीति तत्कर्मसु पातात् ।
> किंच रथागमनकाले वां युवयोः पवयो वज्रा रथनेमयो ना हिरण्यया
> हिरण्मयाः पुषायन् । पुष्पंत्यभिमतं । यद्वा । हिरण्ययानि पवयो
> मधुपात्राणि वां युवाभ्यामर्थाय । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्युवां मध्वो मधुनो
> मधुसदृशस्य सोमरसस्य ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठि ॥ सोमरसं पिबंतावास्वादयंतावुषस
> उषःसंबंधिनि काले सचेथे । यज्ञं संगच्छेथे । अत्र क्रमो न विवक्षितः ।
> उषःकाल एवागत्य मधुरं सोमरसं पिबतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, your horses, the bearers of the chariot, are good controllers (सुयमासः (*suyamāsaḥ*)), i.e. travellers through the three worlds, the रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) being the worlds that delight. When? When your chariot goes round (परि दीयत् (*pari dīyat*)) the अर्णांसि (*arṇāṃsi*), the desired places to be reached; or it goes about them. दीयति (*dīyati*) is a verb of motion, listed among the verbs of that class. Further, at the time of the chariot's coming, your पवयः (*pavayaḥ*), thunderbolts or chariot-fellies, golden (हिरण्यया (*hiraṇyayā*)), पुषायन् (*puṣāyan*) — they nourish (grant) what is desired. Or else: the पवयः (*pavayaḥ*) are golden honey-vessels, for your sake. Since it is so, you, drinking (मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*), genitive in the object sense) the Soma juice that is like honey, relish it and join (सचेथे (*sacethe*)) the sacrifice at the time of dawn. The order is not intended here: come at dawn itself and drink the sweet Soma juice.

### Printed p. 498

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे अश्विनौ (*he aśvinau*)—O Aśvin deities
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वां (*vāṃ*)—of you two
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—the chariot
- अर्णांसि (*arṇāṃsi*)—to the desired places
- परि दीयत् (*pari dīyat*)—goes around (then)
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—of you two
- अश्वाः (*aśvāḥ*)—the chariot-horses
- रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—the three worlds
- सुयमासः (*suyamāsaḥ*)—those that range regularly (and)
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- हिरण्ययाः (*hiraṇyayāḥ*)—golden
- पवयः (*pavayaḥ*)—thunderbolts or chariot-fellies
- प्रषायन् (*praṣāyan*)—sprinkle what is desired (rain down the wished-for object); or: हिरण्ययाः (*hiraṇyayāḥ*) golden पवयः (*pavayaḥ*) honey-vessels वां (*vāṃ*) for you two प्रषायन् (*praṣāyan*) pour (the desired honey); therefore you two
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—the honey-like Soma juice
- पिबंतौ (*pibaṃtau*)—drinking
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—at the time connected with dawn
- सचेथे (*sacethe*)—you join (the sacrifice)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, when your chariot sets out for the place appointed for you, your chariot-horses travel through the three worlds; at this time of the chariot's coming, your golden weapons or chariot-fellies rain down what is desired (the golden honey-vessels pour out for you the honey you like); therefore you two, coming at the dawn time to the sacrificial hall, drink the honey-like Soma juice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ashwins, your horses are traversers of the (three) regions, when your chariot proceeds to (its desired) quarters: the golden fellies of your wheels grant (whatever is wished for): drinking the Soma juice, you participate in the morning (rite).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Ratha: रथः रंहतेर्गतिकर्मणः । स्थिरतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य । रममाणोऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति वा । रपतेर्वा रसतेर्वा ॥ (*rathaḥ raṃhatergatikarmaṇaḥ | sthiratervā syādviparītasya | ramamāṇo 'smiṃstiṣṭhatīti vā | rapatervā rasatervā ‖*) (Ni. 9-11)

The Nirukta authors say that it is formed either from the root raṃh, which gives the meaning motion or speed; or, by inversion of letters, from sthira ("firm"); or from the root ram, meaning "sitting in it one rejoices"; or from the root rap or ras, meaning "to make a sound".

### Printed p. 499

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Citing the Ṛk वनस्पते वीड्वंगो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः । गोभिः सन्नद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेश्वानि ॥ (*vanaspate vīḍvaṃgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ | gobhiḥ sannaddho asi vīḷayasvāsthātā te jayatu jeśvāni ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-26), they have stated the derivation of the word ratha. [In some places the same word is also used to designate sons and others who move about in chariots.] In some places this word is also used as a synonym of Āditya (for example, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-2).

rajāṃsi—रजो रज्यतेर्ज्योती रज उच्यते उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका रजांस्युच्यंते । (*rajo rajyaterjyotī raja ucyate udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte |*) (Ni. 4-19). Derived from the root रंज् (*raṃj*), meaning "to shine", the word रजस् (*rajas*) means light, water and also the worlds.

Citing the Ṛk रजांसि चित्रा वि चरंति तन्यवो दिवः सम्राजा पयसा न उक्षतं । (*rajāṃsi citrā vi caraṃti tanyavo divaḥ samrājā payasā na ukṣataṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-5), the Nirukta-kāras have said that the word रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) means "worlds". In the 44th section of the 10th chapter of the Nirukta, in explaining the Ṛk अज्जामुक्थैरहिं गृणीषे बुध्ने नदीनां रजस्सु षीदन् । (*ajjāmukthairahiṃ gṛṇīṣe budhne nadīnāṃ rajassu ṣīdan |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-16), they say that the word रजस्सु (*rajassu*) means उदकेषु (*udakeṣu*), "in the waters"; and in the 7th section of the 12th chapter, in explaining the Ṛk एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमंजते । (*etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumaṃjate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1), they have explained रजसः (*rajasaḥ*) as the atmosphere (antarikṣa).

The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā, describing Viṣṇu's striding over the three worlds with श्रीणि भांति रजांस्यस्य यत्पदानि तु तेजसा (*śrīṇi bhāṃti rajāṃsyasya yatpadāni tu tejasā*), use the word रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) as a synonym of the three worlds. Rajaḥ, rajāṃsi are in general words meaning "worlds". But in Ṛks such as यन्ना सोमासो ममदन्यदुक्थोभे भयेते रजसी अपारे । (*yannā somāso mamadanyadukthobhe bhayete rajasī apāre |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-42-6) this word stands in the dual and carries the technical sense "heaven and earth". Only in a few places, that is, in

अहं कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेदाभिः (*ahaṃ kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedābhiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1)

### Printed p. 500

and one or two similar Ṛks, is the root meaning, रजसी जगद्रंजयंतौ (*rajasī jagadraṃjayaṃtau*), primary. In the present Ṛk the meaning is "the three shining worlds".

pavayaḥ—the word pavi is read among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23) and among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 3-11). Besides, हवी रथनेमिर्भवति यद्विपुनाति भूमिं (*havī rathanemirbhavati yadvipunāti bhūmiṃ*) (Ni. 5-5): the Nirukta-kāras explain that the wheel of a chariot is called pavi because it cleanses (digs up) the earth, and citing the Ṛk उर पॆव्या रथानामद्रिं भिंदंत्योजसा (*ura pèvyā rathānāmadriṃ bhiṃdaṃtyojasā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-9) they show that pavi there means the felloe of a chariot. Showing also the sense "spear" for the word pavi, citing the Ṛk पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकसादजो दिवो धर्ता सिंधुरापः समुद्रियः । (*pāvīravī tanyaturekasādajo divo dhartā siṃdhurāpaḥ samudriyaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-13), they explain (Ni. 12-30): पविः शल्यो भवति यद्विपुनाति कायं तद्वत्पवीरमायुधं तद्वानिंद्रः पवीरवान् । (*paviḥ śalyo bhavati yadvipunāti kāyaṃ tadvatpavīramāyudhaṃ tadvāniṃdraḥ pavīravān |*). Because it pierces the body, the spear is called pavi; because he possesses it, Indra has the epithet pavīravān. They explain it further by citing the Ṛk यो जनान् महिषा इवातितस्थौ पवीरवान् । उतापवीरवान् युधा । (*yo janān mahiṣā ivātitasthau pavīravān | utāpavīravān yudhā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-60-3). For the present Ṛk, Sāyaṇa gives the alternative meaning पवयः-वज्रा, रथनेमयो वा (*pavayaḥ-vajrā, rathanemayo vā*).

##### Grammar

- युवोः — षष्ठीद्विवचने परे सुपां सुपो भवंति इति वचनात् षष्ठीद्विवचनादेशः भवति । अतः योचॆ (पा. सू. ७-२-८९) इति यादेशः न भवति । शेषे लोपः इति टि इत्यस्य लोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तिः उदात्ता भवति ।
- सुयमासः — आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच् छंदसि (पा. सू. ६-२-११९) इति उत्तरपदस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । जसि परे आज्ञसेरसुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-५०) इति तस्य असुक् आगमः ।
- दीयत् — दीय गतौ छांदसः धातुः । लेटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने इतश्च लोपः (पा. सू. ३-४-९७) इति इकारलोपः । लेटोडाट् (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) इति अडागमः । यद्योगात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । धातुस्वरः अवतिष्ठते । दीयति, तकति इति यास्कैः गतिकर्मकधातूनां मध्ये पाठः कृतः ।

### Printed p. 501
- हिरण्ययाः — ऋत्त्व वास्तव्य वास्तु (पा. सू. ६-४-१७५) इति मकारलोपः आगत्य निपातितः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अकारे उदात्ते सति पूर्वानुदात्तेन सह एकादेशे कृते एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः इति उदात्तः भवति ।
- पुषायन् — पुष प्लुष स्नेहनसेचनपूरणेषु धातुः क्र्यादिः । लेटि प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनस्य अंतादेशे आगते इतश्चलोपः (पा. सू. ३-४-९७) इति अंत्यस्य इकारस्य लोपः । छंदसि शायजपि इति व्यत्ययेन श्नाविकरणस्य शायजादेशः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- मध्वः — जसादिषु छंदसि वा वचनम् इति गुणादीनां अभावे यणादेशः । कर्मार्थे षष्ठी आगता ।
- पिबंतौ — पा पाने धातुः । लटः शत्रादेशः । शप् विकरणः । पाघ्राध्मा (पा. सू. ७-३-७८) इति पिबादेशः । लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवतिष्ठते ।
- सचेथे — षच समवाये धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषद्विवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वमत्य॒स्याव॑ नक्षथो॒ यद्विप॑त्मनो॒ नर्य॑स्य॒ प्रय॑ज्योः ।  
> स्वसा॒ यद्वां॑ विश्वगूर्ति॒ भरा॑ति॒ वाजा॒येट्टे॑ मधुपावि॒षे च॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवं । अत्यस्य । अव । नक्षथः । यत् । विपत्मनः । नर्यस्य । प्रयज्योः ।  
> स्वसा । यत् । वां । विश्वगूर्ति इति विश्वगूर्ति । भराति । वाजाय । ईट्वे ।  
> मधुपौ । इषे । च ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां यदत्यस्यातनशीलस्य सततसंचारिणो विपत्मनो
> विविधगमनस्य विचित्रगमनस्य वा नर्यस्य मनुष्याणां हितस्य प्रयज्योः प्रकर्षेण

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Aśvins, you, to the chariot—which is अत्यस्य (*atyasya*), of constantly active nature, always moving; विपत्मनः (*vipatmanaḥ*), of varied or wondrous going; नर्यस्य (*naryasya*), beneficial to men; प्रयज्योः (*prayajyoḥ*), worthy of worship in a high degree".

### Printed p. 502

> पूज्यस्य ॥ एतानि कर्मणि षष्ठ्यंतानि ॥ उक्तरूपं रथमवावस्तात्तदुदयात्पूर्वं
> नक्षथः व्याप्प्नुथो देवयजनं गंतुं । किंच यद्यदा हे विश्वगूर्ति सर्वस्तुत्यौ
> सर्वदोद्दूर्णौ वा वां युवयोः स्वसा स्वसृस्थानीयौ स्वयंसारिणी पोषा
> भराति पोषते त्वदागमनाय प्रभातं करोति । यदा हे मधुपौ मधुरस्य
> सोमरसस्य पाशारौ युवां यजमानो वाजाय बलाय गमनाय वेषे
> प्रभूतान्नायेट्वे स्तौति । तदा रथं प्राप्नुथ इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These words are genitives standing in the sense of the object. The chariot so described you reach (नक्षथः (*nakṣathaḥ*) means "pervade"), going downward before sunrise, to go to the place of sacrifice. Further, when, O विश्वगूर्ति (*viśvagūrti*)—praised by all, or ever energetic—your sister, that is, Uṣas, who is in the position of a sister and moves of herself, nourishes (भराति (*bharāti*))—that is, brings the dawn for your coming; or when, O मधुपौ (*madhupau*), drinkers of the sweet Soma juice, the sacrificer praises you for strength (वाजाय (*vājāya*)), that is for might or for going, and for इषे (*iṣe*), abundant food—then you reach the chariot. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे अश्विनौ (*he aśvinau*)—O Aśvin deities
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अत्यस्य (*atyasya*)—constantly moving
- विपत्मनः (*vipatmanaḥ*)—of varied (wondrous) course
- नरस्य (*narasya*)—beneficial to men
- प्रयज्योः (*prayajyoḥ*)—especially worshipful (your chariot)
- अव (*ava*)—downward
- नक्षथः (*nakṣathaḥ*)—you attain (to set out for the sacrificial hall)
- किं च (*kiṃ ca*)—and
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- विश्वगूर्ती (*viśvagūrtī*)—O Aśvin deities, praised by all (ever fierce)
- वां (*vāṃ*)—to you two
- स्वसा (*svasā*)—Uṣas, in the place of a sister (having power of going of herself)
- भराति (*bharāti*)—nourishes (you) (makes light for your coming)
- तदा (*tadā*)—then
- मधुपौ (*madhupau*)—O Aśvin deities, drinkers of the Soma juice
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two
- वाजाय (*vājāya*)—for strength or for going
- इषे च (*iṣe ca*)—and for abundant food
- ईट्टे (*īṭṭe*)—(the sacrificer) praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, praised by all and drinkers of Soma! Your chariot—constantly moving, of varied course, beneficial to men, most worshipful—sets out towards the sacrificial hall when Uṣas, who is as a sister to you, has risen for the very purpose of your coming; then the sacrificer praises you, saying "Grant strength and food".

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Direct downwards (the course) of your (car) swift moving, variously going, friendly to man, and to be especially venerated, when, all adorable, your sister (dawn) prepares (for your approach), and (the institutor of the ceremony) worships you, drinkers of the Soma juice, for the sake (of obtaining) strength and food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk both the nature of the Aśvins' chariot and the relation between them and the goddess Uṣas are described.

### Printed p. 503
atyasya—आतनशीलस्य, सततसंचारिणः (*ātanaśīlasya, satatasaṃcāriṇaḥ*). It means "having the nature of moving about always without interruption". As an adjective of the chariot this word shows the chariot's nature. In general the word is used as an adjective of a horse and of Āditya, which are by nature always moving.

In the Ṛk एष प्र पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिषोऽत्यो न योषामुदयंस्त भुर्वणिः । दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसं । (*eṣa pra pūrvīrava tasya camriṣo 'tyo na yoṣāmudayaṃsta bhurvaṇiḥ | dakṣaṃ mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayaṃ rathamāvṛtyā hariyogamṛbhvasaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-1), अत्यः (*atyaḥ*) is used of a horse; and in अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः । मृगाणां न हेतयो यंति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमाया अभि द्यून् । (*asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyāmatyo na yaṃsadyakṣabhṛdvicetāḥ | mṛgāṇāṃ na hetayo yaṃti cemā bṛhaspaterahimāyā abhi dyūn |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-4) the use of the word is such that it also means आतनशीलः आदित्यः (*ātanaśīlaḥ ādityaḥ*). In the present Ṛk it is an adjective of the chariot.

viśvagūrti—the word गूर्ति (*gūrti*) is derived from the root गुरी (गुर्) (*gurī (gur)*) उद्यमने (*udyamane*). In all places where it is used, the word गूर्ति (*gūrti*) shows not merely "exertion" or "effort at an undertaking" but that in the exertion there is also faith and resolve. For example, in यूपव्रस्का उत ये यूपवाहाश्चषालं ये अश्वयूपाय तक्षति । ये चार्वते पचनं संभरंत्युतो तेषामभिगूर्तिर्न इन्वतु । (*yūpavraskā uta ye yūpavāhāścaṣālaṃ ye aśvayūpāya takṣati | ye cārvate pacanaṃ saṃbharaṃtyuto teṣāmabhigūrtirna invatu |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-6), Sāyaṇa has explained it as resolve accompanied by faith. In the same way the meanings suited to the context must be understood for words like स्वगूर्ति (*svagūrti*), राधोगूर्ति (*rādhogūrti*), अरिगूर्ति (*arigūrti*), and for गूर्तमनाः (*gūrtamanāḥ*), गूर्तश्रवाः (*gūrtaśravāḥ*), गूर्तवसुः (*gūrtavasuḥ*). The Nirukta-kāras, citing the Ṛk समस्मिञ्चायमान आसत ग्ना उतेमवर्धन्नद्यंः स्वगूर्ताः । महे यत्त्वा पुरूरवो रणायावर्धयन् दस्युहत्याय देवाः ॥ (*samasmiñcāyamāna āsata gnā utemavardhannadyaṃḥ svagūrtāḥ | mahe yattvā purūravo raṇāyāvardhayan dasyuhatyāya devāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-7), in which the word स्वगूर्ताः (*svagūrtāḥ*) occurs, have explained that word as स्वयंगामिन्यः (*svayaṃgāminyaḥ*). Here there is no reason for the word गूर्त (*gūrta*) to carry meanings such as faith or resolve; it is understood that the usage is only in the sense of going. Likewise,
