in अपद्यथा नो वरुणः सुकीर्तिरिषत् वर्षदरिगूर्तः सूरिः । (*apadyathā no varuṇaḥ sukīrtiriṣat varṣadarigūrtaḥ sūriḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-186-3) too, Sāyaṇa explains शत्रुहननाय उद्युक्तः (*śatruhananāya udyuktaḥ*), showing only the meaning of exertion. But in words such as गूर्तक्रवाः (*gūrtakravāḥ*), गूर्तमवाः (*gūrtamavāḥ*) the word गूर्त (*gūrta*) has the meaning "praiseworthy". For example, in स प्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः । (*sa prādhato nahuṣo daṃsujūtaḥ śardhastaro narāṃ gūrtaśravāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122 10) he has explained गूर्तक्रवाः (*gūrtakravāḥ*) as उद्यूर्णदीप्तिः अथवा प्रख्यातान्नो वा (*udyūrṇadīptiḥ athavā prakhyātānno vā*): one whose splendour is praiseworthy or manifest, or one whose food has gained renown; or else it is understood as "praiseworthy food". And for the word गूर्तमनाः (*gūrtamanāḥ*) in Ṛk 6-63-4 the meaning given is प्रकर्षेण उद्युक्तमनाः (*prakarṣeṇa udyuktamanāḥ*). Since a meaning suited to the context must thus be given for गूर्त (*gūrta*), in the present Ṛk the word विश्वगूर्ति (*viśvagūrti*), an adjective of the Aśvin deities, gives the meaning सर्वस्तुत्यौ (*sarvastutyau*), "those praised by all".

svasā bharāti—here the word स्वसृ (*svasṛ*) is meant to denote Uṣas. The relation between the Aśvins and Uṣas, and the point that when the Aśvins take part in the sacrifice the goddess Uṣas appears and marks the auspicious time, will be explained later.

##### Grammar

- नक्षथः — णक्ष गतौ धातुः । नो नः इति आदेः नत्वम् । लट् मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- विपत्मनः — पत्ल्य गतौ धातुः । औणादिकः मनिन् प्रत्ययः । विविधाः पत्मानः यस्य तस्य । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदं इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- नर्यस्य — नराय हितम् । तस्य । छंदसि च (पा. सू. ५-४-१४२) इति यत् प्रत्ययः । यस्येति च इति अकारलोपः । यतो नावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- विश्वगूर्ती — विश्वा गूर्तिः ययोस्तौ । आमंत्रितस्य च (पा. सू. ८-१-१९) इति निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- भराति — भृञ् भरणे धातुः । लेटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने तिप् । लेटोडाट् (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) इति तस्य आडागमः । शप्निमित्तेन धातोः गुणः । र परे

- यद्योगात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । शप् तिप् अनुदात्तौ इति धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- ईट्टे—ईड स्तुत् धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । व्यत्ययेन आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- इषे—सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू ६-१-१८) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वं पय॑ उ॒स्रिया॑यामधत्तं प॒क्वमा॒माया॒मव॒पूर्व्यं॒गोः।  
> अं॒तर्यद्व॒निनो॑ वामृतप्सू ह्वा॒रो न शुचि॒र्यज॑ते ह॒विष्मा॑न् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवं । पयः । उस्रियायां । अधत्तं । पक्वं । अमायां । अव । पूर्व्यं । गोः ।  
> अंतः । यत् । वनिनः । वां । ऋतप्सू इत्यृतप्सू । ह्वारः । न । शुचिः । यजते ।  
> हविष्मान् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवं युवामुस्रियायां! गोनामैतत् । भोगोत्सृविण्यां
> गनि पयोऽधत्तं । आधारयतं । स्थापितवंत् । तथामायामपक्वायां पक्वं
> परिपक्वं भोगयोग्यं गोसंबंधि दुग्धं पूर्व्यं पूर्वभवं तत्रैवोत्पन्नमवावस्तादधारयतं । गवि क्षीरमुत्पाद पुनर्भोगाय पृथक्कृतवंतावित्यर्थः ।
> यद्यस्मात् हे ऋतप्पू सत्यस्वरूपौ यज्ञियहविर्भक्षयितारौ ना हे अश्विन् वां
> वनिन उदकवत उदकोपलक्षितहविष्मतो यज्ञस्यांतर्मध्यॆ हविष्मान् प्रदेयहविषा तद्वान् शुचिः शुद्धो यजमानो यजते पूजयति युवां तस्मादेवमकुरुतं । यद्वा! यदैवं यजमानः करोति तदेत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वनिनो
> वनसंबंधिवृक्षसमूहस्यांतर्मध्यॆ ह्वारो न चोर इव । स यथा जागरूको
> वर्तते तथा यजमानोऽपीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, you placed (अधत्तं (*adhattaṃ*), "caused to hold, established") milk in the उस्रियायां (*usriyāyāṃ*)—गोनामैतत् (*gonāmaitat*), this is a name of the cow—the cow that yields enjoyments. Likewise, in the unripe (अमायां (*amāyāṃ*)) one you set down the ripe (पक्वं (*pakvaṃ*)), fully matured milk of the cow, fit for enjoyment, which was formed there itself (पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*), "of prior origin"). The meaning is: having produced milk in the cow, you separated it again for enjoyment.

Since, O Ṛtapsū (of true nature, consumers of the sacrificial oblation), O Aśvins, the pure sacrificer, who has the oblation to be offered, worships you in the midst of the sacrifice that is वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*), "possessed of water", that is, of the oblation marked by water—therefore you did so. Or else: "when the sacrificer does thus, then" is the meaning. An illustration follows: वनिनो वनसंबंधिवृक्षसमूहस्यांतर्मध्यॆ ह्वारो न (*vanino vanasaṃbaṃdhivṛkṣasamūhasyāṃtarmadhyè hvāro na*), like a thief in the midst of a group of forest trees; as he is watchful, so the sacrificer too is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे ऋतप्यू (*he ṛtapyū*)—O Aśvin deities, of true nature (eaters of the sacrificial oblation)
- यॆत् (*yèt*)—for which reason
- हविष्मान् (*haviṣmān*)—the one who has the oblation to be offered to you
- शुचिः (*śuciḥ*)—and pure
- यजमाननु (*yajamānanu*)—the sacrificer
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two
- वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*)—of the sacrifice endowed with oblation
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle
- [or वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*)—of the group of trees connected with the forest; अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—situated in the midst]
- ह्यारः नः (*hyāraḥ naḥ*)—as watchful as a thief is (so watchfully)
- यजते (*yajate*)—worships
- तत् (*tat*)—therefore
- (हे अश्विनौ (*he aśvinau*)—O Aśvin deities)
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- उस्तियायां (*ustiyāyāṃ*)—in the cow
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- अधत्तं (*adhattaṃ*)—you established
- गोः (*goḥ*)—in the udder of the cow
- आमायां (*āmāyāṃ*)—unripe
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—arisen in that very place
- पक्वं (*pakvaṃ*)—ripe milk
- अव (*ava*) (अधत्तं (*adhattaṃ*))—you set down
**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, of true nature (eaters of the oblation that is a limb of the sacrifice)! The sacrificer, equipped with oblation and the rest, worships you in the sacrifice as watchfully as a thief hiding in a forest. Therefore you established abundant milk in their cows, and you also produced ripe milk in the heifers belonging to them.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You have restored milk to the cow : you have (brought) down the
prior mature (secretion) into the unripe (or barren udder) of the cow : the
devont offerer of the oblation worships you, whose froms are truth, (as
vigilant in the midst of the ceremony), as a thief (in the midst) of a thicket,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋतप्पू (*ṛtappū*)—The use of the word ṛta in the senses of truth, sacrifice and so on, and how ṛta reflects the order of the universe, were explained earlier in this same volume in the Special Topics on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-179-2. In the present verse the Aśvin deities are described by the word ऋतप्पू (*ṛtappū*) as being of the nature of truth. Because they pervade the whole universe in the forms of heaven and earth, of sun and moon, and of day and night, the sense is that they themselves are the whole universe, which is of the nature of truth.

वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*)—It has been shown that two or three kinds of meaning are possible for this word. First, it is explained as उदकवंतः उदकोपलक्षित हविष्मतो यज्ञस्य (*udakavaṃtaḥ udakopalakṣita haviṣmato yajñasya*); second, as वनसंबंधिवृक्षसमूहस्य (*vanasaṃbaṃdhivṛkṣasamūhasya*).

### Printed p. 507

The word वन (*vana*) is listed among the names of rays (Ni. 2-15) and among the names of water (Ni. 2-23). Besides these meanings, the word is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā in many other senses too. From the root वन—संभक्तौ (*vana—saṃbhaktau*), which gives the sense of a very intense wish or longing, or from the root वनु—याचने (*vanu—yācane*), which gives the sense of asking, entreating, nominal and verbal forms such as वनानि, वनिनः वनामहे, वनतं (*vanāni, vaninaḥ vanāmahe, vanataṃ*) are formed and used, so some examples may be looked at to understand these differences of meaning. Where nominal forms are used the meanings are venerable, water, forest-tree, flower, fruit and so on; where verbal forms are used the meanings are to kill, to give, to serve with devotion and so on. The occasions for these, with examples, were explained at length earlier in this same volume in the Special Topics on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-3. In the present verse the sense is either "of the sacrifice marked by water" or "of the group of trees".

द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*)—The word द्वार (*dvāra*) has been explained as "thief". The meaning thief, deceiver has come to this word by tradition; its original meaning is crooked, bent.

क्रत्वा हि द्रोणे अज्यसेऽग्ने वाजी न कृत्व्यः । परिज्जीव स्वधा गयोऽत्यो न ह्वार्यः शिशुः ॥ (*kratvā hi droṇe ajyase 'gne vājī na kṛtvyaḥ | parijjīva svadhā gayo 'tyo na hvāryaḥ śiśuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-2-8)
Here the word ह्वार्यः (*hvāryaḥ*) shows a quality of the horse; here it is an epithet of Agni. The common property of the horse and Agni is indicated by this word: as the horse has a crooked course, so the flame of Agni also spreads with a crooked course. Likewise in

उत स्म दुर्गृभीयसे पुत्रो न ह्वार्याणां । पुरू यो दग्धासि वनाग्ने पशुर्न यवसे ॥ (*uta sma durgṛbhīyase putro na hvāryāṇāṃ | purū yo dagdhāsi vanāgne paśurna yavase ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-9-4)
the word ह्वार्याणां (*hvāryāṇāṃ*) means कुटिलं गच्छतां सर्पाणां (*kuṭilaṃ gacchatāṃ sarpāṇāṃ*), and conveys the crooked motion of snakes that glide crookedly. With this original meaning, the word has also been used as a synonym for thieves and the like who have the same kind of course: a deceiver who has neither a straight, that is, truthful, disposition nor conduct. Since the thief too has this quality, ह्वारः (*hvāraḥ*) also comes to mean a thief. And further,

वि यदस्थाद्यजतो वातचोदितो ह्वारो न वक्वा जरणा अनाकृतः । तस्य पत्मन्दक्षुषः कृष्णजिंहसः शुचिजन्मनो रज आ व्यध्वनः ॥ (*vi yadasthādyajato vātacodito hvāro na vakvā jaraṇā anākṛtaḥ | tasya patmandakṣuṣaḥ kṛṣṇajiṃhasaḥ śucijanmano raja ā vyadhvanaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-141-7)

### Printed p. 508

in such verses it means a gossipmonger**NOTE**. Since the gossipmonger spreads about beyond measure, he has no straight and definite goal, and so he too has a crooked course. Therefore the वक्व (*vakva*) has the epithet द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*). In the present verse it is explained as thief. But here one more point must be noted. Ordinarily, when this word is used as an epithet of a thief it shows his deceitfulness. But in the present verse it shows the quality common to the performer of the sacrifice and the thief: as the thief carries out his act of theft with vigilance, so the sacrificer carries out his. The devotion to the work and the vigilance of both are the common property here.

उस्रियायां (*usriyāyāṃ*)—This word is listed among the cow-names अघ्न्या, उस्रा, उस्रिया (*aghnyā, usrā, usriyā*) (Ni. 3-8): उस्रियेति गोनाम । उस्राविणः अस्यां भोगाः । (*usriyeti gonāma | usrāviṇaḥ asyāṃ bhogāḥ |*) The Nirukta-author says that the name उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*) has come because milk, the means of happiness, flows; he quotes the verse

उत वां विक्षु मद्यास्वंधो गाव आपश्च पीपयंत देवीः । उतो नो अस्य पूर्व्यः पतिर्दन्वीतं पापं पयस उस्रियायाः ॥ (*uta vāṃ vikṣu madyāsvaṃdho gāva āpaśca pīpayaṃta devīḥ | uto no asya pūrvyaḥ patirdanvītaṃ pāpaṃ payasa usriyāyāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-153-4)
and explains as above (Ni. 4-19).

In the present verse the situation is indicated that the Aśvin deities established milk in the udder of a cow that was unripe. This situation is indicated in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā. In some places its story is told thus:

तयुर्नाम राजर्षिः । सोऽश्विनौ परिचर‍्यया तुष्टावुवाच । मम गौरधेनुनिर्वृत्तप्रसवा वृद्धा च । तां मे धेनुं कुरुतमिति । तामस्मै अश्विनौ धेनुं चक्रतुरित्यत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते ॥ श (*tayurnāma rājarṣiḥ | so 'śvinau paricaryayā tuṣṭāvuvāca | mama gauradhenunirvṛttaprasavā vṛddhā ca | tāṃ me dhenuṃ kurutamiti | tāmasmai aśvinau dhenuṃ cakraturityatretihāsamācakṣate ‖ śa*)**NOTE**

When the royal sage Śayu worshipped the Aśvin deities they were pleased with that worship. Then the royal sage prayed to them: "My cow is barren; make it bear a calf and give milk, and turn it into a milch cow." On his prayer they favoured that aged cow so that it became a milch cow. Many Ṛks indicate this situation. For example—

अथेनुं हस्ता स्तर्यं १ विषक्तामपिन्वतं तयवे अश्विना गां । (*athenuṃ hastā staryaṃ 1 viṣaktāmapinvataṃ tayave aśvinā gāṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-20)

### Printed p. 509

युवं धेनुं शयवे नाधितायापिन्वतमश्विना पूर्व्याय । (*yuvaṃ dhenuṃ śayave nādhitāyāpinvatamaśvinā pūrvyāya |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-8)
दशस्यंता शयवे पिप्यथुर्गामिति च्यवाना सुमतिं भुरण्यू । (*daśasyaṃtā śayave pipyathurgāmiti cyavānā sumatiṃ bhuraṇyū |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-7)
ता वर्तियातं जयुषा वि पर्वतमपिन्वतं शयवे धेनुमश्विना । (*tā vartiyātaṃ jayuṣā vi parvatamapinvataṃ śayave dhenumaśvinā |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-13)
In these and many other Ṛks the situation is told in which the Aśvin deities turned Śayu's barren cow into a milch cow. The present verse too states the same matter, but the name Śayu is not given here. In some places the story is that they made the aged cow bear a calf and filled her with milk; in other places that they turned a barren cow into a milch cow and filled her with milk.

आमायां (*āmāyāṃ*)—अपरिपक्वायां (*aparipakvāyāṃ*): "that which is not ripe" is the meaning. Here it is an epithet of the cow's udder. The word is used of a cow whose udder has not yet filled with milk, or of a barren cow. Just as the Aśvin deities filled such an unripe udder with milk, this skill is described in the case of other deities as well. For example—

इमौ देवौ जायमानौ जुषंतेमौ तमांसि गूहतामजुष्टा । अभ्यामिंद्रः पक्वमामास्वंतः सोमापूषभ्यां जनदुस्रियासु ॥ (*imau devau jāyamānau juṣaṃtemau tamāṃsi gūhatāmajuṣṭā | abhyāmiṃdraḥ pakvamāmāsvaṃtaḥ somāpūṣabhyāṃ janadusriyāsu ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-40-2)
Here it is said that Soma and Pūṣan, both of them, filled the udder of a young cow with milk and turned her into a milch cow. The word आम (*āma*) ordinarily means unripe. Although it is an epithet that can be used in any context, in the Ṛksaṃhitā it is used as an epithet only when describing the udder of a cow, and indicates the sense "not ripened with milk", that is, an udder without milk. For example (U. Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-14; 4-3-9; 2-35-6; 2-40-2; 6-77-4; 8-78-7 and so on)**NOTE**.

##### Grammar

- उस्रियायाम्—वस निवासे इति धातुः । वसंति इति उस्रियाः । “यन्न पदार्थविशेषसमुत्थं प्रत्ययतः प्रकृतेश्च तदूह्यम्” इति वचनात् वस धातोः कर्तरि रियक् प्रत्ययः आगतः इति कार्यात् ऊह्यम् । कित्त्वात् धातोः संप्रसारणं भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण इकार उदात्तो भवति ।

### Printed p. 510

- अथत्तम्—डुधाज् धारणपोषणयोः इति धातुः अंतर्भानित ण्यर्थकः । लज् मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- पूर्व्यम्—पूर्वे भवन् । भवे छंदसि (पा. सू. ४-४-११०) इति यत् प्रत्ययः । यतोनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- ह्यारः—हृ कौटल्ये इति धातुः । अस्मात् ण्यंतात् अच् प्रत्ययः । अचोञ्ञति इति ऋकारस्य वृद्धिः । शेरनिटि (पा. सू. ६-४-५१) इति णिचः लोपः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- यजते—यष्टृत्तान्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधो भवति अतः धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वं ह॑ घ॒र्मं मधु॑मंत॒मत्र॑ये॒ऽपो न क्षोदो॑वृणीतमे॒षे ।  
> तद्वां॑ नरावश्विना॒ पश्व॑इष्टी॒ रथ्ये॑व च॒क्रा प्रति॑ यंति॒ मध्वः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवं । ह । घर्मं । मधुमंतं । अत्रये । अपः । न । क्षोडः । अवृणीतं ।  
> एषे ।  
> शत् । नां । नरौ । अश्विना । पश्वः इष्टिः । रथ्या इव । चक्रा । प्रति । यंति । मध्वः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रेतिहासमाहुः। प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरंतमत्रिं राक्षसास्तप्ते घर्मेऽपातयन्।
> स च तस्यमानोऽश्विन्यौतुष्टाव । शौ च: स्तुत्या हृष्टमनसावरक्षतामिति । अपरेऽग्नौ
> क्षिप्तमपालायतामित्याहुरिति । हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां मथुमंतंपयोथृत
> रूपाभ्यां मधुथ्यां तद्वंतं घर्मं दीप्तं प्रवर्ग्यमेषे सौख्यमिच्छतेऽत्रय

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here they tell an itihāsa. While Atri was performing with the Pravargya, the rākṣasas made him fall into the heated gharma. Thrown thus, he praised the two Aśvins, and the two, with delighted minds, protected him. Others say that, thrown into the fire, he escaped. O Aśvins, you two (युवं युवां (*yuvaṃ yuvāṃ*)) the मथुमंतं (*mathumaṃtaṃ*)—possessing honey by the two forms of milk and ghee**NOTE**—the blazing gharma, the Pravargya, for Atri, who seeks comfort (*eṣe saukhyamicchate 'traya*)

### Printed p. 511
#### Ṛk 3 (continuing)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एतन्नाम्मे महर्षये क्षोदः क्षोदांसि क्षोद्यमानान्यपो नोदकानीवावृणीतं।
> अवारयतं। औष्ण्यं शैत्यसुखं कृतवंतौ। तप्तघर्मसकाशाद्भक्षितवानित्यर्थः । यद्वा।
> अत्रये क्षोदः । उदकनामैतत् । तत्स्थं शैत्यं लक्ष्यते । अपः क्षोदो न । अप इति
> षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया । उदकानां शैत्यं यथा भवति तद्वत् । पक्षांतरे तु घर्मं
> दीप्तमग्निं मधुमंतं कृत्वावृणीतं । सुखयतमित्यर्थः । तथा च मंत्रांतरं ।
> तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावंतमत्रये । ऋ. १-११२-७ । इति । तत्तस्मात् यस्मादेवं
> तस्मात् हे नरौ नेतारौ नराकारौ वाश्विनाश्विन् वां युवाभ्यां पश्वइष्टिः । पशुरित्यग्नेर्नाम । अग्निः पशुरासीदित्यादिश्रुतेः । तै. सं. ५-७-२६ । यद्वा । पशुप्रियत्वात्पशुरित्युच्यते । तस्याग्नेरिष्टिर्भवति । अग्नौ यागः सर्वो युष्मदर्थं प्रवर्तत इत्यर्थः ।
> यद्वा । पशुसाध्यो यागो युवाभ्यां प्रवर्तत इति शेषः। आश्विनं धूम्रललामनू
> लभेत यो दुब्राह्मणः सोमं पिपासेत् । तै. सं. २-१-१०-१ । इत्यादिनाप्यश्विभ्यां
> पशुर्विहितः । तथा मध्यो मधुसदृशाः सोमरसा अपि युवाभ्यां प्रति यंति ।
> अभिगच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथ्येव चक्रा रथसंबंधीनि चक्रा चक्राणीव । तानि यथा
> प्रवणदेशमभिगच्छंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains the word क्षोदः (*kṣodaḥ*) (kṣodaḥ) as "waters that are agitated". The Aśvins "chose" or warded off, as water does, the heat for Atri. They made it a pleasant coolness: they drank from the hot gharma, that is, they took it into themselves. Alternatively, क्षोदः (*kṣodaḥ*) is a name of water, and what is meant is the coolness that resides in it. In अपः क्षोदो न (*apaḥ kṣodo na*) the accusative अपः (*apaḥ*) stands for the genitive, so that it means "as the coolness of waters comes about". On the other view, they made the blazing fire (gharma) honeyed and so brought it relief, that is, they gave it comfort. For this he cites another mantra: तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावंतमत्रये (*taptaṃ gharmamomyāvaṃtamatraye*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-7). "Therefore", for that reason, O leaders, or those of human form, O Aśvins, पश्वइष्टिः (*paśvaiṣṭiḥ*) (paśvā iṣṭiḥ) is for you. *paśuḥ* is a name of Agni, according to the Śruti *agniḥ paśurāsīt* and the rest (Tai. Saṃ. 5-7-26). Or Agni is called paśu because he is dear to animals, and the offering belongs to that Agni: the whole sacrifice in the fire proceeds for your sake. Or else (the sense is) that the sacrifice to be performed with an animal proceeds through you; and an animal for the Aśvins is prescribed by such texts as आश्विनं धूम्रललामनू लभेत (*āśvinaṃ dhūmralalāmanū labheta*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-10-1). Likewise the honey-like Soma juices go towards you, come to you. The illustration is रथ्येव चक्रा (*rathyeva cakrā*): as the wheels belonging to a chariot go towards a sloping place, so do the juices go to you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- *he aśvin*—O Aśvin deities
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—endowed with honey in the form of milk and ghee
- घर्मं (*gharmaṃ*)—the blazing fire
- एषे (*eṣe*)—(cast into the fire) desiring (comfort)
- आत्रये (*ātraye*)—to one named Atri
- क्षोदः (*kṣodaḥ*)—agitated
- अपः न (*apaḥ na*)—(as) water (is cool)
- अवृणीतं ह (*avṛṇītaṃ ha*)—you indeed warded off (the heat of the fire) and made it cool
- तत् (*tat*)—therefore
- नरौ (*narau*)—O leaders, or those of human form
- *he aśvin*—O Aśvin deities
- वां (*vāṃ*)—for you two
- पश्वइष्टिः (*paśvaiṣṭiḥ*)—the sacrifice in the fire, or the animal sacrifice (has begun)
- मध्यः (*madhyaḥ*)—honey-like (Soma juices)
- रथ्या (*rathyā*)—belonging to a chariot
- चक्रा इव (*cakrā iva*)—like wheels (that reach the desired place)
- प्रति यंति (*prati yaṃti*)—set out towards (you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, it is well known that for Atri, who had been cast into the fire and longed for release, you made the fire, blazing and joined with honey in the form of milk and ghee, as cool as agitated water. For that very reason, O Aśvins, leaders of the sacrifice, this animal sacrifice has begun for you, and this honey-like Soma juice has been offered.

### Printed p. 512

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You rendered the heat as soothing as sweet butter to Atri ; wishing (for relief), and invested it with coolness, like water : therefore, for you, Ashwins, leaders (of rites), the fire-offering (is made) ; to you the Soma juices run like chariot wheels (down a declivity).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

To understand the present Ṛk fully, one must know the nature of the deities Agni, Atri and the Aśvins and their mutual relation, and must learn what place they have in the Pravargya, which is of the nature of gharma.

Sāyaṇa has shown that the sentence मधुमंतं घर्मं अत्रये............ अवृणीतं ह (*madhumaṃtaṃ gharmaṃ atraye............ avṛṇītaṃ ha*) can be construed in two ways. These constructions accord with the meaning to be given to the words Atri and gharma.

1. First, Sāyaṇa points to this story as indicating how the Aśvins helped the great seer Atri:
अत्रेतिहासमाहुः । प्रवर्ज्येण प्रचरंतमत्रिं राक्षसास्तप्ते घर्मेऽपातयन् । स च तप्यमानोऽश्विन् तुष्टाव । शौ च स्तुत्या हृष्टमनसावरक्षतामिति ॥ (*atretihāsamāhuḥ | pravarjyeṇa pracaraṃtamatriṃ rākṣasāstapte gharme 'pātayan | sa ca tapyamāno 'śvin tuṣṭāva | śau ca stutyā hṛṣṭamanasāvarakṣatāmiti ‖*).
While Atri was engaged in the Pravargya, demons threw him into the blazing gharma. Then, tormented, Atri cried to the Aśvin deities and prayed to them for protection. Pleased, they protected him; so it is said.

2. Second, just as the present Ṛk has मधमंतं घर्म० आत्रये अवृणीतं (*madhamaṃtaṃ gharma0 ātraye avṛṇītaṃ*), so Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-7 has तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावंतमत्रये (*taptaṃ gharmamomyāvaṃtamatraye*). In that place Sāyaṇa explains the purport just as he has done in the present Ṛk. But there he also cites the view of Yāska: यास्कपक्षे तु अत्रये हविषामक्तेऽग्नये हविरुत्पत्यर्थं सूरकिरणसंतप्तं घर्म० नैदाघं अहः ओम्यावंतं तृप्तिहेतु वृष्टु दकोपेतं कृतवंतौ इति योज्यं । (*yāskapakṣe tu atraye haviṣāmakte 'gnaye havirutpatyarthaṃ sūrakiraṇasaṃtaptaṃ gharma0 naidāghaṃ ahaḥ omyāvaṃtaṃ tṛptihetu vṛṣṭu dakopetaṃ kṛtavaṃtau iti yojyaṃ |*). In Yāska's view, he explains, the word Atri means the fire that eats the oblations, and the sense is that for such a fire they made the day, heated by the sun's rays and belonging to the hot season, one provided with satisfying rain-water. In explaining the present Ṛk also, Sāyaṇa cites the Ṛk 1-112-7: पक्षांतरे तु घर्मं दीप्तमग्निं मधुमंतं कृत्वावृणीतं (*pakṣāṃtare tu gharmaṃ dīptamagniṃ madhumaṃtaṃ kṛtvāvṛṇītaṃ*) ... तथा च मंत्रांतरं तप्तं घर्म (*tathā ca maṃtrāṃtaraṃ taptaṃ gharma*)

### Printed p. 513
मोम्यानंतमत्रये (*momyānaṃtamatraye*) ... **NOTE**. So it appears that the word Atri may be given two meanings: one referring to the seer Atri and one referring to Agni. Or, since the seer Atri is a portion of the god Agni, an identity of the two may also be asserted. In some places Atri is said to be Agni's son, in others to be of the form of Agni.

The story of the birth of the seer Atri is told in the Bṛhaddevatā verses as follows:
त्रिसांवत्सरिकं सत्त्वं प्रजाकामः प्रजापतिः । आहरत्सहितः साध्यैर्विश्वेदेवैः सहेति च ॥ तत्र वाग्दीक्षणीयायां आजगाम शरीरिणी । तां दृष्ट्वा युगपत्तत्र कस्याथ वरुणस्य च ॥ शुक्रं चस्कंद तद्वायुरग्नौ प्रास्यद्यदृच्छया । ततोऽर्चिभ्यो भृगुर्जज्ञॆ अंगारेष्टंगिरा ऋषिः ॥ प्रजापतिं सुतौ दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा वागभ्यभाषत । अभ्यामृषिस्तृतीयोऽपि भवेदत्रैव मे सुतः ॥ प्रजापतिस्तथेत्युक्तः प्रत्यभाषत भारतीं । ऋषिरत्रिस्ततो जज्ञे सूर्यानलसमद्युतिः ॥ (*trisāṃvatsarikaṃ sattvaṃ prajākāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ | āharatsahitaḥ sādhyairviśvedevaiḥ saheti ca ‖ tatra vāgdīkṣaṇīyāyāṃ ājagāma śarīriṇī | tāṃ dṛṣṭvā yugapattatra kasyātha varuṇasya ca ‖ śukraṃ caskaṃda tadvāyuragnau prāsyadyadṛcchayā | tato 'rcibhyo bhṛgurjajñè aṃgāreṣṭaṃgirā ṛṣiḥ ‖ prajāpatiṃ sutau dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā vāgabhyabhāṣata | abhyāmṛṣistṛtīyo 'pi bhavedatraiva me sutaḥ ‖ prajāpatistathetyuktaḥ pratyabhāṣata bhāratīṃ | ṛṣiratristato jajñe sūryānalasamadyutiḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 5-97 to 101).
It is well known that Prajāpati, desiring offspring, together with the Sādhyas and the Viśvedevas, performed a sattra lasting three years. At that time the goddess Vāk came in bodily form to that sattra. As soon as they saw her, Prajāpati and Varuṇa had a discharge of seed; the Wind cast it into the fire. Then from the flames of that fire Bhṛgu was born, and from the embers the seer Aṅgiras. Then the goddess Vāk asked that, together with these two sons, a third son also be born. When Prajāpati granted that a further son be born, Atri, with a splendour equal to that of the sun and fire, was born from that seed which had been cast into the fire. So the story goes. Further, when Yāska gives the meaning of Atri as referring to Agni, he says हविषामत्ते (*haviṣāmatte*), that is, Agni has the name Atri because he eats the oblation. That Agni is not merely the eater of the oblation but the eater of everything is also described by the very words of the Ṛksaṃhitā. For example:
यत्ते कृष्णः शकुन अतुतोद पिपीलः सर्प उत ना श्वापदः । अग्निष्टद्विश्वादगदं कृणोतु सोमश्च यो ब्राह्मणा अविवेश ॥ (*yatte kṛṣṇaḥ śakuna atutoda pipīlaḥ sarpa uta nā śvāpadaḥ | agniṣṭadviśvādagadaṃ kṛṇotu somaśca yo brāhmaṇā aviveśa ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-16-6).
In this Ṛk Agni is praised as विश्वात् (*viśvāt*), that is, the eater of all. And:
युवानं विश्वतिं कविं विश्वादं पुरुवेपसं । अग्निं शुंभामि मन्मभिः ॥ (*yuvānaṃ viśvatiṃ kaviṃ viśvādaṃ puruvepasaṃ | agniṃ śuṃbhāmi manmabhiḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-44-26).

### Printed p. 514
Here too Agni is praised with the same epithet. On these grounds, according to the context, Atri may in some places be understood as Agni.

Besides these epithets, many passages in the Ṛksaṃhitā suggest an identity of Agni and Atri. For example:
ऋषिं नरावंशः पांचजन्यमृबीसादत्रिं मुंचथो गणेन । मिनंता हस्योरशिवस्य माया अनुपूर्वं वृषणा चोदयंता ॥ (*ṛṣiṃ narāvaṃśaḥ pāṃcajanyamṛbīsādatriṃ muṃcatho gaṇena | minaṃtā hasyoraśivasya māyā anupūrvaṃ vṛṣaṇā codayaṃtā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-3).
Here (in a Ṛk addressed to the Aśvin deities) Atri has the epithet पांचजन्य (*pāṃcajanya*). Likewise:
अग्निऋषिः पवमानः पांचजन्यः पुरोहितः । तमीमहे महागयं ॥ (*agniṛṣiḥ pavamānaḥ pāṃcajanyaḥ purohitaḥ | tamīmahe mahāgayaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-66-20).
In these and other Ṛks the word पांचजन्य (*pāṃcajanya*) is an epithet of Agni. Whatever meaning is given to पांचजन्य (*pāṃcajanya*), it is notable that it is an epithet of both Agni and Atri. It would not be wrong to call it an epithet indicating their close relation. And just as in the present Ṛk the Aśvin deities are said to have saved Atri who was in the gharma, so in
अग्निर्ह त्यं जरतः कर्णमावाग्निरद्यो निरदहज्ज रूथं । अग्निरत्रिं घर्म उरुष्यदंतरग्निर्नृमेधं प्रजयासृजत्सं ॥ (*agnirha tyaṃ jarataḥ karṇamāvāgniradyo niradahajja rūthaṃ | agniratriṃ gharma uruṣyadaṃtaragnirnṛmedhaṃ prajayāsṛjatsaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-3)
it is said that Agni saved Atri who was in the gharma. Atri's extraordinary divine qualities are described at length in Sūkta 40 of the fifth Maṇḍala of the Ṛksaṃhitā. If only a few mantras of that sūkta are examined, the deities invoked there are Sūrya, Indra and Atri:
यत्त्वा सूर्य स्वर्भानुस्तमसाविध्यदासुरः । अक्षेत्रविद्यथा मुग्गो भुवनान्यदीधयुः । स्वर्भानोरध यदिंद्र माया अवो दिवो वर्तमाना अवाहन् । गूह्लं सूर्यं तमसापव्रतेन तुरियेण ब्रह्मणाविंददत्रिः ॥ (*yattvā sūrya svarbhānustamasāvidhyadāsuraḥ | akṣetravidyathā muggo bhuvanānyadīdhayuḥ | svarbhānoradha yadiṃdra māyā avo divo vartamānā avāhan | gūhlaṃ sūryaṃ tamasāpavratena turiyeṇa brahmaṇāviṃdadatriḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-5 to 6).
Here, as soon as Svarbhānu covered the sun with darkness, all creatures were bewildered. Then Indra struck the demon down. Atri, with his divine sight, found the place where the sun, enveloped in darkness, was. And:

### Printed p. 515
गाव्यो ब्रह्मा युयुजानः सपर्यन् कीरिणा देवान्नमसोपशिक्षन् । अत्रिः सूर्यस्य दिवि चक्षुराधात्स्वर्भानोरप माया अधुक्षत् ॥ यं वै सूर्यं स्वर्भानुस्तमसाविध्यदासुरः । अत्रयस्तमन्वविंदन्नह्य १ नै अशक्नु वन् ॥ (*gāvyo brahmā yuyujānaḥ saparyan kīriṇā devānnamasopaśikṣan | atriḥ sūryasya divi cakṣurādhātsvarbhānorapa māyā adhukṣat ‖ yaṃ vai sūryaṃ svarbhānustamasāvidhyadāsuraḥ | atrayastamanvaviṃdannahya 1 nai aśaknu van ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-8 to 9).
Here Atri, engaged in sacrifice, by his divine power set the sun's eye in the sky, and destroyed the power of Svarbhānu. In the same sūkta the sun, showing his gratitude to Atri, says:
मा मामिमं तव संतमत्र इरस्या द्रुग्धो भियसा नि गारीत् । त्वं मित्रो असि सत्यराधास्तौ मोहावतं वरुणश्च राजा ॥ (*mā māmimaṃ tava saṃtamatra irasyā drugdho bhiyasā ni gārīt | tvaṃ mitro asi satyarādhāstau mohāvataṃ varuṇaśca rājā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-7).
In this Ṛk the sun seeks Atri's help, and prays: "I am yours, I belong to you; do not give me up to the demons." The description and the prayer in this mantra are like a prayer addressed to Agni. Besides these passages, if some passages in the fifth Maṇḍala, which is famous as the Atri Maṇḍala, are examined, the close relation between Agni and Atri appears there too. For example, the author of the second sūkta of the fifth Maṇḍala is famous under the name Kumāra, born in the line of Atri. But in
कुमारं माता युवतिः समुब्धं गुहा बिभर्ति न ददाति पित्रे । अनीकमस्य न मिनज्जनासः पुरः पश्यंति निहितमरतौ ॥ (*kumāraṃ mātā yuvatiḥ samubdhaṃ guhā bibharti na dadāti pitre | anīkamasya na minajjanāsaḥ puraḥ paśyaṃti nihitamaratau ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-2-1)
it is shown in Sāyaṇa's commentary that कुमारं (*kumāraṃ*) is an epithet of Agni. And in the same way, in the case of Vasuśruta, Īśa, Gaya and other Ātreyas also, a connection with Agni can be seen. It is stated that this word is derived from the root अद् (*ad*); and in the Upaniṣads too Atri is praised in this way:
नागेवात्रिर्वाचा ह्यन्नमद्यतेऽतिर्ह वै नामैतदत्रिरिति सर्वस्यात्ता भवति सर्वमस्यान्नं भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*nāgevātrirvācā hyannamadyate 'tirha vai nāmaitadatririti sarvasyāttā bhavati sarvamasyānnaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 2-2-4).
By such sentences the word Atri is described as of the nature of the Supreme Brahman. In this same sense the word Atri is used in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā as an epithet of Agni.

In the present Ṛk, the first meaning is that the Aśvin deities saved the seer Atri who had fallen into the heated fire-pit. Second, the meaning is that they gave a cooling treatment to the fire that was in the gharma.

### Printed p. 516
But one must know what gharma means here, and what the treatment of Agni there is. Sāyaṇa has explained the word gharma as Pravargya. Are gharma and Pravargya words that indicate identity, with one and the same meaning? What is the authority of the Śruti texts for this? What is the nature of gharma or Pravargya? This must now be examined. One must also know what kind of leadership the Aśvin deities exercise in the Pravargya. The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka passages that will be cited later under Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-180-9 set out clearly the relation between the Pravargya and the Aśvin deities. Here that matter will be stated briefly.
ताभ्यामेतमाश्विनमगृह्णन् । तावेतद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रत्यधत्तां । यत्प्रवर्ग्र्यः । तेन सशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानाः । अवाशिषोरुंधत । अभि सुवर्गं लोकमजयन् । (*tābhyāmetamāśvinamagṛhṇan | tāvetadyajñasya śiraḥ pratyadhattāṃ | yatpravargryaḥ | tena saśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānāḥ | avāśiṣoruṃdhata | abhi suvargaṃ lokamajayan |*)
(Kṛ. Ā. 5-1-7) **NOTE**.
The gods approached the Aśvin deities, the physicians of the gods, and prayed: "You are physicians; join the Pravargya, the head of the sacrifice, again to the body of the sacrifice, which consists of the three pressings." They, having obtained for themselves too a share in the fruit of the sacrifice, fulfilled the prayer of the gods. Hence also:
यत्प्रवर्ग्यं प्रवृणक्ति । यज्ञस्यैव तच्चिरः प्रतिदधाति । तेन सशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानः । अवाशिषो रुंधे । अभि सुवर्गं लोकं जयति । तस्मा देष आश्विनस्रवया इव । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः ॥ (*yatpravargyaṃ pravṛṇakti | yajñasyaiva tacciraḥ pratidadhāti | tena saśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānaḥ | avāśiṣo ruṃdhe | abhi suvargaṃ lokaṃ jayati | tasmā deṣa āśvinasravayā iva | yatpravargyaḥ ‖*)
(Śrī. Ā. 5-1-7) **NOTE**.
Thus the worshipper, by performing the rite called Pravargya, which even the gods honoured as the principal rite, accomplishes his desire and attains the world of heaven; in this way its greatness is praised. Since the Āśvina mantras and the pre-eminence of the Aśvin deities are principal in the time of this rite, it also has the alternative name "आश्विनप्रवयाः (*āśvinapravayāḥ*)". Next one must know the meaning of the words gharma and pravargya. The method of performing it is given in the fourth Prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka. In commenting on this passage, Sāyaṇa cites the sentences of the fifth Prapāṭhaka that explain the words pravargya and gharma, and explains the meanings of these words.
स धनुः प्रतिष्कभ्यातिष्ठत् । ता उषदीका अब्रुवन्वरं वृणामहै । अथ व इमग्ं रंथयाम। यत्र क्व च खनाम । तदपोभितृणदामेति। तस्मादुपडीका यत्र क्व च खनंति । तदपोऽभित्यंदंति। वारे वृतग्ग ह्यासां । (*sa dhanuḥ pratiṣkabhyātiṣṭhat | tā uṣadīkā abruvanvaraṃ vṛṇāmahai | atha va imagṃ raṃthayāma| yatra kva ca khanāma | tadapobhitṛṇadāmeti| tasmādupaḍīkā yatra kva ca khanaṃti | tadapo 'bhityaṃdaṃti| vāre vṛtagga hyāsāṃ |*) तस्य (*tasya*)

### Printed p. 517
…ज्यामप्यादन् । तस्य धनुर्विप्रवमाणग्ं शिर उदवर्तयत् । तष्टावापृथिवी अनुस्रावर्तत । यत्प्रावर्तत । तत्प्रवर्ग्यस्य प्रवर्ग्यत्वं । यद्भ्रा ४ इत्यपतत् । तद्धर्मस्य घर्मत्वं । (*jyāmapyādan | tasya dhanurvipravamāṇagṃ śira udavartayat | taṣṭāvāpṛthivī anusrāvartata | yatprāvartata | tatpravargyasya pravargyatvaṃ | yadbhrā 4 ityapatat | taddharmasya gharmatvaṃ |*) (Kṛ. Ā. 5-1-4-5-6) **NOTE**

This explanation hints at a story, and then states how the names Gharma and so on became well known. As told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the story runs as follows. Indra and the other gods performed a sacrificial session (sattra) at the sacrificial ground called Kurukṣetra. When the question arose of deciding who among them was the greatest, it was resolved that whoever first reached the end of the sacrifice through austerity, faith and sacrificial performance should be reckoned the greatest; Viṣṇu won that contest and was reckoned the greatest. The pride that naturally comes of such a victory also seized Viṣṇu. Full of self-conceit, Viṣṇu took up his bow, strung it, held three arrows in his hand and rested his head on the tip of his bow. None of the gods could face him, and all sat down around him. Then, to drive out his pride, the gods approached the worm-like creatures called vamrī (ants) and asked them to cut the bowstring; they cut the string of Viṣṇu's bow. (There is also a variant reading that Indra himself, in the form of a vamrī, cut it: तस्येंद्रो वम्रिरूपेण ! धनुर्ज्यामभिनत्स्वयं (*tasyeṃdro vamrirūpeṇa ! dhanurjyāmabhinatsvayaṃ*).) Then the tip of the bow sprang up and Viṣṇu's head was cut off.

When the bowstring was cut, it fell making the sound *phṛṇ* (फृण्णिति पतात (*phṛṇṇiti patāta*)); therefore the name Gharma became well known for it. Because the bow, which had been bent, spread out wide the moment the string was cut, the name Pravargya became well known for it.

मखस्य शिरोसीत्याह । यज्ञो वै मखः । (*makhasya śirosītyāha | yajño vai makhaḥ |*) (Kṛ. A. 5-3-2) **NOTE**

In these sentences the passage that praises Pravargya as the head of all sacrifices is quoted, and its primacy is stated. Then:

ब्रह्मन् प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरिष्यामः। होतर्घर्ममभिष्टुहि । (*brahman pravargyeṇa pracariṣyāmaḥ| hotargharmamabhiṣṭuhi |*) (Tai. Ā. 4-4-1)

ब्रह्मन् प्रचरिष्यामः । होतर्घर्ममभिष्टुहि । (*brahman pracariṣyāmaḥ | hotargharmamabhiṣṭuhi |*) (Tai. Ā. 4-5-1)

By such mantras the setting up of the Pravargya is carried out. The nature of the Pravargya and its greatness will also be explained later at a suitable place. Since in the present Ṛk the word Gharma is explained as Pravargya, the aim here is only to show that the two belong to the same rite.

### Printed p. 518
Paśvaiṣṭiḥ (पश्वइष्टिः (*paśvaiṣṭiḥ*))—two explanations are given. First: पशुरित्यग्नेर्नाम । (*paśurityagnernāma |*) Since Agni is also a *paśu* (victim), the sacrifice that has Agni for its nature is called the animal sacrifice; the Taittirīya Saṃhitā passage is also quoted:

अग्निः पशुरासीत्तेनायजंत स एतं लोकमजयद्यस्मिन्नग्निः ॥ (*agniḥ paśurāsīttenāyajaṃta sa etaṃ lokamajayadyasminnagniḥ ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 5-7-26) **NOTE**

Agni was the sacrificial victim, and after he was offered as oblation, they won the world in which Agni now holds sway; thus it is described. On this basis, when "पश्वइष्टिः (*paśvaiṣṭiḥ*)" is said, it can be explained as the Agni-sacrifice having the nature of the victim. Or else: अथवा पशुप्रियत्वात्पशुरित्युच्यते । तस्याग्नेः इष्टिर्भवति । अग्नौ यागः सर्वो युष्मदर्थं प्रवर्तते । (*athavā paśupriyatvātpaśurityucyate | tasyāgneḥ iṣṭirbhavati | agnau yāgaḥ sarvo yuṣmadarthaṃ pravartate |*). Because Agni is fond of animals, the name *paśu* is well known for Agni too. Here the oblation offered in Agni is understood as the present praise, since you also have a share in it and since it is an oblation offered for you. This same sense is supported, Sāyaṇa explains, by sentences such as

आश्विनं धूम्रललाममा लभेत यो दुर्ब्राह्मणः सोमं पिपासेत् । (*āśvinaṃ dhūmralalāmamā labheta yo durbrāhmaṇaḥ somaṃ pipāset |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-10-1)

##### Grammar

- घर्मम्—घर्मः (उ. सू. १-१४६) इति फृ क्षरणदीव्योः इति धातोः मत् प्रत्ययः गुणश्च निपातितः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- अपः—षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया आगता । ऊडिदंपदादि (पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- अवृणीतम्—वृज् संभक्तौ इति धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लज् मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनांतरूपम् । तिणंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- एषे—इषु इच्छायां इति धातुः । अन्येभ्योपि दृश्यंते (पा. सू. ३-२-७५) इति विच् प्रत्ययः । पुगंतलघूपधस्य च इति लघूपधायाः गुणः । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपम् । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- रथ्या—रथाद्यत् (पा. सू. ४-३-१२१) इति संबंधार्थे यत् प्रत्ययः । यॆतोनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । नपुंसकबहुवचने

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Dasras, destroyers of enemies, Aśvins! For your giving (दानाय (*dānāya*)), that is, for the boon we desire, I wish to bring (ववृतीय (*vavṛtīya*)) you; I turn the sacrificial place," that is, I turn you toward it; this is the form of the root वृशे (*vṛśe*) with an inner causative sense. By what means? That is stated: by the conveying (ओहेन (*ohena*)) of गोः (*goḥ*), that is, of speech in the form of praise, as the means. Or else the time of turning is meant: by the bringing of the going Uṣas (गोर्गंत्रा उषसो वहनेन (*gorgaṃtrā uṣaso vahanena*)). Jivri is the aged one, or the victorious one; "like Taugrya", that is, like Bhujyu, son of the king named Tugra. Just as he, struck by enemies and thrown into the sea, pleased you and brought you near himself for his rescue, so is the meaning. This story is well known from passages such as तुगो ह (*tugo ha*) (Ṛ. 1-116-3), भुज्युमंहसः पिपृथः (*bhujyumaṃhasaḥ pipṛthaḥ*) (Ṛ. 10-65-12) and नासत्या भुज्युं (*nāsatyā bhujyuṃ*) (Ṛ. 1-116-4). "What wonder that I turn you? Rather: अपः क्षोणी (*apaḥ kṣoṇī*) …" The gloss of "अपः (*apaḥ*)" begins here and goes on in the next block.

> पापाज्जरालक्षणात्पमुच्याक्षुश्शिरकालव्याप्तो दीर्घजीवी भूयात् । यद्वा ।
> हे यजत्रा वां प्रसादाज्यूर्णो जीर्णो यजमानोऽंहसो दुरितस्य
> हंत्रीरप उक्तलक्षणानि सोमरसरूपाण्युदकानि क्षोणी क्षोण्यां ॥ सप्तम्यर्थे
> प्रगृह्यं ॥ भूम्यां चिरकालमक्षुव्याप्तः सन् माहिना माहात्म्येन सचते ।
> द्वितीयो वामित्ययमादरार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अप (*apa*) is a name of the atmosphere, क्षोणी (*kṣoṇī*) a name of the earth. Heaven and earth too, by your greatness, that is, by your grace, each attends (सचते (*sacate*), serves) your fame as benefactors of all, or your all-pervasiveness. Or else: by your greatness the sacrificer attends heaven and earth. Further, O adorable ones, by your grace this seer, aged in body, freed from the sin of old age, would be long-pervading (अक्षुः (*akṣuḥ*)), long-lived. Or else: O adorable ones, by your grace the aged sacrificer, pervading the earth (क्षोणी (*kṣoṇī*) being locative in the sense of the seventh case, a pragṛhya) for a long time, attends with your greatness the waters of the described kind, the sin-destroying soma-juices. The second वां (*vāṃ*) is for respect.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) दस्रा (*(he) dasrā*)—O Aśvin gods, destroyers of enemies
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two

- तौग्र्यः न (*taugryaḥ na*)—like Bhujyu, son of Tugra (who called you near himself for his rescue)
- आ ववृतीय (*ā vavṛtīya*)—I wish to bring (you) to the sacrificial hall

- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—sin-removing

- क्षोणी (*kṣoṇī*)—on the earth
- अक्षुः (*akṣuḥ*)—pervading (for a long time), (having obtained)
- माहिना (*māhinā*)—by greatness
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two
- सचते (*sacate*)—serves
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the atmosphere (and)
- क्षोणी (*kṣoṇī*)—the earth
- वां (*vāṃ*)—of you two
- माहिना (*māhinā*)—by greatness (having won fame as benefactors of the world)
- सचते (*sacate*)—serve (both of you)
- [or वां (*vāṃ*)—of you two; माहिना (*māhinā*)—by greatness; अपः क्षोणी (*apaḥ kṣoṇī*)—earth and atmosphere; सचते (*sacate*)—(the sacrificer) serves]
- *(kiṃcè)*—and further
- यजत्रा (*yajatrā*)—O Nāsatyas, worthy of sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Dasras, as Bhujyu, son of Tugra, whose body had grown old, once summoned you two for his own rescue, so I too, praising you at dawn, wish to summon you to my sacrificial hall for the fulfilment of my desire. This sacrificer becomes able to attend heaven and earth by your greatness alone. O venerable Aśvin gods, this seer too, aged in body, is freed from old age by your grace and becomes long-lived.

### Printed p. 521

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Dasras, may I bring you, by the vehicle of my prayers, (hither), to bestow (upon me your aid), like the infirm son of Tugra: heaven and earth combine (to worship you) through your greatness: may this, your aged (worshipper), adorable (Ashwins), enjoy long life, (exempt) from sin.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Dasrā (printed हस्रा (*hasrā*) **NOTE**)—दसु उपक्षयी । शत्रुणां उपक्षपयितारौ । यद्वा । देववैद्यत्वेन रोगाणां उपक्षपयितारौ । (*dasu upakṣayī | śatruṇāṃ upakṣapayitārau | yadvā | devavaidyatvena rogāṇāṃ upakṣapayitārau |*). The meaning: destroyers of enemies, or, being the physicians of the gods, destroyers of diseases. "दस्रा (*dasrā*)" can also mean दर्शनीयौ (*darśanīyau*), that is, those with a beautiful form. In the present Ṛk it is explained as destroyers of enemies. Although of the two Aśvins, sons of Saraṇyū, one has the name Dasra and the other Nāsatya, it is customary to speak of both together as "दस्रा (*dasrā*)". The origin and nature of the Aśvin gods will be explained fully later in this same volume, in the Special Topics of Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-4.

Of the words गोः ओहेन (*goḥ ohena*), two meanings are given for गोः (*goḥ*). First, गोः स्तुतिरूपाय वाचः ओहेन वहनेन साथने न। (*goḥ stutirūpāya vācaḥ ohena vahanena sāthane na|*): by means of speech in the form of praise. Second, गोः गंत्र्याः उषसः वहनेन (*goḥ gaṃtryāḥ uṣasaḥ vahanena*): by the bringing, in the form of the movement, of Uṣas.

The author of the Nirukta, having included the word गो (*go*) among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5), then gives the derivation of this word as follows:

गौरिति पृथिव्या नामधेयं । यद्दूरंगता भवति । यच्चास्यां भूतानि गच्छंति। गातेर्नौकाशो नामकरणः । (*gauriti pṛthivyā nāmadheyaṃ | yaddūraṃgatā bhavati | yaccāsyāṃ bhūtāni gacchaṃti| gāternaukāśo nāmakaraṇaḥ |*) (Ni. 2 7-5) **NOTE**

Because it is spread out very far (दूरंगता भवति (*dūraṃgatā bhavati*)), or because beings move on it (भूतानि गच्छंति (*bhūtāni gacchaṃti*)), the word गौः (*gauḥ*) is a synonym of the earth. The author of the Nirukta explains the word, saying that it can be derived also by adding an affix ऽ (*'*) **NOTE** to the root गा (*gā*), and then goes on:

### Printed p. 522
अथाऽपि पतुनापि भवत्येकस्मादेव (*athā 'pi patunāpi bhavatyekasmādeva*)

For this very reason, that is, because it is formed from the root गम् (*gam*) or गा (*gā*) giving the sense stated above, this name is well known also for the animal; and having said so, he says आदित्योऽपि गौरुच्यते ; सर्वेऽपि रत्नयो गाव उच्यंते । (*ādityo 'pi gaurucyate ; sarve 'pi ratnayo gāva ucyaṃte |*) **NOTE**. He shows that the word गो (*go*) is also used in the senses of sun, ray and so on. And in explaining a word in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-28 the author of the Nirukta explains the word गौः (*gauḥ*) as माध्यमिका वाक् (*mādhyamikā vāk*) (Ni. 11-42). In the present Ṛk it is proper to explain it as speech in the form of praise. Earlier, in the Ṛk

इमं रथमथि ये सप्त तस्थुः सप्तचक्रं सप्त वहंत्यश्वाः । सप्त स्वसारो अभि सं नवंते यत्र गवां निहिता सप्त नाम ॥ (*imaṃ rathamathi ye sapta tasthuḥ saptacakraṃ sapta vahaṃtyaśvāḥ | sapta svasāro abhi saṃ navaṃte yatra gavāṃ nihitā sapta nāma ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-3)

just as गवां (*gavāṃ*) is explained as गवां स्तुतिरूपाणां वाजां (*gavāṃ stutirūpāṇāṃ vājāṃ*), so here too स्तुतिरूपायाः वाचः (*stutirūpāyāḥ vācaḥ*) is fitting.

Ohena—this word, formed from the root वह् (*vah*), is used in the sense of "the means that carries". There are many usages such as ओहसा (*ohasā*) and ओहब्रह्माणः (*ohabrahmāṇaḥ*); they will be explained in their own places.

Jivri—Sāyaṇa has said in the bhāṣya that this word can have the two meanings "aged" or "victorious". But in the Ṛks quoted in the Nirukta (Ni. 3-21)

आ त्वा रंभं न जीव्रयो ररंभा शवसस्पते । उष्मसि त्वा सधस्थ आ ॥ (*ā tvā raṃbhaṃ na jīvrayo raraṃbhā śavasaspate | uṣmasi tvā sadhastha ā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-45-20)

एना पत्या तन्वं १ सं सृजस्वाधा जिव्री विदथमा वदाथः । (*enā patyā tanvaṃ 1 saṃ sṛjasvādhā jivrī vidathamā vadāthaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-27)

and the like, Yāska has explained it everywhere as "aged, old". But here the word जूर्ण (*jūrṇa*), which shows the sense of old age, is used again; so in the present Ṛk the word जिव्रि (*jivri*) might also be explained as "victorious".

Jūrṇaḥ—जरया जीर्णांगः (*jarayā jīrṇāṃgaḥ*): the meaning is, one whose body has been worn out by old age. In other places Sāyaṇa has given another meaning to the word जूर्ण (*jūrṇa*). The author of the Nirukta reads the word जूर्ति (*jūrti*) among the names of anger (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of the swift (Ni. 3-9), and gives this derivation:

जीर्णर्जवतेर्वा द्रवरेवा दूनोशेर्वा । (*jīrṇarjavatervā dravarevā dūnośervā |*) (3. 6-4) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 523

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The word is explained as formed either from the root जू (*jū*) meaning "speed", or from the root द्रु (*dru*) meaning "run", or from the root दु (*du*) meaning "injure". To show its use, the Ṛk हतेमसन्न वक्षति क्षिप्ता जूर्णिर्न वक्षति (*hatemasanna vakṣati kṣiptā jūrṇirna vakṣati*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-8) is cited. There जूर्णिः (*jūrṇiḥ*) is explained as "power", because power is connected with casting (क्षेपणसंबंधात्जूर्णिः शक्तिः (*kṣepaṇasaṃbaṃdhātjūrṇiḥ śaktiḥ*)) and has speed. In the present Ṛk, however, there is no room for that meaning. जिव्रिः (*jivriḥ*) must be taken as "victorious" and जूर्णः (*jūrṇaḥ*) as "advanced in years".
जीविः (*jīviḥ*) is an adjective of the word शौग्र्यः (*śaugryaḥ*). Here the sacrificer compares himself with Śaugrya: as Śaugrya was lifted out by the favour of the Aśvins, so he too declares that he will share in their favour.
Sāyaṇa explains: तौग्र्यः न तुग्राख्यस्य राज्ञः पुत्रो भुज्युरिव स यथा शत्रुभिः संताड्य समुद्रे पातितो युवां परितोष्य स्वोद्धाराय स्वसमीपमानयत तद्वदित्यर्थः । (*taugryaḥ na tugrākhyasya rājñaḥ putro bhujyuriva sa yathā śatrubhiḥ saṃtāḍya samudre pātito yuvāṃ paritoṣya svoddhārāya svasamīpamānayata tadvadityarthaḥ |*). That is, as the son of Tugra, Bhujyu, when he had been struck by enemies and thrown into the sea, praised and pleased you and called you to his own help, so [the sacrificer may do]; thus the background story is indicated.
Once enemies defeated the king named Taugrya, bound his hands and feet and threw him into the middle of the sea. Unable to cross the sea, he prayed to the Aśvins for help. At once they yoked horses to their chariot, drove down into the sea and brought him to the shore. Thus Sāyaṇa has cited the earlier story. This son of Tugra is the one famous under the name Bhujyu, and his story is described in many places.
That the Aśvins saved this same son of Tugra, who had sunk in the sea, is described by Kakṣīvān, son of Dīrghatamas, in the sūktas Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116 and 1-117; by Agastya Maitrāvaruṇi in sūkta 1-182; by Brahmātithi of the Kaṇva gotra in sūkta 8-5; and by Ghoṣā, daughter of Kakṣīvān, in 10-39. In sūkta 1-182 it is likewise described, as follows, how they sent boats, and how the son of Tugra, filled with hope, clasped those boats and was saved by their favour.
युवमेतं चक्रथुः सिंधुषु प्लवमात्मनंतं दक्षिणं तौग्राय कं । येन देवत्रा मनसा निरूहथुः सुपप्तनी पेशथुः क्षोदसो महः॥ (*yuvametaṃ cakrathuḥ siṃdhuṣu plavamātmanaṃtaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ taugrāya kaṃ | yena devatrā manasā nirūhathuḥ supaptanī peśathuḥ kṣodaso mahaḥ‖*)
अवविद्धं तौग्रमप्सन्नरनारंभणे तमसि प्रविद्दं । चतस्रो नावो जठलस्य जुष्टा उदश्चिभ्यामिषिताः पारयंति । (*avaviddhaṃ taugramapsannaranāraṃbhaṇe tamasi praviddaṃ | catasro nāvo jaṭhalasya juṣṭā udaścibhyāmiṣitāḥ pārayaṃti |*)

### Printed p. 524
कः सिद्वृक्षो निष्कृतो मध्ये अर्णसो यं तौग्रो नाधितः पर्यषस्वजत् ॥ पर्णा मृगस्य पतरोरिवारभ उदश्विना ऊहथुः श्रोमताय कं ॥ (*kaḥ sidvṛkṣo niṣkṛto madhye arṇaso yaṃ taugro nādhitaḥ paryaṣasvajat ‖ parṇā mṛgasya patarorivārabha udaśvinā ūhathuḥ śromatāya kaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-182-5 to 7)
O Aśvins, for Bhujyu the son of Tugra you made this boat, endowed with life and furnished with wings. For the son of Tugra, who had fallen and was sinking in the fathomless, dark sea, you sent four boats. Like the wings that support flying birds in the sky, the parts of the boat that supported and protected Bhujyu sinking in the sea — from what tree did you make them? Thus it is praised. The same point is indicated in the present Ṛk also.
अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—अंहतिश्चां हंश्चांहुश्च हंतेः (*aṃhatiścāṃ haṃścāṃhuśca haṃteḥ*) (Ni. 4-25). The word अंहस् (*aṃhas*) is formed from the root हन् (*han*) meaning "injure", yet in ordinary use the meaning "sin" is commoner than "injury". In the present Ṛk it means distress (दुरित (*durita*)).
It is stated that three constructions are possible for the second half of this mantra. First, (1) जूर्णः माहिना अंहसः अपः क्षोणी अक्षुः पां सचते (*jūrṇaḥ māhinā aṃhasaḥ apaḥ kṣoṇī akṣuḥ pāṃ sacate*): the aged sacrificer, freed from sin by your favour and having obtained Soma permanently, serves you on earth. Second, (2) वां महिना अपः क्षोणी सचते (*vāṃ mahinā apaḥ kṣoṇī sacate*): by your greatness heaven and earth are both famed as protectors of the world. Third, (3) वां महिना जूर्णः अपः क्षोणी सचते (*vāṃ mahinā jūrṇaḥ apaḥ kṣoṇī sacate*): by your greatness the sacrificer serves heaven and earth. Sāyaṇa's commentary states that the meaning may be any of these.
अपः (*apaḥ*) is read among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 3-8). क्षोणीति पृथिवीनाम (*kṣoṇīti pṛthivīnāma*): क्षोणि (*kṣoṇi*) is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-7).

##### Grammar

- दानाय — डुदाञ् दाने इति धातुः । युच् प्रत्ययः । युवोरनाकौ (पा सू ७-१-१) इति तस्य अनादेशः । चितः इति अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- ववृतीय — वृतु वर्तने इति धातुः । प्रयोजकव्यापारदर्शनात् अंतर्भावितण्यर्थकः भवति । लिट् उत्तमपुरुष एकवचने इट् प्रत्ययः । इटोऽत् (पा. सू. ३-४-१०६) इति तस्य अकारादेशः । लिजः सीयुट् (पा. सू. ३-४-१०२) इति सीयुटागमः । बहुलं छंदसि इति श्लु विकरणः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोः द्वित्वादि । लिजः सलोपो नंत्यस्य (पा. सू. ७-२-७९) इति सकारस्य लोपः । ववृतीय इति रूपं भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।

### Printed p. 525
- दस्रा — सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू ७-१-३९) इति द्विवचनस्य आकारादेशः । आमंत्रितनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- जिव्रिः — जृष् वयोहानौ इति धातुः । जीर्यतेः क्रिन् रश्च वः (उ. सू. ५-७२) इति क्रिन् प्रत्ययः । धातोः रेफस्य वकारादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- जूर्णः — ज्वर संतापे इति धातुः । क्त प्रत्ययः । ज्वरत्वर स्रिव्यवि (पा. सू. ६-४-२०) इति धातोः वकारोपधयोः ऊठादेशः । रदाभ्यां निष्ठातो नः पूर्वस्य च दः (पा. सू. ८-२-४२) इति निष्ठातकारस्य नत्वम् । रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे इति णत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । **NOTE**
- यजत्रा — यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु इति धातुः । अमिनक्षि यजि बंधि (उ. सू. ३-३८५) इति अत्रन् प्रत्ययः । सुपां सुलुक् इति संबोधनाद्विवचनस्य आकारादेशः । आमंत्रितनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- क्षोणी — द्वितीयार्थे सप्तमी एकवचनांतरूपम् । सुपां सुलुक् इति सूत्रेण पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । ईदूतौ च सप्तम्यर्थे (पा. सू. १-१-१९) इति प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा भवति ।

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि यद्यु॒वेथे॑ नि॒युतः॑ सुदानू॒ उप॑ स्व॒धाभिः॑ सृजथः॒ पुरं॑धिं ।  
> प्रेष॒द्वेष॒द्वातो॒ न सू॒रिरा म॒हे द॑दे सुव्र॒तो न वाजं॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । यत् । युवेथे इति । नियुशः । सुदानू इति सुदानू । उप । स्वधाभिः ।  
> सृजथः । पुरंधिं ।  
> प्रेषत् । वेषत् । वातः । न । सूरिः । आ । महे । ददे । सुव्रतः । न । वाजं ॥ ६ ॥
